product_title: Turtle Beach Ear Force Z22 Amplified PC Gaming Headset
review_body:
This is one of the worst investments you could make.

Okay, I don't actually remember when exactly I bought these, but I wanna say it's been a good 2-3 years. At first, the sound and the mic both worked correctly. There were issues with getting some of the functions to work correctly, such as making chat volume adjustable on the amp that came with the headset, and other things of that nature. Now, I'm not technologically inept. I've built my last two computers, and I'm more than able to install devices, update drivers, etc. At any rate, I didn't care too much because the headset itself worked, with pretty good sound, and the mic worked and was decent.

Then, maybe a year or so after having it, I built a new computer, and the mic stopped working. Believe me when I say that I tried everything. I tried finding drivers on the official site, unofficial sites. I tried using every USB port on my system (even though other devices worked perfectly fine). I tried looking up solutions on message forums and such. I even messed around with settings in my Bios. Nothing. I probably kept using the headset for well over a year without a working mic, just because I was too broke to get a new one (after all, the headset's sound still worked). You can see from many reviews that Turtle Beach will deny all responsibility and say the problem is on your end. So after some brief interactions, I no longer bothered with them. But do let me make it abundantly clear that I have NEVER had a single device, before or since, that wouldn't work on this computer, which I've now had for over a year. That includes my new headset that I just got today (different company of course), webcams, game controllers... just about anything you can think of. And that's considering I'm now on Windows 10. Still no issues with any other device.

I am never, and I repeat NEVER, buying a product from Turtle Beach again. If anyone asks me about them, I will warn against buying from the company. I suggest you do the same. Do not buy these. I don't know if I'm allowed to make a recommendation for another headset on here, so I won't, but there are actually good ones out there. Please read the other recent reviews of the multitude of people without a working mic or sound for no good reason.

Once again, DO NOT BUY.

Nowhere in that description are exo-limbs, super jumping, laser rifles, or Kevin Spacey running for his life. This may be the last Call of Duty with normal jumping. Think about that, and also realize that the Hardened Edition is only $26 and includes $50 in DLC (the codes still work). It's a great value, even if you're paying for recycled materials. A bit of a preface, I own way too many computer glasses... in part because I could never find a pair that was just right. Picked these up straight from the Allure website.

This particular model, the CODG4 has definitely gotten close to being the best pair of glasses I have found so far. I have about $300 worth of Gunnar's, a handful of the Gamma Ray glasses, a noscope (fake computer glasses, avoid) and another Allure model (broke, cheaply made).

Pros
The quality of the frame is fantastic, it contours nicely around the eyes. Look good wearing them, which is a rarity with these types of glasses. Extremely lightweight.

Cons
Lens quality is questionable, where most glasses feel smooth when wiping with a microfiber cloth...these feel rough. Could just be the coating applied to the surface. This is worth the cost. Well done Allure, please keep up with this kind of form factor and if you can upgrade the lens quality as well as reduce the tint... I would gladly pay even more for that what these are going for now.

Thoughtfully structured to reward both action and stealth-play in equal measure, Splinter Cell Blacklist is, undoubtedly, the most well-rounded entry in the series. It's clear Ubisoft took note of the SC's core fan-base and their general disdain for 2010's sharp left-turn for the series, Conviction: Blacklist puts heavy emphasis on the mechanics that made the first three (or four, depending who you're talking to) outings particularly rewarding for old-schoolers, namely thrilling cat-and-mouse sequences and a stronger focus of sneaky infiltration. As a fan of Conviction though, I appreciate the fact Ubisoft took time to recognize the fluid, intuitive aspects of that entry, and apply it to some of Blacklist's stickier, less forgiving campaign encounters. The "Press Y and Win" Executions return, as well, but play a far less prominent role in game than they did in Conviction; still, when they are used, it makes for a fun reprieve from the tense technicality of pure stealth-play.

From the extensive customization options with Sam Fisher's spy gear to the wide variety of missions on display here, Blacklist highlights its flexible and robust wiggle-room for play-style top to bottom. Side-missions and co-op are well-designed, and just as rewarding as the single-player campaign. It's nice to see Spy Vs. Mercs make a return as well, though its lost some its signature ability to wrack nerves since its last appearance in '06.

The campaign itself is a bit of a letdown. Despite moments of strong dialogue, the writing on display is mostly a mix of tactical assessment and brooding confrontation. There's a fun, genuinely engaging villain to contend with, but Sam's team, with the exception of his tech guru and a familiar (and, for Sam, unwelcomed) face from Conviction, are largely by-the-numbers espionage players with voice-acting as plastic as their facial-animations. That said, the campaign is rich mission variety and memorable set-pieces: the plot itself is gripping, and the stakes are as high as they've ever been. It's a shame Michael Ironside doesn't man the helm voicing Fisher again, but Eric Johnson doesn't do half a shabby job given the shoes he's expected to fill.

Buyer beware, Splinter Cell Blacklist's massive amount of content begets massive load-times. The HD Texture Pack is a must to get the most out of the game: while graphics typically don't make or break these kinds of games, the atmosphere and lighting effects on display in Blacklist are top-shelf and really enhance the experience on mechanical level as well as an aesthetic one. I'd also recommend installing both discs to significantly cut down load-times, which are a sure-fire way to waste six-minutes of your life otherwise.

Overall, the game is sure to please newcomers and purists alike. A masterclass military stealth game.

review_headline: I want to like this game
review_body: I want to like this game, I really do and while I can appreciate, hell I yearn for challenge in games I can not suffer through the the absolutely horrid controls of this game that has led to a near instant death countless times. Whether its spinning you away from your target just in time for them to land a mortal blow or somehow completely missing a target standing directly in front of you with the target lock on...also leaving yourself wide open for an attack it's just one giant exercise in frustration. Switching  between weapons and the modes of weapons is just as slow and painful.  The currency and experience system is interesting, being one in the same but just adds another dimension of frustration to the game when you have to grind through repetitive areas to collect enough and hope that the game behaves consistently enough for you to make it through, you die and you have to fight back to that point to get back what you lost(it seems many times it just disappears which I assume it a bug). Instead of a novel concept though it just makes the game a bigger headache.   I may come back just to try and get through the story but if they don't either fix these controls or make and easy mode just to cruise through the story I suspect I will just give up again.

product_title: PDP AG7 True Wireless Headset for Xbox One
review_headline: Great sounding headphones, but microphone volume is lacking
review_body:
[[VIDEOID:a9ebb8e7454df6453f81e67fa32070eb]] The AG7's are a great sounding wireless headset for the Xbox One. It has the added bonus of also working with Windows computers through the included USB dongle and will also work with anything else that supports a standard 1/8\\" headphone/headset adapter. That includes mobile devices running Android as well as iPhones and Macs.

The bass is loud and evident even in the standard mode. There's a second audio mode that gives a little more boom but it comes at the expense of overall audio clarity. The default mode is good enough for me.

The biggest issue with AG7, however, is the included mic. The pickup level is very low, meaning you are going to sound very distant during in-game chats. I found this to be the case both with the Xbox One and my Windows PC using the wireless dongle. Plugging in via an analog cable to my Mac resulted in louder audio, so I suspect there's a setting on the dongle that's limiting the mic's audio output.

The mic mute indicator is also confusing. For some reason PDP decided the light on the mic should indicate which audio mode the headphones are in, not the mute status of the microphone. It will indicate mute with a blink every minute or so, but it would have made more sense to have the mic light up red when muted. It also won't mute when it's retracted back into its holder.

If they can fix the mic issues I will rate this set higher. It really does sound very good but it's not the total package it is currently advertising itself to be.

product_title: Elder Scrolls 3 Morrowind Expansion Pack: Bloodmoon - PC
review_body:
It's always great when dev.'s do expansions CORRECTLY, especially when it's adding whole new regions. The only irritant is that every NPC wants to tell you about the place, as if you had no clue what the product description WAS.

Speaking of which...
"Product Dimensions: 5.2 x 7.2 x 1 inches ; 4.8 ounces"
...it didn't arrive in a box, JUST the disk itself. Don't get this if you're a collector like me, it's disappointing to wait on it being shipped for more than a digital copy. Some of us gamers would like the FULL product.

One of the greatest games of the NES era. This has the best graphics I've seen on the system, with a level of detail many NES programmers probably thought impossible. The music is also great, with some catchy adventure-themed tunes and some really moody stuff for when you're making your way through the deepest catacombs of Transylvania. And with four playable characters, multiple routes through the countryside on your journey to Dracula's castle, and a more challenging "second quest" (as if the first quest wasn't challenging enough), this game has a lot of replay value. Best of all the game manages to capture a very spooky gothic-horror feel without any gore to speak of (unless you count all the skeletons and skulls), so the game is mature enough for an adult but family-friendly enough for a child.

The gameplay is very fun - but also very challenging. (If you're not up for replaying levels dozens of times as you learn how to make it through them, you should probably try something easier - or at least look up some cheat codes.) If you like dark and spooky games and don't mind a challenge, I highly recommend this game.

review_headline: Still holds up after all these years.
review_body:
About five or six years ago Namco Bandai released this little gem of a game. In the intervening years, people seem to refer to this game as a "hidden gem," "overlooked," etc. All those descriptors are true. It really is one of the most under appreciated games in recent memory.

I loved this game for many reasons, but above all, I loved it for the relationship between Monkey and Trip. Andy Serkis and Lindsey Shaw are simply superb in this game. In fact, Lindsey Shaw was so good that I'm really, really surprised she hasn't done more voice work since. Maybe she's been approached and decided not to. I dunno. Whatever the case may be, I really wish she'd lend her talents more often. She's great.

Andy Serkis, of course, is no slouch. With a resume that includes Lord of the Rings and the upcoming Star Wars, his bona fides are beyond question and he's amazing in his role of Monkey. For a big brute of a thing, Monkey is grounded in reality and very, very human. This, of course, is thanks to Mr. Serkis.

I won't go into plot or gameplay, though I believe both are superb, because to do so would potentially rob you of the experience. I will say, however, that its one of those games that stays with you long after you complete it. It's a beautiful world filled with engaging, yet simplistic gameplay and anchored by two extraordinary actors.

If you've not played this yet, I highly recommend it.

product_title: Titan Quest Gold (Titan Quest and Titan Quest Immortal Throne)
review_body:
Pros:
- Fun to play.
- Lots of action and cool loot.
- Story and setting based on Greek mythology instead of generic medieval Europe.
- Different skill sets allow you to customize your gameplay to suit your own preferred style.
- Reminds me of old school top-down RPGs like Baldur's Gate and Icewind Dale.

Cons:
- Enemy respawning is very frustrating. You can spend hours clearing out an area or trying to move forward through a new map, but if you have to quit playing for some reason, you end up having to kill the same enemies over again. It can get tedious after a while.

- Most loot has minimum level and/or attribute requirements. For example, some equipment requires at least a certain Strength or certain Dexterity in order to be equipped. This means that, sometimes, when you find an awesome piece of gear, you can't use it right away. If you want to save it for later, you have to haul it around in your inventory until you finally do meet the requirements. And get this: because of the way the savegame function works, if you accidentally sell the item, you have lost it forever.

- While it does have a savegame feature, it is very limited. Essentially, the savegame resets the game world (causing enemies to respawn and unclaimed loot to be lost), and starts you back at the last Rebirth Pool you encountered. If you make a drastic mistake, you can't simply reload. If you die, the game just restarts you at a Rebirth Pool and penalizes your experience.

- It feels a bit dungeon-crawly. The sheer number of enemies on the map, and the distances between the different points of interest, it feels like there is nothing but combat to this game. You really only interact with NPCs for quests, and even those exchanges feel limited.

Other Thoughts:

For the price, this isn't a bad game. I played it for a whole weekend, pretty intently at that, and I barely made it as far as Delphi,the 4th of about 7 major cities in Greece. But it looks like there are even more cities in Egypt and the Orient. So, yeah, there does appear to be lot to this game.

The story is a bit lackluster. Mostly, it's just, "Go to this city and look for this person," followed by miles of wilderness adventure; lather, rinse, repeat.

People used to games like Skyrim will probably find this game somewhat dated.

I can't say I love it, but I can't say I dislike it, either; it is frustrating, but also fun. I will probably finish it just for point, but I'm not sure how likely I am to return to it once I do.

product_title: Thrustmaster T-Flight Hotas X Flight Stick
review_headline: You get what you pay for, I guess...
review_body:
~ PROS ~
- One of the cheapest HOTAS sticks you'll find.
- Nice shape / comfortable grips.
- Throttle stick has a nice "catch" zone at 0 value, letting you easily kill your speed without switching into reverse.

~ CONS ~
- Cheap and noisy plastic construction.
- Catchy, inaccurate movement on every axis of the joystick.
- Huge deadzones that the configuration software won't fix.
- Short cord between the sticks makes fitting a keyboard between pretty difficult.

I've had my eye on a HOTAS setup for a while, and this one in particular for its affordability. I'm a huge fan of space flight games like Elite:Dangerous, Jumpgate, Vendetta Online, Starport Gemini and so on, but I didn't want to dish out hundreds for the immersion a simple throttle + joystick combo can offer. Long story short: I should have.

For a budget HOTAS this one of very few options on the market, which is a huge shame. The throttle stick isn't terrible and would work fine on its own (if you don't mind a little inaccuracy around the "catch" zone when trying to fine tune your thrust for landings), but the joystick is simply awful, with massive deadzones on every axis and very inconsistent, cheap-feeling tension throughout the movement ranges. For a game like Elite: Dangerous, precise yaw control is crucial for micro-adjusting your aim when you've got an enemy in the crosshairs, and the awkward tension of this joystick's yaw axis combined with its large deadzone will leave you swinging dramatically to the left and right of your target. Beyond the poor movement and feel of the stick, the cheap plastic makes a groaning/squeaking sound that I wasn't able to ignore, though I imagine this might have gradually improved if I had taken the time to break in the stick and wear down whatever component was causing the sound.

If none of the above deters you, then congrats! Performance aside, the entire unit feels comfortable to hold and the button placement feels fine, if perhaps a bit sparse. I was able to compensate for the lack of buttons by programming multiple button presses simultaneously, effectively grouping commands by treating the buttons on the throttle stick like "shift," "alt," "control" and so on. I found that the cable between the two sticks was long enough to let me rest each stick comfortably at shoulder width, but not long enough to allow my keyboard to fit between them, which made my overall setup pretty awkward and cumbersome. I tried playing with both halves of the unit connected, but I felt cramped and contorted, so I wouldn't recommend it.

If you simply MUST play with a HOTAS, but you're shopping on a budget and you don't mind trying to aim and steer as though you're riddled with Parkinson's, then go ahead and throw money at this stick. Otherwise, keep shopping around. product_title: Classic Retro N64 Bit USB Wired Controller for PC and MAC - Black
review_headline: Feels Nice, but has serious flaws that are non-starters for me
review_body:
The controller and buttons feel good, but there are some glaring flaws that were dealbreakers for me.

Pros:

Feels like a normal N64 Controller.
USB is convenient.

Cons:

The stick seems to be binary in its positions; you are either in the center or all the way at the edge. This means that if you were to push the stick slightly or part way it would be the same as if you pushed it all the way to the edge. You would normally expect the controller/game to respond incrementally depending on how far you move the stick out from the center.

The stick and directional pad (left) share the same input. Pressing up on the pad is the same as pushing the stick forward. Therefore, you can't map them separately. The may not be a big deal for the many games that don't use the control pad, or use the pad and not the stick, but is a problem otherwise.

There is no rumble feature and you can't plug in a rumble pack or memory pack into the controller.

Moving forward I think I'll just get a controller adapter and use a real N64 controller with it.

product_title: Classic USB NES Controller for PC / Mac - (Not Compatible with NES Classic System)
review_body: I'm not sure how this product received so many good reviews. Maybe people just like the nostalgia of it? Maybe people don't remember how great the original NES controller is compared to this. Maybe people have never used an original NES controller so don't know any better.  I honestly have no idea but as soon as I started using this I knew something was off. I remember using a NES controller from 15+ years ago. I still distinctly remember the weight of the controller, the feel of it, and how to use it.  Right off the bat I could tell this thing was lighter but that's forgivable, I'm sure with more modern technology they were able to do away with a lot of unnecessary (by today's standards) components. The feel of the controller isn't quite the same but again that's also forgivable, I'm sure it's difficult to get something 100% right.  What is unforgivable is the horrible D pad. Yes, horrible. At first I thought it was something I was doing wrong, like maybe I forgot how to properly use a NES controller. I remember being able to flawlessly transition from pushing right to pushing up without ever removing my thumb from the D pad and it would work perfectly; my character would go from moving right to up without a hitch.  With this controller though it's a total crapshoot, it might work perfectly or your character might just keep moving right even though you are now pushing up.  I read a review from another person that summed up this problem perfectly. The problem is if you push down on the center of the D pad the entire D pad moves down, as if you are pushing all 4 directions at once, and that's the problem, you don't want the whole D pad moving down at once.  I pulled out my original NES controller and sure enough, just as I remembered, it was impossible to have the whole D pad move down at the same time if you push the middle of it. The D pad is bound to be leaning towards one direction if you push down the center, meaning only one direction is pushed at once.  I bought a NES controller/USB converter so I could plug my original NES controller into my computer and it is exactly how I remember playing my original NES. The D pad works flawlessly. The buttons work flawlessly. It is perfect.  If you can put up with a poor functioning D pad then this product is alright, it's a bit cheaper than the converter plug alone so it has that going for it.  However if you actually want to enjoy your games I highly recommend buying the converter plug. If you don't already have a NES controller I would recommend paying the extra money to get one and the converter plug. This product is just absolutely aggravating to use.

The problems this product has are beyond Nyko's control. If Sony chooses not to support this 3rd party mod (which they'd have to have a LOT of motivation to do) this product is dead.

I've tried 6Tb drives from two well known manufacturers, as well as 4Tb drives. In all cases you can not use rest mode because the drives are recognized as 3.5 which isn't supported. That's not a big issue, and the initial setup works; you can download games for a few hours maybe without any problems. In my experience over all of the drives during the past week, every one was riddled with random freezes, reboots, and corrupted data that had to be re-downloaded. I don't think this is any issue with the Nyko Data Bank, it simply doesn't work with the Ps4 firmware at this time. Currently, a drive of any size appears to be working at first, but with any use shows that it does break the system and is unusable.

*Update: I've started renting games from Gamefly now but NONE work. The error codes are CE-30012-6 if the Internet is on and CE-30034-4 if it's off. No one really knows the exact problem, but the possible culprit is that the single power cord can run the Playstation 4 and a hard drive up to about 4Tb without errors, but drawing more power for more platters on a hard drive or trying to spin a disk draws too much power and causes the errors. If only Nyko made their Data Bank use a separate power source it would actually play disc games, but then there would be other problems (such as turning off and on with the console).

2nd Update: keeping the power issue in mind I used a 6TB WD brand "purple" hard drive which is specifically designed for always-on security video systems. It's supposed to use less power, run cooler, and be optimized for constant overwriting. Suddenly the problems with random freezing and rebooting are gone. I still can't use the disc drive to play games and rest mode doesnt always work so I just turned that off. So now I have a functional 6Tb drive that I don't ever see being filled and I don't feel like I'm missing out on anything. If I knew all of this to begin with (ie Nyko listed power spec requirements or compatible drives) this would have been a 4 or 5 star product. review_headline: More than a mere Resident Evil 4/Gears of War ripoff.
review_body: The haters and critics can stuff one.  Seriously this game is a blast.  The gameplay is much more fluid than Resident Evil 4, the voice acting is much better than Resident Evil 4 as well (that game got incredibly stale at times) more faster paced and balanced than Gears of War, has a better story than both, and I'm not one to care about graphics but for the time this game is a piece of eye candy.  The only reason this game is bashed constantly is that game designers in Poland do things differently than Americans.  The Poles actually focus on gameplay mechanics, story, basically making the game instead of spending millions on advertisements for a subpar product (take note Microsoft, Nintendo, Sony, etc.).  The complaints I have is that for some reason my computer has a tough time reading the disc (maybe I got a defective one), glitches that causes the game to freeze, difficulty running on modern day products (requires old PhysX software to run which you can google search "Infernal PhysX" to get working on NVidia, I bet it doesn't even work on ATI cards but who knows I have NVidia) and the game is pretty inconsistent in terms of difficulty where some parts are incredibly easy while some are brutal (but no one ever criticizes darling games like GOW or RE4 for that).  Overall, a superb, underrated, masterpiece of a video game that shows that the Polish video game industry is as good or even better than the American one in making quality games and is a reason to ignore the critics infesting the USA.

review_headline: Gorgeous, generous, gratifying but also...heartbreakingly disappointing?
review_body:
I can't help but feel that this could have and should have been much more, especially on next gen. Yes, it is technically rather stunning, but perhaps not the generational leap I was expecting. Where was the dark, dangerous, desperate world we saw in the 'Killing Monsters' trailer? Where is the haunted protagonist whose eyes burned with regret and anger? The demonic army, the end of days, the desperation, the mysterious world you could lose yourself in.

Just look at this trailer:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c0i88t0Kacs

Does anything in the game ever remotely approach the tone, the writing or the atmosphere here?
Instead what we get, and don't take this the wrong way, is a highly polished and gritty Kingdoms of Amalur or Dragon's Dogma. Deep, addictive, enjoyable, sometimes funny, but nothing we haven't seen or played before.

I dare say it may even have been possible on last gen. Just look at Red Dead Redemption, a game so many have compared to this one. A game that even with outdated tech, sold you on its atmosphere, its world and its characters. Or what about The Last of Us, which managed to tell a much more powerful, mature and haunting story in a fraction of the 200+ hours it took me to complete Witcher 3? I still wonder about Joel and Ellen Page from time to time.

Tonally, I feel this game should have been similar to Dark Souls: mad monsters, bloodthirsty brigands, bloody barons, demonic elves that ride around in flying ships, insane kings, a lone warrior on a quest to find a mysterious white haired girl, a world on the brink of destruction.

Instead the world we get is cartoonish. Monsters can often be found mere feet from villages. In the city of Novigrad, you are chopping people's heads off in full view of everyone, only to return minutes later to a game of Gwent with Zoltan the dwarf (I do love his accent).

As big as it is, I felt like the majority of the game takes place in Velen/Novigrad, and both those areas felt samey. Skellige, on the other hand, had some of that mystery, that dreamlike sense of wonder, even if you are killing the same monsters. The desert area you see in the trailers is the only true surprise in the game, yet it is a wasted opportunity, and over far too soon.

The story, starts off intriguingly enough (lilac and gooseberries), but quickly becomes a jumble of exposition, with little of it making any sense. I don’t want to spoil anything for anyone, but the meat of the plot seems to be: find Ciri here, you just missed her, now go look for her there, missed her again. D’oh. Game of Thrones this is not.

Having said that, gotta love that Bloody Baron.

In all of this, in the world building, the story telling, the characters, and the overall conclusion, Witcher 3 felt like nearly next gen.

Perhaps, instead of going open world and stuffing the game with dozens of side missions, if CDPR had focused on a tighter more narrative led game along the lines of Witcher 2, this might have been one of those games of a lifetime. Instead, it winds up being merely excellent,

It will be a while before we see what this generation of consoles is truly capable of. Witcher 3: Wild Hunt is an outstanding warm up. product_title: Final Fantasy XIV: A Realm Reborn
review_headline: Great game put out by an inept company. UPDATED
review_body: This game gets 2 stars because it's actually a really fun and really good game.  I played in the free trial and maxed a character to the max level of 20 (trial limit).  I had gotten my disc in the mail so I figured that now is a good time to register to keep playing (working towards a bad ass Ninja).  The content was fun (even though I had to do the opening content twice with both the Pugilist and Rogue classes).  The music is fantastic.  Sure, it's your typical hot bar MMO but the effects are nice and it feels like a lot is happening.  It has random group quests that pop up on the map that are fun called FATEs (a la Rift, one of its and this games best features).  You can participate in a lot of easily put together group content with the easy to use Duty Finder (a feature that turned many other MMO's into much better games for me).  The areas I have seen are all very interesting and it's easy to track where you can go next thanks to quest giver levels popping up up on maps of even unexplored areas.  The late level gear has sick and fantastic design (interesting design is a hallmark of SE in my opinion).  But Justin... why are you only giving this two stars, it sounds like you really like the game?  I'll tell you why.  It's a average really of a 4 to 5 star deserving game and -3 star deserving delivery by Square Enix.  I made the mistake of starting my free trial on Steam.  I have lots of games on Steam, no big deal there.  Not the best service around by far, but that is a whole different review.  No, because I started a free trial on Steam, I cannot register a non-Steam key and keep the 20 hours I have spent in the game with this character.  I try to register my key and it tells me that I must register a Steam key in order to transfer my character to the full game.  I have posted on the support forums and put in a ticket to SE asking about this, but so far nothing.  It doesn't actually make sense because it's a free trial.  Furthermore, the only difference is thatyou are either launching their launcher (not even the game) from either your Steam library list an icon on your desktop.  It's not like buying it from Steam means you download the game from their servers, you are still only downloaded the launcher from Steam which then downloads the game (on their much slower servers than Steam I would like to point out).  It would have been Ok if it was a mistake I made.  If they had put the information in my face and I ignored it, I wouldn't be here, I would kicking myself  for being an idiot.  I have made that mistake in the past and have only ever had myself to blame.  But no where in the whole process did it tell me that if I did a free trial on Steam that I would need to buy it through Steam.  When I go to transfer the game to a full game it tells me on one page that I need to either purchase a Steam key or a retail key (see attached screenshot).  On the following page it then tells me I need a Steam key in order to transfer my character.  Nowhere on Steam does it say that I need a Steam key to transfer my trial to the full game.  So, they literally got my money for the disc version and stole that 20 hours spent from me.  Furthermore, it's not like I can bite the bullet and say, "darn, that's dumb, I'll just start again since I enjoyed it well enough" (trust me, I woke up this morning and was there, ready to do it).  No, there is no way to register this Amazon bought copy with my current SE account and just start with a non-Steam copy.  I literally MUST cancel my current SE account, register a new account, and then register the game.  I also have to jump through hoops in order to play the game that I bought.  This is some of the most ridiculousness I have ever seen from a company.  They aren't bad, it's not like they are being jerks to people who support them, they are just being inept.  I have played lots of MMO's (2 others on Steam alone) but never never have I seen this kind of thing.  UPDATE 7/23/2015  So, I continued to play the game after passing the one I bought off to my friend and thought I would sum up my experiences here so far.    I bought the game on Steam again because I didn't want to lose my character progress.    Main story: The main story was good.  I liked it, it felt sufficiently epic as the game went on.  At 30 I took the Ninja job for my Rogue and liked the abilities and the Ninja specific gear looked awesome.  Once I learned how to play him, it was really a lot of fun.  That is up until I beat the main ARR story.    At hitting level 50, they lock your leveling.  I personally find this offensive because you don't cut off the leveling when it was expanded with Heavensward.  They just arbitrarily stop it so you can gain anymore experience towards your character.  The gate the increased level cap behind buying Heavensward.  I don't like it, but I also kind of get it.    I was at the end of the main story and couldn't level and still wanted to run through the Coils of Bahamut and whatever other Duties may be available to me, but I didn't want it to be for nothing so I bit the bullet and bought Heavensward.  I also figured that I had enough fun running through the main story for ARR that I wanted to try out that Heavensward content and then just get my character to level 60 and then I could still run all those Duties I wanted to try at least once.   Only, here is the thing, none of the instances are worth anything.  No monsters provide experience, most of them do not provide you with item drops, you are looking at getting about 25 gil per kill and that is it.  You also only get level 50 currency from doing Roulettes and that is it.  So getting your level 50 currency is a matter of doing daily quests, and that is it.  One thing no one really warns you about is that after you beat the main story there are A LOT more story quests... A LOT more.  I don't have a lot of time to play games, maybe a few hours a day at the most.  So I have been working on story quests forwell over a week.  I placed them all on an Excel spreadsheet to be certain.  In my worksheet, assuming "The Ultimate Weapon" is the ideal place to end the story, there are 101 more story quests you have to go through before being allowed to access the Heavensward content.  And you cannot pass this in any way, you have to go through them.    I get it, after ARR came out, they needed to keep adding content, but this is all just filler content.  Sure, along the way they added a few more duties which is always welcome. But the vast majority of these involve things like "Talk to these 5 people" and "Go here and kill 5 of these things" or "Go here and assist character X".  I feel like you spend far more time in loading screens, not because the load times are long, they aren't, but because I'm spending so much of my time fast traveling around to do these inane pointless quests when really, I just want to get onto Heavensward.  But the most atrocious parts are ones that require you to queue into a duty.  I spent hours waiting for enough people to get into some of these.  The issue is that a lot of people aren't doing these level 50 duties anymore and I'm on a highly populated server (Ultros).  I could only imagine the nightmare people on less populated servers have.  One time, I queued up for a duty, it took over an hour to get into one, and we had a couple of people who were just no good at the game so we kicked them after being wiped 5 times, spend more time waiting for someone new, and ultimately end up just quitting the instance.  And I just hope I have better luck next time.  So far as the story is concerned after the main ARR story.. I don't know.  If I were to spend time watching all of these story scenes and reading everything, I would be much further away from actually completing these story quests and much further away from Heavensward.  At this point, I feel like I would have a hard time suggesting to anyone to play this game, which is a real shame because when it's not throwing BS your way, it's a lot of fun.   Production update:  This is a weird one.  The game is all over the place with this one.  Some story sections have voice overs... but a lot do not.  I cannot find any rhyme or reason as to why it's so sporadic.  But I by far prefer the ones without voice overs because the voice acting is horrendously bad... I mean horrible.  It sounds like the only pre-requisite for this job was literacy.  It's riddled with lack of emotion and inflection.  It's bad.  At this point though, I just skip them because I can't be bothered to see all this.. I have 40 more filler BS quests to go through till I can actually get to the Heavensward content.    New Summary:  The main game is fun till you hit level 50.  Then you have to grind through 101 more quests till you can even touch Heavensward.  It's a big giant wall to hit for me since I was really enjoying the game up until this point.  I'll get through and get through Heavensward.. but I'll never play until there is another expansion.  The idea of running an alt through all the filler makes me want to take a long walk off a short pier.

UPDATE: Thanks to Carrman217, I found the code, which had, in fact, been emailed to me by Amazon. UPDATE 2: As noted, my initial review was from when I was only 2-percent into the game, so I hadn't made it to the upgraded batsuit/grapple gun yet. The first 50-60 percent deserves 5 stars, but I have no idea how the guys at Rocksteady thought getting blown up in the Bat-tank over and over again getting chased by a giant drill or a swarm of indestructible tanks would be fun for anyone-- especially when we all bought it so we could "be the Batman." review_headline: My first real strategy game as a kid
review_body:
Most of us have fond memories of that one game that started us on a path to loving a particular genre of game or recalling a specific gaming console very fondly. For many people I grew up with, Super Mario Bros. came to define both the NES and platforming. Mike Tyson's Punch Out or Tecmo Bowl represented sports fans very well. I enjoyed all of these and plenty more formative classics at the time from The Legend of Zelda to Dragon Warrior, Metroid and Final Fantasy. However, one of the most telling games from my childhood was a strategy title very few people seemed to know anything about, called Nobunaga's Ambition.

Considering RPG, Strategy and Sports games probably rank as my top three genres in any give order, I often find myself looking back fondly on those games as I recall what hooked me in the first place. A sense of progression, an appreciation for grinding and feeling like I have some tangible control over a storyline are all traits I enjoy today in my games. Now many games have crossed up features enough that the genre lines have become blurred. SRPG for those who like a combination of strategy and roleplaying, and even in modern sports games you have progression and career modes that focus on experience earned and stories.

Nobunaga's Ambition was the first strategy game I recall playing. Certainly I had played some games with varying levels of strategic elements before (Hunt the Wumpus on my TI99/4a comes to mind), but nothing like Nobunaga's Ambition. This game was set during the Sengoku period during Japan's feudal wars. While the game is named after the famous general Oda Nobunaga, there were plentiful leaders that could be chosen. Different ages and starting states for their fiefs certainly created an uneven playing field, though I seldom actually chose Oda Nobunaga myself - there were a few others that I enjoyed quicker starts with based on their geographical location.

There were a quartet of scenarios to choose from when starting your game and you could choose a smaller map with fewer opponents or the giant map that had considerably more territory to conquer. While many strategy titles hang their hats on the combat alone, there was always a great deal more to consider with this title. There was the military side of things of course, but to be truly successful, your daimyo had to balance peasant loyalty against increased production. There is a market where you want to purchase weapons and sell rice when the price is high and purchase when low. There were ample opportunities for natural disasters as well, from sickness, weather and even revolts.

Political juggling certainly gives you an upper hand, but at the end of the day, taking over a fief usually boils down to combat on a myriad of battlefields. Some units performed better than others, landscape and soldier morale was also a factor. In the end, sheer numbers are usually the deciding factor. The combat is turn-based in structure and serves as the most exciting part of the game.

Nobunaga's Ambition was clearly not for everyone. My dad used to rent me a new game most weekends, and he grabbed this one for me because he knew I had played most of the others available at the time. I had no idea what this was - I certainly would not have gone out of my way to pick it up because I had never heard of the game or Koei for that matter either. However, I was immediately hooked. One of my buddies came over that weekend and wanted to know what I was playing, and he was hooked. You could actually have up to eight people playing it at one time (you just passed the controller around hotseat style).

This certainly had a tendency to make for some long games (it had a save feature, this was no 40 minute Mega Man 2 run), and we never had more than three players attempting to participate at a time. One of them quit on us (you can turn control over to the computer at any time if you want to just speed along and see how things play out) after a few weeks.

A large number of Nobunaga games (over a dozen) came out in subsequent years, though Koei produced other strategy titles as well. Games like Romance of the Three Kingdoms, Bandit Kings of Ancient China, Genghis Kahn, L'Empereur and the fantasy title Gemfire became regularly played titles by myself and other friends. Nobunaga's Ambition opened the door to a whole new genre for myself and also several of my friends and it has been one that stuck with us through the years. These games were not flashy. They were menus upon menus that provided gameplay in measured slices. Waiting for the computer's turn to end was frustrating to be sure - but only because I was so incredibly anxious to make my next set of moves.

Given that there is a new Nobunaga's Ambition coming to the US for the first time in many years this fall, I felt it was time to go back and revisit this title, which still has a place in my NES collection and a favorable position in my memories as well.ow things play out) after a few weeks.

product_title: Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Danger of the OOZE - Nintendo 3DS
review_body: kids love it very awesome couldn't find this product anywhere

I speak as a previous owner of the old Nintendo 3DS XL. This device far exceeded my expectations in terms of performance, design, and functionality. It is everything that the old 3DS should've been.

TOP
Let's start with the physical aspects of the device. By default it is very glossy and gathers fingerprints well, but that is the only downfall as the device feels very premium and the carbon-fiber-esque stripe pattern (I'm told it's called a moiré pattern) is a very neat touch. Up top you'll notice there is no Gamecard slot, it has been moved to a much nicer place on the bottom. In it's place is a centered charging port - this makes it much less likely to get in your way (and it has done so with great success). We have two extra buttons (ZR, ZL) which I assume will be used more in future games. There is still an IR blaster, much more noticeable on this dark grey "Black" model, but not bothersome at all. As well as a slot to add a wrist strap if you so desire.

SIDES AND BOTTOM
One major improvement I see is that the volume and 3D sliders have been moved to both be up on the upper display. Gone are the days when you accidentally blast your ears out while playing Mariokart! On the bottom, as mentioned previously, we have our Gamecard slot, a headphone jack centered in the middle (as to not get in your way, very nice), our stylus which now clicks in very firmly (this one is not gonna fall out), and our power button + indicator lights.

INSIDE CONTROLS
On the inside we have a similar control scheme, the only exceptions being the C-stick and the Start/Select buttons having been moved to the right side like in the old DS lite. I was skeptical of the c-stick at first but it is surprisingly very nice to use. All of the buttons have a very nice feel to them and I appreciate the colouring on the letters.

SCRATCHES
I will also note that Nintendo seems to have fixed the issue where the top screen gets scratched by the plastic border of the bottom screen, the rubber pads are much thicker and wider and provide a lot of protection. However, I'm going to pick up a screen protector to be safe.

3D TECHNOLOGY
The eye-tracking 3D ACTUALLY WORKS. Finally! The day we have waited for! The 3D slider will no longer live in a state of being constantly ignored because the 3D is USABLE now and better than ever!

CAMERAS
I never used the camera extensively on my old 3DS XL, partially because the quality was horrible, especially in low-light. They've improved the sensors a little bit and you can easily tell the difference. The photos are still noisy but, hey, 3D! The front-facing camera is improved, it also has a little IR light so it can see you when it is darker.

DISPLAY QUALITY
Is unchanged. Sadly. It would probably take too much energy to power a higher-resolution glasses-free 3D display. Or we simply don't have the technology yet. This lack of quality isn't very noticeable when playing games, but is very obvious when trying to watch videos not optimized for this display size. (Making the YouTube and Netflix apps kinda useless).

POWER
I've not had the system for very long, but the battery life seems to be very similar to the old model, maybe slightly better. The CPU is noticeably faster and I don't doubt that will impact the battery life. But with the new location of the charging port it isn't as much of an inconvenience to charge while playing so I don't forsee this being a huge issue. Just note, you're going to have to buy a charger if you don't already have a DSi, 3DS, 3DSXL charger (It doesn't come with one).

SYSTEM TRANSFER
It is pretty easy (although can be time consuming) to upgrade and transfer your data from your old system. Just follow the steps and make sure both devices are fully charged!

OVERALL
The improvements are well worth the upgrade IF you're a heavy gamer and willmake good use of the 3D and new controls. For casual gamers, I'd wait until the price drops a little OR buy a used model. Happy Gaming!

review_body:
To play this game on Xbox 360 slim, I bought a 250 G internal hard drive, an xbox live membership, and a wired headset microphone from Amazon. When I inserted Destiny in the disc drive, it automatically began a download from the internet. The download froze at 4% and remained frozen all day. I then got an error message. Then the xbox crashed, with a red ring. I removed the hard drive and the xbox functioned normally. Every time I reinserted the hard drive, the red ring recurred. It appears the Destiny download corrupted the hard drive. I returned the hard drive to amazon and reordered. With the new hard drive, I installed the game directly to the hard drive, as recommended on the destiny troubleshooting website. I then tried to open the game for play on xbox live, only first to get a BOAR error message. I went to settings, downloads, and reinstalled package 4. Then I got another error message.
So, it's taken more than 30 days to try to install Destiny, taking it past Amazon's 30 day return window. And I have an xbox live membership and internal hard drive cost specifically for this product as well.
This is a general product defect that continues to be sold by Bungie without any correction to the basic problems, leaving the customer to try to navigate websites and chat rooms to try and resolve the installation problem.

product_title: Dark Souls II: Scholar of the First Sin
review_body:
(Note: This is an updated review of sorts. I don't think I've been so ambivalent about a game as Dark Souls 2: Scholar of the First Sin. It really is a love or hate situation. I'm tempted to change my score to a 2/5 but that's not quite a fair score with all things considered-- even though I'm tempted to).

I've beaten Demons' Souls, Dark Souls and, recently, Bloodborne. Bloodborne was an amazing experience but it kind of made me miss Dark Souls. So, almost immediately after beating Bloodborne, I purchased the remastered edition of Dark Souls 2. I was probably more excited to play this than Bloodborne just because of how much I loved the original. My optimism, however, got the best of me.

Dark Souls 2: Scholar of the First Sin is not a good game.

Addendum: Dark Souls 2: Scholar of the First Sin is not a good Souls game, and can't hold a candle to From Software's previous efforts or its latest offering, Bloodborne. In all fairness, SotFS is still very much a last-gen game, even with the remastering and rock solid frame rate.

Pros:
--The game runs beautifully at 60fps. Really, it makes a huge difference. The depth of field effects and subtle blurring are also a nice touch.

--The visuals and lighting have been significantly improved in some areas (No Man's Warf). The game still looks last-gen, but it isn't as hideous as it was on the PS3/360.

--The game offers a ton of flexibility with how you play and your build. If you want to be a Mage, you can be a Mage; if you want to be a Cleric/Pyromancer then go right ahead; if you just want to be a badass Tank that hits like a truck, then yes, go right ahead. And if you want to completely respec your character and rebuild him/her from scratch, you can. That's where the beauty of the game shines--not in the (uneven) difficulty but in the freedom to play the game how you want to play it (a shortcoming of Bloodborne, admittedly).

--The devs really tried to create interesting NPCs to interact with (the headless warrior comes mind). Some of the NPC encounters fall a bit short though.

--It's still fun to a degree. If you're a fan of the series, you'll get enjoyment out of the combat and find yourself coming back for more. The addictive nature that defines the series is still there.

Cons:
--GENERAL COMBAT EXPERIENCE: The Combat is clunky. It's a far cry from Bloodborne, that's for sure. Even after investing in Adaptability and keeping your equipment load low. It doesn't help that the targeting system is complete garbage. Too often you'll get killed because the targeting system doesn't lock-on properly. It doesn't designate targets based on distance or priority either and can frequently jump around during combat.

--TRACKING: The tracking, in which enemies basically "slide" towards whichever direction you're facing, is way too aggressive. Enemies will slide around, mid attack, to hit you. This is easily one of the most terrible changes From made to the series. Too often you will get hit by an enemy that can basically slide 180 degrees to hit you. It is cheap as hell. I can't express my frustration over it enough.

--THE MOBS: Instead of designing creative enemy encounters that challenge you, the devs decided to throw mobs at you. This wouldn't be that bad of an issue but, as mentioned, the targeting system isn't very good and was designed for one-on-one encounters. The devs know this (they have to at this point) and use the poor targeting system and mobs to ensure that you'll die or at least be irritated. It's bad design, shows a lack of creativity, and causes you to die, not because you weren't good or patient enough, but because you were outnumbered, plain and simple. It's inexcusable.

--STATUS EFFECTS: Speaking of poor design choices, the devs went way overboard with status effects in this game compared to its predecessors. Poison, Toxic, Bleed, Curse (this is especially annoying), Petrification, Weapon Breakage, etc, are rampant and sloppily thrown in. One area of the game is literally a straight path lined with dozens of statues that bombard you with poison. It's lazy and as irritating as it sounds. Cursing is also rampant to a tedious degree, especially with some of the bosses. Status effects shouldn't be a main course, they should be a spice. Dark Souls understood that. Demons' Souls did as well. When you substitute actual game design for a series of status effects, it weakens the experience.

--AI: The enemy AI, overall, is limited and pretty bad in most cases. The mobs, status effects, and tracking try to hide the fact that most enemies, including bosses, have a limited set of moves and lack any sort of dynamism. Many of the armored enemies seem to share to the same 3 hit combo. The exceptions to the poor AI are the NPC phantoms. They're tough, aggressive, and can give you a run for your money.

--TORCH SYSTEM: The torch system is half-baked. In some areas of the game, it works beautifully and can create a sense of tension. But those instances are rare. 90% of the time you won't need a torch and the system feels kind of tacked on.

--THE WORLD: The world of Dark Souls 2 has no rhyme or reason. The levels are bland, don't convey anything about the lore or a reason why they exist, and the level design is a crapshoot. It ranges from good to awful and uninspired. Drangelic doesn't feel like a cohesive world, and everything you do, ultimately, feels shallow. This is really the nail in the coffin. The game has no Soul.

All-in-all, if you're a fan, try it, but don't expect it to be half as good as the original or Bloodborne (especially Bloodborne). Dark Souls 2 is ultimately a disjointed, flawed, and hollow experience, one that I'm shocked any fan of the series could like, let alone love.

review_headline: This game is the most relaxing war ever (TIPS AND TRICKS + my go-to style)
review_body:
There are a lot of features in this game, so forgive me if I sound all over the place.
Harvest Moon never attracted me until A New Beginning, which got me addicted to this series. They promise a wonderful farming experience, which is definitely provided. It's also a heck of a lot of work. It's Animal Crossing amped, and that's assuming you DO put hours into path placement and landscaping on Animal Crossing.
For ANB owners, not much here is news. You need to gather and purchase materials to create the facilities, decorations, and tools you need to build a successful farming life. In this game, you compete for additional land, and they do not make it easy.
(MILD SPOILER)
The expansion of your private farmland comes on Winter 1 of your first year, and it is not the most enjoyable moment, I will warn you of that. Besides, you compete with three other NPC farmers for public fields (Beehives, Orchard, Tea Field, Root Crops, Leafy Crops, Tall Crops, Grain Field, and Paddy). It's not easy, at least not when you compete through total shipping costs. (It is doable. See my gold linen cloth tip below.) These fields branch off from the road below your private farm, so it's easy access. Crops have a very slight advantage when they grow here, but IMHO, it's not worth it unless the products you are trying to obtain are permanent or exclusive. Therefore, I only plan to rent out the Orchard and Tea Field, filling them with the max tea leaves and one of each tree type minimum, because those crops remain standing and you can continuously fertilize them until the star rank is maxed. The beehives and paddies are convenient and low maintenance as well. Once you have them, you can renew them, so the fight is a one time deal. My horrible rival Elise can have the rest of the public fields.
You sell items through a set of six countries who come to visit with their stalls. All of them sell their own kinds of blueprints, materials, seeds, animals, etc. You can ship anything through them, and the more you sell them, the more rewards you might be surprised with as a thanks for your loyalty. Difficult vendors, Tropical and Ice countries, are unlocked by shipping different types of items, like roads and tools.
Finally, as always, there's a ton of stuff to unlock, and you'll have no easy time doing it. This is good news. It makes it fun to work for the things you really like. More animals, clothes, and decor makes this a worthwhile installation for your consideration.
Those are the serious changes from ANB, all of which make for interesting and ongoing gameplay. Read on for the more specific changes and upgrades.

PROS:
- Customization is heightened. There are NO salons or tailors. You have every facial style, hairstyle, skin color, etc. unlocked from the beginning, and can change any of them, including your name and farm name, at any time. You make clothes by yourself, so it's easier to make that one outfit you've been craving. Cross dressing is back, and it's fantastic. House interior is fully customizable. You can even customize your house exterior (I'm a huge fan of the Log style).
- Cut scenes are non-consequential. No more trying to escape the 10 and 6 cut scenes from ANB. They're almost non existent.
- Crop harvesting is speedy. Make your fields with the hoe (there are no field types- just dig). You get 9 crops per field, and one seed pack or bit of fertilizer covers an entire field. Press A to harvest all 9 at once, and press A again to put the "box" of crops in your bag. Love it to death.
- Horse warp speed. You get a horse almost immediately in the game (save 5 milks from your first gifted cow, Hanako, a.s.a.p.; the game will take you through the rest). If you have carrots, which are cheap to obtain, you can warp to town, the Trading Depot, the Safari (a.k.a. the new Animal Sanctuary and the one mining spot in the game), and back to your farm again. A stack of carrots is as valuable as your hammer.
- Important shops are open like shops in the real world. Typical business hours a minimum of 5 days a week, except for the Antique Shop, but that doesn't matter much. No more memorizing which random weekdays the carpenter is open.
- Maker sheds are beautiful. They're aesthetically pleasing and convenient; now you can make clothing by yourself and participate in fashion shows. You don't even need extra ingredients to dye your fabrics. However, some maker sheds take forever to make things (upwards of days, sometimes). See my Gold Linen Cloth/Flax info in the tips section below. If it still bothers you, there are theme park style "maker sheds" that you unlock a few years into the game. They take up more space and they're a weird theme, but they work faster.
- You do not customize the whole town. This is a HUGE plus for me because that was stressful in ANB. You customize small plazas with your decorations (including a set of cool new illuminated items) instead.
- Almost all bachelors and bachelorettes are unlocked right away. My favorite, Licorice, has yet to come, but I waited for Sanjay last time so I can certainly be patient.

CONS:
- If you want any shot at a reasonably sized farm, keep some milk and egg cooked dishes on hand. You have a bigger farm than your given stamina can handle so early on. Your stamina runs out fast until you can create jewelry combos for stamina saving, which comes later in the game. Those products raise star rank the quickest and are easiest to make in large quantities. Eat when you're about to pass out, but you're not quite done with your second evening round of watering. (If anyone has tips for this, let me know in the comments.)
- Military time. I don't know if this is changeable. I'm very used to my typical game clocks and the clocks on ANB, so I often get confused for a minute after 12 p.m., thinking it's 6 p.m. when it's 16:00. Not a huge deal, but it's an annoyance.
- Occasionally, when your animals run out of food, they scream. And it's terrifying. Both the sheep and cows will make a horrible noise that sounds nothing like a sheep or a cow, and it makes me wonder why the game developers wouldn't just pitch down the normal sounds to show that the animals are frustrated.
- Hats come with a preset hairstyle. You can't imagine my disappointment when I made the Blue Mini Hat and discovered it made my male character's neat, cropped short hair into those wispy pigtails. The hats were a great idea. The execution didn't reflect that. I'll just use them for fashion shows. Glasses don't have the same issue.
- Pets do less. I'm considering not having one, since I didn't like them too much on ANB anyway.
- Your horse is always in your way. If it loves you, it follows you and gets in the way of you brushing and feeding your animals in the barn. There are ways around this, but it's easier to ignore it.

TIPS:
- For the love of everything, PLAY ON SEEDLING MODE. There is NO benefit to "original" mode. Prices of items are higher. That's it. You don't need that in this game; things are hard enough as it is. It doesn't add to the challenge- just the frustration.
- You can obtain fragile gold crop seeds by shipping a few hundred of the crop type. (Only the main crops, like Cucumber and Strawberry, have this feature.) If you obtain such seeds, save them. It will take a while, but you will unlock a Ferris Wheel Greenhouse in a few in-game years, which You don't want to bother with such advanced stuff this early on anyway. There's enough to do.
- I have 2 designated fields, until I get rich enough to live however I want: Flax Field and Fertilizer Field. Fence in a plot of land with enough room for ONE FIELD of each seasonal crop. Plant accordingly and fertilize every day. Make ONE of the nine harvested items into a seed pack and save or sell the rest. Rinse and repeat until you have 5 star seedsof everything. Then multiply using the maker shed when you're comfortable.
Utilize the rest of your space farming 5 star flax. Make the flax into linen cloth, then gold linen cloth. Load them into the makers in stacks of 11. It still takes forever, but it's not weeks, like it would be if you inserted all 99 at once. Make all that gold linen cloth, sell it, and watch the money roll in.
Farming like this means you have less crop materials for your blueprints, such as stacks of half star white roses, but hold off until you can afford things first. Then you can farm like a normal person and grow at your leisure.

Gameplay: Amazing. You basically get to program what your characters do, when they do them, and how they do them. It really is interesting, and I wish it had been brought to more games. Magic looks great, and the weaknesses do significantly more damage than normal, which is good.

Graphics: I personally really don't care about graphics too much, but I must say that these graphics are quite stunning. They are almost on par with ps3, which is quite the feat considering their limitations with the ps2.

product_title: The Witcher: Wild Hunt Collector's Edition - PlayStation 4
review_body: First of all lets talk about the Collector's edition. This collector's edition is one of those which is definitely worth its money. A little background on  CD Projekt Red (developer of the Witcher series). Back in 1990's after the civil war ended in Poland where CDPR is located the company came to fruition but not as developers instead as game distributors. The founders of  CDPR started playing video games as means of having fun. The laws were strict and or being created. Only a handful of people had computers. The games that the founders started playing were either borrowed or pirated. They had to pirate because games would either be too costly to import or not available at all. Based on this experience, they learned something that regardless how much tricks developers create to stop people from pirating games, there is always a way out. This thinking in turn is CDPR's biggest strength in today's age as developers which they became after founding their studio in  2002. CDPR's core philosophy believes in giving their consumers all the money's worth. CDPR doesn't believe in DRM. DRM is a means to confirm that people are playing games that were bought legally. Your game has to make connection to the server of that particular game or has to remain connected to the server throughout the time that you play that game. On other hand pirates use different tactics especially in Single player games like Witcher series. It does not stop them from pirating and playing games. At end of this all, the people who buy games legally are put on back foot of all Draconian policies of developers. That looks too much to read but it is important to write about this fact of the company so people who read the review or thinking about buying the game can make a decision based solely on their own with acknowledging the developers. Fun Fact: The name of the company is based on back in the day floppy's could not store much data and when Compact Discs (CD) became standard way to play games theygot overwhelmed by the fact of how much more data could be stored.  Finally I can talk about the collectors edition. I, however, will not be writing a review for the game as of now because i have not played it. I don't have a PS4 which I will be getting at the end of this month which is when i will update the game review after playing the game. I will also review how limited edition Arkham Knight PS4 console is at the same time.  The box is at least 1.5 to 2 feet tall in height. First as soon as you open the box you will see about 200 or more signatures embedded on to the box of everyone who helped develop the game. Next thing you will see is collector's box which stores the full size 200 page Art book which contains major  spoilers, so I would suggest if you have a system play the game first then read the book and do not make the mistake that I did. The collectors box also houses the game, Steel book with awesome witcher art on it. Now interesting thing here is both are separate. The game discs comes in a plastic game case which one can get when you buy any PS4 game. Both game case and steel book are separately stored in the collectors box. The game comes with all the bonus items that are available in the standard version of the game. The witcher compendium, the detailed map of northern realm of the game where the story takes place with all the side missions, Wolf head stickers and official soundtrack CD. There are 31 soundtracks on the CD with some missing which ones can be heard on youtube or other channels. I found out that some full version of the tracks were released online back in 2014 before the game release so people can hear it. That is why I believe they did not included those versions in the official soundtrack disc. Now the steel book comes with space to store in two discs instead of one. I  think this is great way to treat fans as you will able to store PS4 game as well as soundtrack disc in your steel book. Now final item in collector's box is witchermedallion. This is a full collector's grade medallion made out the metal that is heavy. This is not a cheap version of the pre-order bonus key chain that game stop gave with the standard version or collector's version of the game depending which one people bought.  The statue stands at 10 inches tall carefully wrapped in plastic and stored in foam box specifically designed to store the statue. Statue is hand painted so i believe everyone has different shades of same color on the statue because it depends on how many persons were involved in painting or was this done by only one person. I have seen some videos on youtube opening of collector's edition where paint is light or dark, but I guess many other factors needed to considered as what kind of camera was used for recording or if it was sunlight or artificial light was reflecting of the surface. All in all you won't be disappointed. The tail of the griffin and Geralt's  hand holding sword are stored separately in the box so they do not break off. I love this little things that CDPR has done in order to make sure we get our money's worth. In other words the sword and tail is detachable, if you decide to move some where and you need to pack the statue again back in the box. This collector's edition is worth every penny apart from the game as I am yet to play it. I will update the review once I play the game.

The graphics are great and the game runs great on my system. Now if I could figure out the controls and how to play....... OK, I'm not really that experienced playing this kind of game, but I expected a bit of a "lead-in" so I could get the idea of the game a bit before being dumped into a battle. Picture gta San Andreas' landscape with zombies instead of people and random events taking place across the whole map.
Add some scavenging and running to keep from dying and you've come close to what state of decay is.
Graphic wise there's not much there, but it's in its tone and sense of urgency that this game shines.
It forces you to think on your feet by making your characters fatigued while on the run so you can't always run from zombies.
It forces you to run into buildings or out into the open if you get attacked
Your cars breakdown if they have taken too much damage so you can't always run them over.
Guns and ammo are scarce so you're forced to scavenge.
You raid houses and abandoned construction sites for anything you can find to build your camp as the ever increasing amount of survivors need a bigger place to stay, workshops and medical camps to keep morale high.
The game does a great job at reminding you not to care for the characters much as a horde of zombies or a feral zombie might just devour you and your team at any moment, forcing you to try and keep all survivors at a good balanced skill set.
I played the hour long demo on Xbox 360 and as soon as I saw the graphics I was disappointed.
I told myself I'd play it the whole hour before judging too harshly though, being that I have heard so many good things.
After about 30 minutes in, I was hooked.
I started doing research and found out the Xbox one version would be released soon.
I immediately preordered it.
I've been playing this game for about a week or two now, and the fun factor is still there, I'm hoping to play this for at least 2 more weeks before it comes to and end.
this is what the walking dead survival instinct should have been.
Hands down one of the best survival horror games I've ever played.
It's got rpg elements mixed in in all the right ways.
I prefer ps3/ps4 games, but I had to buy an Xbox one for its exclusives, dead rising 3 and state of decay are two of the top 5 games I've ever played on an Xbox system.
I can only hope left for dead 3 shows up on the system as well.
I highly recommend this game to all as it has something for everyone.

product_title: Collective Minds 2.5" Hard Drive Enclosure & 3 Front USB 3.0 Ports Media HUB - Xbox One
review_headline: If you are having trouble getting your Xbox One to detect the drive...
review_body:
I really like this product but it did take a bit of effort to get it working. I had great difficulty getting it setup initially. It seemed like no matter what I did, I could not get my Xbox One to detect the drive (A 2TB Samsung Seagate drive in my case).

I followed the included instructions and turned on the Energy Saver feature in order to fully power down the Xbox (Yes I know that I could just hold down the front power button to the same effect). I then plugged in the hub and turned on the Xbox. I was supposed to be greeted by a wizard that would allow me to format the drive. Nothing happened. I rebooted a few times and still nothing. The drive was not showing up under Settings -> System -> Storage. So I took the hub off the Xbox and plugged it into my PC as a test. Windows detected the drive without any issues. For grins and giggles, I added a partition and formatted the drive. I plugged it back into the Xbox and it still would not detect the drive.

At this point I turned to Collective Minds' support web page. They suggested plugging the hub in while the unit was on which is contrary to what the included instructions say. I tried that anyway and it finally detected the drive. However, it would only allow pictures and video to be put on the drive, not games. There was no option to reformat the drive via the Xbox.

What finally worked for me was taking it back over to my PC and deleting the partition. I plugged the hub back in while the Xbox was on and did a full reboot. When it booted back up, I went to Settings -> System -> Storage and the drive was there with the option to format it. After formatting I was able install games to it.

I can't be sure whether it was the hard drive, the enclosure, or the Xbox that was the problem but I suspect it was probably the Xbox since everything worked perfectly in Windows. I hope this might help anyone else that is having trouble getting their drive to show up. This is a really great product - once you get it working. The 500GB hard drive that comes with the Xbox One is just far too small for this generation's games. review_headline: A child-like tale meant for teens and adults alike.
review_body:
*I’ll include non-spoiler/non-puzzle-ruining hints at the very bottom*
This is a wonderfully crafted point-and-click filled with memorable characters, imaginative and visually inspiring setting, and a storyline that simply has amazing twist and turns. Need I say the humor is infectious, too? However, keep in mind that though it visually looks like one of those “young kid’s app” kind of things, it is far from it. The themes are very mature and at times the scenes can be scary. Some of the dialogue is might not be what you expect from a “children’s game” (ex…there’s a talking knife that really likes to cut things…and talks like a gangster hitman). This is, in fact, more of an allegory meant for teens and adults…and it’s “childlike look” is part of it’s telling. The game took me about 9 hours to complete.

THIS IS THE ONE THING THAT BROUGHT DOWN THE SCORE:
Everything was 5 stars until the 2nd half of the game. You see, up to the 2nd half, there were tons of sufficient subtle hints to give you a general idea of what you needed to do or how to solve a puzzle. They weren’t annoyingly obvious…but they were enough to get your gears moving. In the 2nd half, though, it started out fine…but increasingly became less obvious for what you are to do. For instance, there was absolutely know hint that suggested that to finish some of the puzzles, you would have to switch to the other character’s perspective (the first half had nothing like that). And there were other instances like that. Basically, where I made it through the first half without a walkthrough (once or twice), the 2nd half needed me to refer to it 5 to 7 times because some of the puzzles were convoluted. As such, it became a little bit of a chore at times.

All in all, this is a beautiful game with a beautiful atmosphere and an inspiring message. Even with the con mentioned above, that should not deter you from trying out this hope-filled game.

*promised non-spoiler/non-puzzle-ruining tips:
1. Sometimes inaction is an action.
2. Sometimes you simply need to switch to an outside perspective (aka switch between Vella and Shay)
3. Everything that’s clickable is actually useful in some way.
4. Listen to the dialogue…LISTEN
5. It’s okay to make mistakes, you won’t wind up with a deadend ending.
6. Save constantly in the 2nd half…and use different save slots.
7. 2nd half will be much easier if you have pen and paper (or take screenshots) to make a diagram about info…one case especially being for when you have to fix Vella’s and Shay’s respective hexabots.
8. Just enjoy the experience!d game.

review_headline: A Wild, Wild Quest to Hip City
review_body: Chester Cheetah: Wild, Wild Quest for the Sega Genesis is a surprisingly fun game. I remember renting this game years ago from Blockbuster. Chester is on his way to Hip City when Mean Eugene takes his map and tears into 10 pieces. He then scatters the pieces across the USA and you have to help Chester find all 10 pieces. Upon starting up the game, you can pick a starting location from one of three areas. Afterwards, 5 other locations show up after beating the first stage and the 10th and final stage unlocks after completing the other 9. The names for each location are all parodies of cities in the US. Little Shock, Lostin, Numb, Omahog, Unclearwater, Not-So-Great Falls, etc. Each stage ends with a boss battle. Bosses include a missle-shooting tractor that can also spread bombs, a robotic seal with spiked beach ball bombs, a killer plant, a UFO, a Biplane, a Thunder Cloud Man, a beach lady, a submarine, an apple harvesting machine and a race car. As for the difficulty, the game is kinda hard. The main complaint I have with this game is the one-hit deaths. The only way to save yourself is with a bag of Cheetohs. But there are only a couple of bags in each level. Also it doesn't help that enemies respawn if you leave the screen. You can run and high jump but it's really risky. You can run into an enemy if you don't know it's there or you could jump into a bird. The music in this game is amazing. Especially the boss music. Graphics are pretty decent. Controls can be set to one of four settings. And the game has 3 difficulties: Easy, Normal and Hard. Overall, it's solid Genesis game that's definitely worth a try.
