review_body:
This review has been a long time coming, and unfortunately it's not a good one. Though this game will soon go free to play I feel it is important to voice my opinions on it as no one should have to endure any further torture from Electronic Arts.

From the start this game was doomed to failure, owing mainly to the fact that it was released quickly off the heels of Battlefield 3. Very little development occurred to make this game good and it is basically a carbon copy of its predecessor with new maps and a lot of copy pasted old ones.

This would be the case at least except that to access most of that content you would have two effectively by the game twice, buying into their premium system, which allows you access to all of content that should have been released with the initial game.

Veterans of the series will find the battlefield for is lacking in many key areas and continues the series push towards infantry focused battles. There are vehicles and the full suite of things we have come to expect from battlefield however much of the map design is infantry focused and parts that are not feel rushed and poorly thought out.

Though I can't imagine anyone is still looking to buy this game, again due to the fact that it will soon be free to play, it is well worth noting that investing in the game currently and likely any future versions of it, including hardline, is an investment in failure and disappointment.

EA should know better, and likely do know better, but their greed and laziness have triumphed over good design decisions and the desire to help and support their user base.

review_headline: A great game with a few niggling flaws.
review_body:
This is a game I wanted to rate both 5 stars and 3 stars. It's just that type of game, one that will divide you in ways games perhaps have never divided you before. You'll love it, you'll hate it, but most of all you'll play it. I'm going to break my review down into 4 quick sections; what I think is great about the game, what is good, what is bad, and finally what is awful.

Things I think are great about the game...
Really this comes down to the story and setting. I've never been as engrossed into a video game story as I was with Bloodborne. What I absolutely love about it is the detail that went into creating the world and the story. Both intertwine quite nicely. They don't feed you details about your world you need to uncover them, piece them together, and come to your own conclusion about them. This has proven to be an amazingly thought provoking experience unlike anything I've ever had with a game before.

While this isn't a RPG there are a few little side quests that add greatly to the experience. Decisions you make will have minor but very interesting impact on the story. A few actually manage to tug at the heart strings depending on how you go about it.

Then there's the setting itself. Visually it is probably the best looking game I've personally played on the PS4. Amazingly detailed, incredibly rendered, and with very few graphical flaws. I did encounter some frame rate issues when the screen was full of fire but nothing too major.

Finally, one of the reasons I think the setting/theme is so great is because they do not pull any punches with the story they are telling. Without spoiling anything it's graphic, grotesque, and truly horrific.

What I think is good about the game...
Almost everything else falls into this category including the much discussed difficulty of the game. I know this is billed as a "difficult" game but I rarely found anything that I could not eventually overcome (seeexceptions below). Some things just require a bit of strategy and forethought to tackle (strategy that could change depending on the type of character you build). This isn't a game you'll button smash your way through. And though you will die (and die often) each death should teach you something which will help you get further and further into the game. They also do a good job of providing shortcuts to help you shoot through earlier parts of a level once you've mastered it. Overall I had no problem with the difficulty or challenge level of this game, in fact I quite enjoyed it.

While character generation is minimal (see below) your ability to customize your character is really quite impressive in its simplicity. I've played through the game with two different builds and each one played very differently than the other. One was a strength build the other was a skill/arcane build. Even though it was the same game I got two very different (and enjoyable) experiences.

Another solid part of the game is PVP. I'm not normally a PVP type person but I really enjoy it here. It's just fun. That's true of all the multiplayer features. Being able to summon other hunters to help you through a difficult area is just amazing. I would not have been able to clear some optional areas without it. The one downside is that attempting to summon someone to help costs you a point of Insight regardless of whether or not someone actually comes.

What I thought was bad about the game...
First up is character generation. They give you a lot of options but, really, aside from hair color and style none of them really amount to much. Especially since you'll be hidden in armor for most of the game. It is quick, however, and there are a decent number of options I've just been spoiled by games like Skyrim and Dragonage.

What I thought was awful about the game...
This really boils down to two things; a few optional bosses and the user community.

While the overall difficulty of the game is fine there are a few optional bosses that prove a bit too challenging. "Difficult" here often equals one hit kills regardless of how much health you have. There were only 2 bosses in the entire game that I just felt I could not defeat on my own. To be fair I did manage to get past them with the help of a multiplayer companion but I hated that I had to rely on that to get past these bosses. There's nothing worse than spending 5+ minutes doing what you think is well against a boss, sticking to your meticulous strategy throughout, only to have it all come crashing down to a lucky one hit kill or getting stuck on some piece of terrain.

Finally, and I hate to say it, but the diehard user community for Bloodborne is pretty awful. Not all of them but a good vocal chunk of them. I can't count the number of times I went to a message board seeking help through a part of the game and was meet with "git good casul" (this being some Dark Souls/Bloodborne chant of the die hard). I was told that my presence wasn't wanted in the community and that I should just go away. Now I also met some very nice and helpful souls out there but the large section of vocal and vile diehards that I encountered soured me very much on the game.

There are also some bugs that I believe have been patched with v. 1.03 that potentially broke the game. NPCs can go missing and your ability to progress can literally be broken at a certain point due to a multiplayer bug. For a game this difficult such game breaking bugs can really ruin the experience.

Overall I think this is a must buy if you're into action horror games. Just be prepared for a challenge and get use to dying! Despite some frustrations and poor experiences in the user community this is probably the best game I've played in a very long time!

review_headline: If you don't normally like RPG's, this game will change your mind!
review_body:
The Witcher 3 base copy I got included a user’s manual, poster of the world map, wolf stickers, a thank you note from the creators, game soundtrack, and a black pouch that contained a wolf metal key-chain; which I made into a necklace. Not to mention the 16 FREE DLC’s they will be releasing; very impressive indeed. The creators made it clear they care about my business, unlike many big AAA game companies. Anyway below is my take on the pros and cons.

*Pro's:
-Huge open world, great graphics, lush vivid colors, cool crafting feature, tons of missions/quests, many unique enemies, incredible detail & textures, beautiful dynamic weather, movie style cinematic dialog exchanges, true freedom to explore, gorgeous scenery, hypnotizing music, very funny humor, lots of blood, thrilling combat with cool abilities, 36 different end-game save-states with multiple endings, and so much more.
-The dialog option you select can ENTIRELY change the outcome of that particular situation, and the outcome of the story.
-You don't need to have played the other Witcher titles to enjoy or understand this one, I know because this was my first Witcher game.
-Game of Thrones style drama.
-The horses are actually fast, much faster than the mounts on Dragon Age: IN.
-Upgrade your horse and sail around on a boat.
-You can save your game at any time and there's unlimited save slots.
-Color blind friendly option was added/patched in.
-Stash spot was added/patched in.
-Vast amount of content.
-The optional card game "Gwent" is the best mini-game within a game that I've ever played. There are 4 different playable decks with special leader abilities. It's very addictive and you can collect cards from random vendors throughout the world.

*Con's:
-Enemies can either be extremely difficult or very easy.
-Fall damage is bonkers, but you can press "O" to barrel roll as you land to reduce the damage.
-You are forced to use your "Witcher Senses" in the majority of quests, it can get a bit annoying. **Thankfully they patched in a color blind option that helps me see the red spots easier.
-You will frequently light/extinguish candles and lanterns on accident (you will understand after you play).
-You can only fast travel from road signs, not a big deal but there it is.

I want to proudly add that I have NOT experienced any serious issues, glitches, or frame rate problems while playing The Witcher 3.

I hope they add a New Game Plus (NG+) feature, that would be perfect. Overall this game is absolutely amazing and will provide tons of fun for a very long time. I normally don't support DLC, but I'm going to buy the Season Pass to support CD Projekt RED; they really outdid themselves and truly deserve it. product_title: Rock Candy Wired Controller for Xbox One
review_headline: If you're looking for a controller that is cheaper than the official, and don't need use a headset, this is a great alternative.
review_body:
As stated in the title, this controller DOES NOT have an input for use with headsets. I see a lot of people upset about this because they bought it first, but a simple google search will show you all you need to know about the product. Regardless of that fact, I think the controller is still very decent.

You can compare it to the official Xbox One controller, however, please understand that this is not intended to be a premium product. It's not marketed that way; it's mostly for pure aesthetic, and better value. The Xbox One controller undoubtedly feels more premium, so if you are a person that really values how things feel, you may want to pass on this.

First, this does work on PC, (which is the primary reason I bought it) just plug it in, and the drivers should start installing. It's important to keep in mind that controller is a wired one, meaning that even though the USB is removable, it will not function unless plugged in. The wire that connects is very lengthy, so if you are using it on your Xbox One, it gives you a great amount of slack.

I'll discuss the body next. The overall build of the controller is plastic, and had next to no grip. This doesn't mean it slides out of your hands, but it is noticeably different than the official controller. Speaking of different, the sticks are made of a hard plastic that is slightly indented in the middle. I was worried about how it might feel, but after hours of continuous gaming, but felt fine, and really wasn't an issue. I've seen reviews that complain about "sweaty hands" and I am usually one of those people that will sweat while gaming. I was say the effect was minimal after about 4 hours straight- bottom line, there is worse out there. The buttons feel similar to the official controller other than the Xbox button with is clearly a type of resin.I feel like it's somehow easier to hit the bumpers, and the triggers have less resistance, which will be a good or bad thing for eachperson.

Aesthetically, the controller looks great. (to me) I'm a 90's child so see-through devices are always nostalgic and usually attract me. Coupled with the fact that he red/white color scheme is my favorite, I'm very pleased with how this looks.

Truth be told, I was worried about purchasing this. I just wanted a dedicated controller to use when I play PC games, and not completely wear down the official controller which are used frequently enough in my household. I know this product is manufactured by PDP, and honestly, they have not always made quality products. At the moment, I really have no complaints about the controller and have been pleased with the performance. I do understand why some buyers would be upset about the lack of a 3.5 mm jack, however, I think the product as a whole is intended to be an add-on to the amount of controllers you have, not your main controller.

review_headline: Not a worthy entry in the series and has lots of shortcomings.
review_body:
This game is OK, I pre-loaded it after playing through both the open and closed betas but I just needed something new to play. I still enjoy BF4 more than this and here is why I give this game 2 stars.
Pros:
- Campaign is one of the best so far.
- New modes like Heists, Hotwire, Crosshair, blood money and the typical death match as well as the staple mode of the series which is conquest mode.
- The hit detection seems to be a lot better than the hit detection on BF4.
- Faster pace for those who hate the slower pace and large scale maps of BF4.

Cons:
- 64 player conquest can be atrocious since the maps are so small in comparison to previous entries, add the fact that destruction is very limited, you're going to experience madness everywhere you go, giving you very little time to strategize with teammates.
- Battlefield is and has always been a game that requires teamwork for the win. It was never about one man armies. It seems like the players who have populated the servers are former CoD player with their first taste of Battlefield. While it encourages teamwork for helping capture or deliver cash, a lot of these people will leave you for dead so it's not really Visceral's fault but that of the player who populate the game. Play with 4 of your friends for a better experience.
- The game has made some really awkward changes, RPG's & LMG's are considered special weapons and can only be unlocked from the trunk of your vehicle or by knowing their spawn locations which appear on the Mimi map.
- The lack of destruction on all maps makes the game an easy campfest. Dust bowl is a prime example where players camp in motel in conquest matches. This motel can't be destroyed.
- The lack of weaponry and attachments make the game feel outdated. Online the graphics are more suited for last gen entries and not PC, PS4 & XBOX One quality.
-BFH is not worth $59.99, it only has 9 maps, around 7 or 8 game modes, barely any weapons and the maps sometimes repeat themselves back to back. We played 4 rounds of blood money in the everglades the other night... I like to learn maps but wow.

If you want a good BF game, save your money until the price drop or wait for DICE's next installment which is due to be released by 2016. This is a rental at best.
It is a new concept with some fun modes but it is a novelty that wears off really quick.

This game is hard. I never played Demon's Souls or the Dark Souls games but I heard a lot of good things about Bloodborne and decided to pick it up. Day 1, I was stuck on literally the first enemy for hours. I figured out that the best way is to go past him until you get your first weapons. Once that's done, the game has started. I'm still only in the first area after the first day and a half of playing, but I'm getting better at the control scheme and timing my attacks and parries better. I'm giving this game a 4 star because I do understand the frustration of dying over and over again as well as the seemingly long load screens. HOWEVER, I do appreciate the art and environment of this game and I'm sure that with practice and patience, I will become better at this game. I also think back to the days of games like Crash Bandicoot on older consoles and how frustrating those were. As a kid, I would literally spend hours on one level trying to get past a certain part and failing over and over and over again. Bloodborne is very similar in that regard, and I believe that the learning curve is immense. In my opinion, games shouldn't baby the player and allow them to use the same tactic repeatedly to succeed. Call of Duty comes to mind and I think games like that is the reason games like this have gotten some bad reviews from players (obviously this game is doing great on Metacritic, IGN, Gamespot, etc.). A game should challenge you and make you learn from your mistakes from reoccurring errors, and that's exactly what this game does. I would recommend this game to any hardcore gamer, just know that if you're like me (not having played the Souls games), you will die A LOT, and you will get frustrated. But stay in there champ and together, we may just conquer this bloody, detailed, and darkly beautiful world.

review_headline: A fair challenge, but sometimes too much of one.
review_body:
To start things off, I will say that this game is at least fair. It does expect you to experiment and learn things on your own, and every single one of your deaths is a result of one of the following things:

Lack of understanding of game mechanics.
Lack of understanding of enemy movesets.
Poor decisions on behalf of the player.
Not being observant of one's surroundings.

Yes,every time you die, it is your own fault. The game was well designed in that regard. It is a fair challenge. BUT! The challenge is incredibly high, and in some sections, so high that the game, at least in those sections, is not fun. Now, I am a Souls player; I have the platinum in all three Souls games. I came into this game expecting that my Souls experience would get me through it with relative ease. I was wrong. Even if you are a Souls veteran, this game will still be a major challenge for you, but a fair one.

Don't get me wrong, when you win, you feel very rewarded, and there are a lot of really cool enemies/bosses in this games that are an absolute joy to fight. There is a wide variety of enemies in this game and they all feel unique and interesting, and none of them ever get stale. The environment and lore work wonderfully well together to create an ominous atmosphere, and it makes the game world exciting to explore.

The reason I'm giving this game three stars is because it is definitely not a game for everyone, and it is not perfect and has its fair share of problems. This game was made for Souls veterans who are looking for an even greater challenge. This game was not made for a general audience. And even for it's target audience, there are parts of this game that are so challenging that it somewhat ruins the experience. But to reiterate, this game is fair, but can at times be way too hard.

review_headline: The Game I Love To Hate
review_body:
Ah, the game I love to hate.

The first couple of days trying to play this beast was, well, frustrating to say the least. I got killed, then got killed again, and then got killed some more. It drove me insane.

After learning that you can parry in this game, it is now pretty simple.

I think that most folks that pick this game up and give it poor reviews are ones that like to play 'run and gun' style. This game will punish you for this type of play. You have to slow down, learn the characters moves and then die, a bunch of times. After a while, it gets pretty easy. You know exactly when to parry and get a gruesome visceral attack, or back stab.

Dodge is your friend. Don't be greedy. Slash, slash, dodge, parry, visceral, repeat. Also, level up! Grind them baddies. I'll go through the first level a dozen times before I get start really playing. Quick way to get Echoes.

Explore the areas. The design does seem like it is setting you on a certain course, but, look around. Creep around buildings or alleys and find out if their is a secret hiding behind some crates or barrels.

This game is fun, frustrating, but fun. After you level up and level your weapons up, you'll cut through the baddies like a hot knife through butter.

I feel, for the first time in a long time, that spending $60 on a game, I'm getting my monies worth.

The game is beautiful, dark, scary at times, and very unforgiving. Keep with it. Enjoy and learn from each death.

Throw away the old adage, 'what doesn't kill you makes you stronger'. Because, in this game, 'what kills you, actually makes you smarter... and bald. Great great!

My game would NOT run (black screen) until I configured it to run at high resolutions, and it looks fantastic for its age.

After you do that, do yourself a favor, and on the same Wiki page, download and install the HD Textures mod, it is also painless and noticeably enhances many of the games textures throughout the game. Follow the instructions using the Freelancer Mod Manager, take a few minutes to do this, it's pretty easy to do, and when you're finished with the single player game, try one of the total conversion mods to extend play. The game changes things up from the Souls style gameplay, and for that I'm happy as that formula, while amazing, was wearing a bit thin. Now the game pushes you to be more aggressive, dodging is essential as you can not block, guns will stun enemies and even set them up for a counter attack for massive damage. Weapons have large movesets and can transform, ultimately giving you two full weapons in one. The world layout is very cleaver where checkpoints are far and few between each other, but there are copious amounts of shortcuts to open up, which makes the small amount of checkpoints manageable. Enemy encounters are tons of fun and stressful (in a fun way), and boss encounters are super fun. A couple of complaints hold the game back from being 5 stars, load times seem to be even longer than the other games they've made (running around 40 seconds), which can be painful when you die a lot, FromSoftware has stated they are looking into a way to fix this in the next patch, so we'll see if this improves. The other thing is that areas can have a lot of junk littered around, which is fantastic for atmosphere and immersion, sucks hard when you're trying to dodge and get stuck on stuff you can't see around you. The camera at times can also mess you up.
EDIT:
I just want to say this game will not be for everyone. It is not a hack and slash game in the vein of Devil May Cry or Bayonetta, while it's faster than the Souls games it's still more strategic and groups of enemies can easily kill you. The beginning area may actually be one of the hardest parts, as it has a steep learning curve. Once you get past the first boss you'll find that you understand things more and the game is a bit "easier" but really it's you getting better. Also the long load times may be a killing blow to your enjoyment of the game since it happens anytime you die or go to the hub world to level up and buy stuff or upgrade. I'd say if you're unsure of this game do as much research on it beforehand, it's fantastic but it's also to a specific audience. There's no world map, checkpoints are rare, no compass telling you where to go.
So some positives are
-Great Art Design
-Weapons/Movesets
-Dodging is quick and works well
-World Design/Shortcuts
-Hidden areas and secrets
-No set path, your game can be very different from someone else
Some Negatives
-Occasional Camera issues
-Bad Load times
-Stuff around area is counterintuitive to dodge design

R3: "lock onto enemy" It's good to use this to keep track of an enemy. but sometimes it's better to remain unlocked for camera/aiming reasons.

O: Circle performs a roll when not locked on and a dash when locked on. Dashing is essential to the game. dashes and rolls give you a small window of invulnerability to attacks. Dodges are the key to surviving enemies in this game.

Where are my blood vials when I have 20 and I pick up more? Extra vials and bullets go straight into storage. When you die, or visit a lamp they are automatically refilled from your inventory.

How to level up? Leveling up happens in the Hunter's dream. You talk to the doll. She awakens after you meet the first boss "The Cleric Beast" for the first time. You pay her blood echoes to increase your stats by one point at a time.

Shoot the enemy with your gun at close range right before and enemy attacks and they will be stunned. During this stun press r1 to execute a visceral attack for high damage. This is an essential skill for quickly dealing with enemies that hit hard and fast.

Playstation TV is a great idea on paper with 3 key selling points: take a fledgling handheld platform and reintroduce it to the market in repackaged form, make the barrier to entry less expensive than its handheld counterpart, and allow it to function as a home console instead of a handheld. All of this sounds like a great way to reboot the Vita and hopefully make it more relevant. Sadly, much like the Vita, Sony hasn't really supported the Playstation TV.

So what are the issues?

1. Many apps are missing, including something as standard as Netflix. Unacceptable.

2. But it's all about the games, right? That would be an okay argument if compatibility wasn't so iffy. Some Vita games are compatible, most aren't. For example, some of the best Vita games, namely Uncharted: Golden Abyss and Wipeout 2048, two games that would look great on a big screen, aren't supported. Unlike a few games that were patched to add Playstation TV functionality and remove Vita's touch screen controls, those two were never patched for the Playstation TV, and that's really too bad considering the quality titles that they are. As for what's compatible, the list is full of games that can be played elsewhere with better graphics, Many of the supported titles are multiplatform and independent titles that are already on home consoles that support a higher resolution than Vita games. If you just have a Playstation TV, you may be fine with this. Honestly, though, I can't see someone who doesn't have any other consoles spending upwards of $100 on a PSTV when you can get a used PS3 or 360 for that.

3. The wifi is completely shoddy. Unless you have this very close to your router, you will get slow speeds, and perhaps even dropped connections. Playstation TV is best played wired. That said, PS4 games still look pixelated and less impressive with PSTV's 720p max resolution. So why would I sacrifice image quality? I just don't use this feature.

As for the pros, there aren't many. So why did I give it two stars? Because I like the premise. I do enjoy playing some of the games that are compatible instead of having my giant man hands cramp up with the Vita handheld.

Much like the Vita, Sony's support for the Playstation TV has been absolutely dismal. It's so disappointing to see platforms with so much potential being sent to die. I have played most FPS games since 1990, including Battlefield. So far I played the game for 12 hours/30 mins lvl 36 and finished the campaign. Let's talk about campaign first since it was really fun.

The single player feels like Rainbow Six Vegas mixed with Splinter Cell. Stealth is the #1 priority, but you can go gun crazy if you like it that way. Story is interesting and it takes you to very exciting environments from deserts to swamps and mansions in LA. Graphics are ok, but it could be lot better for a 2015 video game.

Lets talk about Multiplayer NOW:

Graphics in MP are slightly tuned down due to lag and nasty problems that we had in BF4. The gameplay is fast-paced, don't expect something like BF4/3. If you have played BF3 Close Quarters DLC, you can get a sense of how this game is. Game modes are interesting and fun AS LONG AS you are playing as a team and not running around like a lone wolf. Some maps are smaller than the others, but in general map size is ok for this game except for teamdeathmach which is a disaster. 64 players in a relatively small map and a HORRIBLE re-spawn system for TM, but other game modes are ok. Just like other BF titles, Conquest is the heart of the game; however, heist is another fun game mode that most players spend their time playing as well. Blood money game mode is fun IF you have good team mates.

Now that I mentioned the positive aspects of the game, let me cry about some negative aspects.

1- The game doesn't have region lock just like BF3-4. What is region lock you ask? It's simple, that means if I'm in U.S. and I choose U.S. servers only ( East and West regions) I MOST play with U.S. players, but this game allows players from U.K., China, Japan,.. join U.S. servers. This is one of the factors that affect hit detection and lag. Last night I was playing a match of conquest and for some reason I was getting killed by a same guy over and over again, and he was like 50 kills and 3 deaths. I realized other players in my team are also having problem killing the guy; it was like he was a ghost and he was able to do instant kills. After looking at his battlelog profile, I found out he was from China and we were playing in West U.S servers ;-( This could be game breaking few months down the line, just like BF4 and 3

When you get like 100 kills with a gun, you start unlocking attachments for that particular gun. So you may end up using a same gun for a while. [[VIDEOID:9fcb9e6858dd44a8bd2a4d452a827902]] This is probably the most important PS4 accessory I've been searching for. It's the Ortz Vertical Stand with Charging and USB.

If you do a lot of gaming, then you probably have limited space plus a lot of accessories to use with your game consoles. If I'm playing online I need to connect my headset, my controller for charging, and then a keyboard dongle. How am I even supposed to fit this small dongle in there? I was using a USB hub, but then you end up with this mess. And I still forget to plug in my controller when I' m done, so it's never charged.

The Ortz stand solves several of those problems. First the most obvious benefit is that you can have your PS4 vertical which is mostly a matter of preference, but a vertical orientation will fit better in some home entertainment setups. It also includes a fan at the base that can be turned on or off via the switch on the front. Extra cooling is never a bad thing, especially seeing how the last generation of consoles had so many overheating issues. The stand is fairly stable, I wouldn't worry about it got knocked over in an average setup. If you really have issues with electronics getting knocked over due to pets or young kids, you'll probably need to take other precautions to keep your PS4 safe.

Setup is super simple. Just place your PS4 in the stand and connect the built in cable. This little USB cable powers everything. There is no need for an external cable running into an outlet. This is very convenient. Obviously, you're PS4 needs to be on or in standby mode for the charger and hub to work. The stand has two fitted slots for storing and charging your controllers. The controllers fit very easily and it's convenient storage for those who can never find their controllers.

The USB hub is very easily accessible and now I can finally plug in my keyboard dongle, the usb headset, and even a micro usb cable for charging if I'm really using the controller for a long time.

The Ortz vertical stand is incredibly useful. It currently retails at $24.99 on Amazon which is not a bad price for a multipurpose stand. I can highly recommend this stand if you need one or all of the features I mentioned in this review. review_headline: Unless you're okay with spending $60 dollars for the demo of an actual good game, this probably isn't worth your money
review_body: Originally reviewed by me at somnambulant-gamer.com:  Normally I'm the kind of person who, if I don't have anything positive to say about a game, just doesn't say anything. It's not really worth my time to write about a game I don't care about, right? But Final Fantasy Type-0 is terrible, and I really feel it's only fair to let you know. This game was actually so bad, I had to wait a day to write about it, because yesterday afternoon I actually wanted to title this post "Type 0: a crappy game from crappy people who want you to waste your money on crappy things". My grumpiness was compounded somewhat by the fact that all the big review sites like IGN and Gamespot were giving this game glowing reviews that it frankly didn't deserve, which led to me wasting money. Okay, enough venting, let me get into this.  The game starts out with a cinematic that was probably only 15 to 20 minutes long, but felt like 3 hours. It was atrocious, disjointed, and fully 3/4 of the cinematic is spent on the tragic death of a character I can only assume you're supposed to care about, because you have absolutely no idea who he is at this point. The graphics look to be polished versions of something you might expect to see on a hand-held device that's a generation or two out of date (because they are), which isn't too terrible, except in a few instances where you've got characters with highly detailed faces and wafting individual strands of hair who still have blocky shovel hands reminiscent of World of Warcraft characters prior to the Warlords of Draenor update. Apparently, the game is about 4 countries (that maybe have crystals?) that are represented by signature beasts: a white tiger, an azure dragon, a red phoenix, and a black tortoise. Fans of the franchise will recognize the references to (and overt appearances of) staples such as the Bahamut and Phoenix eidolons. The country with the tigers has magitek machines, and apparently they go to war against the country with the phoenix, which for reasons inadequately explained until many, many hours later leads them to attack the stronghold of the country with the azure dragon.  You're dropped into this war as three kids who just saw another kid (presumably one of their number based on the uniform and pretty much nothing else at this point) die after struggling to find them (with no other apparent purpose) and apparently being too wounded to be healed by magic despite the fact that it takes him fully ten freaking minutes of cinematics after the attempt to finally kick the bucket, at which point his chocobo (big two-legged riding bird, staple of the franchise), who's seemed dead for about eight of those ten minutes, gives a mournful cry in a blatantly manipulative attempt to evoke an emotion the game hasn't earned. Then you get to spend about an hour and some change running through the city being subjected to some of the most boring and uninspired combat and maps you've seen in the last decade. The combat itself is brutally disappointing, reminiscent of the repetitive slogs seen in games like Devil May Cry where you hack and slash your way through dozens of faceless mooks over and over, without the inspired combo systems and flashy design that made that game a success. There's lots of small issues interspersed through the combat system as well, including clunky targeting with a mind of its own, frequent (if fairly short) load times, and one of my personal pet peeves - camera angles that are a greater hindrance to your party's advancement than the actual enemies.  You get to control three (of an eventual fourteen) characters during this section, a character who uses magical cards to attack and perform other maneuvers (a cool and almost successful call-back to fan-favorites of the franchise like Setzer in Final Fantasy III / VI), one who uses a spear and a jump attack (the "dragoon"), and a character who fights with a chinese longsword. Each character has all of four combat options available at this point, a standard attack, their special trick (card shuffling, jumping, and an AoE aura effect), one spell of a given element, and their defensive option. The combat has been compared to Crisis Core by several sites, but I really feel that does a disservice to Crisis Core, which had a robust combat interface that flowed seamlessly between the combat and exploration phases and utilized a highly customizable materia system that was actually pretty advanced for its time.  I feel like I have to find some redeeming quality in the game at this point... Okay, there's two things. The first, is that the cinematics, while climactically disjointed and painfully, brutally boring, go to places that are out of the norm for the franchise, in a good way. You'll see Square-Enix referring to this game as a "more mature" entry. While the actual story-line is about as mature as a twelve year writing his first piece of fan fiction, what this is really referencing is the fact that in this war-time environment, we actually see spurts of blood when someone is shot or stabbed, soldiers ruthlessly gunning down or bayoneting enemy wizards and civilians, etc. If some real character and story development had been married to a cohesive plotline and a modern combat interface, this could have been an amazing step for the Final Fantasy franchise, whose original fans are now at an age where they have kids, or even grandkids, of their own.  The second redeeming quality is that the game comes with a playable demo of Final Fantasy XV, an actual next-gen game set in the same world. Final Fantasy XV seems to be set to offer many of the things this game lacks: strong character development, a cohesive story, true next-gen graphics, and a robust combat system. While obviously still in the developmental stage, this fledgling game helped to restore some of the faith and hope that the actual game it was packaged with sucked out of me like some kind of vampiric leech that feeds on joy and nostalgia. Unfortunately, at the end of the day Type-0 isn't really a game; it's an advertisement for the actual game that they expect you to pay $60 for.

review_headline: Spoilers - It's great but you need to know the pros and cons
review_body:
Please don't read this if you don't want spoilers for P3:FES and P4. This is a really long post, too.

If you purchase this, you should only do so after playing Persona 3 FES. There's good reason for this. The game really isn't made for people who have not played the original nor is it made for people not deeply in love with the characters. You must be familiar with the original game in order to enjoy this one fully.

The biggest pro to this is the fact you can play as the female to see a different perspective and to engage in different relationships with the characters. This is really important if you're like me and play mainly for the stories. Also, when you replay the game as a female character you can chose who to spend the end with. Most of all Shinjiro-senpai! You can make him stay alive and see you at the end if you max out his social link. (I suggest tsundere Shinji in his romance. It's cute.)

Another pro is dating the male characters, this is great addition. (I suggest romancing them all first playthrough.) Ryoji's romance is weird, but funny. Aki's is cute as a button. Shinji's is sad because you can't spend more time with him. Ken's is strangely adorable but not offensive, more on this later.

The biggest pro is the gameplay, actually. It's so much fun! They made it like Persona 4. (The worst part of the console versions was the gameplay.) They brought Margret back so you could re-fight old bosses with added rewards plus other fights. But that isn't all. You now finally get to control the party members! You don't have to rely on dumb AI anymore! I was finally able to add Mitsuru back to the mix since she was not able to spam charm spells any longer. (She's a great magical tank.)

There's a lot of gameplay replay value. The new costumes you will love. (I love Team Butler!) Another great facet is the characters actually have dialogue if you wear or they wear different costumes. You don't have to talk to them to see their stats either. (That all changed to be like P4 where it's automatically on the menu when you access it. Makes equipping stuff easy.) Instead you get to have conversations with them.

Translation and censorship, needs to be mentioned. I can't categorize it as pro or con because this is something that really depends on the player's morality and how they view localizations. For myself, I despise censorship. But in this case it isn't too shabby. Let me explain, you can have a romantic relationship with Ken who is like 10 years old. The English version just makes this into a crush of sorts. In the Japanese however, this is a full blown romance. It even ends in your room like many of the others. Before you rage, there's really no sex, sexual touching, or kissing of any kind. Instead the main character says she is going to wait until Ken is of age to be with him. Persona 3 has a pension for tackling controversial themes without coming off as offensive to anyone. This is exactly how both versions are made.

Most of the dialogue for everyone is the same as the original version. (Both the console and Japanese.) The problems I have with the translation is really that sometimes it's not handled very well. Not because of such mishandling as not coming across like intended, more so it had many spelling mistakes and grammar ones in some places. It's weird because I've caught a few words that do not exist in English or any language really.

Another big con of the game is that it's a visual novel. While the new aspects of the story will be some welcome added editions to the family for you, the fact it is a visual novel can be a bit of a throwback to it's quality. For example, in the scene where Aki confronts Shinji about drug addiction, it's not as emotional impacting to me as it was in the console version because you don't actually see interaction between the characters. There's no questioning that Nintendo has a storied history of creating and releasing video games for decades. More notably, a lot of these games are pretty frickin' CHALLENGING! If you were to have played New Super Mario Bros. 2, and then went on to play Super Mario Bros. 3 afterwards, you could easily tell the difference in difficulty! NES Remix Pack plays on this idea of challenging events by centering around exactly that.

This pack consists of two games released on the eShop (NES Remix & NES Remix 2, respectively), but I will say that it is kind of disappointing that there aren't full versions of the represented NES games included in the pack. At least a few like Mario 3, Kid Icarus, and Kirby's Adventure would be nice! The closest we have in this case is a version of Super Mario Bros. where the levels are all backwards. More interestingly is a remake of the Nintendo World Championships competition, this time with a better choice of games utilized, and the scores are shared on online leaderboards.

So if these aren't full NES games, then what are they? Why, this is a gigantic mishmash of them, that's what!
NES Remix Pack contains a bunch of stages for each game represented in which you must take on specifically designed challenges for said game. For example, in Mario Bros., you must defeat all the enemies in a set time, or in Zelda, you must defeat enemies to get enough Rupees to buy something, or in Mario 3, you must defeat Bowser, etc, etc. There are also "Remix Stages" where certain games would be modified in a weird way for the challenges you play then (EX: Luigi rescues Mario from Donkey Kong or control two Ice Climbers at once).

This might not sound like much, but truth be told, there's a serious arcade/mobile game-like feel that comes from accomplishing each and every challenge. You gain stars and stamps, and then you unlock more challenges and representatives. It's a very addictive experience that in itself derives from oldschool Nintendo games. In fact, this game allows me to have fun with certain old titles that I would otherwise NOT be in the mood to play full versions of. I never feel like playing Donkey Kong or Balloon Fight at home anymore because they are just high-score games, which I feel can only truly be experienced in the arcades since other people are competing for the higher score. Here? I'm completing challenges that involve Donkey Kong and Balloon Fight! How about that?

If there's anything I have to complain about in this regard, it's that the Remix Stages aren't as over the top as I want them to be. This game is kinda boring really. It may have been a cutting edge FPS engine in its day, but I think this game marked the beginning of the end for Call of Duty. I even like Call of Duty 3 more than Modern Warfare.

The World War II CoD's were all based on a real war. You knew what you were doing and why. The guns were realistic and vintage. Some had more power than other. World at War was an especially good game, with amazing graphics, game mechanics, and storylines. Modern Warfare took everything that made Call of Duty great and threw it out the window. The other Call of Duty's stood out. Modern Warfare is just another shooter. I don't think I'm going to even bother buying and playing Modern Warfare 2 and 3.

They go from speaking on the tv's speakers to speaking on the portal's speaker (i.e., it really sounds like they are being sucked into the trap). When you have a villain "in" the portal, he always knows what's going on and comments appropriately. A villain may notice when you need health, that you are wearing a new hat, that something bad is about to happen. They are always saying comical things. This game is THE BEST way to spend the days when you're snowed in and even though we've spent a lot, I can't say I regret it....  What you need to play- if you can't afford everything, you should abuy the portal, at least one Trap Master for each element (you need them to get through special optional doors), at least one of each elemental trap (personally I think you should have an extra Life one so Broccoli guy and his healing powers are always available). * UPDATE 3/2/15 *     So Team Ninja rolled out an update over the weekend for this game. Version 1.01A seems to fix a few things, like the issues with freezing during throwdowns and ranked matches. However, even on their official site, it says the freezing/crashing \\"should happen less frequently\\". So this doesn't exactly boost my confidence. However, they did make an update so you can unlock all costumes, story mode, and movies with a click of a few buttons in the options screen. Seems this is their apology for people (like me) who got their save-data deleted from the DOA5U update. BUT - I am still having issues with paid DLC transfer. SOME of the costumes I paid for were available for free on the Xbox One store, however about half were not. I originally had the \\"Pop Idols\\" from when I preordered DOA5U in 2013, and I cannot download them for free as promised. I was able to download come costumes for Marie Rose and Phase 4 that I had originally paid for. So beware! This game has been patched, but it is still not completely fixed.       My original review:    First I want to say I am a big DOA fan. I've followed the series since DOA2 on the Dreamcast. I was really anticipating the latest installment, but there are some issues with DOA5LR that are difficult to forgive. This review is not to inform you of what's new and what's great about this game. For complete details, check out the official DOA5LR website. This review covers my own experience  on the problems with this game, so for any of you that are thinking about buying this game, don't say I didn't warn you. This is regarding the Xbox One version of this game.    My first example of Team Ninja's incompetence is the update on the Xbox 360 version of DOA5U. You'll see warnings on the game about how to properly update the game so your save file doesn't get deleted. However, if you were like me and downloaded the update directly from the Xbox Marketplace before booting the game up, your save file was lost. The idea was to upload the save file from DOA5U to use for DOA5LR on Xbox One. But, mine got deleted so I had to start a fresh new save file (not that big of a deal, I'll get over it). However, these next two issues with DOA5LR are the most frustrating.    Team Ninja advertises that you can \\"carry over your paid DLC!\\" to DOA5LR. Now, I didn't buy every single costume pack from DOA5U on Xbox 360, but I bought a few. For example, I have Pop Idols Team O and Marie Rose with all her extra costumes that I paid for. According to the official website, you have to re-download this content from the same Microsoft account that the content was originally purchased for, and the Xbox Marketplace will not charge you again.    Guess what? This doesn't work. I've tried several methods to get this to work, like reinstalling the game, downloading them again on the 360, and it doesn't work. The content I originally paid for on DOA5U does not transfer to DOA5LR for free.    Next, the game has some horrible freezing issues. Online matchmaking is an absolute mess. Each time I try to search for a ranked or player match, the game freezes up and crashes, forcing me to the Xbox One dashboard. It's bad. It also does this when you activate \\"throwdowns\\" when you are in training mode. The game locks up and forces you to reboot.    Now, according to Team Ninja's Facebook page, they are \\"aware\\" of some issues and they \\"appreciate\\" our patience while they figure this out. But in my opinion, this is just unacceptable. I paid $40 for a game I can't play online with features that were promised and not delivered. I imagine the freezing issues will get fixed soon, but who knows about the DLC issues. I've emailed Tecmo and Team Ninja and complained, but I doubt I'll see a reply or any compensation. So this is a fair warning to the rest of you who are thinking about buying this game.

Strategy games are not my wheelhouse. My competency with the genre fluctuates at points depending on the sub-genre a particular game falls under, though the shortcomings I face have a tendency to be consistent across the board. There have been a rare handful which clicked for me - Final Fantasy Tactics, Advance Wars - both of which, you will notice, are not real-time or simulations, a fact I've become increasingly aware of every time I try my hand at them. It's the number of moving parts which get me along with the min/max nature of the genre, and though I tend to be okay with these separately, when pushed together, they're a lot like rubbing your head and patting your belly at the same time. Something just doesn't fall into place no matter how many times I try to fit a round peg into that square hole. Though Awakening is my first foray into the Fire Emblem series, I'd heard enough praise to know I at least wanted to give them a go, and it appeared take-your-time versus real-time, more or less sealing the eventual deal.

It's good. I get the appeal. The story isn't anything to write home about, but it has its charm in that quirky way a fair amount of heavily Japanese influenced games will. The strange makes it a bit of a bipolar thing, however, the backdrop one of war, death, and - as most fantasy tends to mill - total annihilation from an ancient evil, these parts juxtaposed by the goofiness of the characters in your army. Between battles you're able to stop by the Barracks and listen in on either conversations between characters or the solitary musings of one, both of which may yield either an item, some gained experience, or relationship boost among friends, and after checking there, you might also be able to utilize the Support ability which gives a small cut-scene as two characters improve their standing with one another, a statistic raising their usefulnessin battle alongside one another. These meetings are often silly in nature. There's Frederick who's the Prince's knight and so fastidious and particular as to remove every rock from the path prior to the army's march, or to watch someone bathe in order to be sure they don't catch a chill. Lissa who cannot cook and is always trying horrible recipes on unsuspecting allies. Kellam, dressed in tank-sized armor who no one appears to ever notice, claiming he crept up on them in spite of being right there the entire time. Tharja, the psychotic Dark Mage in love with the main character. Vaike who cannot stop flexing. You get the idea. These vignettes add a good deal to the flavor, and for a game with a permanent death option (which I used in my play-through), also lead to me making some heavier choices between who to/not to use for sake of not wanting to lose that person in case things went south. But again, played against the attempted heaviness of the story, the result is an uneven one without either side ever really meeting in the middle or melding well. Though I never truly would, a small part of me would almost recommend ignoring the option to speak with your team in an effort to buoy the narrative and make it more focused. I understand the dichotomy is a part of the series' charm, and not one I can wholly fault as I'm the target market for oddities (Catherine, by example, is one of my favorite PS3 games), only something worth mentioning for those of you heading in blind.

To touch briefly on the story rather than using broad strokes, they do an excellent job with the time travel element. It doesn't feel horribly tacked on, and though a large part of the narrative, it also doesn't feel too gimmicky, oddly subtle with more of a background noise approach. Often I find time travel in any medium too heavily explained. Not that it's bad to have solid reasoning to carry your audience from point A to B (or in the case of time travel, B to A) - the StarTrek reboot handled things quite well, even if there are dissenters - with a fleshed anchor, only saying sometimes less is more, as is the case here. I'm being intentionally vague, I know. Point being: I like its use, and it made what would have otherwise been a bland, other-than slog through bad guys/heroes/save-the-day far more appealing. My only slight is in the enemy camp. For a game focusing so heavily on its characters, they went full cookie-cutter with the opposition. There is a single moment where we get life in the enemy, and for that moment, it rises above even what I expect out of other titles, but just as quickly the characters slump leaving us with generic bad guy who's evil because he's evil. Yawn.

Graphics are a mix of Super Nintendo Era and typical 3DS, a bird's eye view used as you move your troops around the battlefield. There are a few animated clips throughout and these are gorgeous. Many of the cut-scenes are not, unfortunately, more function over style, though I wouldn't say the game loses any points for it graphically, but many of the parts feel recycled the further you delve becoming familiar with camera placement, sparse landscapes, and three or so characters huddled close to one another. When one piece is so graphically stunning and the other so unimaginative, the disparity only becomes more pronounced.

I'm going to be a little inconsistent here, and for a second I want you to ignore everything I said above about too many moving parts. Okay? Good. Awakening is easy. It borders going through the motions without quite slipping over the edge, but the difficulty curve is more a straight line to slightly elevated straight line than anything. Between Chapters which constitute the main story, there are side skirmishes available from time to time along with a side-story popping up occasionally as well, and you can also purchase an item known as a Reeking Box triggering a side skirmish wherever you choose to openit. As a person who often becomes mired in quests off the beaten path until I've exhausted every avenue before plunging back into the main fray, these distractions serve only to placate my OCD and level up my characters to seeming Herculean results. I want to say I bought two, maybe three of those Reeking Boxes in total, getting only into other fights when they appeared on my map, and even following that pattern left me well outside the enemy's reach. Around halfway through is when I first noticed the gap, and while there were still some elements to each battle requiring a dash of planning, there was little fear of either failure or losing a unit unless I went completely reckless, two points yanking all tension from the experience. Awakening has a fair number of classes available, all of which are able to be upgraded into one or two different advanced classes (Fighter to Barbarian, Archer to Sniper) specializing in a certain style of play. Further, if you find yourself unimpressed with any new units acquired either by the side missions or main story, their classes can be changed as well offering more structure for how you'd like to approach the game. And as you level, new abilities become available to each of your characters which will also change the way you might use them in battle, this coupled with newer weapons unlocking through progression or class upgrades along with those advancements make for a healthy amount of customization. Unfortunately, there's very little need for it. Oh you should upgrade, absolutely, as the advanced classes are going to be obviously stronger and allow for more options, however the abilities were never something I felt necessary to mess with. I got them, stuck them on, didn't try to rearrange any specific thing to again min/max, and still managed to steamroll the competition. In spite of how prone I am to easily drowning in "too much" with this genre, I couldn't help but feel Awakening might have benefited from more purposeful variety. Much of what I found was simple window dressing, nothing I needed to worry about getting right or wrong lest it cause me failure somewhere down the line. Even a narrowing of the number of ability slots each character has would have provoked more interaction, forcing me into either a meaningful decision around my desired "loadout" or, at the very least, a particular leaning toward certain unit types. As it was, I could just roll with whomever the game selected for me and have at it. To be fair, I did personally select who did/did not go into battle, but the argument remains the same. Though I do tend to grind in my RPGs as is the nature of that beast, I never feel overpowered the further I venture, and though the genre has a tendency to over inflate its difficulty near the end, I would have liked a closer struggle here.

Fire Emblem Awakening is a good game. I don't mean to give the impression it's not. I'd call it worth the price of admission. Uneven in a number of places, when it shines it shines brightly, and I'm sure those more familiar with the series will find it an easy addition to their collection. I am tempted to go backwards in the catalog to see what nods to fans I likely missed. A number of spots felt self-referential, and I'm a sucker for that sort of thing. Overall recommended if you can overlook a few missteps.

review_headline: A solid, fun followup to Mario Kart Wii
review_body:
A great game! I've always been a huge fan of Mario Kart, and this one keeps the quality and action high! It's also nice to have a game in HD; the game looks fantastic, and they did not sacrifice gameplay for graphics.

The computer is quite difficult on the 150cc levels (very aggressive rubber-banding), but it's certainly challenging and the only way you'll win is to not make ANY mistakes. Even if you don't make mistakes, the computer is likely to get you with an item on the last lap, and you won't be able to recover. So you really have to EARN your 1st place finishes.

If you've played Mario Kart Wii, it's similar but there are a few differences. The biggest difference in my mind is that when you play teams your items do affect your teammates. There are some new items and some of the older ones removed. You can fully customize your kart and unlock more customizations as you play.

This is also the first MK that has DLC. As of this writing, they've only unlocked one DLC set with some new karts, characters, and tracks. Some of the tracks are replays from previous MKs, but some are new, all with Nintendo themes (ExciteBike, Zelda, etc).

This game is tons of fun for friends and family. The more people playing, the better!

Even if you already have MK Wii, this one is worth it. We still play MK Wii, but tend to play this one more, possibly because it's more challenging. We still haven't earned gold cups on all tracks on 150cc.

product_title: Doctor Lautrec and the Forgotten Knights - Nintendo 3DS
review_headline: Fell flat on my already low expectations. Not the worst, but nothing to make it shine either
review_body:
After putting some hours into this game, I think I finally have to just give up on it.

Complete Professor Layton copy cat business aside, the game couldn't stand up on it's own to be charming enough to keep my invested. I was hoping the characters might be nice, especially since just like the Layton series, this game gets some very nicely animated cutscenes. But no matter how nice animated scenes are, if you're not invested into the characters or stories it's nothing but just something pretty to look at.

The characters all felt very two dimensional. This 'Doctor' guy is an amazing Mystery solver who goes underground with his assistant Sophie. All he cares about is solving mysteries and that is his character, inside and out. Sophie is in love with him despite this for some reason? And he is clueless. And it stays very cliche throughout. I couldn't care for the two of them at all really!

I play games for the stories and characters, so I give this game a rating of 2 just for that alone. The only nice thing about the game is probably just the art, animation, and music. But those flashy things really don't add up to much when not even the gameplay is much fun either.

You walk around in underground places pushing crates to make a path, and avoiding guards who will send you to the start of the room if you get caught. Sometimes you come across doors that need to be unlocked by solving puzzles such as cross word puzzles and 'find the difference' type things. Then they have some sort of battle monster event that I could never really figure out how it worked (Never really cared enough to bother though) Supposedly if you can place certain items on the boards in certain spots, it could possibly boost your monster's attack. But that's all you do, place them on the board. And once you run out of spots and you didn't bring down the monster's HP down low enough you lose. Not very fun if you ask me!

Having previously played 50 Cent, Blood on the Sand for Xbox 360, I thought I would give the original version a shot. I've always been under the motto: There's no bad game under $5.00. After attempting to Bulletproof, I'm going to have to change my thinking. I have never had such difficulty in getting a third person shooting game protege to aim at the enemies trying to gun either him or her down. If memory serves me correctly, aiming is handled via the R joystick, while the camera/view is handled via the L joystick, which normally isn't a problem. However, even with being able to adjust the aiming speed in the options menu, getting 50 to aim & hit an enemy is virtually impossible.
I tried to like this game, I really did, but if I can't hit an enemy, it doesn't take too long, before your body armor is gone, then your health is gone and it's time to reload the game. So if you want to advance in the game, break out your memory caps to remember where the enemies are located on the various levels, so you can at least, find cover, take forever lining up your shots and then shoot your enemies. review_headline: It was fun, but I couldn't see why anyone would play ...
review_body:
This game and expansion are well worth the money... as long as you have friends to play it with you.

I bought D3 on the PC when it first came out. I played the whole thing solo and made it through the storyline once and decided I was done with it. It was fun, but I couldn't see why anyone would play past that point.

I got it on the console when a buddy told me he was getting it, and I convinced my dad to get it too (we're all big Xbox live players), and I found out why people play beyond that point. Then, we got the expansion, and I lost another hundred hours to it.

It's a loot grind. Plain and simple. So the real joy is finding gear that help you and your buddies delve into harder and harder modes. It's also helpful for you or your buddies to look online at what CAN be found, so you can get excited about what might be coming up. Then, when you get it, it's fun to show off to your buddies, and if you find another, you can give them one of yours (the one that's not as good of course).

I have every character at level 70, plus a couple at level 70 in hardcore mode (where if you die, you don't regenerate), and I'm finding other things to play after my dad and buddy don't get on as often and after we've all dumped upwards of 3 or 4 hundred hours into it. Well worth the money, again, so long as you have buddies to play it with.

review_headline: Don't waste your time or money.
review_body: I wanted to like it... but it's a terrible waste of time and money. This should be a free to play game, but they somehow still charged full price for it. It feels incomplete; can you say lack-of-content? The full game feels like a demo or a beta... there is not even a campaign mode. Graphics are ok, some of the special moves are slightly cool but gameplay is very boring. No back story, no point to doing anything really. They advertised "800,000 combinations", but there's not... it's basically the same thing no matter what. In my opinion, it's obvious that game developers have their hands in the wallets/pockets of professional game reviewers when they give games like Evolve a review score of 9 out of 10!  This game is also the perfect example of how greedy developers have become. I don't mind DLC, I know at the end of the day it's about money... but this game takes it to the next level of greed and shamelessness with the paid DLC. Hands-down the best option for recording original gameplay of older games!

The video quality is absolutely outstanding, with pixel perfect clarity and several filters that can occasionally make the pixels look less harsh, but they usually just muddy it up and make everything unreasonably blurry. I found one filter that made Chrono Trigger look like it had a watercolor motif, so it's cool to have the option!

The widescreen simulation is somehow really easy on the eyes (although I stick with standard 4:3) and every game I've put in has been recognized! Sometimes it won't read the ROM, but once I remove it and put it back in, it always works, even with Pocket Monsters Midori, or Pokemon Green, which never came to the US originally. This includes reproduction carts like Bahamut Lagoon, Star Fox 2 and Clock Tower for the SNES.

For a game like Pokemon where I want to save all my data to the cartridge, there's an option to "Save to Cart" which essentially overwrites any save data on the cartridge using the current emulated state. You can also save to the console itself but after trying it once and losing a lot of data I haven't messed with it since.

The controller is indeed awkward as everyone says, but I love how the buttons click like a mouse, and there are two programmable buttons on the top corners that I have mapped for "Fast Forward" and "Save State." The stick is unnecessary and I wish they put a sturdy D-pad because there aren't any SNES games I can think of that benefit from an analog stick, save for maybe Star Fox. It's fine for turn-based games that don't require immediate input, but any other fast-paced games that require more careful timing suffer immensely from the lack of precision the control stick offers.

I have NOT had any issues with the games being messed up from the tightness of the console - everything slides out very easily. I suppose they fixed the issue after so many people complained, because I was expecting a big hassle and experienced none!

The sides have controller input slots for your original controllers, but mine weren't working, so I'm mailing it back to Hyperkin soon to get it fixed.

It's worth noting how unnecessary their update/system restore functions are - they could have included a way to wirelessly update the firmware but everything needs to be done on a freshly reformatted SD card on a local computer before plugging into the back of the console. Huge pain in the ass.

All in all, for someone like me who's trying to capture retro footage for YouTube videos, this is something I cannot live without. Contra III: The Alien Wars is one of those games I missed out on as a kid but recall constantly skimming through Nintendo Power magazines and enjoying the intense looking pictures.  Seeing a bulky little dude walking around being destructive as his only means of survival and glancing at the fire-covered explosions all around him just made a little boy like myself instantly take notice of it like a little kid in a candy store.  However I had a suspicious feeling that since the original NES Contra was notorious for its difficulty, that Contra III would be the same way.  That's why I never played it then.  Well that turns out to be both true and untrue.  Contra III's actually easier than the NES Contra.  That is, if you're playing on easy mode.  Medium difficulty is probably a tad easier than NES Contra, but the hardest setting is much MUCH harder than the NES game!  Don't even THINK about playing Contra III on hard mode!    One thing this game does really well is update the graphics in convincing fashion, so the game looks exactly like how a Contra game *should* be designed.  Contra III features a  bigger, brighter and more animated style in comparison to the NES Contra game which only makes perfect sense.  I strongly admire this.  It means Konami was doing the series justice by maintaining what made the series so memorable in the first place.  Of course you still have to deal with \\"one hit you die\\" gameplay courtesy of all kinds of surrounding danger (mainly enemy bullets flying from a million different directions of course being the biggest issue you'll face) but this danger feels slightly more tolerable compared to the NES Contra game.  The enemies consist of swarms (and swarms and more swarms!) of aliens, dragons and oversized insects all animated beautifully and respectably.    The levels are different from the NES Contra in that you face an enormous amount of bosses.  The levels are focused more on rocky or mechanical-designed boss fights instead of frequent regular enemy encounters.  I like this change however since it not only keeps your heart pumping with tension, but the variety of bosses and their cool-looking designs is pretty staggering.  The strategies required to defeat these bosses is quite diverse too, and fast movements are necessary to take most of them down as well as memorizing their attack patterns so you can evade all the chaos.  Chaos... that probably would have been a more fitting title for the game instead of Contra, lol.  I don't really care for the aerial view levels, but they are admittedly sort of easier than the other ones.  The fast-moving sky and motorcycle stages are REALLY intense.  Amazingly hard levels those ones are, haha.    Oh and the final boss fight totally reminds me of Phantoon from Super Metroid in more ways than one.  They both have nearly identical attack methods.  Strange that a google search didn't provide any results regarding these similarities, so maybe I'm the only one who sees them.  Overall Contra III's a great game but incredibly hard... and short.  You can blaze through this game in less than 40 minutes if you're good.  I'm not that good though, so it takes me more like an hour and that's just on the easiest setting.
