product_title: HORI Battle Pad Turbo for Wii U (Luigi Version) - Nintendo Wii U
review_headline: just like a Classic or Classic Pro controller
review_body:
Overview:

The Hori Battle Pad is a very capable Nintendo GameCube (henceforth "GCN") style controller that works by connecting to a Wiimote, just like a Classic or Classic Pro controller. It is a solid value and a great alternative for games like Super Smash Bros. (works with both the new Wii U game and the older Brawl).

Technical:

The Battle Pad functions as a Wii Classic Pro Controller, and must be plugged in to a Wiimote. If you don't have a Wiimote lying around, this controller will not work. It doesn't require any batteries, since it derives power from the Wiimote.

The controller works wonderfully with Super Smash Bros. for Wii U, as well as any game that supports the Classic Pro (or Classic) controller for Wii. This includes several Wii U and many Wii games, including Mario Kart 8, Mario Kart Wii, Super Smash Bros. Brawl, most Virtual Console games (both for Wii U and Wii), Xenoblade Chronicles, The Last Story, and Monster Hunter Tri (for Wii). The controller did NOT work however with Wind Waker HD and Donkey Kong Country: Tropical Freeze. This is of course no fault of the controller itself: those games simply do not support the Wii Classic or Classic Pro controllers.

Build Quality:

The Hori Battle Pad is a solidly constructed and attractive piece of kit. The plastic shell has a slight matte finish, which helps grip when your hands inevitably get sweaty. Similar products, such as the PDP Fight Pad, are glossy and get slippery when wet. Despite my best attempts, I was unable to cause the controller to creak or flex when applying significant pressure. It's rock solid. The primary face buttons (ABXY) are all identically placed to the original GCN controller and feel great when pressed. For comparison, I used my GCN Wavebird controller, and the face buttons felt identical. The c-stick is an exact replica of what's on the GCN controller as well, which will please purists but likely annoy anyone who found the original c-stick too small. Other controller's such as PDP's Fight Pad have enlarged the stick in their revisions, but Hori remains faithful to the original. That isn't to say everything is faithfully reproduced 1:1, as Hori has made some modifications and tweaks in other places, for better or worse.

The original GCN controller had two analog triggers (R and L), and when fully depressed they would "click" in. The triggers were very "deep" and had a lot of travel to fully activate in certain games. Likely some find this ideal and others annoying (I count myself among the latter). The Hori Battle Pad eschews the deep analog triggers of the GCN controller and replaces them with digital buttons for R and L, which can best be described as "paddles." I was hesitant about the change, but in actuality they feel great. The buttons have very short travel, and in games like Super Smash Bros., it means blocking can be executed much more quickly and reliably. Additionally, Hori improves on the original GCN controller design by providing two Z buttons (or ZR and ZL, as on the Classic Pro controller) on the right and left. The effect is similar to most modern controllers which have both shoulder buttons and triggers. These buttons are a marked improvement over the original Z button, of which there was only one on the right shoulder, and it was finicky to press. These additions alone may make the Hori Battle Pad a sweeter option than even an original GCN controller for Smash fanatics.

The other tweaks Hori has made come in the left analog stick and the d-pad. The left analog looks identical to the GCN's analog, however in practice it feels different. Hori has opted to flatten the top of the analog stick, whereas Nintendo's GCN controller had a rounded feel. The grippy rubber also feels less plush on the Hori pad, making it easier for your thumb to slide. I prefer the GCN's analog, but it is a subtle difference that is not a deal breaker. Hori's d-pad, on the other hand, is a huge improvement. One of the biggest criticisms of Nintendo's GCN controller was the diminutive d-pad, tucked away almost as an afterthought - a reflection of the 3D nature of games who only relied on the d-pad as glorified buttons (rather than a directional movement). Hori's d-pad is much larger than the original, and the controller benefits from it. Since the pad also works as a Classic controller in Wii and Wii U Virtual Console games, the larger d-pad makes playing SNES and NES games enjoyable. It should be noted, however, that the Classic, Classic Pro, and Wii U Pro controller all have much larger d-pads which feel substantially "clickier" than Hori's, which will make them go-to options for most retro gamers.

It should also be noted that the Start/+, Select/-, and Home buttons on the controller are all made out of an awfully mushy rubber, and they feel awful to press on this controller. Thankfully these buttons are not essential to gameplay, and I never had an issue with them failing to activate. It's clearly Hori skimped here, but the truth is I barely notice them. Finally, the cord on the controller, which must be plugged in to the accessory port on a Wiimote (where you attach the Nunchuck), is of generous length, and satisfactorily pliable. My biggest complaint with PDP's Fight Pad was it's super short cord, and the fact that it was very stiff - so much that it caused the attached Wiimote to turn itself over, and fall off my couch when moving the controller. I never had such an issue with the Hori Battle Pad, and in fact the length of the cord is a big improvement over Nintendo's own Classic and Classic Pro controllers.

Odds and Ends:

The Hori Battle Pad includes a turbo function, which I relegated to "odds and ends" status since most serious gamers won't ever bother with this feature. I don't see how it could give you any real competitive edge, but it works like this: holding down Turbo (which is near Start/Select/Home on the controller) and then pressing the desired button at the same time, will result in the controller spamming that input. There are 3 presets for speed: 5, 10, and 20, which can be changed on the fly with a slider. I don't use this feature myself, but it's there for anyone who wants it.

I generally avoid third-party controllers because of poor build quality and their overall cheap aesthetic, but by and large the Battle Pad looks great. One weird thing really undercuts what Hori has accomplished here, however: the Luigi logo painted on the controller appears off center. This is such a minor thing, but reinforces the stereotype that third-party controllers are cheap and low-quality. Perhaps mine was just an aberration - I've included a photo. It's barely noticeable and doesn't affect my use of the controller whatsoever, but I thought it worth mentioning.

Summary:

The Hori Battle Pad is a fantastic, solidly-constructed controller which emulates the original GCN controller faithfully, with the exception of a few notable improvements. The controller works with any Wii or Wii U game that is compatible with a Classic or Classic Pro controller, and is a great value at $25. For comparison, Nintendo charges $20 for their GameCube adapter for Wii U, and a controller (if you don't already own one) is another $30. And that GCN controller will ONLY work with Smash Bros. Wii U, whereas the Hori Battle Pad works with ANY game (including Smash) that accepts a Classic/Classic Pro controller. If your a fan of Nintendo's original GCN controller layout, or just a huge Smash Bros. fan, buy this controller!

Rocksmith 2014 is an amazing tool. I've been messing around with guitars for 30 years, but never had the patience to methodically learn to play. I don't really have time for lessons from a teacher or the patience to teach myself tab. So I diddled around with an acoustic for literally decades. When I heard about Rocksmith I though it was a neat idea, but the original version had pretty mediocre review so I never tried it. When 2014 came out and I started to hear good things about it, I bought it as soon as it went on sale.

Since the day I brought it home, I've been addicted. The game itself has a few technical problems - it crashes occasionally - it loses audio from my guitar occasionally - the interface is clearly designed for a console and is clunky in windows - and the note detection is not perfect. That said this game does an AMAZING job of teaching songs. The song selection is fantastic - just a great collection of songs from many sub-genres of rock. The note track is intuitive, the custom tones are excellent, and the dynamic difficulty is very clever. I find the random playlist "Nonstop Play" to be extremely addictive - and I've been having a great time playing songs I've never even heard before. I don't mess with the arcade games much, but they are pretty solid and I can see why some people enjoy them. I spend a few minutes in Session Mode as part of my normal practice - some day I will be able to improvise leads I swear!

I even bought the original Rocksmith for the exportable songs and the extra cord so my son (10 years old) can play along with me. He's becoming a MEAN bass player, too. His teacher is very impressed by his playing and it's never a problem to get him to practice using Rocksmith. His teacher and I coordinate sometimes so he can work on songs that are available on RS.

The Rocksmith team is also doing an amazing job of producing DLC songs, ranging from Classic Rock to Alternative and a half-dozen flavors of Metal, even a 5 song Classical pack. I have to keep that temptation under control, because otherwise I'd be buying new DLC every 2-3 weeks.

Now... about the latency issue. Yeah I struggled at first and pulled my hair out trying to cut the lag. It turns out the answer to nearly every problem is THE TV. Running sound through the HDMI port introduces lag because nearly every TV these days does audio signal processing. You probably don't notice it watching TV, but audio, even when watching TV, has a latency that is too much for playing music. The "Use Game Mode" suggestion did not work on my TV. YOU NEED TO ROUTE SOUND DIRECTLY FROM COMPUTER/CONSOLE TO AN AMP AND SPEAKERS OR HEADPHONES.

It's kind of silly to ding Rocksmith 2014 stars because of this issue. The problem is with the TV and there's no software solution that Rocksmith can use to fix it. In order to overcome that issue, they'd have to send the signal before you even played the note. You need a no/very low-latency audio output!

Rocksmith might not replace a good teacher, its "gaming" aspect might be a little bit weak, and it does have some minor technical issues, but I really feel that Rocksmith is a game-changer for people learning guitar. I look forward to the next version of Rocksmith as well as other programs inspired by the idea.

review_headline: The Best Console Gaming Controller on the Market
review_body:
The Xbox One controller on its own is just another step in the gradual improvement of Microsoft's gaming controllers. The joysticks have a great grip going around the inner circle, the left- and right-bumpers are much improved over the Xbox 360 controller, and overall the controllers has a lot more heft to it and, at least on my initial few uses of it, seems to be a more durable controller overall.

My only gripe with the controller has to do with the headset input. It's not nearly as straightforward as the Xbox 360 input was, and can sometimes be a bit of a hassle to attach at the bottom. It also occasionally seems to have problems working properly when plugged in, requiring a detaching and reattachment. This is really a very minor drawback though when compared to the overall construction of the controller.

The Armed Forces camouflage has a very cool look to it, so much so that I prefer using it to the regular black controller that came with the system. Overall another great controller in a long line of outstanding Xbox controllers. Highly recommended for gamers who enjoy shooters and action games in particular.

review_headline: And I first thought Black Flag was a somewhat lackluster game... oh how wrong I was.
review_body:
Just calling this game \\"decent at best\\" is an overstatement. Occasionally the gameplay has its moments, but the story is so bland and dull that it in turn, also makes the gameplay bland and dull as well. 75% of this game's storyline consists of Arno going to different locations and assassinating random people whom he believes are responsible for his adopted father's death.

Hands down, this has got to be one of the most repetitive games I have ever played. One of the best things about having a large franchise such as Assassins Creed (especially with new titles being consecutively released almost every year) is that it gives companies like Ubisoft a chance to look back on their past work to improve on the mistakes that they've made in previous projects.

So the big question is: Is this the case for AC Unity? Hell no. Co-op is a terribly executed idea and is nowhere near as good enough to replace the competitive multiplayer concept featured in past games, the controls have not only NOT improved, but have in fact gotten even worse. Arno is slow to control and glitchy too, jumping through a window is nearly impossible (good luck finishing some chase missions within your first 5 tries), stealth mode is completely redundant and most of the time makes it nearly impossible to control Arno when activated, and worst of all, if you climb one bad wall with nothing left above you to be used to climb up or over, you will get stuck on it with nowhere to jump over or eject from. Honestly the only decent thing that I like about the new controls is the new \\"controlled decent\\" and even that has a few minor flaws of its own.

One good thing that this game did for me is that it taught me an important lesson. It taught me to NEVER pre-order a single game from Ubisoft and never buy a single game from Ubisoft (or from any company for that matter) without first checking the reviews. This is easily one of the worst games I have ever played and in my opinion, wasa huge waste of money. When Black Flag was released last year I thought that game was a little bland but after watching some story walkthroughs in order to try and understand the storyline more, it's actually not that bad at all and the gameplay is miles ahead of Unity's. I would rather play that game any day than play this garbage again.

product_title: Etrian Odyssey Untold: The Millennium Girl - Nintendo 3DS
review_headline: A review from the perspective of someone who played the DS version
review_body:
If you think that playing the DS version of Etrian Odyssey would prepare you or make the game easier, I'll tell you that, beyond the first map, mostly all the floor levels have had some level of changes to them, while others are completely different. Some changes make the levels harder and force you to craft some level of strategy to get around obstacles, while others are welcome changes that make levels less mind-numbingly tedious.

If you play under the new story mode, you get an ongoing story element, with the trade-off being that you can't create your own party. The characters have fun personalities, have great voice acting, and I enjoy their banter back and forth. It also adds a new dungeon, which has a new level accessible after you finish each area of levels in the main labyrinth area of the game.

The redone music is gorgeous. The tunes are familiar, but orchestral elements are added to make each set of levels less monotonous to listen to. And believe me, you'll want to have the sound on when you can, as your party members will point out hidden elements like secret passageways, events, and little quirks that could actually refill your MP or HP (at least in story mode, can't say for classic mode). You'll also know when a FOE (aka hard enemies that are shown with a special flowing icon on the map) spots you, and make the decision whether to avoid or engage them.

In story mode (not sure if this is in classic mode), you get your own mansion, along with a maid who gives requests, serves various types of tea that give different benefits, a storage area for items you want to keep, and a place to store grimoires, which are another new element added to this game. Grimoires are equipable items that allow you to gain abilities limited to monsters or other classes, and you have the option of combining them. The combination system was a little difficult for me to get the hang of, but other people may not have as much trouble with it.

All in all, even if you played the first Etrian Odyssey, I'd recommend giving this remake a play. review_headline: Needs more time in the oven
review_body:
Designed from the ground up for next-gen systems only (XB1, PS4, PC) this Assassin's Creed title set in nineteenth century Paris is a big and gorgeous game that never really allows you to soak up its splendor in full glory due to the frequency of graphical glitches and minor game bugs that pop up far too often shattering whatever illusion of reality you had to the point of annoyance. This truly is a title that came out of the oven half-baked and would've really benefited with a few months more time under development for polish and quality control. As evidence look no further than the just released (Nov. 25) patch #3 that fixes over 300 game issues with another corrective update scheduled to release in early December 2014. Tsk-Tsk...

Still, after 18+ hours with the game I'm having a reasonably good time with it. The world is vibrant and gorgeous with a level of environmental detail that is just stunning and being a sucker for this series I still enjoy the series' tried and true (and a bit overplayed) mechanics ranging from tower climbs to the vast amount of collectible hunt challenges scattered throughout the game. If you've played earlier titles in the series the core DNA is very much intact, not much has changed but the window dressing has certainly been spruced up to a whole other level. Overall a somewhat shallow update but one that still manages to scratch the right itch for me.

Out of the 2 games in the series currently out for the xbox one I still prefer [[ASIN:B00CX8VYM0 Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag Action/Adventure Game - Xbox One]] mostly because it is a more polished experience. Regardless, fans of the series should still give Unity a shot - the quality of its visual presentation makes it all worthwhile (sorta) in the end.

I've been playing these wrestling games for a long time, since 'Smackdown: Just Bring It'. My absolute favorite and still to this day is 'Here Comes The Pain'. Since then, these wrestling games have been rather disappointing, with a few exceptions along the way. Last year's 'WWE 2k14' game was actually really enjoyable, and I was very excited for this new game to be on PS4. However, it just doesn't quite deliver.

A big reason why I pre-ordered this game was the MyCareer mode. I've heard great things about 2K's career mode in their basketball game and I felt positive that they were going to have a stellar mode for my CAW. They didn't. There's a few aspects they handled well, but there's hardly any cut-scenes or interactions backstage with other superstars. My CAW can upgrade and practice which is nice, but besides that, I have little options to becoming a heel or a face. I wanted this mode to be similar to the season mode in 'Here Comes The Pain'. A 15 year career sounds impressive, but your CAW only wrestles like one match a month, so your career is not THAT long. And the A.I. in this mode is unstable; you'll dominate a superstar one match, then in the next match you'll get destroyed, then in the following match you'll win again, and then you'll lose and win and lose and win and lose. Also, you'll get the same text messages over and over from Vicky Guerrero, and you'll chose between the same three match types over and over, and it gets stale quick. A side note, I read in articles that it does not matter if you win or lose, you can still gain lots of points to level up, but that's rare. When you win, you'll gain higher points and when you lose, you'll get hardly anything.

PROS =
GRAPHICS - The graphics are incredible. Definitely the highlight of the game.
GAMEPLAY - The controls are pretty solid. It does have a delay at times, but that's when your character is low on stamina. The chain wrestling feature is a nice addition. And I do enjoy the stamina bar and the more realistic flow of the match.
WWE UNIVERSE MODE - Glad it's there to fill the void for a lack luster MyCareer mode.

CONS =
LOAD TIMES - We're onto the next generation of consoles and we still have to sit through long load times? Unacceptable.
MYCAREER MODE - Not a lot of fun, but I feel like they can improve it next year, if they go down the right path.
MATCH TYPES - This year they cut a lot of match types. I'm not upset that they took out certain matches, but not having a one-on-one ladder match? That's ridiculous!
CAW - They made lots of cuts to this department, when in fact they should have approved on it since we now have more powerful game consoles.

2K delivered on the gameplay and the graphics. However, I'm not too fond of the mode options. Instead of having MyCareer mode, Showcase mode and Universe mode separate, they need to just combine them all and have one super amazing season mode. I am still going to play this game, like I do every year, but 'WWE 2K15' is not a top contender. Hopefully next year will be better. If you really want to play this game but don't feel like paying full price, I would wait until the price drops.

review_headline: Prolongs the 3DS' battery for up to 9 hours!
review_body:
This little device gives the original 3DS (not the 3DS XL) some much needed extra juice. Before I got this, I was always having to turn off my 3DS to keep the battery from dying. Especially when I took the device on the go. But with the Power Grip, I practically never have to worry about the battery dying on me.

It will easily give me 6 extra hours, aside from the 3 hours you normally get. Which is usually more than enough.

The Power Grip has a little red light that will turn on & off whenever it's battery is low. It will stay on when you begin charging it with the 3DS' power adapter. And it will turn into a GREEN light when it's fully charged.

In terms of acting as a grip, it's a mix bag. If you have small hands or if the 3DS is for a child, the grip will work fine. But if you're a teen or an adult with large hands, the grip won't feel very comfortable. But I personally wasn't bothered by its ergonomics. And was able to play games fine using it.

However, the Power Grip also works as a protector for the lower part of your 3DS. Since it practically covers it entirely. It is really easy to put on and pull apart (hint: you start removing it from the back, not the front).

These days, most people own the 3DS XL. But if you happen to own an original 3DS, then the Power Grip is one of the best battery extenders around for it.

product_title: Ace Combat Assault Horizon Legacy - Nintendo 3DS
review_headline: I can't believe a handheld could have a flying game this good.
review_body:
I have 100% completed this game, and it was a blast from start to finish. If you like planes and/or ace combat, you'll get a kick out of this.

I must admit, getting used to only one stick for flight control was a little difficult at first, as I am used to the "standard" setting for ace combat on the PlayStation 2, but once I got the hang of it (I'd say about the 3rd or 4th mission), it really took off from there, pun not intended.

There are so many planes to fly that some kind of feel similar, but really, it's like comparing french vanilla and vanilla ice cream. They're similar, but different enough to earn a separate label.

Just a heads up, the game can drop in frame rate when things get hairy and a lot of stuff is happening on-screen. I know for some people that's a huge turn-off, and ordinarily, it would be for me, too. But really, I was having too much fun to care. It felt more like a slow-motion camera shot than anything, but that might just be the fun in my eyes.

The game does look really pretty. The ground models are as basic as ever, but the planes are gorgeous. 3D is fun to fly in, if you can handle it. It's even more fun using the cockpit view with 3D on, but I personally liked using the 3rd person view with the one stick control. I think it helped my brain to transition from one plane style to another (i.e. Ace Combat on PS2 to this), but it defiantly was a fun thing to do every so often. The 3D did seem to cause the frame rate to dip a little more easily than when it was turned off, but the main reason I turned it off was to prolong battery life. Otherwise, I would have left it on.

All that to say, definitely a fun game and worth a purchase. Highly recommend it.

review_headline: Bad Value! Go for the Cheaper Starter Pack!
review_body:
First, this review is referring to the Marvel Avengers Collector's Edition starter pack -- not the overall game. Disney Infinity 2 is a fun game, but this collector's edition is NOT good value for money. The basic starter pack itself is around $75. And the four additional characters would cost around $60 -- assuming you couldn't find them on sale somewhere. (I noticed a certain toy store has already started a buy one get one half-off sale.)

So you're paying the additional money to have the large monster battle play stand, which just holds your figures. I mistakenly thought this would somehow be part of the game, but it is NOT. It's just a fancy stand for your figures. It lights up, but that's all. (Also, it's really big. That's cool for some kids, but I literally have no place to put it)

Regarding the game itself, I read online that Disney said that each play set would have three times the length of the previous play-sets in the first Disney Infinity game, but this is NOT TRUE. (The first Disney Infinity game had six play-sets, but Disney Infinity 2 only has three). I beat the Avengers game in just over six hours. I paid this very high price for something that was very easy to beat -- even easier and shorter than the original Disney Infinity game. Again, this isn't good value, so why spring for the super-expensive collector's edition?

Also, on this game, having all of the figures gives you no real advantage. In Skylanders, you need various characters to unlock certain levels. This is NOT the case in Disney Infinity 2.0. Having all of the characters gives you no real advantages in the playset. This is great news for parents on a budget. You do not need to buy your kids all of the figures for them to enjoy the game. But this also makes buying the collectors edition less attractive. So my recommendation is to buy the basic Marvel Avengers starter pack and buy one or two figures to go with it.

Also, two of the Marvel characters (Hawkeye and Black Widow) are pretty lame. Their powers and fighting abilities are relatively weak compared to the other ones. Iron Man and Thor are the best, because they can fly around. The Hulk is the strongest. Captain America is sort of strong, but not necessary. But Hawkeye and Black Widow feel like a real waste.

So in conclusion... The Avengers game is very short -- certainly not worth 125 quid. Two of the six characters are weak and useless relative to the others. And the very large light stand has no impact on the game. So why go for the collector's edition? You shouldn't.

If I had it to do all over again, I'd buy the basic Avengers pack and the Hulk figure, and that would be it.

review_headline: Just As Great As its Predecessors
review_body:
I've been a fan of Borderlands practically since day one, and have poured countless hours into the series and loved every minute of it. This game was no different, in that respect (and many others, too). The Pre-Sequel, though it has new mechanics and variables to give it its own feel, is not substantially different from Borderlands 2, sharing its predecessor's graphical engine, user interfaces, and much of the loot, which isn't necessarily a bad thing. I'm not sure what they could have done to evolve the series, graphics wise, when the plan was to only release the game on last generation consoles, and using what was already available rather than starting anew probably shaved a year off from the release date. I feel like the title screen, menus, and loading screens could have been changed up to give it more of a unique vibe, but that's no big deal. Borderlands 2 was a solid foundation, I'm not bothered that they built upon it.

It only took me two days to beat the first play through (split between two very long marathon sessions), and I went solo. If anyone found this game too difficult then I'm not entirely sure what to say to that. I've yet to experience any game breaking glitches, nothing's kept me from completing any missions, so I can't say I understand why people are complaining about bugs. It wasn't hard to adapt to the low gravity physics, and they became a large part of my survival strategy once I had. The limited oxygen wasn't as much of a hindrance as some had me believing it would be. There's a great many ways to replenish your O2 kits, almost any enemy defeated in a vacuum area will drop a canister of oxygen for you, natural vents and geysers are spread all throughout the moon's surface, and an artificial atmosphere environment is rarely ever very far away. If you stay observant, it is very hard to run out of oxygen, and even when you do there is ample time to get more (there's a trophy for suffocating five minutes straight without dying). The added vertical dimensions can make it a bit trickier to find waypoints, but thankfully, the minimap will alert you to the altitude of your destination in relation to your position with a handy little arrow pointing up for when your destination is above you, down for when it is below (this system applies for enemies as well). Not too complicated.

The addition of lasers and the cryo element are fantastic. I spent much of my time searching for either of these, or even better, a combination of both, a cryo laser. The lasers themselves coming in four variations, each having a unique style and feel, ranging from a steady stream of energy to blast of rays that fire off in a shotgun-like spread, and when factoring in the different gun manufacturers, they become even more diverse. Cryo has easily become my favorite element, freezing enemies solid and then shattering them is incredibly satisfying. It also gives you the chance temporarily remove an enemy from the fray, as long as they're encased in ice, they pose no threat, allowing you to focus on other targets. The grinder is also particularly useful, collecting piles of guns I'd otherwise leave behind in hopes of combining them into a more formidable weapon adds an extra layer to the already deep cycle of looting. I only hope these features make it into future iterations.

The main story line itself was interesting enough, especially the parts set after the events of Borderlands 2 rather than the characters recounting the events that led up to it. The end sets up the next game very nicely, unfortunately, it will be quite some time before we see anything from the third official chapter. It's interesting seeing Handsome Jack from a different perspective, protagonist or antagonist, either way, he's a great character. The only real downside of the role reversal is that we see some of our favorite characters painted as villains. It was good to see the Eridian guardians return, they were a nice bit of nostalgia from the first game, and they certainly change the pace from the rest of the enemies leading up to them. I have to say, though, that the Pre-Sequel's end boss was the most challenging yet, it constantly had me on my toes, the low gravity and double jumps were key in avoiding it (and when I couldn't, the gladiator's aspis would take the majority of the damage). In the previous games, the big bad end boss really only required finding a safe place to shoot a giant target from, but there was no safety from the Sentinel, only dodging its constant assault. Even though it required more attentive action to survive, I didn't find the Sentinel to be overly difficult, though I'm sure It will be a bit harder on the second play through.

Overall, I'm satisfied with the game. I would have preferred a lower price tag, but I was willing to pay in full for more Borderlands, and I don't regret it. Some people apparently have issues with this game, fortunately for me, I do not. My experience with the Pre-Sequel, after having completed the game, has been enjoyable, a little short, but that is in part due to be engrossing enough to have me keep playing for hours on end. review_headline: Fun FPS, Very Good Call of Duty Game
review_body:
We go through the same thing each year, seeing a new Call of Duty and Battlefield game, we buy them and play them and we feel like we've played the same game again and again. While Call of Duty Advance Warfare isn't exactly original, it does give us a new way to play with \\"future\\" technology creating a new way to revisit the same old thing.

Advanced Warfare gameplay reminds me of classic Call of Duty/Modern Warfare mixed with [[ASIN:B0050SXGU8 Crysis 3 - Playstation 3]]. It is fast, fun and makes you sometimes think before you act as their may be a be a better way of approaching a situation now that you have the technology.

For the most part, this is your basic FPS that we all know and love. The technology, ability to jump/hover/glide and weapon technology make the game more fun and enjoyable. You have a wide range of grenades including EMP, smart and threat which seek out enemies. You also have a drone which you can toss in the air and use to kill enemies from the air. It is difficult at times, but for the most part it is all you could ask for.

What they did right!
+ Not the best graphics in the world, but still very good with many open areas. I wish they would have make this just a next generation game. It would have looked so much better. Close-up textures also look a little blocky.
+ Classic style and control with a future technology upgrade. You have the power to jump, kick/hit, climb walls and eliminate the enemies like never before.
+ Solid FPS with a few challenges. Fun and enjoyable to play.
+ The ability to upgrade your character is awesome, something I really like about this game.
+ Great character models and voice-acting. The sound is also quite good.

What could have used more attention...
- There are a few glitches throughout the game, and from what I have heard, it is inconsistent and different for every player. Some may have issues, so may not. I had an issue where a fellow character who was with me was suppose to open a door for me so we could continue. Well, the character just stood there like a moron and refused to open the door. I reloaded the checkpoint and nothing, so I had to start the level over again. Others have had similar issues, which a future patch could correct. It seems to be random.
- Multiplayer is decent, but the maps seem small and basic. Still a lot of fun and a challenge with the new abilities.
- Longer single-player campaign than Ghosts, but I still wanted more.

Over-all the fun first person shooter we have been asking for. The new technology abilities and weapons, while basic at times, still makes the game fun and more of a challenge at times. I wish the levels wouldn't be so linear at times and more of an open world, but for a FPS this game really pulls off the fun level and over-all game enjoyment factor.

product_title: Thrustmaster T-Flight Hotas X Flight Stick
review_body:
My last good joystick, a Logitech WingMan Force Feedback, still works after about 12 years, but it's slowly wearing out. I've looked at several possible replacements and came across this Thrustmaster T.Flight Hotas X. The most helpful review to date is by gump92139 and, along with other reviews, convinced me to try the Thrustmaster. Gump's review has a good description and is well worth reading.

I'm very impressed and pleased so far. I have used it in FSX, mostly with the Carenado Cessna 340, but also with DodoSim's Bell Jet Ranger using the helicopter's most difficult and realistic settings. The Thrustmaster provided very stable control, and the DodoSim helicopter is one of the most difficult to fly. The stick has a very solid, positive feel.

From the photo, I was concerned about the ergonomics of the throttle – it looked like it might be uncomfortable to use. It might be a bit uncomfortable for some at first, but being able to separate it from the stick by about 18 inches in any direction allows for many different placements, at different levels from the stick, etc. I was surprised at how user friendly and comfortable it is.

And regarding user friendliness, as gump92139 described, I simply plugged it into a USB port and ready to go. The manual says to access the control panel to configure and test the joystick, but I didn't need to do that – it was ready to go simply by plugging it in. (I'm using Windows 7, 32 bit.)

However, during the first test “flight,” I accessed the settings in FlightSim X and made some changes in the button assignments, as well as adding a few assignments for the unused buttons: flaps, trim, views, etc. It's very easy and quick to do without exiting the simulator.

One minor complaint is that buttons 3 and 4 are placed on the stick opposite each other, 4 on the back right towards the operator, and 3 on the front right. I found myself pressing both buttons at the same time with the thumb and index finger. Since the trim wheels in many airplanes are on the pilot's right, I had assigned these buttons on the right for trim up and trim down – not good to press both together, but the placement and right hand grip seems to encourage pressing both buttons at once. Might have to reassign them, or just get used to the placements.

All in all, it's a fine HOTAS system at a very reasonable price.

review_headline: Do I need to remind you what is out there?
review_body:
The Last of Us:

I remember how I first discovered this game. I was arguing with a friend over Naughty Dog's tendency to only release one franchise per platform. My friend was arguing that I was wrong because there were Crash Bandicoot games on the PlayStation 2 (There are but not made by Naughty Dog). I pulled up some information on the internet and started to boast about how I was right and I hear him ask: "What the hell is The Last of Us?". This was shortly after the game was announced.

After seeing the announce trailer, I never had spent so much time scouring gaming news sites to find any scrap of information on this game. I highly anticipated this game for over a year, I hyped it up to anyone that would listen. Ultimately, I should have been setting myself up for a let down, as a lot of other games probably would have.

When the game was released in June, 2013 for the PlayStation 3 I was as happy as I could possibly be. I quickly immersed myself in the game and was taken along an incredible journey.

Synopsis:

You play as Joel, set 20 years after the outbreak and 20 years after a heartbreaking tragedy, Joel is a strong, fierce and brutal man who's only care in the world is surviving. His partner in crime (literally) and seemingly former life partner Tess set out to find a man who stole their supply of guns and who attempted to kill them. Upon finding the man, Robert, they learn he sold their guns to the Fireflies, an anti-military group. The leader of the Fireflies, Marlene, makes Joel and Tess a deal: Smuggle something out of the city in exchange for the guns.

That "something" is Ellie. A 14 year-old girl who's whole life has been lived in a military safe zone. She's never seen the outside world. So why is she so important? *Minor Spoilers Follow* Ellie has been bitten by one of the infected, a zombie like creature that can either a) literally just look like a zombie or b) have heavy plates of fungi growing out of their heads, blinding them. The average time it takes to turn into an infected after being bitten is two days. Ellie's bite is three weeks old. She is immune to the virus and is the key to finding a cure. Joel and Tess's job is to get her to the Fireflies outside the safe zone so they can find a cure and end this virus once and for all.

Of course, nothings that easy:

On your journey you'll encounter multiple enemies including soldiers, hunters, different forms of infected. You won't have a dull moment!

Gameplay:

Some people have criticized the gameplay, others have praised it. I personally love it. The game is a TPS style that consists of running, sneaking, hiding, solving puzzles, fighting etc...Joel uses his backpack as an inventory system where he can craft different items like a health pack or a Molotov Cocktail. Both use the same ingredients so it's up to you pick which one you need the most. Aside from those items, he can craft shivs, smoke bombs, nail bombs and even make a melee weapon into a one-hit kill weapon (limited use, of course). You'll also find supplements in the game to boost Joel's health, weapon sway, and even give him perks against fighting Clickers, the second stage of the virus. Overall, the gameplay isn't doing anything innovative, but it doesn't have to. It works well and is brilliantly executed.

Combat:

Joel has a vast amount of weapons he can use to take down his enemies. He'll use anything from his bare hands to a flamethrower acquired later on in the game. Throughout the game, you'll find different parts that can be used to upgrade your weapons. These parts are essential, as they will increase clip capacities, give Joel and extra holster, reduce recoil, improve armor piercing etc....You'll find work stations in different chapters and use them to upgrade.

Weapons aren't everything though. This is a "Survival Horror" game,so there will be times in which you won't have much ammo. Joel can crouch down and sneak up behind enemies to strangle them or use a shiv to the head. Strangling an enemy is especially brutal. Unlike Uncharted (Naughty Dog's other PS3/4 franchise) where it's just a quick neck snap, it takes a few seconds to actually kill the enemy. You'll hear the enemy struggle and fight for his life, all while risking other enemies seeing you.

Sound:

Playing this game with headphones is a different experience than playing without. Playing with headphones you hear every little detail from NPC's conversations, the crisp sound of the rain, to the truly disturbing sound of the infected (Seriously, the infected sound much worse with headphones). From the brilliant clacking of the guns to the meat pounding sounds of fist fighting, the sound designers did their jobs well, here.

The Soundtrack is brilliant. Probably my favorite game/movie soundtrack of all time. Gustavo Santaolalla does a beautiful job of blending different instruments and other items to really bring the game together. Some of the heartfelt moments of the game wouldn't have been nearly as impactful without Santaolalla.

Graphics:

I usually don't care about graphics. As longs as they're not so bad that they're taking me out of the immersion, I'm fine. But, the graphics are absolutely beautiful here. What was the best looking game on the PS3, is now arguably the best looking game on the PS4. Everything is so clear. The buildings have so much detail, blood runs down Joel's arm and face at certain points of the game. This version of the game is how we were meant to see it!

Multiplayer:

Heralded by Naught Dog as the most innovative multiplayer ever, it is a disappointment. It's really not that innovative. Instead of running around and shooting people like in Uncharted, you're sneaking around and shooting people. While there are some cool features like using friends from Facebook as a part of your clan and even the crafting system from the single player, I expected more out of this. It's fun, but not what I was expecting. But still, this is just icing on the cake.

PS3 - PS4:

FYI: If you have already owned The Last of Us on PS3 and purchased all of the DLC, there really isn't much incentive for you to buy this other than the visual improvements.

Conclusion:

The Last of Us is brilliant. It is a once-in-a-generation type game that focuses on story telling, but doesn't suffer from gameplay. It is now my favorite game of all time, and while I'll admit it isn't really the survival horror that intends to be, it is an intense, action packed story that will leave you wanting for more. This is the only game that I started a second playthrough, immediately after completing my first one. Half a dozen playthrough's later, I still absolutely love this game and will probably never tire of it.

review_headline: GAMING AS AN ART-FORM. AND THIS IS A MASTERPIECE!
review_body:
If there ever was any doubt that gaming is an art-form, this game shreds it to pieces.

The game offers traditional Japanese settings (from the temples and the castles to the mythology and the paintings), rich late 80's environments (from shipyards and inner courtyards to caves and snowy mountains) and a great collection of interesting guns. It may be only 9 in total yet I got more excited when I got the shotgun or the rocket launcher than I ever was finding any one of the bazzilion guns in [[ASIN:B00ERDGMO4 Borderlands 2]].

Each type of enemy has different strengths and different weaknesses so you will have to try to figure out the best and quickest way to put them down. Each gun comes with three purchasable upgrades and augmentations. No sniper rifle because this game wants you to be up close and personal.

The music is sublime, the dialog witty, the atmosphere mesmerizing, the hidden secrets will keep you exploring every nook and cranny (and try again and again to find your way to that impossible to reach bonus statue) and the story unfolds in twists and turns and double-crosses. And the ending will make you misty.

I know it is not fair to this epic game but it does bring to mind the game [[ASIN:B00001ZT47 Daikatana]] should had been. See, Mr Romero, if you fail to get it right, someone else eventually will. Now, I usually subtract a full star for games that come with an online DRM such as STEAM (required here); however, because the game is so good - and also available in the DRM-free GOG version, I decided to make a rare exception.

HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!
Hands down one of my favorites.

review_headline: I don't necessarily care about a game's graphic appeal if it has a great story, game play

I don't necessarily care about a game's graphic appeal if it has a great story, game play, etc., but this game looks like it was (at least graphically) designed for a PS2 and not any modern platform. The game's gameplay mechanics are wonderful. I like how stealth was added to the survival-horror genre that I came to expect from the creator of Resident Evil. I also appreciate that this game deviated from the past few Resident Evil games in that shooting is discouraged and trap-setting/melee kills are encouraged. It just adds to the suspenseful atmosphere of the game. A coherent storyline is absent from the game play. The player is thrust into a world with no backstory or purpose for the character doing what they're doing. It seems as the developing team spent all their time and effort in gameplay mechanics and not on anything else.

review_headline: The COD That NEEDED to happen!
review_body: After the not so well received "Ghosts" last year I was fairly skeptical whether this franchise would be able to pull a swift recovery. Most likely this is the case due to the design team that created MW 3 being directly involved. Regardless of your feelings on this franchise love it or hate it this is a solid FPS for me personally. Visceral is going to have to hit a grand slam next year with BF Hardline to be able to rival this... which they are def capable of no doubt. Undoubtedly trolls and haters will slam every bit of this and not everyone will be pleased.. go figure. So on to the game itself. First off the campaign.. while I just started on it is very immersive thus far and maintains your attention. The action is intense and immersive as well. If you have played MW 3 you know what to expect with quite a few additions. The graphics are clean and smooth and the variety of grenades is awesome. Multiplayer... this would be my only gripe if I were to state a con. During multiplayer that jump boost is not my thing its impossible to see anyone jump over you or behind you and be able to detect them. Makes the game kind of frustrating at times. Not sure on armor or anything of the sorts yet considering I blew this guy out of his socks point blank with a shotgun and he was the survivor with me getting killed. Little things but no serious gripes. Great game all around and highly recommended!

review_headline: Great quality headset and amazing sound with the correct profile!

I bought the Pulse headset along with the Gold to compare them. They are similar but also very different. The Pulse sends pulses/vibrations which I thought would sound and feel good but were actually not. Also the Pulse headset was lacking in comfort and seemed fragile.

The Gold headsets however does the exact same thing compared to the Pulse with no vibration, greater comfort, better build and a much lesser cost. I bought it when it was $70.

However I do recommend that you download the companion app and upload one of the sound profiles to the headset (note: the headset has to be connected by cable) and select option 2. The default option 1 is highly lacking in depth. I generally always use the Infamous SS sound profile as default because it gives that best sound. Also, select the proper sound profile makes a lot of difference.

I know some people say that the sound in virtual surround is not good. I disagree. The sound is great as long as the correct profile has been selected for option 2 - and there really is surround. It is not as prominent as a good surround sound system, but it is very good given the price and it is of course better than waking up the whole neighborhood.

product_title: PDP Wired Fight Pad for Wii U
review_headline: Great idea for a controller--connects through your Wii Remote Plus
review_body:
The PDP Wired Fight Pad for Wii U is a good controller for Wii U games that need

You have to have a Motion Plus or Remote Plus-type controller--anything that can take a nunchuck. It uses the same connector as the nunchuck does, so if you have one, you know this will work. But since the Wii U doesn't come with a Remote Plus controller, you can't use this with a Wii U out of the box. But if you're playing a game that can use this controller, you probably already have the right controller already.

The description says this is "virtually wireless." I didn't understand the claim until I saw how it connects. You connect your Remote Plus controller to the Wii U, and then you connect this to the Remote Plus controller. The cord on this controller isn't very long, but it won't be a problem unless you want to put the Remote Plus controller on the floor, then you might have a bit of an issue.

The best thing about the tethering design of this controller is that this device doesn't need any batteries, so adding it to your collection of controllers doesn't add any duty to change batteries or keep this device charged.

Game play is good, and the device is comfortable to hold. And the color is bright red, just like the picture.

I have no hesitation recommending this controller.

review_headline: Still my favorite screen protector thus far
review_body:
I got my screen protector from iLLumiShield for my NVIDIA SHIELD tablet and loved it. Perfect fit, easy to install (and I am terrible at these things) installing it without the assist of rubbing alcohol or soap water even. I knocked this down to 4 stars since the actual screen protector is 1.5 millimeters too small from both the top and side. However I had to do my best to place it dead center to make the 1.5 mm gaps less noticeable, thus getting some dust specks under it. Now I was able to remove the dust by wiping down with alcohol, however near impossible to keep any dust off it when trying to place it dead center. Like I said, its a minor complaint, but if the screen would fit perfect I could have negated the issue of the fact I do not have a clean room available to me.

It comes with 3 in the pack so you will have plenty of leeway to do it right, just take your time and do your best to be in the cleanest room you can find. Also I would recommend a compressed air duster to easily remove dust on the screen, as using the cloth can just push it to the indented sides.

Sadness is in every game, someone dies, you're sad, but a feeling of revenge, a feeling of taking what you deserve, a feeling of creating justice, a feeling of Righteous Anger, now that takes quality time and effort to evoke in a person. product_title: Black E-3lue E-Blue Mazer 1600 DPI LED USB Wired Optical Gaming Mouse
review_body:
I do a lot of CAD work and powerpoint work, so I’m always looking for precise mice. The gaming mice are the best as they are sharp and work on almost any type of surfaces. I was looking at the Black E-3lue E-Blue Mazer 1600 because it answers to the challenge making it portable to go to meetings when carrying a laptop.

The feel is good and the 3 top buttons (2 + wheel) are sharp. The only thing I like less (not using « dislike”) are the grooves on the center wheel. It forces to be at a specific position, which might be great on some application, but makes CAD work a bit tedious.

The DPI goes pretty high (2500DPI, 3000FPS), too fast for desk work, but the Black E-3lue E-Blue Mazer 1600 offers lower settings, better suited for desk work. I find this is a very good and useful option.

When powered on, there are two settings, one with and one without blue LED. When the LEDs are on, the mouse looks great and unique, but for my usage, I appreciate the possibility to turn these lights off.

The mouse uses 2 AA batteries. A set of alkaline “Kendal” (brand) were provided with the mouse, but since my usage leads to several months period between battery replacement, I’m planning to use rechargeable Eneloops (LSD cells) when these Kendal runs out. If I was to use for more gaming purpose and would need battery replacement much more often, I would go with higher power rechargeable like Powerex, or maybe Duracell ion-core.

I have been using the mouse for about 3 months now. I would classify it in the “very good mouse I owned” category. I did not have any problem with it, but I’m not putting it to the “gaming test” like other peoples surely do. For my usage, it seems a robust and long lasting mouse (time will tell if I am right).

I’m still trying to evaluate the battery consumption. I have the mouse since 3 months, but I use it only few minutes to few hours per day, only when going to meetings, so the reference is not great, but my first set of batteries is still going strong. The recent release of Borderlands the Pre Sequel shows a change in know-how-locale,i.e Australia,hasn't made for a better game.In fact we have been presented with Glitch-city.I have never run in to a Borderlands game,or any game for that matter, that has had so many glitches.One is bad enough,but I am only about half way through and there are four major faults with this game already.
The first biggie is the fact that they have for the first time made playing with friends the default mode.In games past it has always been the user which has determined whether to connect and play with friends,play solo,or what have you.I prefer solo first,as I always wish to learn a game on my own ,so if I do decide to play with friends,I have somewhat of an idea of how to play without embarrassing myself.
The second one is if you change it to offline(solo) it does NOT remember your selection for the next time you play.That is every game you return to play you have to pick your choice of how to play all over again.C'mon.
Thirdly, as you approach a door to the first boss battle(against Deadlift),it does no open!?? That's right,there is no access or continuance of play beyond that area.The only way to get around it is to play solo(offline) and then it will open.I only found that out by trial and error.
Fourth and finally there is a Vault key symbol in the Titan Robot Production Plant...the only one.You approach it to press\\"e\\" to discover it, but it won't let you.You cannot discover the symbol.So there goes your perfect game,if you,like me,are trying to obtain one.
As I say I am not all the way through yet,so who knows what else I will find.
On the good side the game's controls and handling are pretty much the same from previous versions.And they give you an in game \\"reward\\" if this game detects any other installed version of Borderlands.
All in all a Borderlands all players of the previous versions will appreciate.However the glitches are something that should NOT be in a game like this and in that many numbers.Somebody screwed up royally in the testing department.It is not what we previous Borderlands players and/or newbies to the game should find when shelling out our hard earned bucks. 2 1/2-3 stars.And don't get me started on the guide(see my review on that)!

review_headline: Good Stereo Sound, Easy Set-Up, Questionable Comfort.
review_body:
The headset personally has pretty good stereo sound for the price. Before using it, you must first update your Xbox One controller with the Stereo Headset Adapter attached to it. Once updated, you are good to go. Essentially, you are wireless in the sense that no other wires or connections must be connected to the Xbox One console. All you have to do is just plug in the actual headset into the controller adapter and you get stereo sound and voice chat ready to go. I applaud Microsoft for the easy set-up.

The build quality feels very plastic-y, which might mean that it could be easier to break if you were to say for example, step on it or accidentally sit on it.

The Headset Adapter has 5 buttons: a game sound balance button, a chat sound balance button, a mute button, and the last two are the master volume buttons. It works really great. My only minor complaint is that you cannot check the volume, be it the master volume or game/chat balance, visually. There is only an audio cue that tells you whether you've reach the min/max volume.

Here is where I have to dock it two stars. For me personally, I guess I have a big head because the headset just fit on me way too tight, even extended all the way out. After an hour, I had to take them off and take a break because it was getting rather uncomfortable. My old pair of Turtle Beach X11's (which I have owned since late 2010) I could game with for hours on end and they would never get uncomfortable. That's a major important part of a good headset, besides great sound, it needs to have great comfort as well, and this headset did not offer me comfort, so that is the first star off.

The second star off would be the fact that the microphone does fall short of expectations. It nicely tucks away within the headset which is cool, but either the mic extension is too short for my voice to be picked up properly or the mic sensitivity is much too low or both. Friends have told that they cannot hear me unless I speak considerably louder, which is not so much an option for me since I tend to play late at night. Another downside is that your own voice is not transmitted back to you via the headset which means that you might have a harder time trying to control the strength of your voice since the headset does quite a fine job of isolating the outside noise. I pretty much had to stick a post-it note on the microphone in order for my voice to bounce off the paper and into the mic to be heard properly (no joke, so it probably is the fact that the microphone extension is to short).

Overall, its not too bad of a headset, but these two flaws prevent me from fully enjoying it. review_headline: Good game with a couple caveats...
review_body:
First off, let me start by saying that this is a wonderful game that is very addictive. The worlds are beautifully done, there are no glitches that I have encountered and the enemies are fun to shoot. I have spent many hours playing that game and have stunted my own leveling by spending just as much time exploring as questing.

-There are some spoilers in the following review; If you don't want spoilers then skip to the end for a summary-

That being said, there are a few issues I have with the game. This is an example of a 'safe' MMO. There is no public chat, this was done to keep people from trolling others. The downside is that this makes it very difficult to find others for a fireteam. There is no chat in PvP, once again done to prevent trolling. There is a trend going on here.

The worlds feel somewhat empty. When you are going through the Patrol missions, which allow you to roam the entire world, there are groups of enemies spread out. There will be clumps in certain areas, then an empty run between the two. With the number of players in the worlds, sometimes the enemies will become mined out in prime areas.

Unlike Halo, you don't get to use any futuristic weapons. You get a rocket launcher, shotgun, machine gun, etc. The aliens get lasers and plasma guns, but you are not able to pick them up even temporarily.

-End of Spoilers-

All in all, I do recommend this game. I took away one star for not including any kind of public chat, not populating the worlds with enough enemies, and not allowing anything other than standard weapons.

This game had so much potential. The only reason I'm giving it 3 stars instead of 2 is because there have been some fun moments with friends - so I can't say I don't like it entirely. I'll probably grind my way to level 26 (currently 24) just to see if the Raids have anything new to offer, although for some reason I highly doubt it because even when they opened up "new material" with the Queens Wrath it's just the same stuff with more difficult enemies / bosses.

Pros:
* Fast Halo-esque game play with friends
* Decent Story
* Great graphics
* Sorta MMO - very limited.
* Cool Bosses
* Cool Vehicles - sorta

Cons:
* Repetitive - this game is SOOOOOOOoooo repetitive. There's a hand-full of things to do in this game. Story, Strike, Crucible, Roam all of which are on the same maps. After you complete the story ~level 13-15 if you just burn through it with friends it just becomes a grind with little reward.

* Bosses - Yeah, sure they're cool but good grief how many times do you have to beat them at different difficulty levels? And when you do beat them, even on the more difficult levels the rewards are weak. You don't feel like you got anything done. I know... it's "grinding" but holy hell, make it rewarding to grind. Spending an hour going through a level to get to a boss to get rewarded with junk 95% of the time isn't fun.

* MMO - very limited MMO. The Tower (town) is just a place to turn in quests, bounties and decode engrams... it also pushes the story if you're playing through the story. You can't trade equipment with your team-mates/friends... I get that for the armor - There's specific armor for each class but you should be able to trade weapons, Glimmer (currency), and all the miscellaneous things you pick up with your friends to help them along. Instead, you have to "disassemble" the equipment that's useless to you and get parts for weapons upgrades and such.

* Cut scenes - UGH... how many times do I have to go through the cut-scenes? They're not skippable.

* Loading Screens - There HAS to be a better way. WOW was such a great example of how to do seamless transitions with very few "loading screens" all of which were pretty damn fast from what I recall (it's been a number of years since I've touched that game so my memory may be falsly remembering the time it took to load dungeons and raids).

* Exploration - Sure they have a free-roam mode but there's just not much to free-roam. There's a lot of boundaries and it doesn't feel "free." It's handled similarly to Halo or Battlefield "out of zone" or just simply die because you jumped backwards off a cliff into an abyss. There's tons of "doorways" that are just blacked out as "spawn-points" for enemies. No space exploration - so forget any of those ideas you might have hoped for.

* Vehicles - I have a love hate relationship with these. The Sparrow, and like (ground) vehicles have a very Star Wars speeder feel to them. Pike's are the alien variant with the ability to shoot and dodge. Interceptor's are the heavy ground units. All of which are pretty cool to get around the maps on. My primary gripe is with the spaceships. Absolutely useless as they're all for show. Essentially just used for jumping from planet to planet during the loading screen (see above).

* Rewards - Initially the rewards for your questing felt reasonable. Now however it's just a GRIND. Same enemies, same missions - Go here scout this, kill these, collect these turn in here, get a crappy reward rinse... repeat.

*Ghost - Limited dialogue after you've gone through the missions the first time. Very repetitive... I wish you could just turn him off after you've heard his dialogue more than once.

* Way-points - Who's idea was it to make you hit the "back" button ever couple seconds to see where the hell you're suppose to go. Just make it so you can turn them on or off with a single tap rather than having to tap tap tap to figure out where you're going.

I keep reading "it will get better over time," and these people may be right... it might get better over time as a lot of MMO's do. However, instead of releasing it like it is, they should have developed it further, for at least another year. TONS of potential but, as it stands right now, it's fallen WAY short... not sure I would have spent $60 on it had I known what I know now. There's two expansions scheduled but I don't think it's kept me engaged enough to entice me to purchase them at this point. I hope when they release The Division it doesn't fall short like Destiny has on its release.

Wait for it to go on sale - Grab it at $30.00 and you wont be as disappointed - hopefully by the time it drops in price a lot of the monotony will be fixed with patches and expansions.

review_headline: SCOPA is the only true gem to steal from this adventure!
review_body:
This is my 15th review and completed adventure in the Nancy Drew series.

First, I'd like to start by dividing my review into two factions.
1) The game itself
2) My personal detective work.

* PART 1 *

PLOT: Sent as an undercover agent to one of the best cities in Italy, Nancy gets a chance to crack open a theft ring in which artwork is stolen under direct surveillance left & right! I am not too intrigued with spy-like adventures [more of a horror buff], but I was willing to put aside my biases and tackle this adventure full-on!

INITIAL SCORE: 82

CHARACTERS:

Colin Baxter : An English art restorer that has a self-serving infatuation with Nancy. He is loose in temperament and was the #1 suspect according to my gut feeling. All the while \\"Justin\\" was working at Ca' Nascosta, I wondered when he would break away and start stealing.

Margherita Faubourg : Attempting to frolic among the elite in Venetian social status, this widow casts sarcastic remarks to Nancy the whole time, such as pointed barbs about her limited wardrobe and the ridiculousness of her boyfriends token locket. I didn't have much respect for her, because all she did was tan on her roof, but I did play my part humbly as I was undercover.

Helena Berg : I had an affection for her as one does about an older gal still holding her own in the crux of current society. With her journalism profession, I wanted to learn what information she held and what leads she felt she could offer me about the thief.

Enrico Tazza : I actually liked dealing with this head of an organized crime ring. He forced me to play a card game Scopa [which I loved] and sent me on an interesting mission to collect a sapphire jewel in order to gain trust.

CUMUL SCORE: - 2 = 80

SCORE/GRAPHICS/SOUND EFFECTS:
I actually find the \\"beauty\\" of Venice not that appealing at all. I see a lot of old boats floating along in dirty water with warped, stylized houses that are slowly deteriorating. I don't mean to be cruel, but I didn't exactly get it. I love HERs' authenticity on presenting the city in its' actual state. The voiceovers of Prudence Rutherford and the gondola singers were simply horrible. I understand that this may have been included for comic effect, but it doesn't really work. It sounds as if Mrs. Doubtfire [or someone in drag] was my contact and it threw off the focus of the plot line. They should have hired professionals singers also.

CUMUL SCORE: - 2 = 78

PUZZLES/MINI-GAMES: Scopa, right now, is one of the top two mini-games that HER has ever produced. I love that they included well-informed instructions for one to learn the culture of this iconic game. Right there the game enhances its replay value. The card game were so addicting that it actually overshadowed extreme fallouts to the final two excruciating dilemmas at the end of the story. The water tunnel puzzle was unnecessarily difficult without any reasoning on how one were to solve it. The timed valve puzzle gave the gamer NO room for error and, without a walkthrough, you may have failed 15+ times easily....totally unreasonable. HER should have given the gamer at least three minutes to solve this. The chess notation game wasn't even understood, nor fun. Without a cheat, I daresay it was impossible to discover the answer within a few days. The dancing contest bothered some people, but I actually thought it was okay. Different and unusual to be sure.

CUMUL SCORE: Even = 78

ADVENTURE ENDING: I was correct on the general idea of who the thieves were. Capturing the actual leader was done in literally 10 seconds and that was the highlight of my detective game. I still think there was a lot of loose explanations that never wrapped up the elements of the story for me. I suppose I had to just enjoy the pleasure of the culprits being apprehended. I loved learning the Italian dialogue [I took it one year in college btw] and how this material would benefit the average gamer in constructive education.

CUMUL SCORE: + 2 = 80

* PART 2 *

I try to solve cases without any hints, walkthroughs, etc, even if it were to
take weeks! Well, it took me three days [10 hours] and I gave myself a
Detective Score Of : 63

My Strong Points: I never got held up in frustration at any main part of the adventure and I was quick to finish up the most important tasks of the game by being poignant with my mental machinery. ha, ha

My Weak Points: I did need a lot of clues to help kickstart linear exploits I found myself limited in. I felt I was forced to use the walkthrough because the timed puzzles and confusing navigation of my character bogged me down. I would gladly admit to cheating, because I saved literally five hours of endless circle-running otherwise.

OVERALL GAME SCORE: 80 + 63/ 2 = 71.5 [ B - ]

BOTTOMLINE: This game was actually better than I expected, but I didn't feel I was as engaged as I was supposed to be. I think the characters really bothered me from a bonding standpoint. ha, ha

product_title: Ninja Gaiden II: The Dark Sword of Chaos
review_body: An improvement over the original Ninja Gaiden due to being slightly more manageable and not as luck-based, but still flawed in the extreme difficulty department because seriously, who wants to play a game so challenging more than once a year?  The enemies seem to take a turn for the worse- they seem smaller overall and less interesting to admire with their weaker animations this time around, and of course the music is *nowhere* as legendary as in the original.    However the gameplay and specifically the level design is where the sequel shines much higher than the original.  You go through train levels, waterfall areas, fire-scrolling background stages which are all phenomenal to look at with familiar city street and cave areas as well.  The boss fights are excruciatingly hard just like in the original but often times you feel like there's an element of skill involved while battling them if you're willing to give them a chance.  With some of the bosses in the original Ninja Gaiden you have to tightly grip your controller hoping you're able to take them out before they take YOU out.  The sequel is ever so slightly more forgiving in that regard.    The storyline is this games biggest improvement.  I seriously couldn't understand the story in the first game at all.  Now I can plainly tell it's about a ninja having to stop demons from turning the world into eternal darkness.  Nothing flashy and certainly nothing I haven't heard a million times already in plenty of other video games, but I suppose the Ninja Gaiden series was one of the first to utilize cutscenes in between completed levels which is an idea that is WAY too common nowadays (a negative influence).  Still, an influence is an influence and such a concept supposedly began with the Ninja Gaiden series so I have to give the game props for that.    I do unfortunately have to stand by the high difficulty being the main reason I never feel like playing the Ninja Gaiden series, so I believe it's highly recommended if you're interested in old school NES games to seek elsewhere such as the Mega Man, Mario, Zelda, Metroid and Punch Out series which are all certainly beatable.  There's no guarantees you'll beat this game.  Then if you wish to progress down harder territory check out Castlevania and Ninja Gaiden.  Overall not a bad game at all and the levels are quite fun.  Just a ninja with a sword, fast-paced action like in the original and a pretty fun time.

review_headline: The Game I've Been Waiting For!
review_body: Update (10/3/14): My original review was about five hours into the game. I've now played close to 20 hours. There are several things that have come up that I wanted to share.       1) I love how different cars handle on different surfaces. I was driving an upgraded Audi TT and that thing was so difficult to drive off-road, hated any races that required me to leave the street! I then    bought a Lancia Stratos (have loved this car since Forza Motorsport 4). The Stratos is AMAZING off-road. This thing is an absolute blast! Every moment I can, I take detours through the forests. Most cars are pretty easy to handle on the road, but I love that once you take a shortcut, you better hope your car was made for it!    2) The bucket lists are pretty fun, not amazing. Every now and then you'll do one that puts a huge smile on your face. I recently did the one with the Lancia Delta (pretty sure it was the Delta), where it was night time and you had to cut through a forest to get to a checkpoint in time. This race was pretty difficult, took me a few tries, but WOW was it intense and exciting! There have been a couple of bucket lists like that, so I'm glad they're in the game.    3) I really like the physics in this game. Of course its not a full on sim like FM5, but it sure is close when you use a wheel with sim steering. I'm glad that they added a small arcade feel to it, keeps the game fun and exciting, instead of having to use X to rewind every time you came into a turn slightly fast and messed up your lap time by a second or push the gas a little too hard causing a spin out.    4) Slow credits. That's one of the painful things about this game. Its taking me a really long time to save up credits to buy some of the more expensive cars. The most expensive one I have right now is the SLS, and that's because I won it in a lottery spin. I like that I have to work for some cars I want, but at the same time it seems a little too slow. Maybe its because I've only got a green wristband right now? Once Turn 10 figure out their server issues, the Tier rewards will help out a lot, which should make everything ok.    5) The last thing that I noticed and am not a huge fan of is that every time I start up the game I start at a car meet. This is annoying when the car meet is pretty far away from where I left the game which was right next to the hub with races to join.    That's all for now. I plan on playing a lot more over the weekend, will update next week if there's more to share!    Original:  Forza Horizon 2 is the game I've been waiting a very long time for! After having played Test Drive Unlimited for countless hours, I didn't think anything would come close to the happiness it brought me. When the original Forza Horizon was announced, I got excited, thinking that a racing game was finally coming along to take TDU's place as my all time favorite open world racer. While Forza Horizon was an awesome game, it still fell short in a lot of areas. The fact that it wasn't really open world, you couldn't drive very far off any roads, made it not fulfill what I was hoping for.    Forza Horizon 2 is exactly what I've been waiting many years for. There's finally a game that's topped what TDU did for me. While the map may not be as big as TDU, the graphics, car list, sounds, car tuning, etc., more than make up for it. When I first started up the game I couldn't believe how good it looked, driving those super-cars along the coast was jaw dropping! I picked the Camaro as my first car (love some good ol' American muscle), started driving to the first destination, saw a field to my left, and decided to take a detour. I don't remember the last time I had so much fun in a racing game! Driving through fields, vineyards, dodging trees, it all just left a huge smile on my face. I ended up completely forgetting about my destination and spent a good 30 minutes just driving around and loving every minute of it.    I use a Thrustmaster TX with a Playseat Challenge, thewheel feels great with this game once some adjustments are made. Sim steering on, force feedback bumped up a little, and my degrees of rotation taken down a bit. Its such a blast! I know that this game is going to bring countless hours of fun, even without doing any of the races/events. I can't wait to build up my garage with some iconic cars and drive the crap out of them! Would highly recommend this game to anyone who loves cars! Can't wait to get home and continue playing, thanks Turn 10!
