Since I was so surprisingly engrossed in Killzone Mercenary, I decided to pick up the Killzone Trilogy. If this was a novel series, you'd want to start your consumption from the beginning of the series. But video games, unlike movies, improve dramatically over time, so you want to start in the inverse order with Killzone 3 first.

Basically, the game is setup to have an arena of play, followed by a cut-scene, and followed by another arena. The mode of play most of the time is FPS, but occasionally, you get a rail shooter. To mix things up, on occasion you get to pilot a jetpack (though incompetently), and a mech. These are a lot of fun, albeit they tend to break up the flow since they have completely different mechanics.

The story told in the cut scenes is entertaining enough, though not high art. The ending sucks, but seems in character for what's been going on in the series: the characters continually argue and bicker with each other while the protagonist hothead runs off and does something randomly crazy. It makes for a fun game, but a cliched story.

In any case, the game's got a few things that makes it fun even for a terrible FPS player like me:

Plenty of NPC allies. You're almost never alone, and there's always fire support and if you don't rush off in front of your allies, someone will revive you even if you're killed. This is huge! It cuts down on the frustrations a lot, and you're never stuck for long.
Plenty of variety in game play, and multiple paths to victory. In particular, even the stealth section is forgiving. You don't just die because you didn't stealth right. You get a chance to pick up an enemy's weapon and just blast your way through. Again, not frustrating.
Lots of eye candy. The environments change a lot, and it's very different each time.
Plenty of ammo reload locations. I think I ran out of ammo once. And you can always pick up the enemy's weapons.
In other words, the game's perfect for a beginner, and the game's not so long that you get bored or sick of the game play. I ended the game wanting more, which is always a good sign. The ending was a bit anti-climatic, but maybe it's just an invitation to start over with the Playstation Move controller.

I played the game in 3D for a bit, and it's OK, but didn't add enough to the experience for me to want to put on those 3D glasses in addition to my normal glasses.

All in all, the game's entertaining, and worth a play, even if you suck at FPS. Recommended.

review_headline: Time to pin our hopes on The Sims 5
review_body:
The rumor is that The Sims 4 began life as a multiplayer online game a la Second Life, and it appears to be true going by the released game. We haven't had such small neighborhoods since the original Sims and the non-young adult age groups feel like an afterthought. Some of the new tools included in build mode and create-a-sim are impressive, but they quickly feel limited with the lack of create-a-style or even a color wheel, and absurd limits on the number of buildable levels. These limitations make sense when you think of the Sims 4 as an online game, where only a small area can be loaded at once, too many levels wouldn't work for the weakest of computers, and create-a-style would slow everything to a crawl as the computer would have had to download dozens of textures. Still, the Sims 4 is reasonably fun to play for a little while, though it doesn't feel like a firm base for 5+ years of expansion packs.

The Good:

The overall look of the sims is much improved over previous versions. The neighborhoods are beautiful, if frustratingly inaccessible.

New tools in build mode.

The ability to search through the game catalog is a great improvement over the cumbersome collections of Sims 2 and 3.

The Bad:

Loading screens everywhere you look. They're quick at the moment, but I doubt they'll stay that way as expansion and stuff packs are piled on.

You are required to run Origin in the background while the game is running. You don't need to be online, but it has to be open.

No pools, no toddler life stage, and infants are little more than the objects they were in the original Sims game.

The Irritating:

Careers are ridiculous rather than reality-based, and on top of that they've regressed to Sims 1 and 2 style friend-requirements for promotions. Add in that there's no aspiration reward to prevent relationship decay and you may find that you spend a lot of time meeting little goals instead of enjoying the sand box.

Neighbors like to wander into your sim's house without being invited and try to use the bathroom while your sim is showering. Then they're all stuck in such a state of embarrassment that it's difficult to make them do anything useful until it passes.

Sims can no longer eat the fruit they pick from wild plants.

Overall as someone who's played the Sims series for years, the Sims 4 is not what I had hoped it would be. The two largest draws for the Sims 3, the open neighborhood and create-a-style, are noticeably absent. Graphics are much improved, but that much is to be expected with a reboot. Gameplay is smooth, but it would have to be given how little the engine seems to be doing. I'd say that all the Sims 4 needed to make it a great game was another year or so of development so that they could have at least included the missing toddlers, fixed up the babies, made the worlds five times as large as they are, and included pools, which have been in the game since the beginning, but ultimately the problem with the Sims 4 is that they tried to use as much of the original online-only game as they could, and with such a lousy foundation the game is already locked into a style that seems very contrary to the spirit of past Sims games.

review_headline: Enemy Zero is far from being a Zero in my books, It's a great game!
review_body: Enemy Zero might not be everybody's cup 'O' tea but not everybody liked The Beatles, but did that make them less awesome? I think not! EZ for the Sega Saturn is a stealth-survival-horror game and sequel to 'D', both starring the character Laura ( not Laura Croft ) voiced by the singer Jill Cunniff of the band Luscious Jackson. I did a review of 'D' already so I won't talk much on that game. ( It's very creepy ) You play Laura Lewis, who after being wakened from her cryogenic slumber by an explosion on the the massive AKI space craft she's a crew member of, must find who or what's attacking them. ( whew, that's a mouthful! ) Enemy Zero's game-play goes between interactive FMV ( point & click ) and a first person shooter. The unique thing about EZ is the enemy's invisible! ( oooooh ) In this game stealth is your friend, and avoiding the invisible monster is the best way to survive. Again, not everybody's cup of tea, but it makes for a creepy good time. Your weapon is an electro-charger gun that takes a few seconds to charge up, and you have a earring shaped guidance system witch gives her aural warnings. You walk the corridor's searching for surviving crew members, fighting invisible monster's, solving many puzzles, and ultimately escaping the AKI. ( the big ship, pay attention! ) This game was also in the Guinness Book of World Records as the most expensive and exclusive video game ever. It cost over 20,000 yen ( $2,500 ) to have one of twenty hand delivered by Kenji Eno himself! ( wow ) There was also a very popular soundtrack performed by Michael Nyman & Sara Leonard. But you ask, \\" what does this all mean? \\" Well I'll tell you young Skywalker, it means if you're going to play a creepy survival game, the music better be damned great or it will fall flat on it's face. EZ is one of the best ( in my books ) survival type games out there. It's truly an original and very scary game! The first time I played it, and I heard the monster coming towards me I almost totally lost it. I was walking around one of the storage area's and I heard that ...beep.......beep.......beep... coming at me faster and faster; I was running into walls and blocked corridors, then I died, and the beast's scream you won't soon forget. I forgot you have to charge up your gun first, and if you charge it up to soon it shuts off, thus death happens! ( get used to it! )  The graphics are great for the day, and it moves along quite nicely. The voice acting is cheesy as can be, but I love cheesy voice acting. And yes, it does at times move very slow, but any good survival game should. The critics of the day poo-pooed it, but I normally like what the powers that be hate. Enemy Zero for the Sega Saturn is a first rate game that should be enjoyed with the headphones on, and in the dark. product_title: Call of Duty: Black Ops II - PlayStation 3
review_body: Excellente

\\"A fantasy you have when you are creating an experience is that someone else is going to enjoy it.\\" - Jason Jones, Co-Founder of Bungie, Pathways Out of Darkness ViDoc

Fantasy indeed. This was the most disappointing and boringly repetitive game I have ever played.

Story and character background lore are virtually non-existent and almost entirely provided by pop-ups to read the Grimoire Card descriptions (digital trading cards that are unlocked by progressing in the game) that must be accessed out-of-game via the developer's website bungie.net or the Destiny Companion iPhone app. The very little story that is included in-game is either delivered via voice-over dialogue by an uninspired and seemingly bored Peter Dinklage (Tyrion Lannister from Game of Thrones TV series) as your companion Ghost (advisor/helper companion bot), or a few brief in-game cut-scene cinematics (which total around 30 minutes and are all unskippable) via Bill Nighy (Viktor from Underworld and Davy Jones from Pirates of the Caribbean films) as the mysterious speaker for the Traveler who outright refuses to elaborate further on the story via actual in-game dialogue, Lauren Cohan (Maggie Greene from The Walking Dead TV series) as the mysterious Exo Stranger (exoskeleton cyborg) who also disgustingly says she has no time to explain anything and rather than interact with you on Story missions only alludes to further adventures via paid DLC, or Kirsten Potter (Natsuhi from Naruto and Ran'Tao from Bleach TV series) and Brandon O'Neill (Dom Estacado from The Hit List film) as the ruling Awoken (vampire/dark elf-like humans with ambiguous allegiance to the Darkness) of the Reef (asteroid belt/debris field) who also allude to further adventures via paid DLC. See a pattern here? The infamous Mass Effect 3 ending, even with the deus ex machina ghost child and 3 color explosion choices, was a 100 times better ending than the Destiny ending, and more memorable and complete. I might add that Destiny had a much larger budget at 500 million dollars than Mass Effect 3's estimated budget at 200 million dollars, so it doesn't make any sense to me that more story, character dialogue, and cut-scene cinematics didn't make it into the final released game. Bungie also didn't have to worry about tying up subplots from thousands of character choice variations, just provide a satisfying explanation and resolution for the story, which they failed to do. Having completed the game, I still don't know what the Traveler or Darkness are, among many other basic story elements, and am confused what my actions by completing the Story missions did to advance or resolve the conflict. It is fairly alarming that Joseph Staten, longtime Bungie veteran and writer and design director for Destiny, left Bungie on September 24, 2013, to pursue new creative challenges. I hope this wasn't because Bungie and/or Activision (publisher of Destiny) chose to include so little of his story in the actual game via character dialogue or cut-scene cinematics. So much for his assistance on story expansion DLC or sequel continuity.

\\"Your choice of the character class and the character race will condition the way that character is going to evolve over time.\\" - Patrick O'Kelley, Executive Producer on Destiny, Out Here in the Wild ViDoc

The player character creation options are a complete joke with no body type choices and very little variety to face, hair, tattoo/marking and color choices (which are covered by a generic helmet 99.9% of the game anyway, regardless of player character class). Why Bungie chose to include such a bare bones character creation tool yet couldn't improve on the usability and variety provided by game series like Mass Effect and Elder Scrolls is beyond me. It is dismal and they should have just given everyone standard models. It's not like the game provides you the option to role-play anyway, especially with gear choices necessary for level 20+ content. After completing the game with all 3 character classes (Hunter, Warlock, and Titan) to level 20+ (which took about 14 hours each for the Story missions and Strikes and another 6 hours each for Patrol missions, Bounties, and Crucible matches to level grind), I didn't see any of the amazing costumes and customizations featured in Bungie concept art, videos, or interviews that got me so excited for the game and to try and acquire all of the weapons, armor, and equipment for my favorite designs. All the 4 primary weapon classes (Hand Cannons, Auto Rifles, Scout Rifles, and Pulse Rifles), 3 special weapon classes (Sniper Rifles, Shotguns, and Fusion Rifles), 2 heavy weapon classes (Machine Guns and Rocket Launchers) and armor each look pretty similar and generic other than increased statistics per level and upgrades on rare (blue), legendary (purple) and exotic (gold) weapons and armor. Legendary weapons and armor basically have custom paint jobs per faction you can join only after level 20, much better stats, and more upgrade options. Only exotic weapons and armor truly look unique (and a few of the exotic weapons have received numerous complaints as being very underpowered). Bungie provided very little option for players to uniquely equip their characters for personal aesthetic appeal and there are no unique player character paths to speak of for any of the 3 player classes or species, other than subclass abilities per player character class that all players will eventually unlock in Bungie's rigid pre-determined order. No option to pick up and use enemy weapons and ammo as has been Bungie's custom in prior Halo games. No option to accent your player character with enemy armor pieces picked up from the battlefield for a unique look and personality. No unique weapons, armor, or ability combinations for the 3 player character species, only gear and abilities locked to the 3 player character classes. Awoken Hunters look the same as Exo Hunters in their armor and very similar to Titans and Warlocks, which are all basically slight variations of Master Chief (a very bland change in direction from the early concept art). Not surprisingly, there is zero customization for your vehicles or ships. You choice of character player species has absolutely zero effect on the way that character is going to evolve over time.

Bungie didn't even bother to properly introduce or provide in-game background for the game's 3 player species (Human, Awoken, and Exo, which all absurdly have the same intro cinematics and super abilities), 4 enemy species (Fallen, Hive, Vex, and Cabal), or player or enemy factions such as Vanguard, Dead Orbit, Future War Cult, New Monarchy, or Queen's Wrath. Nor did Bungie provide an explanation why you could not align with and join a player faction and contribute reputation points to it to increase rank necessary to acquire faction-specific gear from the first time you visit the Tower social hub where they are based and are able to interact with them. Bungie should have allowed players to join factions and work toward acquiring faction-specific gear with unique faction-specific missions prior to the arbitrary level 20. None of the faction representative or vendors are given introductions or unique personalities. Bungie might as well have just done away with them and included thumbnail images in the menus. Vendors never seem to cycle new or significantly better items despite the countdown timers. None of the enemy bosses are given introductions or unique personalities either. They are simply larger versions of existing enemies with better weapons and 10,000 times the health and shields (bullet sponges without any unique battle strategy or variety) and you will encounter them repeatedly on your grind for better gear. Even Borderlands and Red Dead Redemption, among many other games, managed to have memorable bosses. Yeah, you were likely to get mostly junk loot by beating bosses in Borderlands, but at least the battles were unique and entertaining, there was the excitement of seeing lots of loot, and it genuinely felt like you were regularly rewarded. How could Bungie not improve on this? It is even more important to have unique and memorable characters and AI behavior variety if you will encounter them repeatedly, and oftentimes against your will or better judgment. How cool would it have been for the Fallen Walker spider tank mini-boss to actually move around and jump toward the players causing the most damage to it rather than just sit there firing its weapons.

The Fallen Vandals reminded me of General Grievous from Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith. The Sparrow vehicle reminded me of the speeder bikes from Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi. Most of the ships wouldn't feel out of place in the Star Wars or Mass Effect universes. I might add that you can't use the Sparrows or ships in any meaningful way other than faster ground transport or something unique to look at during the very long loading screens before each Story mission, Patrol, Strike, or Raid. No epic space battles or exploration for your ships. No races, chases, or massive ground vehicle battles for your Sparrows that would have gone a long way to providing some gameplay variety. Your Ghost is basically Halo's 343 Guilty Spark possessed by a male version of Cortana, and fulfilling a similar role. None of the game's environments, characters, or weapons would have been out of place in Bungie's previous Halo series, which to me is very sad as I had high hopes that Destiny would be a clean break from their prior Halo series and achieve its own unique look and feel. Bungie complained about being relegated to infinite Halo sequels under Microsoft, but once they got their freedom, they just fell back to the familiar Halo elements. It's a real shame as all of the early concept art, videos, and interviews looked truly amazing and even the watered down elements that ended up in the final game still ooze untapped potential. The dynamic skyboxes by Mark Goldsworthy and his sky art team are truly exceptional and beautiful to look at. Geometry, textures, and particle effects on PlayStation 4 looked disappointingly very similar to Halo 4 on Xbox360, with a slight improvement to the lighting model and material shaders. This game definitely looks cross-gen with marginal improvements to the previous generation console counterparts. You will be fine playing this on Xbox360 or PlayStation 3 and not missing much at all on the so-called next-gen Xbox One or PlayStation 4. Marcus Lehto, longtime Bungie veteran and creative art director for Destiny, suddenly and inexplicably left Bungie on October 4, 2012.

The music is excellent and in line with Martin O'Donnell's (longtime Bungie veteran and Destiny's co-composer) prior work on Halo. However, I was expecting something different to radically set the tone apart from the Halo series. Sound effects are also in line with the Halo series. Both failed to give Destiny a unique iconic sound that sets it apart from other similar space-based fantasy games. I might add that Bungie's board of directors terminated Martin O'Donnell without cause on April 11, 2014 prior to the games release. So much for his assistance on story expansion DLC or sequel music score continuity. So we have the lead writer, artist, and sound guy all leaving Bungie before their new franchise is launched. It's never a good sign for a company when veterans are dropping like flies.

While the gunplay is great and will be very familiar to Halo series fans with primary, special, and heavy weapon slots, in my experience, the 3 character classes - Hunter (sniper/rogue), Warlock (mage), and Titan (tank/warrior) play almost identically other than their super abilities, which must be leveled up via separate skill trees and are only very rarely available to use. There are absurdly and inexplicably no unique super abilities for each of the player character species. Bungie provided no explanation on why alternate subclass skill trees are only available to characters once they reach level 15 and they really should have been explained and made available from the character creation stage or at least once you visit the Tower for the first time. Players may find that the alternate subclass skill trees unlocked only after level 15 enable better abilities more suited to their play-style than the default tree and they will have to start from level zero in the alternate tree, unlocking jump, grenade, super, and other class enhancements all over again in Bungie's rigidly set order while encountering much higher level enemies. I think it was a mistake not to make it a single tree with various branches in solar, arc, and void elemental tree branches (with branches and abilities unique to each player character class and species combination) and allow the player to freely choose which ability upgrades they want to unlock and when, similar to the freedom provided by the Mass Effect, Elder Scrolls or Borderlands series.

In fact, unless Bungie fixes a very broken world economy and progression system that are essentially color coded slot machine tokens and arbitrary armor light stat increases after level 20, you will need to create and level up all 3 character classes to use high level gear locked to a specific character class (usually other than the one you like and were likely playing as when you received it). A power gamer's wet dream (and not in a good way), you will often use weapons and armor for their better stats rather than because you like how they look and feel and the abilities they modify that you actually use. For example, you will often use rare, legendary, or exotic weapons based purely on their rarity, peak damage and elemental damage modifiers, rather than the ones you spent hours grinding to upgrade and that better fit your preferred play-style. You will always use armor with the highest light stats (if you want to exceed the soft level 20 cap and complete the end-game level 20+ Strikes and level 26+ Raids), regardless of how ridiculous or ugly it looks or if it matches the rest of your set. You may even end up developing and using a character class you don't particularly like just because you decoded some legendary or exotic gear locked to that specific character class. You will be asked to use a specific character class with specific subclass tree leveled abilities and gear to participate in the higher level Strikes and Raids. You are out of luck if the character you like and have developed is not needed or your fireteam (group of players) repeatedly hard wipes (all players die and your fireteam has to reset at the last checkpoint) because you played anyway despite not having the character build needed to fill a specific role or gear specialized for the Raid. For Strikes and Raids, you are mostly restricted to private instances (copies) of zones only you playing solo or your fireteam may access. I think Bungie should have only restricted these private instanced zones to mini-bosses or final boss battles as it breaks the social gameplay.

There are so many different in-game currencies, even Bungie got confused and included upgrade material requirements for a Future War Cult faction Hunter armor that weren't even available for the Hunter character class (patched in Update 1.0.1.4). After nearly a hundred hours of grinding, none of my 3 character classes ended up meeting the level 26 light requirement for Raids and I only had 3 legendary engrams (purple) successfully convert to legendary gear (always for other character classes than the ones currently being played and ironically the day after I put my game copy up for sale). Almost all of my legendary engrams converted to major downgrades to unusable uncommon (green) and rare (blue) kit or upgrade materials I was unlikely to use without exotic (gold) gear, if ever. Bungie should have locked all engram decodes to their rarity level or higher and for the character class you are playing when used. Even better, they should have locked the engram decodes to the gear you use the most and are likely to upgrade and/or have the best statistical efficiency with as far as total kills and precision kills. Best case scenario is for Bungie to just allow players to trade whatever engrams they have for the same or better rarity type weapons, armor, equipment, or shaders based on their Cryptarch's level (similar how Bungie allowed players to choose weapons, armor, vehicle, and ship type throughout the Story missions). The higher the Cryptarch level, the more options unlocked and possibility for higher rarity level gear choices. This would go a long way in reducing the randomness and unreliability of engram drops and allow players to have better control of crafting their own Guardians according to their own unique aesthetic tastes and play-style. Some of the materials required for upgrades to legendary and exotic gear (such as ascendant shards and ascendant energy) are almost impossible to acquire without grinding for days. Bungie should have provided a better means of acquiring or exchanging for the specific upgrade materials you need without the need for endless grinding.

Players are not guaranteed good rewards for completing difficult missions, defeating high level enemies, or performing well on missions or Crucible matches with more kills, precisions kills, assists, teammate revivals, kill/death ratio, or some other notable feat similar to Goldeneye 007. Many players have resorted to loot farming by either following looped routes for loot chest spawn points or camping enemy group spawn points rather than completing difficult missions or performing well in Crucible matches as Bungie probably intended, since abusing spawn point exploits are essentially an easier and more consistent source of purple slot machine tokens for better light stat gear and you could grind for weeks at Strikes with no meaningful improvement. Bungie, in their never-ending crusade to control and micro manage players, even nerfed the respawn timers for all of the popular enemy group spawn points in a recent patch (Update 1.0.1.5), naming the most popular location the \\"Treasure Cave\\", and removing the ability of frustrated players to use them as a source for legendary engrams to get their characters better gear in order to reach the required level 26+ for Raids. In the same patch, Bungie also reduced the drop rate of engrams following a hard wipe and removed the possibility of acquiring ascendant material by dismantling Queen's Wrath gear, making it even more difficult to acquire coveted legendary engrams or rare upgrade materials. Again, so much for the models Mass Effect and Elder Scrolls had already established that Bungie could easily have emulated and improved. So much wasted from the lessons Blizzard already learned on broken loot and reward systems in Diablo III Loot 2.0. The fact that players are willing to fire into a popular monster cave for hours (an activity even less fun, more boring and repetitive than the horde mode grind of the actual game) in the hopes of legendary engram drops that will likely convert to rare pulse rifles or uncommon helmets 5 levels below them speaks volumes to the failure of the game's design. You will basically hit a brick wall at level 20 in an endless grind for totally unreliable and random gear with slight light stat increases. So much for Bungie's promise of the game opening up after level 20. Bungie should have either provided a better way to increase the light stat (perhaps with rare or better weapons or some light orb collection/loss mechanic) or provided an alternative path to increasing your level past the soft level 20 cap (perhaps by leveling up arc, solar, or void abilities or an alternative darkness stat and darkness abilities similar to a paragon/renegade system). Even the Stranger's Pulse Rifle (a character Bungie didn't bother to develop or create player empathy for through Story missions, scripted interaction, or cinematics, so her weapon has almost no sentimental value) that you are rewarded for completing all of the Story missions is just a rare (blue) and you are likely to have much better weapons by that time anyways. If any weapon deserved to be at least a legendary (purple) or exotic (gold), the Stranger's Pulse Rifle deserved this. Bungie needs to go back to the drawing board and redo the entire game economy, loot reward system, and character progression options.

\\"You can go from Earth to Venus to Mars to the Moon to Saturn\\" -Ryan Ellis, Technical Art Director on Destiny, Out Here in the Wild ViDoc

The game's PvE mode (player versus environment, but some would say player versus engram) where players can solo or join a fireteam for cooperative missions includes dismal content with just 4 very linear areas on 4 worlds to explore and complete extremely repetitive horde mode missions. No Saturn. The main areas are all contained by invisible walls and kill volumes, so exploring off the beaten path is strongly discouraged by Bungie, unless you are adept at glitching into locked off areas. There are inexplicably currently no missions on the Reef other than 2 brief cut-scene cinematics, even though concept art, videos, and interviews released by Bungie contain footage of player characters in a playable Reef environment.

\\"The number one priority was to make a world that people wanted to be in. Something that you want to go back to and you want to explore and to have enough variety where you never get bored.\\" - Christopher Barrett, Art Director on Destiny, Out Here in the Wild ViDoc

The games missions are very repetitive and boring - almost all of which are poor excuses to spawn waves of the games monsters to defend against and kill. Go to location \\"A\\" to analyze location/device/door to trigger a horde mode event. Go to location \\"B\\" to kill a specific monster to trigger a horde mode event. Go to location \\"C\\" to clear the area of a set number of monsters to trigger a horde mode event. Go to location \\"D\\" to defend location/device/door to trigger a horde mode event. Go to location \\"E\\" to collect a set number of items to trigger a horde mode event. It is horde mode to infinity. Sadly, almost all of the game's Story missions, Patrol missions, Bounties, Strikes, Raids, and public events seem to be based on subtle variations of this same formula. Higher level Strikes and Raids just mean repeating the same horde modes with higher level enemies with more health and shields, all spawning at the exact same places in the exact same order, and watching the same boring, nonsensical, unskippalbe cut-scene cinematics over and over.

Further, very few players actually use a headset to communicate and this becomes critical on the higher difficulty Strikes and Raids. There are very few options to communicate with character body language (pointing, bowing, sitting, dancing, shooting or meleeing a teammate to get or direct their attention) and the social experience is extremely lackluster with the Tower, which was intended as a social hub, serving more as a place to access and store valuable gear for safekeeping in your vault, buy gear at loot shops, materials exchange for glimmer, or suicide platform for those players diving to their deaths after having their 25th legendary engram convert to one more piece of unusable rare or uncommon gear. There is currently no way to voice communicate with other players in your area. Why Bungie chose not to include any gameplay variety (other than the level 26+ Raids that most players will likely give up on trying to unlock) is totally baffling. No 6 person fireteams to practice communication, strategy, and roles to practice for level 26+ locked Raids. No puzzles. No platforming precision. No characters to interact with and aid during mission gameplay or whowill aid you. No rescue or infiltration missions. No missions to unlock and deploy risky tech. No scenarios uniquely designed to showcase each character class' super abilities. No incentive to discover hidden areas or explore all areas of the maps for unique enemies or loot, other than the static 5 gold loot chests per world, dead Ghosts, and loot chest spawn points. No incentive to help mentor lower level players. No unique or surprising enemy AI behavior like distracting, flanking, retreating, ambushes, random rushes, or calls for dropship or monster cave reinforcements. No random appearances by other alien enemy species. No panic waves with unique dropships, enemy species, or enemy AI behavior. No trading or gifting loot with friends if duplicates, locked to another player character class, gear you don't like and will never use, or gear friends would love to have. The Story campaign, Patrol missions, and Strikes are a design abomination. Even the Assassin's Creed series, which got blasted for repetitive gameplay, included more diversity and variety. If Bungie just implemented random number generated enemy group spawns as like loot drops, at least the fixation on horde mode would have been more interesting and exciting and the same areas you visit endlessly would require a unique strategy each time. Throw in a chance for random mini-boss spawns near enemy group spawn points and alternate enemy species surprise replacement/appearances to spice things up.

The game's Crucible PvP mode (player versus player) where players solo or are randomly assigned to teams for competitive multiplayer matches is also dismal with just 11 multiplayer maps and 7 game modes (I've only unlocked and ever seen 5) and Bungie seemingly enables and disables them at their whim. There are no match customization options, Halo Forge mode-like modification tools, or friend lobbies/private matches. Also, player's weapon stats are supposedly normalized, but all upgrades on rare, legendary, and exotic gear and maxed skill tree abilities seem to work perfectly fine in providing an advantage. The matchmaking often pairs you with teams/groups that are grossly underpowered or overpowered. Many players dropout from matches as soon as they think they may lose if it interferes with their Crucible Mark grind or Bounty progress, or are AFK (away from keyboard/controller) in the hopes of collecting the best loot in last place. I often watched in dismay as players that did not contribute at all or performed poorly in Crucible matches were rewarded with legendary engrams or exotic weapons and armor while the best contributors and performers received nothing. Bungie needs to discourage players from actively dropping from matches by their choice or repeatedly due network problems with meaningful penalties. It's not fair to the rest of their team or other players. Players that are AFK or not contributing should be dropped from matches automatically. Players that contribute more kills, precisions kills, assists, teammate revivals, have the best kill/death ratio, or some other notable feat should be guaranteed rewards. Bungie should segregate high level players or players with high kill/death ratios into separate tiers/matches. It would be nice to have some other multiplayer game mode types like capture the flag and escort. Bungie has a long way to go to improving the matchmaking and competitive multiplayer variety. No doubt future maps and modes will come via paid DLC.

Bungie has promised to address many of these issues in the future. Bungie fixed that engrams will always decode into items at or above the rarity quality of the engram (in Update 1.0.2), but not locked to the character class in use and without regard to duplicates. For example, legendary engrams will always decrypt to legendary gear or upgrade materials; rare engrams will always decrypt to rare gear or upgrade materials with a greater chance of decrypting to legendary gear or upgrade materials. But for me, this is too little too late with slim to none chance of fixing the lack of story problem and incomplete nature of the game. While updates for client/server stability and security are to be expected, for every step Bungie thinks they are taking forward, they take two steps back. Resetting every enemy group spawn timer in the game to prevent spawn point camping? Why not provide better, more frequent, and reliable rewards for completing difficult Strikes and Raids or performing well in the Crucible? Why not empower players to choose their own weapons, armor and equipment when turning in engrams? Nerfing perfectly good exotic weapons to oblivion that are supposed to feel overpowered because of a few PvP complaints? Why not buff other underpowered exotic weapons and make them more accessible or lock legendary and exotic weapons if unbalanced in PvP solely to the Iron Banner? Nerfing Auto Rifles and buffing Scout Rifles so players aren't fixated on one weapon type? Why not unlock all weapons to any player level without minimum level requirements so players can have more options to experiment with other weapon types throughout the game rather than being forced to power game by the numbers? If everyone wants to use Autorifles and Shotguns, why force their hands? Let them play how they want to play. Adding kill volumes to sniper platforms? Why not let players use the same playground provided to their enemies with whatever clever strategy they wish? Adding \\"baby bumpers\\" for Aethon? Why not fix and improve his AI script? Almost all of Bungie's focus on game improvements seem to be obsessive compulsive petty micro management changes to force players to play the way Bungie intended rather than fixing more severe gameplay variety and content problems. Bungie are clearly prioritizing limitations on player strategy and asserting control over player choice rather than providing more freedom and variety to players to choose their own destiny. You have to wonder if Bungie are fans of Harbinger in the Mass Effect series as they seem to have truly taken \\"assuming direct control\\" to heart.

The universe that Bungie has created seems genuinely interesting and, even if derivative, makes you want to discover more, but only if you are willing to endlessly grind extremely repetitive horde mode missions for color coded slot machine tokens in the vain hope they decrypt into the game's best weapons, armor, and equipment for your character class and play-style, and only if you are willing to pay for missing variety and content as future DLC. I'll pass. The game is not what Bungie promised to deliver and feels like a significant amount of content was cut to be resold as DLC. I sold my copy within 2 weeks and may come back for a used super-duper deluxe edition once Bungie completes the game and fixes the progression, loot, and reward systems.

TL/DR:

The solo/cooperative campaign has little to no in-game story and is basically a galactic genocide simulator based on 5 variations of horde mode repeated to infinity. It has an abysmal ending, forgettable characters, environments and sound, a broken loot system, a laughable reward system, and a broken character progression system with a tedious required grind after level 20 solely for light stat increases, which will require you to continue grinding said horde mode formula and/or via a bare bones competitive multiplayer for completely random and unreliable loot.

If you are ok with the above and insist on getting a copy of the game in its current broken and unfinished state, I'd recommend you either rent, borrow from a friend, or pick up a used copy. Xbox360 and PlayStation 3 are perfectly fine. You won't be missing anything passing on next-gen versions. Or you could just save your money and thank me later.

Amazing game and value. I would have paid the full $60 but i'm happy not to. The main game and expansion are both tons of fun both alone and when played with a friend. Couch co-op is where this game shines, I miss the days of friends sitting around a room playing games together. Online can be fun but its just not the same. This game has a lot of replay value with the different characters. The console updates included with Reaper of Souls have been great so far with adding new content and balancing existing. The story is a little weak but not enough to warrant less of a rating. This is definitely on my best of the year list.

review_headline: One step forward, three steps back
review_body:
Let me start that I admire EA for making the characters deeper. For a life simulator, deeper characters are definitely a plus. EA has emphasized this, and it's definitely delivers as a proof-of-concept. This, along with the graphical overhaul deserves two stars.

However, this game feels like it regressed in many other ways. I won't go into the lack of toddlers and pools, that's been beaten to death. What people aren't talking about as much are:

1. Create-a-sim has been nerfed. You only have around 5 patterns or colors per furniture/piece of clothing
- No more thousands of combinations of patterns to customize clothing
- You don't have a color wheel as well to edit

2. You are back to dollhouse mode like in Sims 1 and 2.
- No more open world like in Sims 3. You have to go to a loading screen even just to visit the people next door.
- Loading screens are signs of a bygone era. This is unacceptable considering Sims 3 got us past this already.

3. Character interactions are much less and just weird.
- You don't have as much character interactions.
- There are weird interactions like when you are having your sim talk to someone, another person your sim doesn't know just joins the conversation, and you can't kick that extra person out of the combined conversation without quitting it.

I really wanted to like the Sims 4. However it feels like it took us too many steps back to give us the new emotion system. This is not a game, but a proof-of-concept of the emotion system. Compared to the Sims 3 base game, which really made you feel like you cannot go back to the Sims 2, this incomplete version of a game only makes me want to go back to the Sims 3.

review_headline: A Very Fast, Addictive, and Compelling 25 Hours
review_body: Professor Layton vs Phoenix Wright is a highly addictive and not predictable combination of the two previous series.  The game switches back in forth between investigating and solving puzzles with the professor, and court cases with Phoenix.  The back in forth I found to be very well paced.  As soon as I was starting to get a little bored with one style it switched back over to the other.  The game took me about 25 hours to beat, but it went by extremely fast.  The story is very interesting from the very beginning and does a good job of keeping things interesting and generally avoiding cliches. The one exception to this I found was the unveiling of the climax of the story at the end.  I found it a bit drawn out.  Certain conclusions became very obvious, but the game didn't allow you to make them without spelling them out in trial in a slow drawn out manner.  The last trial was extremely long and it felt so unnecessarily.  As a whole the gameplay never felt dull or stagnant.  There is a wide variety of puzzles to beat, and the court cases have some of the most ludicrous plots and memorable characters from any Phoenix Wright game that I have played.  Highly recommended to anyone.

review_headline: I don't know what game others are reviewing, but this is for the Sims 4
review_body:
I don’t know what game most of the reviewers here are reviewing, but this review is for the Sims 4. Having read many of the reviews before purchasing, I decided what most complained about I wouldn’t mind, and that I still wanted to see for myself. However, I was in for a shock when I started playing, for the game appeared completely different. Here, I will try to list as many of the pros and cons as I can, generally in relation to Sims 3, other times to Sims 2.
In my personal opinion, the game seems much more intelligent than the previous games; it seems more realistic; and it seems they tried to meet many of the requests that lots of people had been asking for in a sims game since Sims 2. Many people said this game was a step backwards and did not offer any significantly new upgrades in technology. However, I found the exact opposite.
• The game-time has been slowed just a bit. It is now much more reasonable and sims can take a shower, go to the bathroom, and eat breakfast in the hour before going to work or school. It fits, actually, about perfectly, and once they are done doing those things it is usually exactly time to go to work (or school).
• If you do not pay your bills, rather than a repo-man coming (as it was in the other Sims games), your utilities get shut off one-by-one. It gives you a warning about this when a bill arrives. Curious to how this would play out, I let the sim not pay the bill. You only have 24-hours to pay it. After that 24-hours ran out, the electricity turned off. This turned made all electronics unusable, forced all the lights to be off, and wouldn’t allow cooking with a stove (which apparently must not be gas stoves). I let him still not pay the bills, and a day later the water turned off. He could not take a bath or use a sink (unfortunately, I can’t remember now if he could still use a toilet). I then had him pay the bills, so I don’t know what would have happened next.
• When you send your sim for a jog, rather than clicking on where you would like them to jog to, you click on the sim and there is (always) an option to go jogging. When you do this, the sim jogs for a while and then turns around and jogs back to where they started; sometimes, if they can, they will jog in a circle instead (such as around the block). If you felt that jog was too short, you can click on them again and have them jog again (push the limits, it says), and they will do a much longer jog the same way.
• If two sims are headed each other’s way so they block each other’s path, rather than stop and wait forever (to likely begin moving at the same time to have to stop and wait again), one of the sims simply steps to the side for a brief second while the other continues walking smoothly; once that sim is just a tiny bit past the sim who stepped to the side, the side-stepped sim then continues. This generally takes a second or less for them to complete, and looks very smooth and natural.
• Sims can really multitask. They can do almost anything while eating, drinking, or reading. They can have conversations, answer the door and invite someone in, watch TV, and even do something on their phone while eating, drinking, or reading. While eating or drinking, they can do even more, such as paint or play cards (with painting, they hold the plate in one hand and a brush in the other, taking pauses to grab a bite). They also do not stop eating, drinking, or reading when you tell them to move someplace else or do most things; they will even read on the toilet if you tell them to go while reading!
• Cooking sims can have conversations with other sims. In addition, sims’ conversations don’t have to be locked; they don’t need to face each other or stop what they are doing to do almost every social interaction. Unless the interaction requires physical touch (and even sometimes when it does), the sims do not need to face each other. A sim who wantsto give someone cooking a compliment can simply give it to him/her while walking past him/her from behind. Everyone still behaves right and reacts to it, the cook looking back behind his/her shoulder to the speaker.
• Contrary to what I had read in many reviews, the emotions in the game affect everything. The way the sim talks, behaves, and walks; whether or not they will do something you told them (tense sims might cancel-out something you told them to do; usually, if you tell them again, they will do it). The way they talk to people is changed, and what should be a happy chit-chat can start making their relationship grow sour if the sim is angry or tense, which makes them speak snappily and rudely. Emotions can change the socialization options, also, giving you knew ones you didn’t have without that emotion. The emotion options are vast; I don’t think I have encountered them all yet, and each emotion has stages (such as basic, very, very very). Emotions can also affect how well they learn a new skill, how well they do something (like cook or woohoo), and how long it takes them to do some things. Sims can also feel multiple emotions at once, but usually one emotion is stronger than the others and is the one dictating the social options.
• It is a partially open world. It is true that the game has to load to go to people’s houses, but it is not true that it is like Sims 2 where you have to stay on their lot or have a loading screen. Sims can freely leave their house and wander around, collecting things like rocks, flowers, and mushrooms, and interacting with other people who are also wandering around. Once you approach a house, though, it will make you load to enter it, but the loading is not even a minute’s wait. The game also has the worlds separated into districts. You must load to go from one district to another, but within each district you can wander around freely. It’s my own personal opinion that this makes it easier formachines to run; I know for my own computer it runs much more smoothly than even the base Sims 3 game did, and I think it’s ‘cause it’s not having to load the entire world constantly.
• There are two worlds presented, and your sim can easily travel between the worlds and does not loose anything from doing it; it is treated just like traveling to a district or a house. NPCs also travel between worlds, so while it is apparent that some are supposed to call home only one of the worlds, you might occasionally see them in the other world, apparently visiting. The two worlds are a fantasy-like woods and a New-World-style desert (with cacti and everything).
• The game has finally added tacos as a meal to make at home, and also has chips-and-salsa to eat. I don’t know about you, but I had been waiting for that (which never came) in Sims 3.
• Unfortunately, there are no cars. There are cars driving in the streets, but none for your sim to drive. Since both Sims 3 and Sims 2 added cars later, I going to assume that’s what they will do, but who knows.
• Sims do not take taxis everywhere; they walk. This is made tolerable by the loading of districts, so you don’t really have to wait that long for them to get anywhere, despite walking.
• Once everyone in the house is asleep, the game goes into this super-super speed that I can’t seem to access manually. The first-digit of minutes go by like seconds, so that an hour is more like a minute. You don’t have to wait very long at all for them to finish sleeping because of this. It automatically stops and goes to whatever speed you last had it at when someone wakes up. You can also tell it to go at a different speed if you don’t like it buzzing by so fast.
• Sims can sit on the sides of beds, like they do on sofas, and can do all the normal bed-interactions from the edge like that.
• All of the loading screens are very fast. It saves in less than a minute, too. The Sims 3 was never as fast as this game for me, in terms of loading.
• In making outfits, rather than have each outfit category limited (and requiring some real round-about skill to recategorize an outfit if you wanted it in a different category), each outfit category has a filter. It is automatically set to its own filter; each top, bottoms, or outfit is tagged for certain things. So, if you go to make a formal outfit, it automatically brings up everything tagged “formal”. However, you can click to remove that filter or change it to another one. What that does is lets you have access to all of the clothing for all categories. You are no longer restricted in this.
• Hats do not come with hair; they can sit on top of any hairstyle, and the hair simply morphs a bit to fit the hat realistically.
• If you give a sim multiple outfits for one category (so far I have given four just for everyday, but there is still a plus-sign to add more), they will automatically rotate between their outfits each day randomly. So every time they shower or wake up, they will wear a different outfit. Because it is random, it may have them wear the same ones a couple days in a row, but it is usually a different one. This applies to all outfit categories. You can also still tell them to wear what you want by clicking on them, so if they put one on you don’t want them to wear, you can simply tell them to change.
• There is no toddler stage. Infants grow up into children. However, you can interact with infants a lot more, but as far as I can tell cannot carry them around. They sit in a carriage, and you can go to the carriage to interact with the baby.
• Sims gain a skill instantly when doing something that requires that skill. The skills seem to progress faster than in other games, but not by an extreme amount (except for that first immediate one). Sims can try to read skill books of any level, but if it is below their own level, it will make them feel bored, and if it is too advanced for them, it will make them feel confused.
• The face and body creation is very detailed. You can really change their body shape and face shape. Unfortunately, there is no color wheel, and you must select color slots for eyes, hair, and skin. However, their skin colors are decently varied and numerous, though only have two fantasy options: green and blue. Before working with a face you will need to pick the shape you want for each part out of a selection, and then go from there. This changes things like whether the sim has an eyelid-fold, whether they have a cleft-chin, or how long their lashes are. After that, you can morph the face like crazy by pulling it around (no sliders).
• Again, no color wheel for clothes, furniture, floors, or walls, either. You are limited in your choices. Each item does have choices, but it is still more limiting in this area than Sims 3. If you are big on architecture or interior design, you will probably be disappointed with this game. They have made house-building easier and faster, but have not catered to architects at all. That’s fine for me, as I normally just used pre-made houses, but may be terrible for some players.
• The skin of sims changes what it looks like depending on their fitness. Muscular sims will have muscle definition. Skinny sims have visible bones. Overweight sims have rolls. The skin fades into each other, so that a muscular skinny sim has both bones and muscle definition, and someone neither skinny nor overweight has neither bones nor rolls. However, someone who is both muscular and overweight will have rolls. These are sliders, and so the skin slowly changes as their fitness does in the sliders. I assume this would change in-game, but haven’t had a sim change enough to notice a difference.
• Mannerisms, behavior, and speech change depending on age. Children behave like children, fairly playful in mannerisms and behavior (or more tantrum-like if upset); young adults behave and speak more like real young adults (at least in the US), adults behave and speak more maturely, and elderly behave and speak very maturely and often with an air of authority.
• You can select a walking style for your sim from a selection of rather goofy walking styles. This will be how they normally walk. You can also change it later at the dresser in plan-outfit mode. However, their emotions can affect their walk, too, so the walk will still change sometimes, but most emotions will not affect the walk you chose for your sim.
• They have made it extremely difficult to change a sim’s surname. If your sims marry, neither sim will change their last name, and there is no way in the game to change it. You must use a cheat. After Ctrl-shift-C, you have to type in testingcheats true, then cas.editfullmode, esc to exit the cheat bar, and then shift-click on the sim you want to change the name of, select “modify in cas”, and then change their name there. This is very frustrating and probably the worst part of the game that really needs to be fixed.
• If your sim goes to talk to someone who is already talking to someone else, the other sim will not stop talking to them, and so your sim will enter a broader conversation. In some cases, it may say your sim is talking to six or more people. However, individual conversations can still happen here. Whoever you click on is where your interaction will be directed towards. If you click to give a flirty joke with some sim named John, everyone will laugh, but only John’s relationship with you will be affected. This applies this way for everything. However, an in-general “chat” will be going on with everyone, though some sims your sim doesn’t know may be skipped (your sim may avoid conversing with a sim they don’t know who is talking to someone they do, in some cases; loner sims seem especially inclined to this).
•Unlike what I read in three different reviews, sims do in fact take care of their own needs. Unless you have them fishing or reading, they will automatically go to the bathroom, feed themselves, bathe, or have fun if you ignore them for a few seconds. Sometimes they will while reading, but not as easily. There is an option to turn autonomy off, but normally they take care of themselves unless you tell them to do otherwise.
• Sims get up a little before having to pee their pants, giving you time to tell them to go to the toilet (or for them to choose to on their own) instead of them waking up to simply pee their pants.
• Sims automatically flush toilets that haven’t been flushed before using. No idea what slob sims would do.
• It is true that story progression is not around. Other sims do not change (they do not get married, have kids, get or change jobs) unless you go to play them and make them do the changes. However, everyone still ages at the same rate.
• The game allows for multiple accounts on the same computer. So, you and your partner or children could each have your own version of the game. You log in to your own portion of the game that has your own saves.
• It is true that the hair selection is limited, but from what I remember it is a bit more than what Sims 3 started out with, but I may be wrong on that. It feels especially limited for the males, as usual. Males also have less full outfits to pick from, and still no dresses or skirts.
• Work stories, like done in the Sims 2, are back. While your sim is at work, a window may appear saying something is happening, and you have to select what you want your sim to do. I have found in the Tech occupation it is awfully repetitive, having seen only two stories brought up multiple times, but I suppose it is better than nothing. You can tell your sim how to perform at work or school by clicking on a corner symbol on their picture. It is possible for sims to be in different districts, and you can kind-of control what the other (that you are not with) is doing by their picture, or you can switch back-and-forth between them.
• Sims can put things like plates on bookshelves.
• There are no cookbooks/recipe-books. There might be one for $2500, not sure (it is titled as a cookbook). This is a bit disappointing for me.
• With infants, breastfeed is an option for females (at least the mom, have not tried other females).
• One weird thing is the sims love to play musical chairs. They tend to get up and switch places a lot, and I haven’t figured out why. They also tend to just get up and down. So a sim eating breakfast at the table may suddenly decide to stand beside the table to eat it, but last minute decide to finish it at the table (or not). Two sims eating at the table may constantly switch seats while eating. They don’t do this every time, but enough that it seems weird and almost annoying. Thy also play musical chairs at the bar, but don’t seem to have a problem on sofas or when sitting on the bed.
• Occasionally, seated sims (no matter where seated) will get up and reset. This has only happened when many people are seated and talking to each other. It happens rarely, but it is very strange, and I have not figured out why it is happening (in part because it happens too fewly).
• “Woohoos” can be good or bad (often based on the emotions they felt while doing it) and how good it was affects their mood after.
• Pregnant sims do not change clothes. They keep the clothes they had while pregnant, and you can still change their clothes.
• You can change hairstyle and makeup in plan-outfit mode, along with clothes.
• Long periods of cleaning trigger a very tense emotion, which claims to be caused by so much cleaning.
• One really annoying thing is the game saves every single notification. It tells you when your sim has left off to work,when they have returned and how much money they earned, when they level up or do something else; and saves it to a long list. It also groups the lists of all sims you have played together. If you do not delete these as they come, the game will eventually run out of room and tell you it has. You then have to go deleting them one-by-one. If you stay on top of it and delete them as they come it is not as bad, but this is still a very annoying feature that seems like it could have been done better.
• You can alter any lot while visiting it without having to leave your game.
• How much babies are fed determines their weight when they become children.
• Their selection of idle behaviors is a bit limited, because twice I saw sims have the same idle at the same time. This is a little annoying as it reminds one that it is a game and makes everything else seem more fake (I don’t know how else to describe it). However, most of the time it is fine.
Overall, the game seems more realistic. The pros, for me, outweigh the cons. While being more realistic, it is also very playful and goofy; if you are into very seriousness, then that might annoy you in the game. (For example, when sims are happy, they go around with the biggest smile on their face.) If you like more playfulness in games, though, it may delight you (as it does me). I was lucky enough to have bought it after the patch was released which fixed all of the bugs. EA has never been known before to actually fix the glitches in their games (at least not for the Sims), especially not so quickly. I’m taking that as an indication they are going to try to have better ethics this time.

product_title: Record of Agarest War Zero - Standard Edition - Playstation 3
review_body: Without a doubt, this is the single worst strategy RPG I've ever played. In general, that might mean that the game was still good (the SRPG has been one of the strongest categories of games, at least in my lifetime), but holy crap - is this bad. For now, let me ignore the creepy fanservice which is present throughout this game. It's such an easy target, but there is so much more to hate about this steaming pile.    Let me begin with the actual \\"tactical\\" gameplay. As everyone knows, the SRPG generally sets up turn-based-style tactics, where advantages and disadvantages are conferred on players through the use of terrain, position, and other factors. For example, in Final Fantasy Tactics, a player might gain advantage by positioning his archer on a mountain, in order to gain range with his attacks. Or, she might be put at disadvantage because an enemy attacks her from a flanking position. Even small details like Zodiac signs could play a role in the outcome of a battle. In a game like Suikoden Tactics, relative position of a character and his allies might allow for special unison attacks to be used. Of course, since people move at different times, setting up such an attack might be difficult, because an enemy might move out of the way of a carefully planned attack before all of your characters are in position.    Agarest War Zero plays at these ideas, but misses the point completely. Yes - advantages are granted based on relative position, but there is no rhyme or reason to exactly WHY such position matters. For example, one character might grant bonuses to allies who are situated within a sort-of \\"wing\\" formation to his right and left. Another character might grant positional bonuses for characters who are lined up directly beside her. These bonuses are absolutely vital to any success in this game - failure to utilize them appropriately will result in an early rage-quit. But it's completely arbitrary. It's not like a fighter seeks to have archers protecting his flanks, and thus the formation grants bonuses accordingly. It's just a series of lit-up squares. Further, there are no terrain bonuses whatsoever. All terrain is a flat grid.    Movement of characters is the biggest problem. Yes, you can attack an enemy from a flank and receive a bonus. However, each individual character doesn't get his own turn to move. Rather, you determine the movements of ALL characters in your party, completely oblivious to the enemy movements. That is, you will put in the movements for six characters, and only after making the decisions will you see where any enemy goes.    It's hard to describe just how stupid this is, but this is my best effort: imagine you are playing chess. However, instead of alternating movements, each of you have to make...6 movements, all at once, and only afterwards can you see where the pieces fall. It kind of defeats the purpose.    Thus, your movements are pretty simple: you will move your characters within the \\"good\\" squares (and hopefully, you were able to pick an appropriate formation and memorized the \\"good\\" squares of a character, because the game certainly isn't going to help you with that). Then, you hope that an enemy doesn't use an attack which moves one of your characters, since if he does, your ENTIRE strategy for that round is shot. That's how important those bonuses are. The boggling stupidity of this is incredible to me.    Thankfully (tongue-in-cheek), the game provides you with hundreds of battles to fight. It is absolutely mind-numbing. Further, while winning battles does carry rewards in the form of experience, leveling is actually pretty useless in this game. Most of your attack and defense prowess comes from the equipment you carry, and not your level. That's not to say stats are unimportant. For example, if you aren't getting hit points, you should have pumped vitality. If you can't hit enemies, your luck and agility are lacking. And if you pumped strength without realizing this, well, it sucks tobe you! After all, far be it from the developer to explain it to you - you should have bought the guide!    Speaking of equipment, ugh. Most of the stuff you can find/buy is useless. In order to get the good stuff, you'll need to investigate the game's item creation system. If you've ever played Cross Edge, you know what a pain that's going to be. Again, nothing is explained in the least. Good luck figuring it out without a guide. My advice for anyone who is still considering this: download the free gear from PSN. It's much better than pretty much anything you'll stumble over or create in your fumbling manner. If you insist, prepare to grind. Of course you didn't think that materials would be purchase-able? Mostly, you'll need drops from enemies.    And so now, we get to the story. What a slog. There is one redeeming value: the localization is so amateurish that it actually comes off sounding (or, more precisely, reading) hilariously. It feels like an undergrad majoring in Japanese translated this script. Of course, that novelty wears off quickly, but we take our victories where we can. The story itself is standard Japanese dreck. Forces of light and darkness are clashing. You are a chosen one (completely by accident). After a few boring betrayals and a LOT of boring interpersonal relationship, you get to save the world. HOORAY!    The graphics are a joke. Enough said.    And that finally leaves the fanservice, which I won't badmouth. I don't even need to. This game is plenty disastrous. If you think this is good SRPG, you haven't played good SRPG. I would recommend something like Tactics Ogre, or Final Fantasy Tactics, or Vandal Hearts (PS1). Or even lesser titles like Dynasty Tactics and Gladius (PS2).    Heck, if you're one of those creepy people who can't get enough of seeing underage cartoon characters in various states of undress, there are much better titles out there that will satisfy that urge AND keep you entertained in between.

review_headline: One of the better console games, good for non-gamers
review_body:
I played the first and second Diablo way back when they first came out at LAN parties with friends. It was a fun and easy to get into time sink. This latest version brings back those old feelings, and proves to be simply executed enough that most non-gamers can get into it.

I've played this with many people new to gaming, and they not only like it, but do pretty well. It's more than likely due to the simple controls, and that not being that adept in all the various button presses only slows progress, doesn't preclude you from totally progressing at all. For example, if you only use your primary attack, you can still kill things and run around the world collecting stuff. It takes some instruction and practice to figure out the equipment screen, which is one of the weaker parts to the game (I can't help but completely backing out when switching between different categories). We just always equip the most expensive item. The game is long, and doesn't feel too repetitive. Single player is fun, multi-player is more fun.

I have a wish list of missed opportunities: I wish the environment was more interactive, or that abilities your character does, and perhaps even abilities of other co-op players or enemies, could interact with each other (flaming tornados of hurt?). And the game doesn't feel as near as deep and interconnected as Blizzard's initial claims, but it's still a fun game.

The graphics aren't incredibly impressive, I could imagine much more could be done; more sprites, more poly counts, more -stuff-, but it's better than indie, and sufficient.

All in all, as many others have said, this -is- the way the game was meant to play. The PC version (which I have since given away to a girl friend) did, in hindsight, feel like a beta test. I recommend this game to everyone, and so far a couple of non-gaming friends (girls, if that matters), have bought this and we all have fun playing for WAY too many hours.

product_title: Metal Silver Bullet Buttons + Thumbsticks For Dual Shock 4 PS4 Controller Mod Kit
review_body:
This product definitely makes a controller look pretty cool, and its not all bad, but there are a lot of reasons why you may want to consider not using this mod for your controller at this point.

Construction Quality: The buttons and thumb sticks are actually metal, just in case you are thinking about purchasing this and would be disappointed if they were plastic. The D-Pad is still plastic, but everything else is actually metal, and unlike the pictures, the buttons appear to now be created out of one solid block. The actual precision with which the thumb sticks are made is pretty impressive. That said, the buttons are slightly undersized. You might be surprised how a fraction of a millimeter can matter here, but they will wiggle around on you to a perceptible degree, perhaps even to a degree you cannot ignore. There were also problems with how the thumb sticks connect to the pegs on the inside of your controllers. If you haven't taken one apart, the peg is roughly I-shaped, so that it holds the thumbstick with a constant orientation, it doesn't twist left or right. One of my thumb sticks was drilled in such a manner. The other was more of an X-shape, which means that the stick rotates (easily) left and right. E-Mods was not willing to replace this part for me, so you shouldn't expect great customer service if they send you bad parts.

Usability: Once you get everything installed, the question I've gotten most is "do your thumbs slip?" The interior of the thumbstick is concave but it is very smooth aluminum. Your thumb will probably move around on this a lot easier than it will on any rubberized surface. There is a lip, and then the grooved outer bezel. I have what I would call as relatively normal sized man hands. I generally place the majority of my thumb into this divot. My thumbs don't slip around too much like this, because it catches the lip. If you hold your thumbs in almost any other way, you won't have the same level of control.If you have smaller hands or are playing in a competitive situation, I could see these thumb sticks being a real problem from a usability standpoint.

I would have given RS2014 5 stars were it not for the intermittent crashes and glitches I have experienced. The game has frozen up on me several times, most often when playing guitarcade games. I'm not laying all of the blame on Ubisoft though. I think It's more of a platform issue - PC games are, in general, more buggy than their console counterparts.

review_headline: Naughty Dog Scores HUGE with this game!
review_body:
First things first, this game is simply a masterpiece! It will easily go down as one of my top 5 favorite games played to date, on any console. Everything from the writing to the voice acting to the game play was top notch. You will be hard pressed to find a game this complete for years to come.

Graphics:
The game is simply beautiful to look at. The variety and detail that was put into constructing each section of the game really pulls you in and makes you feel immersed in the game. Everything from tree filled forests, broken down and dilapidated buildings, to snow storms and trudging through the sewers. Solid 9.7 for graphics.

Voice Acting:
I cant say enough good things here. The voice actors that portray Joel and Ellie are simply incredible. The emotion and grit of the characters shines through in their performances and they rightly deserve any award they receive for this game. Its a perfect pairing of a seasoned man with a chip on his shoulder and a mouthy misunderstood teen with something to prove. Perfect 10!

Game Play:
The flow of the game is near perfect. Naughty Dog continues to find success using the "Havok" engine to run the game and it certainly didn't fail them here. The movement is realistic and the control of the characters is very tight. Now, I have heard some people say that the game is too hard but in my opinion, its perfect. Its a survival game! It was never meant to me a "run and gun" game where all you do is fire aimlessly at enemies hoping to rack up the kills. There are games that can pull that off, this was never meant to be one of them. The suspense from having limited supplies and having to decide how to sneak around a bunch of enemies is done perfectly. I was on the edge of my seat more times than I can count contemplating which decision to make, and being nervous as I executed it. Wonderful mix of strategy and rationing supplies to see yourself through the game. 9.8 for this section.

Audio:
I played the game on a surround sound and it was incredible. Every little movement and noise came through perfectly and I actually had to stop myself from turning around in my seat as I heard something behind me. The music that was chosen for the game fits right in and only serves to enhance the emotional experience of the game. Composers and sound mixers get a perfect 10 from me here!

Replayability:
Yes! I played the game on Hard and can not wait for the challenge/experience of playing it on Survivor. 10 here as well.

Overall, this game went above and beyond any of my expectations. One of the best games of this decade, hands down. I highly recommend this game to anyone that enjoys a Survival game. It will test your strategy and your gaming wits. 9.9 of 10! Amazing game!. 9.8 for this section.

review_headline: If you like the 'Assassin's Creed' saga then this game is for you
review_body:
After all the hype behind this game more than a year before its release I was really excited to finally being able to play it. My original idea was to get the PS4 version, since I was recently playing 'Second Son' I decided to wait until I completed that one in the hopes of a price drop on 'Watch Dogs'. While the reviews were mixed, I wanted to play the game myself, the idea of a hacker manipulating his surroundings looked great in the first gameplays. I was then given the opportunity to play the PS3 version, I had read the PS4 version did not come up at 1080p so that helped me make my decision.

The game looks incredible on a PS3, which is not a surprise after the amount of data the game installs before playing it for the first time (it took over 10 minutes in my system for the install only, this is not including the patch it downloaded and also installed) Graphics are excellent and the city looks detailed, then again, character's faces are not that great but this is something Ubisoft is known for in their games.

So how does the premise of the hacker work in the finished game? It feels like a wasted opportunity, which is a shame. Discussing this with a friend he made a point in which we both agreed, this game feels a lot like the first 'Assassin's Creed', it is a novel idea with repetitive gameplay. That is not necessarily a bad thing, the 'Assassin's Creed' games have evolved quite well in my opinion so I am hoping the same will happen with 'Watch Dogs' should they make a sequel. The game does have some very interesting missions (like the stealth ones in which you have to plan your attack before making your move) but it also has missions that feel like a chore, the car chases being the ones I hated the most. Someone said driving a car in 'Watch Dogs' is like driving the ice tracks in 'Mario Kart' and I could not agree more. The idea of chasing another car and hacking into traffic lights and other potential hazards to stop the guy you're chasing may sound exciting until you actually play those missions, the gameplay for those sequences does not seem polished at all, again, a missed opportunity. Also you have the ability to hack bank accounts of the citizens around you and withdraw the money for ATMs, that money can be used to buy things you can earn in the game without having to buy them and skins, the latter are awful in my opinion (still I purchased them all in the hopes I would get a trophy and surprise! I didn't)

I have to admit though I enjoyed playing it for a while, I don't want to give away any spoilers so I will not get into details, but while the story was entertaining, I think it could have been told in a better way as to make it less confusing in the end.
