review_headline: Mixed bag, could've been much better
review_body: What a shame. X/Y is not a horrible game, but left much to be desired.    X/Y's story is poorly paced with several heavily underutilized characters. A shame because had the execution been better it would've been pretty good. Not that Pokemon has ever been amazing in that department, but after Pokemon Black/White 2, it felt like it took a 180 and felt very unsatisfying. It's still a better story then say Gold/Silver though. Team Flare is also easily the worst Team of any Pokemon game to date. A new level of stupid and boring, really.    Kalos itself is not very interesting as a region. I wasn't a fan of the extravagant French vibe going on. Lumoise City successfully captured the vibe of a bustling central capital better then any Pokemon game to date although packed with many utterly useless cafes. The biggest con of Kalos though is that all the routes felt extremely short and uninteresting, more so then any other Pokemon game. Maybe Gamefreak thought they could compensate for that with a huge amount of Pokemon to be captured in this game alone and maybe that does to some people I guess. I don't know about you but routes should be their own little journey and you should felt a twinge of excitement reaching the next town. I can name just three places where dungeons/routes had any actual length and two of them are near the end of the game or optional end-game content.    Lack of post game content is another really big negative point here, probably the most disappointing. After Black/White 2's packed post-game, it left much to be desired. You've got the Battle Maison, which itself is fun, but...that's it really it. Capture a few legendaries, of which don't exactly count in my eyes except one. The Friend Safari is another interesting end-game feature, but felt gimmicky to me and doesn't exactly make for long-term content. The Looker missions, which are short and have no replay value. It's quite evident Gamefreak tried to shoe-horn everyone into competitive battling as themain post-game content.     That's it really. It's far from my favourite Pokemon game, but what it does right it does well (Online features, 3D, Pokemon Amie, Super Training and trainer customization) and it is still a good introduction to Pokemon. If you're obsessed with Catching Them All and competitive battling you'll feel right at home here, everyone else will play it, put it down and probably not pick it up again.

review_headline: This is just a re-post for different platform.
review_body:
I got the game for PS3, but I think it will be more visible here to inform people of what they are getting. Graphics and sound might be slightly better on PS4 and Xbox one, but the game will be the same.

This game gets 3 stars, mainly because of it's replay value. Let me break down what I mean:

Does not feature a game+ system, so you literally start over fresh every time you complete the game and want to start another play through after completion. This game is good for 6 play throughs, and that's if someone is adamant about playing all 3 of the available classes as masters of each individual class with good alignment and evil alignment. Unless a person doesn't mind grinding out the levels to master all 3 classes which gets boring after a while, then it'd be good for 2 times through. Fights are wash rinse and repeat, especially towards the end in Blackfrost's Domain. Trash mobs are ridiculously long fights there, as they are excessively resilient and borderline boring to fight, think the scale of some of the trash mobs in Dark Souls 2.

This game is progressive, not open world exploration. You complete a \\"Chapter\\" you are ushered to a new zone, so make sure you complete all the side quests BEFORE you progress the main story line because there is no going back and finishing anything for the xp bump. The zones are fairly large, and can give you a sense that you are going some where as you trek around, but it's more along the lines of how Last of Us is with chapters and zones.

The companions you can have tag along with you are extremely squishy, and the casters are particularly ignorant even after you change their combat tendencies and set their combat roles. The healer isn't as useful as one would originally believe, the mages are useful with their cc ability neither has any sense to move away from their attackers, so they usually go down pretty quickly. They also do not do a very good job of keeping up with you when you sprint area to area. I fought several mobs all by my lonesome, having absolutely no idea where my companion was. Also, there are irritating parts of certain chapters that you have absolutely no input on who your companion is, and the companion you are stuck with may only be good to keep some of the mobs off of you until the companion is killed while you set your traps and work on the archers.

Ok, those were the cons, now for the positives:

Combat works smoothly. Few hiccups here and there, but nothing major. Works a lot like Dark Souls 2, without the 2h wielding of a weapon for boosted damage, and you don't have to worry about stamina.

Weapon/Armor customizing is nice, however, you will develop your favorites based on effects more than aesthetics. To be effective you MAY not look exactly like you want to look.

The atmosphere is pretty cool, and the music, though mostly one song on repeat the whole game minus the boss fights, is pretty good. It just meshes with the atmosphere in my opinion, probably why they picked it...

Though the fights are repetitive and sometimes extremely frustrating, each fight gives a sense of accomplishment, because anything has the potential to kill you at any given time if you are not paying attention. This is especially true with boss fights.

Crafting consumables is convenient, and very necessary to make life easier. Very easy to get the hang of.

Well, that sums it up I think. 3 stars, but primarily because of the lack of a game+ system. Myself, I do not want to start over, level 1 with crap gear every time I complete the game. The story line is WAY too short not to have a game+ system. All that work that goes into a play through is wiped away when you kill the final boss, and for me, it killed any desire to do it all over again knowing that everything I had achieved, gained and found was null and void and I'd have to play the same content over as if I just opened the box.

review_headline: Most other games don't get close to this masterpiece!
review_body:
Having read a recent interview with one of the game designers from this game's developer YAGER and the statement, that the low and disappointing sales of the game would prohibit YAGER from ever even considering a sequel compel me to write this review more than two years after the game's release.
Spec Ops – the Line is a 3rd person anti-war shooter with plenty of style and action that in fact managed to impress me in ways that only the Metal Gear series had before, and that in itself is a huge compliment. The game's storyline is absolute powerful, haunting and deeply meaningful, the whole tone/vibration of the setting in postapocalyptic Dubai is groundbreakingly executed. Both the visual/artistic style and art and the sound/music pull the player deep inside the terrible events the game portrays. The game as well as it's characters feel absolutely genuine and real and I have rarely found playing a game as impactful as having completed Spec Ops – The Line multiple times. While many critics and players critisized some of the rather „casual“ gameplay mechanics I on the contrary found that very aspect of not having to study the control scheme that extensively to be rather accessible and polished. I am a hardore gamer and by no means a casual gamer by the way, but I believe gameplay should be accesible without multiple hours of getting into it.
Summing it up and referencing aspects of the aforementioned interview with one of the game's producers obviously video gamers seem to prefer simple and in fact rather idiotic stories that add nothing to the gameplay experience itself because they are rather perceived as a waste of time anyway.

review_headline: Decent distraction if gotten on the cheap.
review_body:
It's an OK game at best. I only play single player campaigns so can't speak for any multiplayer features. The story is decent, but the game play is repetitive with the player essentially battling the same 3 enemy units of varying attributes and skins throughout the entire game with some vehicle scenes interspersed. The graphics are sub par, the controls are difficult, but since the AI is pretty bad the clunky controls are not the end of the world. Reloading was a pain where it sometimes would not take the first time. Maybe they were going for more realism but when comparing it to the slew of other good games out there it just felt off. The game seemed as though it had potential, the player can go around to distract the enemy units, but unless the NPCs specifically tell you to flank (which they rarely do), they do not take advantage of your distractions and may or may not ever get around to destroying the enemy while you are pinned down. One of the best aspects of the game was the "cover" interface and the ability to jump between cover pretty much without injury but it was easy to get stuck behind cover as well. While this didn't cost a battle it was still frustrating.

There are games for sale now for under $5 so with shipping, if you can get it for under $10 total it isn't a bad distraction for a very short story, but any more than that and there are other better options out there.

product_title: DanganRonpa: Trigger Happy Havoc - PlayStation Vita
review_headline: Great at times, but attempts to imitate don't always work.
review_body: Really good story, really good characters and an amazingly addictive trial mechanic. The resolution to the game gets a bit idiotic, though. It's to be expected that an NIS game be completely insane, but the narrative suffers for it at the end. The school life bonus is okay, but isn't very alluring for the average player. If you're a perfectionist and have to have all loose ends tied, even to the degree of being willing to chug through hours of what's essentially an irrelevant game mechanic, then it's not going to bother you. It's not a bad game, in fact, it's actually a rather good one. It's just hindered by its extra peripherals and obligatory NIS eccentricity. I also know I'm probably unfairly comparing it to the "Zero Escape" and "Ace Attorney" games. Going on that comparison, though, I think "Dangan Ronpa: Trigger Happy Havoc" could be described as thus: It's a trial game with a more engaging mechanic than "Ace Attorney," but the humor isn't as concise in the dialogue. It makes an attempt at a plot similar to "Zero Escape," but it just isn't as smart or conducive to choice.

product_title: HDE Playstation 2/3 to Xbox360 Controller Adapter
review_headline: Not a perfect solution for frustrated Xbox 360 owners, but it'll do!
review_body:
Can't stand the stock Xbox 360 controllers? Want to take that joystick you bought years ago out of mothballs? Here's your solution. The HDE controller adapter isn't the most elegant solution to Microsoft's controller lockout chip, but it works, and it will free you from the dreadful D-pad on the standard Xbox 360 joypad if you're a fan of fighters and old-school arcade games. I used the adapter with two different Playstation 2 controllers- a replica Sega Saturn pad and Namco's Tekken 5 arcade joystick- and it worked brilliantly with both of them, with no discernible lag. It also bears mentioning that the HDE adapter- at least the one I bought from an auction site- works just fine with older Xbox 360 models. Maybe earlier models had compatibility issues, but this one has no such issues.

There are downsides, although likely unavoidable ones. As another reviewer mentioned, there's no apparent way to reconfigure buttons with the adapter, so you'll have to do that in the games themselves... if they offer that option. If you want to press the guide button, you'll have to do it from another controller, because you won't find an equivalent on a Playstation 2 controller and there's evidently no keystroke to replace it. Finally, you're going to get tangled up in a lot of wires due to the way the adapter uses a wired Xbox 360 controller to circumvent Microsoft's infuriating proprietary technology. It's a kludge, but it gets the job done. Why settle for the controllers Microsoft gives you when you can use your favorites instead?

product_title: The Legend of Zelda:  Phantom Hourglass
review_headline: Like Sand Through the Phantom Hourglass, These Are the Days of My Life
review_body: The sequel to the GameCube hit The Wind Waker, Phantom Hourglass follows Toon Link who, with help from a fairy and a conniving sailor, tries to save the pirate Tetra and the Great Sea.  Introducing the touch-screen-only control scheme exclusive to this and Spirit Tracks, it's slightly polished in the latter game but there's a lot less blowing into the mic.    The travel aspect of this title is also better compared to ST.  Drawing your route with the stylus, you can go anywhere you want from your ship compared to riding the rails on a train.  You can also scrawl on a magic slate that's sends you flying to different spots.  PH even takes the load off gathering ship parts by salvaging them from the ocean floor, discovering treasure chests, and buying parts from Beedle's storefront.  But I still can't complete my armored ship!    More headaches abound in the Temple of the Ocean King.  Like the Tower of Spirits in Spirit Tracks, you have to backtrack to the place and avoid traps and Phantoms to access every floor before the sand runs out in the titular Hourglass.  Once that happens, you're dealing with the very essence of the temple draining your life away.  Any way you slice it, a time limit is imposed.  A time limit in a Zelda game.  A time limit in a game that's all about free exploration and checking every nook and cranny for heart containers and treasure!  Fortunately, checkpoints are added to shorten each session and 2 minutes' worth of sand is salvaged at sea and won in boss fights.    Speaking of which, the bosses are pushovers once you figure out what to do--with the exception of a doozy of a final boss in a 3-phase battle.  Between all this and a whole trading sequence I wound up skipping, the whole experience felt rather short.  Regardless, I put Phantom Hourglass just above Spirit Tracks in terms of playability though not as much for lasting appeal.    This game is rated E for Everyone and contains mild violence.

review_headline: Not Bad, Not Great, But Definitely Better Than Average
review_body:
I am a big fan of the original GRID as well as Colin McRae DiRT, so when a driving game comes out that tries to implement style, I am sure going to give it everything I got and enjoy the ride. Codemasters is one of the few who carries that style, but surely they have had their ups and downs. So far I have put around 15 hours into the game and from what I have played, I would say that GRID Autosport is a ride worth taking. GRID Autosport is an attempt to right some of those wrongs with the simulator fan-base, without pushing away the casual drivers.

The single player career has five disciplines, with the introduction of touring cars, open wheel racing, tuner events, endurance and street racing, there is almost something for everyone. They all require a very particular way of racing, so each time you switch from one group to another you'll need to readjust the way you play and the A.I seems to do the same. The AI seems very good and exhibits different racing personalities and the game features a wide range of tracks, boasting of around 100. The game demands that you level up in all disciplines if you wish to take part in the special GRID Masters/Legends events that take place at every so many levels. Career progress is measured in seasons. Each season, you pick a discipline and sign up with a sponsored team and that team gives you specific objectives to fulfill, like no collision damage and so on.

The cockpit view has returned as well as car tuning, something that GRID 2 was sadly lacking. Each option is accompanied by a helpful summary of what each tweak will do, so there is no need to have a in-depth technical car knowledge in order to understand the tuning. GRID Autosport or simply the GRID series in general is not a simulation or arcade, it is both, it mixes simulation and the arcade experience both in one. At times it can seem really hard because an induced over-steer is easy to achieve, but practice makes perfect and that's what true racing is about. The game also has an online mode but I'm not much of an online player so I can't comment about those features, but I do know someone who is playing it and they say it does have lots to do in it.

In all it is a really fun game, even if some of the major gaming sites are giving it some borderline low scores. GRID Autosport is a quality product, as one would expect from Codemasters when developing a racing game. It's just difficult these days for many people to pick up and play when there are next gen racing games on the way. Many of the problems I hear people saying about this game is that it suffers with an extremely linear career mode by having limited progression choices.

Ultimately the objective is to play in each of the five racing categories to reach a certain level to unlock the GRID event and repeat, and this tells the player that it is progression for the sake of progression. GRID Autosport does have a lack of choices, and simply asks the player if they want to choose whether they play a Street event or an Endurance one. The cars are picked for you, their upgrades are limited and even your ability to tweak or alter a vehicle's setup is decided by the event you participate in.

You can still customize the difficulty of the game, tailoring every aspect of the underlying systems, such as realistic damage to assisted braking and you earn cumulative extra XP based on your settings. However, even with the said, GRID Autosport is much more of a racer than GRID 2 and racing is what this game is really about. As it stands, there are plenty of RPG games available for players that are looking to make choices, so the true essence of GRID Autosport is held within the walls of racing, so it is racing you will be doing. review_headline: Good game for AA/Edgeworth fans, but could be better
review_body:
Having played the Ace Attorney 1,2,3 games + Dual Destinies, I found the Investigation series a different yet similar experience from the originals. There's some merit, and I enjoyed the exeperience, but I think Capcom could have done better, regarding storyline and character development.

Simply put:

Pro:
-Different perspective than the defense attorney (focus on the scene)
-Focus on Miles Edgeworth (I am an Edgeworth fan :D) and other characters (Gumshoe)

Con:
-Limited gameplay (scene of the crime minus the courtroom scene, which was a huge factor in the original Pheonix Wright series)
-Kinda forced "original dynamic" (rebuttals and analysis in the courtroom) into the crime scene
-Decreased level of difficulty, which shortens gameplay time (and you can't really replay the game which is a real bummer)

I gave four stars because I think this is a great play for anyone who's played the AA series (and is a fan), and I'm biased because of Edgeworth (I was so sad when he wasn't as prominant in AA 2 an 3 compared to the first one......). However, I am disappointed because this game had so much more potential, and failed to accomplish everything it could have achieved.

As a former pre-law student who interned as an investigator intern at an actual criminal defense law firm, I can say that the game accurately reflects the skills and abilities (logic and deduction) required for a real investigator. However, I think Capcom could have done better than try to reuse what tactics were used in the Pheonix Wright series. Yes, prosecutors spend a lot of time on the scene but Miles Edgeworth shined in the courtroom, and like other reviewers said, it would have been nice to show that prosecutors, too, can win in the courtroom. It would have been more interesting if there were diverse outcomes possible throughout the game, extending gameplay, and in my opinion, okay for Capcom to push up the price abit more.

Compared to a lot of the TV shows regarding criminal justice, the AA series show a better description of the current law system, including the "dark age of the law" depicted in the Dual Destinies series. However, I wish Capcom was more "neutral" in the sense that it didn't try to only show defense attorneys as the main character. Like Pheonix Wright and Miles Edgeworth shows, it takes both the defense and the prosecution to reveal the truth behind a case.

For those of you that don't know, this game is actually a sequel to Tokyo Xtreme Racer 3. The name is just different presumably because of a publisher change.

Where to start? If you are familiar with the series, you will enjoy this game. However, a few obvious shortcomings make it fall short of what it could have been. First and foremost, there are about a dozen cars. It gets really old racing against the same few models, and unlike the previous games, you never need to buy a second car. The gains from doing so are so tiny it's best to stick with whatever you got at the start. This game is much shorter as a result, since there is a lot less room for working your way up. It is devoid of the joy of getting that next car you've been saving up for. Another annoying thing about the vehicle collection is that some of the old favorites, such as the AE86 are no longer customizable. You get a "custom" version that you can't modify. Not even performance-wise, which makes them useless.The races are also WAY too easy. The AI's never take turns or even gradual bends at speed. Learn to corner and you've already beaten the game. You never really feel triumphant for taking down a boss anymore. This game just simply isn't rewarding in the way the older games were, which makes it a lot less fun.

review_headline: This is a retro game lovers dream come true!
review_body:
I have been a gamer since the late 70s and the days of Atari. I have been very much anticipating the release of the Retron 5 and I am pleased to say that it is an amazing device!

I won't spend a lot of time going over the specs of the system as they are well documented. There have been a lot of negative things said about it, so I want to address them and present how I dealt with them. They are not as big a deal as some people are saying.

The first negative thing is that the power plug adaptor has a very short cord, which was unexpected. I was able to plug it into an extension cord with no problems. Just something to keep in mind. It did include an HDMI cord that was plenty long enough, and converters for other power systems outside the US, which is very nice.

Make sure you turn on the system before you plug in the controller to the back, as it has to be calibrated first. I didn't do this and was afraid that my controller was broken. After you calibrate you can plug in and charge it.

The firmware update process can be confusing, but it is worth it to get to the good stuff. You have to download the first update from Hyperkin's website onto an SD card. The SD card is NOT required for saving your games, but you do have to have one for the update. After that is done you have to put the SD card back into a PC and download another file from their website (you have to put in a Captcha code to prove you are human) to get the system running. Annoying, but not a big deal.

In order to use the SNES/NES/Genesis controllers, you have to go into the setup screens and designate them for each system individually. You also have to create a profile for each if you wish to reassign buttons. I did this once and it didn't work, then I realized I forgot to set the new profile to each system as well. Once I did that it saved it and all was good.

The system does hold the carts tightly, but after a few switches mine is loosening up nicely.

And now for the good:

The picture quality is AMAZING!! Much better than I ever thought it would be. All the NES games I have tested so far have worked, with the exception of a few which I think need to be cleaned, and some of the reproduction carts I own. They are supposed to be working on that so hopefully that will change soon.

SNES and Genesis games look incredible! The Sega Master System games (with the converter) also play and look wonderful!

Also had no problem with GameBoy/GBC/GBA games. It even read one of the Cartoon Network GBA carts I had, which is nice.

It is VERY nice to have save states and hopefully they will get the battery issue solved soon.

Overall definitely worth the price and the wait! I can't wait to start playing my next game! :)

UPDATE: They have put out a new firmware update, and now some of my reproduction carts are working, and the cheats are working for NES too! I am definitely enjoying this system even more now. :)

review_body: I bought this as a backup mouse for my Logitech MX-518, it is becoming a permanent replacement now. It is pretty pointless spending more than $20 for a good gaming mouse now. I have purchased many Logitech and Razor gaming mouse, and they have no edge over this Sharkk mouse. The only thing that the MX518 has over this Sharkk is the slight curve near the pinky and the rubber grip, but as far as everything else goes that is it. The Sharkk actually has more advantages compared to the MX 518 like better clicks, bigger buttons, wider/gripper/smoother/softer-click scrolling wheel, colored-LEDs design and indicator, adjustable-weights, and it looks a lot cooler. A major complaint with Logitech mouse is that the mouse buttons are controlled by the software, which only works sometimes. It is my main reason to not switch back to the MX-518. The Sharkk mouse does not rely on the software. The Sharkk software actually loads the configurations directly into the mouse every time you apply settings. You can see the mouse rebooting itself. This means that if you take the mouse and plug it into another computer without the Sharkk software, your macros will work on the other computer. I have tried playing SC2 on it, and it works great. My mousepad is the Steelseries 9HD which is extremely smooth with the Sharkk until it is broken in some more. As for the quality, it is very high quality. The shell is smooth, the wires are braided, the USB is \\"gold\\" and quite thick. For the time being, my MX-518 will be the backup mouse for the Sharkk. So unless Logitech, Razor, or Mad Catz is selling you a mouse way WAY beyond the features of this Sharkk mouse, I don't think you should be spending more than the price of this Sharkk mouse.

product_title: Cartoon Network: Punch Time Explosion XL - Playstation 3
review_body:
Cartoon Network Punch-time Explosion (Referred to as CN PTE from here on) was an alright experience for me personally.
If you enjoyed watching shows on an from CN like Dexter's Laboratory, The Powerpuff Girls, Ben 10, and even Kids Next Door. Then this is a good recommendation for you.

CN PTE is a brawler similar to the popular Nintendo hit Super Smash bros. but with CN characters instead of Nintendo. the game itself offers more than what I expected when I first played this game.

Story: This game has a story mode similar to Super Smash bros. Brawl's Subspace Emissary mode. You travel through the worlds of CN and recruit teammates to defeat an evil source destroying the worlds. I love the feature that allows you to have up to four players on one team, video games like this are more fun when you're playing with friends.

Collectibles: This game awards players with points that they can spend on some locked characters, alternative outfits, arenas, and even video clips from shows. The collectables give you the more reason to unlock them all (it'll be worthwhile to earn a certain trophy for the PS3 version of the game while doing this.)

Replay value: If you like CN shows from the 90's and turn of the 2010 decade, then this is a great game for you. But the lack of variety in the story and sudden difficulty spikes can turn people away from replaying the game. If you wind up playing the majority of the game by yourself (which I did) the game can get really boring really fast.

Negatives: Every product has something that doesn't meet one's needs. For me, this would be the lack of an online battle mode, that would allow me to play the game much longer than I did. I liked the roster for whom it had, but it would've felt better with other characters from shows like Ed, Edd, n Eddy; Courage the cowardly Dog, Adventure Time, and Regular Show.

Overall review:
The game itself as a whole is very similar to Smash bros.while yet at the same time tries to have it's own identity and stray from the mentioned franchise. Yes, this game was made with that concept in mind, I however saw minor tweaks to make the two games vary drastically. If you have friends or family that like to play videogames with you and you like CN shows, this is a great recommendation for you. If you're trying to find a gift for your teenager or friend who loves to watch Cartoon Network shows from the 90's and the turn of the 2010 decade, I would definitely recommend giving this product a try.

My final rating is a 4 out of 5 stars; being as that this game can be well enjoyed, but like most brawlers, can get repetitive after awhile and lose it's touch, and the lack of an online mode didn't engage me as long as Smash bros. does.

Thank you for reading this review, and Happy Gaming.

review_headline: Highly Impressed!! Iron Galaxy deserves some praise!
review_body:
Hi all, I want to start off by saying that iron Galaxy deserves a lot more praise than most of the gamer sites are giving them. I worked in the games industry for 8 years as a sound designer for EA and worked on many games, so i know that being given this large of a game and making it fit into a handheld was an almost impossible task and i truly feel they pulled it off superbly. Are there some small issues, yes. What game doesn't have issues? The fact for me is, these small issues don't detract from the fun i'm having with this game. I'm having a blast playing borderlands 2 again, just as much as i did on the 360. I'm super excited to have this in portable form to play anywhere.

Lets get to some of the issues i've heard and read about. The back touch screen. i've heard people complain about it being unresponsive, i personally have not had that issue at all. The back touch screen has felt very responsive and i actually like their choice of run and melee as default in those slots. It's felt pretty natural actually. Also, as i've used my Vita grip casing it's allowed my hands to have more space as not to accidentally hit the back touch screen. there are some points the system bogs down a bit, and frames rates drop, but again this is a huge game on a handheld and most importantly for me it hasn't distracted me enough to take away from any of the fun and intensity.

Yes, there are some long load times, when going between maps, but still manageable, this game is good enough to wait for it to load up the fun in my opinion so they don't get on my nerves at all. Just be understanding of the limitations the system brings to the table and you should have tons of fun with this game! it is still a fantastic looking game, it still plays really fun and you can still see far into the distance unlike some of the reviews i've read. The art and sounds are still great, and again my hats off to the team that pulled this game off on a handheld!! THANK YOU!! I've said it before and i'll say it again, I LOVE HAVING THIS GAME IN PORTABLE FORM!! Here's the last thing i'll say, when playing this game just ask yourself, are you having fun? I know I am!

This game is, by far, one of the most complex video games that I have ever played. At the start of the game, the player can choose to be any race they would like from the Elder Scrolls series (Dark Elf, Kahjiit, Nord, Redguard, Argonian, etc.) and alter their appearance in ANY way imaginable, from eye color to jaw width. The races, as expected, have different attributes that can aid or harm your gameplay, depending. My favorite race is the Dark Elf, which has natural resistance to fire. Whichever race you choose, this is your character throughout the game, which you also name. The basic plot is basically that the dragons are returning and you, the player, is the only one who can end their existence in Skyrim. Of course the plot becomes much more in depth as the game progresses wherein you must choose your path, siding with allies and making enemies.

The fighting style is fairly simple. You choose a weapon (a staff. sword, bow, mace etc.) to place either in the left or right hand. Magic, any one handed weapon, or a shield can be wielded either by your character's left or right hand. Larger weapons are restricted to two hands. Pressing the trigger buttons allows the figure to attack, heal, or whatever is necessary to survive. You can choose to fight however you want, by taking a head on hack and slash approach or my preferred method of stealth. However you play, you are sure to have fun.

A few downfalls are, of course, to be expected. There is so much to do and so many sidequests that I feel overwhelmed to get them all done. I get distracted and do not finish the quest I was originally doing, because of all the subplots. Also, I am frustrated that it doesn't matter where you strike an enemy. I could shoot an arrow in someone's head six times and it does no more damage than if I hit them in the toe. Some glitches have occured where I have been able to see through walls, but does not alter gameplay. I have experienced the game freezing on multiple occasions, but it may because my console is a few years old.

review_headline: If you saw the trailer and thought, "This game is gonna be epic!" READ THIS FIRST!
review_body:
As you can imagine from the title, I saw the trailer for this game and immediately added it to my list of upcoming titles to try. The graphics looked fantastic, the fight scenes and monsters glorious and the storyline possibilities EPIC. However, when I played the game for the first time, I felt there was a drastic difference between the game I saw in that trailer and the game I was playing. I'm not going to sit here and tell you this game is terrible or this game is awesome, I'm going to describe my experience and let you decide for yourself if it's something you should invest your $40 and your time in.

Graphics:

Again, because of the trailer, I was expecting characters, monsters and scenery in beautiful detail. However, I wasn't impressed at all. The characters themselves are rendered well, but the scenery looks blocked and fuzzy. At first I thought it was just poorly rendered, but it seems almost stylized, it's hard to tell. Either way, I wasn't very impressed.

Gameplay:

Inventory is infinitely customizable, but you need components in order to do it. Although I didn't play very far into the game, the time I did spend yielded very few of these. You can improve really anything in your possession: weapons, armor, build traps or craft healing potions, which is a cool feature. Perhaps later you have access to more components, but initially this versatility wasn't very useful as I couldn't get what I needed. The first 10 level ups came rather quickly and gave ample opportunities to increase skills in one of three categories, so you're not stuck in one fighting class.

Expect battles to be difficult. I started the game on what equates to the 'average' difficulty setting, expecting it to be easy at first until you acclimate to the controls and combat but boy was I wrong. If you don't sit back, plan your moves, block patiently, set traps and use everything else at your disposal constantly, then be ready to die, over and over and over. It's fight or die, right from the get go and this really soured the game for me. If an all out struggle for survival is what you want every battle, this game is for you. You must strategize and be patient, button mashing is out of the question.

Areas are expansive as well. You can't clear an area of enemies and then hunt for treasure, they continually respawn. Even if you manage to clear part of a level, the day/night cycle will bring them back. Combined with the difficulty of battles, exploration is just tedious and frustrating. This was another point that really soured the game for me. Even the first town is fairly large and although you can't talk with everyone, there is still a fair number to get through. Conversations can be quite lengthy if you exhaust all your options. In the first town, it is possible to spend 1 to 2 hours exploring everything there is to offer. For me, this tipped the scales, the game became more work than play and I'm in the process of selling it back.

Again, I'm not telling you this game is good or bad, simply my experience with it. I was expecting an action RPG that was mainly action with a bit of RPG, but got just the opposite. If you want expansive levels, oodles of customization, side quests, allies and sometimes maddeningly difficult combat, then this game is probably for you. If you're looking for mostly action with a bit of customization and something not too lengthy or involved, this is probably not the game for you.

review_body:
Originally skeptical with the few reviewers giving low ratings, I decided to take the plunge seeing as it is only $8. The controller is fantastic for emulators. Highly recommended if you are into retro gaming. You may have to configure the buttons specifically on the emulator itself, but its not an issue at all. On Windows 7 its just plug and play, but if you want the vibration features, you will need to install the drivers. Depending on the emulator/game you will get vibration support.

As for playing other games, I haven't tried any others, but I did try Castle Crashers from Steam. The game works great, and there is no configuration needed. I found this suprising as I would like the ability to remap keys if I wanted to, but it does work, so nothing too crazy there.

If you install the drivers, you can actually see the precision of the analog sticks. If you need absolute precision, this is where the controller falls short. For retro gaming, and Castle Crashers this isn't a major problem, but the drivers seem to show some sort of deadzone on the sticks, before it registers a move. I would say its about a 20%'ish deadzone, a little more than the accidental brushes of moving the stick to register.

As far as the look and feel, it looks and feels just like the Playstation 2 controllers. Nothing more, nothing less. I will say that the Etekcity logo on the front of the controller is not what you get, rather it appears to be some chinese company slapping their logo on it. The packaging does say Etekcity on it though. Nevertheless, this whole branding thing doesn't effect the performance or feel of the controller in anyway.

I will say that the value of this controller is fantastic, and I will give it 5 stars despite the deadzone on the analog stick, its not a problem for me but it may be for others. If you want a controller to play Castle Crashers with a couple of friends, or play a few retro games this is the controller to get. At less than $8 you will be very hard pressed to find anything better, while still providing all the functionality this controller provides.

I want to keep this simple - Dark Souls 2 is another great game, equally as impressive as it's predecessors. But I also want to tell you about what to to expect.

First of all you don't need to play the other two games before attempting this one - they are all separate stories and experiences. Dark Souls 2 is almost identical to Dark Souls though in a lot of the mechanics of the game. I really recommend picking up the other two first - they are bound to be available at lower prices now, so it would be ideal to start with those and then move onto this one...so I am going to review this assuming that readers have played both of the original games.

So yes players should feel immediately at home. There is a tutorial session to start you off, with some easy enemies and some very mild predicaments to get through - plus a few nasty surprises of course, to make sure you get used to dying! Once this is over you will reach the games central hub, which is the place you need to return to over and over again to level up. Branching from here are paths to other places to explore, and as usual, nothing is really spelled out for you, so off you roam, attempting to explore areas and discover new items, weapons and armour, open new doors and try to kill everything before it kills you.

As you'd expect, the environments are spectacular. Castles, ruins, lakes, forests, pits and dungeons, everything you would expect is here. Enemies are merciless, so you have to take every precaution to fight well and never be lazy or impatient. This makes for nail biting gameplay, and as before, huge relief when you reach a milestone or a bonfire.

Changes players may have heard about...fast travel between bonfires is now available from the start - this is a great idea. Most notably for soul gathering, because the reward for making it to a bonfire is that if you save/rest, and then walk back the other way that you originally came from, nearly all the enemies will now no longer be able to surprise you, in fact a lot of them have their backs to you. Sweet revenge! You'll need to make the most of advantages like this to gather more souls, as enemies do not respawn forever any more, so eventually you'll be playing a game with a lot of empty and lonely environments (if you replay each one to the point where the enemies don't come back any more). Good news for cowards (like me) in that you can now make clear runs to reach bosses, rather than arrive at a boss gate every time with half your healing supplies wasted on the route just to get there. Particularly kind at pathways like the one with the gang of corrosive mushroom beetles which was right by a bonfire - so there was no running by that impediment without all your weapons and armour falling apart. Those beetles had to DIE!

Apart from this almost everything else is the same. There are tons of weapons, armour, spells and items, and by the end my inventory was overflowing with stuff I never used. You can't try and use everything, but the game lets you choose your own style, so you can focus on what works for you. Bosses are of course as punishing as before, and very cruelly, some ( The Pursuer, the Smelter Demon) become available at a time when you have no chance of beating them, but of course when you take up certain challenges is up to you.

There are still things I don't like. I play for the in-game challenge only and I really resent the fact that other players can invade your game and kill you for fun, if you play online. I think this causes frustration, and there should have been a way to block invasions in the system options. I did resort to starting in offline mode a number of times just to stop this.

If anything though, I think Dark Souls 2 is actually kinder than the two first games. The fast travel between bonfires and the clearing out of enemies can be a real relief. Reports on the fact that each death lowers your maximum health bar isjust scaremongering - in the previous games, being dead (\\"hollow\\") always made you play with a shorter health bar. Here it just gets gradually shorter starting from the full amount - and it stops once you reach halfway, so this is actually hardly different at all. Plus, not long into the game you get a ring that makes health loss stop at three-quarters full, which, once you find you will equip immediately and never remove again. Make sure you don't miss it! On that topic, it's hard to resist playing the game without constant reference to online forums and guides, as everything is so cryptic within the game itself. Some of it's secrets are so well hidden, chances are you'd never ever stumble on them without help. Using on line help is the cowards way out...it would taker stronger nerves than mine to play without assistance of any kind.

I still recommend Dark Souls 2 wholeheartedly. Be brave and dive in, as even the scarediest player will eventually learn how to progress, and the thrill of beating the bosses is unrivalled in my experience of gameplay, because you really earn it every time. So at first I had no idea what this adapter was to be used for but as I looked more into this I realized it was the perfect thing. The fact that you can use "any" 3.5mm plug headphones with this is the biggest bonus ever If you've invested in some high end headphones well you now have a use for them on your Xbox One. You can have game sound and chat come through your headphones. Let me tell you its quite awesome. For those nights you are playing late and don't want to disturb your spouse or just want to be able to hear all the sounds in your game.

The adapter has 5 buttons. 2 of which control whether you hear just the game sound or just the chat from others. Depending on which of those you choose you can manipulate the volume for either. Then of course there is the mute button in the center of the adapter. It glows orange when you are muted so there is no second guessing whether people can hear your personal conversations or not.

If you have Turtle beach headphones then the included adapter which converts 2.5mm to 3.5mm so you have use them for chat as well as have them still connected to your game.

The adapter isn't obstructive to gameplay either so you don't have to really worry about it getting in the way. I did find that when its time to unplug to charge my controller it takes a bit of effort to unplug it.

In conclusion I highly recommend this adapter.

review_headline: Fun for a short time, but soon forgotten
review_body:
Watch Dogs is a game that is loaded with content. By now you've read the reviews and heard about all the side missions and minigames that literally litter the Chicago landscape of Watch Dogs' world. There's just one problem... all the content doesn't add up to some kind of cohesive whole.

Graphically, Watch Dogs looks decent (Xbox One version), but I wouldn't call it "next gen." That's not to say the graphics are bad, but you do get the feeling that on these newer systems they could have been much better.

This is easily forgivable if a game has a great story and content to pull you along from start to finish. In my opinion, this is where Watch Dogs falls woefully short. The plot is a mess of hacker movie clichés and inane plot threads that loosely link together a story that, by the midpoint you'll find yourself asking, "Why the hell am I doing this again?". Not to mention that Aiden is the worst main character I've ever played in a game. He's just... boring. There's no other way to say it than that.

Watch Dogs has fun moments. Once you get past the first hour, the entire world opens up to you, and there's a ton of mini games to divert your attention from the sub-par main campaign. Each of these are fun, but only for a while. It really feels like the developers just threw a bunch of ideas at the wall and said, "Ooo that's fun, throw it in!"

In the end, Watch Dogs ends up being a briefly fun and soon forgettable experience. My recommendation is to wait until the price comes down and read reviews other than 10/10 "OMG BEST GAME EVER" and get an honest feel for this game's good and bad before you decide whether or not to buy the game.

review_headline: Amazing Spiderman 2 PS4 Great Game But Spidey Can't Swim

This is a comparison to the Spiderman 3 game on PS3. I don't own the first Amazing Spiderman Game but I do own Spiderman 3 Movie Game on PS3.

I really like this game the missions are fun and I love the petty crimes and other side missions but were the free roaming disappoints is Spiderman can't swim in any body of water compared to Spiderman 3 were he could swim in lakes as well as ponds and even in the sewers. This feature shouldn't have been left out of the amazing spiderman 2 game as this is also a free roaming game.

Pros
I love the car chase missions. Their much better then they was in Spiderman 3 and the cars are easiier to catch.

The fighting mechanics and interactions seem much better in this game then they did in SP3.

There is a Fast Web Slinging interaction that can get you to a distant building real quick. This can get you to were you need to go faster.

If you ordered from Gamestop like I did you get a code to get 4 additional spiderman outifts including the black suit. The game comes with a lot to. The game ones have to be unlocked and found. Once you find them you have access to any spiderman outfit by going to the closet. You go to Peter Parker's grandmother's house and once you unlock it it shows on the map and you catch a train to it. This is were you switch spider suits.

Comicbook shoip lets you play an arcade machine that lets you practice fighitng and Stan Lee owns it. You can even replay missions you've beaten here.

You can choose to do free roam,petty crime missions,fire rescues,photo missions,races or storymode.

Playing on PS4 and the fact that this is a newer spiderman game the city is more beautiful then it was in SP3.

Cons
Freeroaming game that won't let you swim. They missed the mark here.

NYC seems smaller then it did in SP3. I haven't seen the island that is out to itself of course I just started playing the game.

The map doesn't show every spot unless it's unlocked. Eg I don't see a way to get to the subway. You can't zoom in to specific buildings on this map. You could with SP3.

Suits seem like they have to be upgraded per outfit so for the black suit you'll need to upgrade the armour on it when you start playing.

Unlike SP3 sometimes there are places in this game that won't allow Spidey to shoot webs.

Camera and controls are very aggrevating especially the camera.

I also have Spiderman 2 on the PS2 and it also has the peddy crime and hospital missions.

This is my first game on the PS4 and I'm pretty amazed. The graphics are very beautiful and amzing. I have my ps4 hooked up via hdmi to a hd tv which I just bought. The city looks very alive and the npc pedestrians look a lot better then they ever did in a spiderman game on ps3. What a great first game on the ps4. I'm amazed. The only thing that keeps me from giving it 5 stars is no ability to swim in the large bodies of water like I can do in Sp3 on ps3.

I also recommend Spiderman 3 on PS3 if you can still find it but SP3 on PS2 is not the same and is watered down. Get the PS3 version.

What I really can't wait for though and the reason I bought a PS4 is Batman Arkham Knight which allows you to drive the batmobile and is the last batman game of the seriies. The city is much bigger also. Batman Arkham Knight will only be available to PS4,Xbox 1 and PC. It won't be coming out on PS3 or the Xbox 360.

It's okay. Nothing spectacular. The original Metro 2033 is much better.

Both games are as linear as can be but in the original the challenging scenarios, story, atmosphere and characters were so amazing and immersive that you didn't really care. Even after finishing it you wanted to play it again just to re-experience those things. At least, I did.

Last Light offers almost none of that. To me it comes off as just another dumbed-down, generic rail-shooter capitalizing on the unique appeal of it's predecessor.

I don't know... The game IS good, I suppose, maybe better than I imagine but it shares very little of the things that I thought made 2033 such a great game. This may serve to exaggerate my disappointment.

If you have never played 2033 I recommend you play Last Light first and 2033 after. Why? Well. first of all Last Light simply does not offer the greatness of the original. It'll be less of a let down if you go ahead and play it first and because Last Light doesn't hinge on 2033 there is no need to play them in order to get a proper "feel" for the second installment.

Yes, the beginning of Last Light will give away some of the things that will happen in 2033 but c'mon, we aren't babies. We already know pretty much how all these games play out anyway and by the time you get around to 2033 you'll probably have forgotten most of what they showed you about it.

So, why the 4 stars? Because it's Metro, silly!

I had a long standing preorder for the RetroN 5, which is good considering the price went up since it was announced (thank you Amazon Price Guarantee).  The thing people have said about having to hold the power button for several second to start the unit is true, and a bit weird, but other than that it seems to live up to it's hype.  So far I've thrown some NES, SNES, and GBA carts at it and it has handled them all mostly flawlessly.  It pulled in my save from Zelda 2 a bit garbled (I started with Thunder magic for some reason, and my name was just ink instead of Link), but I blame that more on a 25+ year old battery in the cartridge than the RetroN reading the save.  It couldn't automatically identify my copy of Megaman Zero, but it played it fine regardless.  The included controller isn't exactly the most ergonomic or well designed thing, but it is still leaps and bounds above the normal cheapy clone system pack in controllers, and it is rechargeable via USB (Hyperkin even gives you a port on the unit, and a cable, how nice of them).  This is a semi moot point if you and vintage supported controllers (NES, SNES, or Genesis) as it can just map them to whatever you need them to be (the manual gives the example of playing a 4 player NESgame using 2 SNES pads, a Genesis pad, and the pack in wireless controller).  The internal system upscaling to HD is far superior to the upscaling hardware in my TV.  If you don't like how SD res systems look on your TV this is a great solution.  As of launch there are a few features that haven't been implemented yet, the biggest of which being support for cheats, nor does the Retron 5 website seem to mention upgrades anywhere at launch. My only other gripe is the price.  The system is nice, and does what it promised it would do (for the most part), but the original $100 price point was hard enough to swallow, let alone the marked up price that units are going for at launch.  If you are considering one and are on the fence you might want to wait for the promised firmware updates to materialize, and to catch a unit on some sort of sale.  If you are fine paying what is being asked for, you probably will not be disappointed by what you receive.

Have you ever heard a new song, and thought, wow, this is the greatest song i've ever heard? The song is stuck in your head and you need to play it for your friends, so you talk the song up all week long, telling all your pals just how great it is, and how it's like nothing you've ever heard, and then you finally get the chance to play this song for all your buddies, and then they hear it, and no one likes it... Yeah that's how I felt playing this.
Square Enix toted this game as something that it was not. The idea was creative, but the game itself was not. It feels thrown together, and rushed. You have the illusion of making choices and solving puzzles, but the choices you make have no consequence at all, ,and if you make the wrong choice you can keep guessing as much as you like. the areas where you find clues are laughable, you just walk around a small area and find the clues, oh, and the clues glow!
The game is so short too, it took me all of 6 hours to get through it, I even took my time and did some side missions (I think there are only 3 or 4 total, and take about 5 min to solve) The only challenge in the game are the demons. after the first couple encounters, you quickly realize, you can just stealthy walk past them, no need to encounter them at all! HA! Also another laughable note is that the only way to get rid of a demon, is to sneak up on it! yeah, you read right, you have to SNEAK UP ON A DEMON! So as silly as that sounds, you can only hide by stepping into a residual ghost energy. You can't crouch, you can't jump, you can't "sneak" even, you just slowly walk up behind a demon and hit your prompt buttons. Yes, it is as lame as it sounds.
For me the A.I. had to be the worst part of the game, The few residents out and about that you could "possess" to read there minds had about 5 different thoughts amongst everyone. so if you possessed someone towards the beginning of the game, you were likely to hear the exactsame thoughts about 20 times in different people through out the rest of the game, that's just laziness on Square Enix's part. And the aspect of "possession doesn't really even work on people, just a cat. the cat is the most interesting part of the entire game, possessing the cat allows you to get into some tight spots and find some bonus items. Unfortunately the cat was only used in one mission!
There is absolutely no sense of urgency in this game, you can take as long as you want with no consequence what so ever. and what really bothered me about that, is the game takes place all in one night! You die, at the hands of a cereal killer you've been hunting for some time, you learn to be a ghost, you find a friend in the living realm that can see you. You solve some mysteries about the case, you hunt down the killer, and case closed! ALL IN ONE NIGHT!!! The time line of the game is maybe a few hours! It's just bad writing and development.
There were so many things that could have made this game better! Better A.I. for one, longer story, more side mission, bigger map, etc,. etc. etc...

I'm ranting, I'm sorry. I really wanted to like this game! I did! I was excited to play it. I guess I was expecting too much? I know Square Enix is capable of producing good games! We've seen it before with Tomb Raider, and Deus Ex... Just so disappointing.

product_title: Nancy Drew: Message in a Haunted Mansion - PC
review_headline: Great Older Game - One of the Classics
review_body:
First of all, when you install this game on a newer operating system, take the following steps to ensure it will play:

1.) Create a folder under "Program Files," I called mine "Nancy Drew." If you're going to play many of the older games, you might want to create a sub-heading with the name of the game.
2.) When you're installing the game, change the install location to your created Nancy Drew or specific game sub-folder instead of the default it gives.

Solves the INI error issue. :) And you're playing!

This is one of the original 5 Nancy Drew games. Definitely one of the best of the 5, I think it outshines both Secrets Can Kill and Stay Tuned For Danger.

You play Nancy Drew, gone to San Fransisco to help with the renovations on an old mansion. However, there have been some mysterious accidents, and the owner, Rose, is getting fed up. You have full run of the mansion as Nancy, and there are 4 characters to interact with in-person, and 3 people reachable by phone. You can change the time of day by using Nancy's alarm clock in her bedroom, which is important when you want to make sure people are (or aren't!) around the areas you're exploring. It's a pretty straight-forward point and click mystery game other than that, but the story is very strong, and the voices, music, and sound effects are top-notch. Even if you're used to the newer games with the cell phone, task list, and notepad, if you haven't played this game, you're missing out.

A+ Game. Just make sure you take the time to change the install location to avoid the dreaded error message when you try to play.

product_title: D.I.R.T. Origin of the Species - PC
review_body: Very Nice with a few minor flaws that didn't take away from the enjoyment value for me.    Lets cover the cons first.     First, the copy protection system. I noted, as noted in another review, it was StarForce. It was and in my case it was an outdated version that was included with the game. Since I collect a lot of older game titles, I'm not surprised to run into this. What did surprise me was the lack of a system DLL I needed to even run the copy protection driver at all. After adding this DDL to the system, the copy protection system loaded OK.  The next thing I ran into was that the Copy Protection system didn't support Win 7. Since this was a game not originally made for Win 7, this didn't surprise me either and after going online, I found the needed update for this item. I ran it and it did what it was made to do, checked the DVD in the drive to make sure it was a legal DVD. After that the game loaded and I was able to play it. (As an aside, I have had many games that use a CD or DVD drive disk check before you can run a game and to this time, I'm still using the drive I originally installed on my system without any problems. I did note that this game loading system seems a bit more intrusive than some do, but I have used those before too. Most of the time the user isn't notified unless the game CD or DVD isn't in the drive.)  Anyway after this long \\"run-around\\" the game play OK.     Second item.     The game will support a Xbox 360 gamepad BUT in my case I had to set up every button on the pad one by one. The manual seems to indicate that that's not needed and all you have to do was select the \\"default options\\" and reset it and the gamepad would be \\"seen\\". This didn't work for me and I had to set them up one at a time. Not a huge problem but worth considering.     Those things out of the way, the game plays very well on my system (Win7 Ultimate SP-1 32-bit P4 3.0, 4 gigs RAM, HIS  HD4670, 1 gig RAM at ViewSonic running at 1366x768 in 32 bit colors. Not the latest but all I can effort now.) I fooled around with it a bit and it's smooth and seems easy to move around. The only thing I need to do now is finish fine-tuning the gamepad and that will remove some small problems.  Runs very well so far. I'll update if I run into something, but it's a nice game.

I am pretty new to the Tales series but love it very much and feel like I've known the series forever.

STORY: The storyline for Tales of Xillia is a mixture of fantasy, fiction, with a hint of sci-fi. It's definitely not the best story I've ever heard but it gets the job done and has substantial rewards when you play it all the way through to the end. Two protangonist, means two different paths, two different perspectives and finally two different endings. B

GAMEPLAY: Tales of Xillia plays much like it's predecessors only with a heck of a lot more style and attachments :) Xillia introduces us to the \\"Double Raid Linear Motion Battle System\\" or DR-LMBS, which you and another character combine your artes to make a whole new and powerful attack. Some characters work better with certain characters then others but is still a very nice addition to the combat system. Also, each character has their own mystic artes with their unique abilities as well as support skills. The environment in which you traverse with your party is new but at the same time pretty bland with minimal interaction besides finding treasure chests and the occasional \\"Aifreads Treasure\\" which sole purpose is to alter your character's appearance. Also, the atmosphere in Fenmont (a place you will travel) is absolutely beautiful! A-

CHARACTERS: Not much to say here, other than the fact that they are all very well thought out and unique. Each has a back story with the two main protagonist's having the most though. My personal favorites are Jude and Leia. :) A

SOUND: Xillia isn't going to win any awards for best sound, but it is pretty good and memorable melodies that you will most likely have stuck in your head for a while. Songs match their environment/scene to the letter. Also, I don't know if anybody else notices this but I noticed when you switch your party leader, their footsteps sound different due to them having different footwear. Usually they all sound the same-in any game but I thought that was pretty cool. A

OVERALL: This game is an insta-buy for anybody who like JRPGs or just RPGs in general. The game's atmosphere is absolutely stunning as well as it's gorgeous artwork. Buy this, you will not regret it. A++e same-in any game but I thought that was pretty cool. A

Many games I enjoy are, unfortunately, forgotten by the annals of time. Games that I feel are unique and invigorating, a solid break from the usual hokum this industry offers and a concentrated effort of original ideas are, unfortunately, mauled critically for their unwillingness to conform to industry norms and current trends. It happened to personal favorites "Wet," "Enslaved: Odyssey to the West," and last year's excellent "Remember Me." These were experiences that, while definitely not the most polished in the world, were nevertheless worthy of commendation and praise based on the very purpose of their existence. By my standards, a game should not be reviewed based on how pretty it is, or how much it's like whatever's big on the market at that moment in time. It should be judged on how fun it is, and what it brings to the table in terms of what content it's trying to put forth, whether that be tactical gameplay, mindless chaos, or narrative depth.

And from where I stand, "Murdered Soul Suspect" was squarely focused on that last one, perhaps even at the expense of other gameplay elements. But the thing is? Those other elements actually work, and in fact, don't really hinder the game at all. Everything else in the piece simply exists to further the plot, and never really bothers to hamper the player with padding or artificial difficulty. What we're left with, then, is a game that has a fantastic story leagues above anything out there, aided by simple yet engaging gameplay which serves its purposes admirably and without fault, complemented by an interesting art direction and elegant score. For a game that many contemporaries are savaging for not being enough of one thing or another, I feel like too few people are really appreciating this game on its own merits, or appreciating it for what it truly is.

And what is it? Well, at its core, it's a modern-day noir mystery engaged in a head-on collision with a classic ghost story. "Murdered" follows detective Ronan O'Connor, who's hot on the trail of a vicious serial murderer known only as The Bell Killer. A little wrench gets thrown in his case, though, when he's hurled out of a window, then shot in the chest seven times. He dies on the spot, but the game doesn't end there. Ronan, unsatisfied with how his life ended, must roam the streets of Salem as a ghost, trying to solve his murder and get some sense of closure before he can move onto the next plane of existence with his deceased wife, Julia. But to do that, he'll need to enlist the help of Joy, a sassy delinquent who happens to be a spiritual medium... and quite possibly the next target of the killer. As Ronan helps Joy find her missing mother, and she helps him solve the murders, players will be dragged along a winding plot of twists and turns that genuinely manage to surprise and engage.

There's no superlative that I can immediately drudge up to describe how bizarre and wonderful Anna Megill's script for this game is. Some may call it inconsistent in tone, or scattershot in its approach, but to me, that's actually part of the charm. Much like SWERY's perverse masterpiece, "Deadly Premonition," "Murdered" throws several things at the wall and doesn't really care what sticks. The result is a game that is thrilling yet darkly humorous, disturbing but still somehow lighthearted. It's really unlike anything else that's come out this year, in the narrative department, and it takes some interesting risks that most writers would shy away from out of fear of being a bit too risky, a bit too "out there." And because of this, it comes across as patently genuine, something that I really can't say for many games, or movies, or books. This is not a story that is meant to have mass appeal, or to "broaden the audience" of the game. Instead, the narrative of "Murdered" is a heartfelt piece with equal amounts of pathos and humor, not to mention a compelling core mystery that kept me guessing until the out-of-left-field, "what in the heck did I just play" finale.

Part of what makes this narrative so good, I feel, is the massive amount of plot that exists within Salem itself. The game operates within a series of very small sandboxes, connected by the hub world of the town, and within all of these spaces exist numerous opportunities to expand the universe, explain character motivations, and even engage in entirely tangential plot threads. Ronan can help other ghosts pass on, or simply engage in clever banter with the deceased about their predicaments. NPCs in this game are handled well, ranging from deranged ghosts haunting people for varying reasons, to lost souls unable to realize that they're dead. Other narratives come in the form of collectible notes, objects, and other trinkets that actually serve purposes, instead of the obligatory and annoying trend of "audio logs" that modern games seem so attached to. From Julia's notes on her life and death, to the killer's modus operandi, players would be well-served finding and taking all of the narrative content this game has to offer. Rest assured, you won't find it on your first playthrough.

Another thing that does this game justice is the great characterization. Ronan is a fascinating character, fedora/trilby notwithstanding, and manages to nicely straddle the line of pulpy detective archetype and tortured man looking for redemption. And Joy, honestly, is one of the more refreshing female characters in gaming this year. She's resourceful and interesting, not ever held down by Ronan's commands or defined by any male characters. It's nice seeing interesting, well-written female characters in an industry where the norm is gradually becoming "white dudes do white dude stuff, and sometimes there's a girl or somebody who isn't white." The supporting cast is a bit less interesting, composed primarily of ancillary characters defined by collectible artifacts. While I do wish the core, driving cast was slightly larger, the fact remains the characters here are compelling and intriguing, and somehow, the writing makes you care for even the less important players. Good stuff, all around.

As stated above, the gameplay here simply exists to drive forward the plot, with one novel hook: you're a ghost. Airtight Games, historically, has promised big things but present games flawed in their execution, with their 2010 definition of mediocrity, "Dark Void" as a prime example of this. Naturally, I was very skeptical of their work here, yet somehow they've actually managed something quite interesting. Ronan, as a ghost, can walk through most objects and people, possess things, and affect real world objects. There's some disappointment on my part when it comes to this, because I feel like there was a lot of potential with this concept, and the result is kind of a compromise. See, certain things are "consecrated," and what that means for a player is that they cannot go through them. This applies to most of the buildings in the main hub, and it's disappointing that the world was, in fact, not my oyster as a ghost. Yet despite that, I did really feel empowered in the other departments. There's a definite pleasure in activating copiers or coffee machines to spook cops while Joy sneaks through a police station, or sprinting through walls in order to get to a place faster, as once you're inside a building virtually anything is fair game to ghost through. Despite compromises, I enjoyed the abilities I had at my disposal, and felt like they gave me an experience that was actually special and quirky. Think gritty "Ghost Trick" and you're halfway there.

As far as the actual detective mechanics go, things are very much like point-and-click adventure games of days past. Ronan walks around a crime scene, gathers clues, then mentally pieces together different things in order to reach conclusions. Sometimes, you'll need to collect a lot of clues, and others, only one or two out of the several available will need to be sniffed out. It falls in a nice, comfortable middle ground, where obsessive sleuths will want to hunt down everything in order to know every little detail, while more casual players will be okay with just getting what they need and progressing the story. Still, the game doesn't handhold you, and expects you to figure out how to find clues, where to find them, and the ways they fit together. It's a nice departure from, say, a David Cage game, which essentially smack players in the face with the answer before the question is even asked.

Speaking of demonic, soul-sucking entities (sorry, I still haven't gotten over "Beyond: Two Souls,") the combat in this game is mercifully nonexistent. From where I stand, too many developers find it necessary to implement shooter or brawler mechanics where they simply don't belong. Airtight, learning from its mistake with the last AAA title it was in charge of producing, decided to have players execute the antagonistic demons in a strategic, almost puzzle-esque fashion. Players are completely defenseless against them hand-to-hand, and must approach them from behind and perform a speedy exorcism. This makes a combat more of a cross between stealth and light survival horror, making strong use of the ghost abilities. Hiding through walls, and inside residual living spirit energy where the demons can't spot him, Ronan sneaks up the demons, sometimes employing distractions, and takes them out... or tries to simply sneak around them and get out of wherever they're roaming. It's a cool mechanic that remains faithful to the rest of the core experience, and doesn't simply try to lazily cop whatever else is out there.

Perhaps the only ill words I could speak of "Murdered" are that it was obvious Square Enix pushed Airtight into releasing this last-gen game on the current-gen consoles, as it really doesn't benefit from the horsepower of the PS4. It looks like an upscaled PS3/360 game, to be frank, but not bad by any stretch of the imagination. Anybody who actually buys a game based on graphics (read: too many people) might be patently offended that a game might dare to not run at 60fps and look like a cutscene out of a modern "Final Fantasy" at all times, but all others shouldn't be bothered too much, thanks to the great art direction and cool imagery. If I were to leverage a legitimate graphical complaint, though, it would be that the cutscenes are poorly compressed, and sometimes look a bit distorted. A shame, yes, but nothing truly upsetting or too distracting. All-in-all, it's a decent-looking game that is greatly aided by designers that put some serious effort and thought into Salem and its inhabitants.

How do I review a game like "Murdered Soul Suspect"? Yes, it has definite flaws, and might not be the most polished game in the world yet... yet it's still subjectively better by my standards than so many things released today. This is the concentrated effort of a developer to release something smart, something that's unlike anything else being trotted out from a major publisher. Honestly, I have to applaud Square Enix for releasing and funding something so rare and special. It's not a perfect experience, no, and it's not for everyone. Not by a long shot. Still, for those who want a great story with a bizarre, almost "so bad it's good" atmosphere, and gameplay that's more interesting than shooting or driving or bludgeoning, this is definitely for you. Even though it's not perfect, I have a feeling it will be one of those special gems that everybody else forgets about, but I will be recommending years from now.

Hopefully, it has a ghost of a chance with other players. Sorry, I had to.

Having purchased 99% of all gaming consoles dating back to the original Nintendo, I was excited for the new Xbox One. Upon opening and setting up the new console, I was excited to get the initial set up complete and throw in Titanfall and start playing. My excitement quickly faded when the initial set-up/download took over an hour and a half. After the download for the set-up was finished, I decided to check my internet connection and it was working at a fast speed with no foreseeable problems which drew more questions. I then went to type in the code to download the Titanfall game that was included in my bundle. After close to 3 hours, the download was only at 7% and I became worried. Still not wanting to give up on the Xbox one before I had even played it yet, I decided to throw in a game my wife had gotten and the console made me do an immediate update for her game which only took half an hour. Once the update was completed, it made me download the game to the hard drive which took an hour and a half. After her game finally finished downloading, she played it for about 20 minutes before we headed to bed for the night. Thinking that leaving the console for the next few hours to let Titanfall download seemed like a good idea. When I woke up in the morning and not only had the game not downloaded but the Xbox had turned off right after I went to sleep. When I turned the console on in the morning, the download had stopped and had gone back down to 1%. Just to be clear, I don't have a slow internet connection and the downloads were still taking forever to get anywhere at all. I've always been a fan of Microsoft, but it seems like they're going away from wanting to have user friendly systems and wanting to make a non-user friendly system that's as high tech as they can get it with taking away from user control. This is the worst system I've ever purchased and I will have a full refund by the end of the week. Despite the positive reviews on this page, please read user reviews online and you'll see the massive amount of complaints dealing with incredibly slow download times. A few things to keep in mind before purchasing this console..... the graphics are the exact same as the 360. Also, when a new system comes out for purchase there are several things you expect. You should expect it to be more streamlined and smaller with the new technology that's out there. With the xbox one, you get none of these things. The console itself is big and bulky and the new Kinect is twice as big as the 360 version. If you're seriously considering purchasing the Xbox One and are a fan of Microsoft gaming consoles, please just stick with the Xbox 360 and like I stated before, if you don't believe my review, look on all the Xbox One blogs online and you'll see how much it really is sinking in popularity. Thanks
