I bought this just a couple of months ago, obviously several years after its release. To me, a game like this isn't really worth the full asking price. I play it occasionally as a multi-player game with family members, and for that purpose it's fun. We run around and shoot at things and occasionally get mauled by zombies or shot by enemy soldiers.

I've been working on the campaign a little from time to time, and it's fun overall. I do hit some sections where the directions seem unclear about what the game expects me to do next. I'm thinking that perhaps Call of Duty veterans probably have a better instinct for how the games tend to play out, and the campaign is just tuned toward them with just a little less pointing at the next target than I could use. It isn't too bad though. There've been two times so far that I had to start a mission over entirely to get into the flow of things and figure out what the computer had been intending for me to attempt to do all along.

I actually like the fact that it's not quite as skill-driven as some of the FPS games that put a really heavy emphasis on your skills and knowing everything about every weapon. It's a lot easier for someone to pick this up and play occasionally with friends and family than seems to be possible with those games. On the other hand, for extremely hard core players it doesn't offer quite as much room for growth and for continuing to challenge yourself as some other choices do.

One place where they really do an exceptional job is on the characters in the Zombie levels. Everyone has their own sayings, there's some really good humor mixed in, and the characters really come through over time. In just little snippets shouted out here and there in automatic response to what's happening in the game, you can get a sense of their relationships to each other and who they are. I was surprised how well it was done.

Edit: I just want to add that, if your primary goal is playingwith random people online that the system pairs you with, I wouldn't worry too much about getting the expansions/map packs. There's still a solid pool of people playing the core game Zombies and Multiplayer, but fewer playing on the expansion maps. They're still fun(particularly if you have a few friends you can set up times to play with, or if you prefer playing alone) but it can be sorta irritating waiting around for a game to get set up by the automated matching system on the less-used maps.

review_headline: Mass Effect for the Strategy Gamer, with a B-movie Flare
review_body:
I'll start off by saying I've never played the original XCOM, so there'll be no comparisons made for that. However, I've totally played Mass Effect, and this follows a somewhat similar premise: mysterious aliens are out to get humanity, and the player is out to defend it. It approaches this premise with a similar mix of high-level strategy and tactical squad-based combat, but gives actual game-play an emphasis that Mass Effect left only for the plot.

Long term decisions matter in terms of actual game-play, and missions are very engrossing turn based tactical affairs. If a soldier in your squad dies (mind you, you personally create and customize every single soldier you field, promoting them over missions to become hand-picked badasses) then they stay dead. You can't restart missions, or go to your autosave, or anything. They die if you screw up, and sometimes if the aliens are just really on their game - and its awesome. This stroke of genius gives XCOM characters a personal stake that other games just can't achieve through scripted scenes and cheap death. Each character and each playthrough is a unique experience, with events, tactics, and decisions unfolding in a myriad of different ways.

The depth of gameplay and the level of customization/replayability that XCOM offers makes it an excellent choice by any standard, but especially for this rather strategy-barren system.
Basically, buy this game.

If you buy it and like it, then maybe try out CIVILIZATION REVOLUTION, R.U.S.E., or COMMAND AND CONQUER: RED ALERT 3

What can I say? It's the follow-up, or soul-successor, rather, to the great Snatcher, also by Hideo Kojima. This game is similar to its predecessor, but it is not a direct sequel. It is a new story with new characters in new locations, but it carries a whiff of nostalgia to anyone who has played the original. It shares the same mechanics, but each of them are presented here more refined and detailed: instead of just clicking through and selecting different phrases or options, you get to click around the screen and delve into details from newspaper clippings to a cigarette-butt filled ash tray. You are given a bevy of information and get a glimpse of main character's consciousness, his thoughts, his memories, his feelings. You can flirt with stewardesses, you examine billboards...hell, you can even check your office's answering machine from time to time. Every little thing in this game seems to have a meaning or story behind it, for example: if you examine a cigarette, you'll be given long descriptions of how cigarettes no longer give off second-hand smoke, or how they don't need to be lit with fire anymore, but rather, are lit with a pinch (but they don't burn). Seriously, I'm in awe of Kojima's genius. He really knows how to weave a story and create other worlds for the players to explore. The level of immersion is without compare. The shooting mechanics have also been expanded and perfected from the original (Snatcher). They are far more fun. More suited for using a lightgun. I really hope to see re-releases of these games. It'd be great to receive an English version here in the US someday. Maybe Kojima will release the two games in a double pack here in the States sometime in the future. I can only hope. It's just too bad that I can't really recommend this game to anyone unless they know Japanese. Really, it's a shame we never received an English translation, because this one would have been a hit.

review_headline: Great system and games, but one small gripe. If you can work with/around it, get the system. If not, you should pass.
review_body:
I think it's great that Amazon offered up a Vita bundle like this. Being that it was Black Friday and I didn't own a Vita yet (not to mention that I'd missed a lot of great bundles in the past because I didn't act fast enough), I jumped on this opportunity. When this was first listed for $260, I wasn't really enticed, but when it dropped to $175, I knew it was a great value. All the games are digital downloads and are easy to get onto the system.

That being said though, I wish that this bundle came with a larger memory card, or just flat-out gave some of the games to you as physical copies instead of digital downloads. Hard copies do not take up nearly as much space as much of the game is stored on the game card itself; in fact, as far as I know, only the save data of the game is actually put on the Vita, and these files are very small. You only get a 4GB card in this bundle, which can only hold The Walking Dead, Sly Cooper, or Uncharted at any one time (they're each about 3GB), along with Retro City Rampage (which is tiny, at something like 50MB). If you have a PS3 or PC with enough hard drive space, you can download the games there and copy them back and forth between the PS3/PC and Vita whenever you want to play them. It's annoying, but it's doable if you can't afford more for the proprietary Sony memory cards (which cost quite a bit). So if you are willing to spend some extra time shifting the games back and forth, or willing to spend more money on a larger memory card so that you don't even need to do the previous, then get the bundle. Otherwise, pass on it.

Still, the games are great and the system itself is fantastic. The only game I've yet to play is Uncharted, but given the series' popularity as a platformer, I'm sure I will enjoy that too. I quite like adventure games. The Vita itself is a very well-built system and has a great battery life. The screen also looks crisp and sharp. When I turned it up on full brightness, I felt like myeyes popped. Just wow. There are a lot of great games on the Vita, too, but seems to be lacking in FPS games as well as RPGs (though the former moreso than the latter). I like RPGs and JRPGs, and for me the selection (while small) is sufficient for the time being, though some of the actual selection comes from the PSP library. Also, I share my Vita with my brother. He's the complete opposite of me and he dislikes the Vita because it does not have as many FPS games as he had expected. So both of these are something to keep in mind.

Overall, I'd recommend this bundle to anyone who is looking to get a Vita. It's only gone up $5 since Black Friday, and still very much worth it. If the games interest you too, then that's even more reason. If not, you can at least sell off The Walking Dead code to a friend who's interested or something.

review_headline: More of the same Rocksmith! What's not to love?
review_body:
So many improvements from the first Rocksmith!
First I would like to say that as a guitar player, the original Rocksmith provided hours and hours of fun while learning to play some new songs. For that reason alone I would have bought this version just for the new songs to practice and learn. I was surprised to find how much Ubisoft was able to improve upon an already great product!

Features that used to take a long time to unlock, are now available from the beginning. Song difficulty is easy to change in the practice mode, so experienced players can turn up the difficulty so they aren't just plunking one or two notes during the whole song. You can also adjust difficulty for just a particular section of a song, so if you really want to focus on a solo or know the chords to a section, you can turn those sections up while letting the game adjust difficulty automatically in areas you might not know as well.

This game has also been fun for family members that do play guitar. The scaling difficulty really does allow players of all levels to play the game and most of the music is great and easy to listen to.

review_headline: The old barriers to a Vita purchase are gone or greatly reduced!
review_body:
The Playstation Vita is such an amazing handheld! I'd been eyeing a Vita for a long time, but several factors had always held me back have recently changed:

Price: The Vita finally got a much needed price cut a while back, dropping to $199 for a Vita WiFi model.

Memory Cards: Yes, the memory card prices were exorbitantly high, and they still are rather high. Amazon and other retailers have price cuts from time to time that makes it easier, but this is still by far the most bitter pill you have to swallow if you buy a Vita. Sony itself dropped the prices a little bit from their crazy prices at the launch.

Software Library: The myth is that the Vita has no games. This hasn't been true for quite some time now, in fact - I just bought a PS4 and I'm not thrilled with much that's out for the PS4 yet and the PS4 has basically become a Netflix machine while I wait for the types of PS4 titles in which I'm most interested. It's going to be a bit of a long wait. This is so unbelievably not true of the Vita. Uncharted, Killzone, Tearaway, the un-missable Persona 4 Golden (Buy this game even if you hate JRPGs), Ys Memories of Celceta, WRC 4, Gravity Rush, and the plethora of indie games out for Vita. There are more games for Vita than I have money or time to play right now.

OLED: The '2000' revision of the Vita is coming to the North America soon - it adds a very slightly longer battery life, micro-USB charging, and a minuscule amount of on-board memory but it drops the Vita's most endearing feature - that beautiful OLED screen! The '2000' model trades the OLED for an LED. This model with the OLED is the model you want! If you're thinking about getting a Vita, get these OLED originals before you can't find them anymore!

Now a basic review of the Vita itself:

The Vita is a marvel of handheld technology - the twin stick analogs are small, but compared to the single circle pad of the 3DS, they are vastly superior! Your thumbs will have no problem with sliding or finding the controls, especially if you've used a Dual Shock 3 or the amazing Dual Shock 4 controllers for Sony's Playstation 3 and 4 home consoles. The OS is very responsive and easy to figure out, although I haven't plumbed the depths of customizability yet (I'm too busy playing Persona 4 Golden - seriously, if you have a Vita, you simply MUST buy and play this game!). Everything is about where you'd expect it to be if you've used a modern smartphone OS recently. Apps and games show up as 'bubble' icons on swipe-able 'pages'. Loading times for games vary quite a bit, although unless you're switching apps/games often, you'll likely not notice as the 'sleep' state of the system has been a revelation for me. Regardless of save points or progress, you can hit the top 'power' button once quickly to immediately suspend whatever game or app you're in and come back immediately to exactly where you left off again by simply tapping the button again and swiping the blue page 'welcome back' screen. It's weird, but the lack of this 'pick up, put down' accessibility has really kept me from playing my PS3 or PS4 as often as I might otherwise, as even the simple and customary barriers of turning on home console, waiting for the UI, selecting the game, loading it, and then selecting 'continue' or finding the save and loading it are high enough barriers that I won't go through all that unless I'm in a 'I'm going to game for a few hours' mindset. The Vita has no such barriers - you just pick it up and, assuming you want to play the game you've already been playing, you just dive in right where you left off - no muss, no fuss. In a modern adult life with all it's interruptions, it really has been a blessing.

As for portability - the Vita is what I would call more of a 'transportable' system than a truly portable one - it's not pocket-friendly, being just too large to carry around with you everywhere yougo without a bag. If you're a teenager or young adult who carries a bag with you everywhere you go, this won't be a problem - but it doesn't have the 'pick up and play' quality that a modern smartphone does - however - the addition of actual game controls greatly makes up for this. I've stopped playing smartphone games due to the fact that FAR too many are moving to a 'free-to-play' model that makes them unforgivably 'grindy' or expensive. Platformers or 'twitch' games are ridiculous on smartphones as well, as touchscreen controls simply cannot give you the experience you'd want with those types of games. Lastly, gaming on a smartphone drains the battery inexcusably fast! You'd better have a charge cable at the ready, as even a quick game of Tilt-to-Live (let alone more graphically intensive games) can leave with with a dead battery far sooner than you might feel it should.

The screen - OMG that OLED! It is, quite simply, a beautiful thing! There's little more that can be said - blacks are black and colors are vibrant!

Ergonomics: The Vita falls short here, although the 3DS isn't much better. If you buy a Vita, buy a grip to go with it. I understand why Sony didn't add a more ergonomic fit to the Vita to begin with, as it would somewhat reduce its already limited portability, but for long sessions, you'll really be glad you got something to make things more comfortable.

And that's it, really. The rear touchscreen works as advertised, as do the gyro controls on games that use them. I'd just like to finish by saying that I've spent more time gaming on the Vita than on any of my home systems lately - that 'pick up and play' quality just can't be beaten. Heck, some of those clones are [[ASIN:B0037AF3HA HANDHELD SYSTEMS]], and they still plug into the TV! If you are an old school coin-op purist and want to have the luxury of owning the legendary sword slasher that dominated the 90s, this is the collection to pick up. product_title: Nintendo Wii U Deluxe Set: Super Mario Bros U & Luigi U (32 GB)
review_headline: Really glad I got this for Christmas for my kids!
review_body: Seems like there have been some real negative reviews over an unfortunate network breakdown from Nintendo's side that is being fixed as I type this out that has absolutely NOTHING to do with the hardware.  Yes, even I was affected by the crash on Christmas morning, but understood immediately that it was an overload problem and would be corrected in time.  For those who don't realize, this pretty much happens EVERY Christmas and is not because Nintendo sucks or they are stupid.  Netflix had a similar issue on Christmas one year.  Barnes and Noble had a similar issue on Christmas with the Nook a couple of years ago.  Internet systems crash all the time because of excess traffic.  It's happened to even the most robust of all gaming networks, Xbox Live.  The Wii U itself has been an absolute joy to own so far and the system has worked flawlessly.  I have been a long time Nintendo fan since purchasing the original NES back in 1987 with my own hard earned cash at the age of 13.  I've owned every Nintendo system since, but this was the first one I was a little hesitant with purchasing.  I am happy to say I couldn't have been more wrong in my hesitation.  My biggest fear was with one game pad that fighting would ensue between my two kids, 6 and 4 years old, or they would end up breaking the game pad.  Surprisingly, they have worked out sharing the game pad with almost no effort on my part (occasional arguments but we fix it pretty quick) and the pad itself seems very solid.  I know a lot of people will say the Wii U is not a "next gen" system and don't waste your money and get the Xbox One or PS4 instead.  Well, as much as I would love to get an Xbox One, spending $500+ on a console alone is not what most families can afford, mine included.  My decision to finally take a leap was the price drop with the included games along with more available game titles to purchase which the system was lacking, in my opinion, at release.  Also picked up Super Mario 3D World.  Since getting this hooked up the kids have been nothing but enthralled with the Wii U.  A small learning curve for them to be able to navigate the system menu, but they are completely in love with it.  I read a review were it was stated the game pad doesn't work.  I believe that persons unit is defective, because mine works perfectly with absolutely no issue from as far as about 30 feet from the Wii U out of line of sight.  I have it set up to control my TV and Direct TV box as well and it was, by far, the easiest "remote control" I have EVER programmed.  No codes, no magical button combinations, just "Who made your TV?" with a list.  I picked Panasonic and it was working immediately.  Same with the Direct TV box, it worked with almost no effort on my part.  I have it streaming Netflix and Amazon Prime with no problems.  I am looking forward to a lot of great Nintendo exclusives like MarioKart and Zelda.  I am really hoping to get a new Metroid game in the future, too!  I haven't tried doing the Wii transfer yet, but after reading another reviewer's comments I am definitely going to try it out soon.  Another big bonus is if you have a Wii than all of your remotes will work with the Wii U! If you are a Nintendo fan or have a family on a budget like us you will not be disappointed, I'm looking forward to many years of fun with this system!

review_headline: End of the Call of Duty franchise.  DOn't waste your money on this game.
review_body: Wow..... this is one of the biggest disappointments in video games in recent memory.  To start off, you have to install disc 2 to play disc 1 and use 2.9 GB of hard drive space, so if you do not have a 250 GB hard drive, you're going to have to delete some other files.  The graphics are very bland and average and honestly are substandard for a game that had this much hype.  Multiplayer is atrocious as the levels are too big.  What really makes multiplayer so bad is the spawning:  you literally spawn right in front of the enemies, so be prepared to go 5-25 or 3-18 repeatedly.  I played multiplayer for two days then got so pissed off I never touched it again.  The campaign mode is actually pretty interesting and different, but way too short.  Even on Veteran you're looking at 6-7 hours TOPS.  The loadouts for your characters are extremely confusing, having up to 10 characters and 10 slots per is just overkill.  Extinction mode is the best new feature, but its basically Horde mode from Gears of War.  COD: Ghosts is extremely average for an FPS and even diehard COD fans will have trouble giving this game a high rating.  This game can single handedly kill Infinity Ward and the COD franchise off.  I would not say this is a bad game, but its nowhere near being good.  Bland and average as can be, wait for this one to go to Greatest hits in a few months.  Very, very disappointing.

Been playing it for two hours and it's overwhelmingly... okay?

I loved and was mesmerized by the first two games. This game is certainly fine enough but, as was mentioned in other reviews, feels more like above-average DLC than a full-fledged game in its own rite.

The good... It's a Batman Arkham game, and it has all of the features of the old games, and the same engine, so there's no way to screw it up completely. It's always fun roaming the city and stopping crimes in progress, or finding stealthy ways to take on foes one by one. And one place in which this game really excels is giving you the assassins to fight. It's a nice change of pace from the usual Batman villains.

Now for the not so good...

First, the game purports to be a prequel in which Batman is young and inexperienced. That's great, but the game doesn't really sell that in any way that affects gameplay. The gadgets are the same and no less effective. The moves are the same and also no less effective. I would have liked the challenge of a Batman who had to rely on more physicality, or more intellectual detective work, and less gadgetry. Aside from the fact that many of the thugs don't seem to know who he is, and the fact that the returning characters look and sound younger, you wouldn't know that this was a prequel. Frankly, the decision to make it a prequel at all is curious; it's obvious that the only reasons why they did it was to bring the Joker back, and justify not bringing back the same voice actors.

Second, as I said above, the game itself really feels more like an expansion than a separate game. This is most obvious in the setting, which is basically the setting of Arkham City before it became a prison, plus an additional portion of Gotham across the bridge which is about half the size. So the sense of deja vu is enormous. That could have easily been fixed by having people walking the streets or having cars on the road. If Spider-Man gamescan do it, why not Arkham Origins? Sure, I get that WB had deadlines: they needed this game to hit the market before next gen consoles erased it from memory, so they had to cut corners, but it's a rather glaring omission here. The lack of innocents on the street was integral to the plot of Arkham City, as well as the feeling of isolation (though it's interesting and somewhat bizarre to note that there were in fact some innocents on the streets of Arkham City that Batman had to rescue). Here, it's just laziness. I would have settled for the addition of a bat-cycle, which would allow Batman to navigate the streets of the expanded city, and give the gamer a different experience in this go-around.

So, with the exceptions of the expanded size of the city, the introduction of a fast travel system, and a new more advanced case-solving system (which, again, works against the theme of a younger Batman), this game does not really bring anything new to the table. And I would argue that those three factors are really not game-changers, not in the way that Arkham City was over Arkham Asylum. Which itself is fine, since, let's face it - Arkham City was a damn near-perfect game. But it also had a near-perfect plot, which Arkham Origins is sadly lacking. Sure, it sounds daunting enough - a bunch of assassins gunning for Batman on Christmas Eve - but it just doesn't play out as interesting as it sounds. The game is structured linearly, so there's no spontaneity. It's not like Deadshot can take a shot at you at any moment, or Deathstroke is there to surprise you when you venture to the wrong rooftop. For a guy with a $5 million price on his head, Batman is remarkably safe most of the time. The sense of danger the plot seems to want you to feel is absent from the game world.

Overall, this is a fun game that suffers from, if nothing else, a lack of ambition and attention. It's capitalizing on the fact that you loved Arkham City so much that you'll want to play what is essentially the same game all over again. And, well, I do. But I probably won't be re-playing it anytime soon after that.

This is certainly not the first time I have had problems with an Xbox branded product, but at least when I did I was able to get in contact with customer support.

EDIT 11/23/2013: After waiting on the phone for Microsoft Support for a reasonable amount of time considering today is the launch of a major new product from them, I managed to arrange an exchange for my defective unit. They offer two exchange options. An \\"advance exchange\\" where they send you a new unit for you to swap with the old one and you give them your credit information so they can charge you if they don't receive the defective unit within 15 days. And a normal exchange where you pack up your defective unit and return it to them and they send a replacement. I chose option 1 because fortunately the defective unit still plays digitally purchased games.

I will adjust my rating if the replacement console works without issue.

EDIT 12/5/2013: Received my replacement unit today. It worked without any issue, and the replacement was very simple. I will adjust my rating to 4 stars from the 1 I initially gave it. It's certainly not the perfect system, and I had some real issues with the hardware, but I had good experiences with Microsoft Customer Service. Now that all the features work, my only complaint would be the lack of audio options in Movie playback through HDMI out of the box, though Microsoft says they will be adding more options with a future update. The controller is comfortable but it will take some getting used to from the old 360 controller which I'm so used to using. The library is diverse, I have found 8 games out of the initial 22 launch titles to hold me over until next year when we get more releases. Overall, if not for the defective first unit, I must say the XBox One is a decent purchase and a foundation for a solid console gaming future.

review_headline: One of the most unique games around.
review_body:
I remember playing this when I was younger.
The disc stopped working after while, though, and after my Xbox deteriorated, it must have gotten lost.

I'm glad I gave it a second try on PC.
The island of Vvardenfell is unforgettable.
The whale-like echo of Silt Striders.
The weird jellyfish/horseshoe crab-like Netch.
And the ash wastes around Red Mountain.
All while listening to quite possibly the best soundtracks of gaming history.

However, it does have one MAJOR draw back:
The engine.
That god forsaken engine.
Melee combat is VERY awkward.
Actually, pretty much all combat is pretty awkward.

However, the visuals (For a 2002 game.) are amazing.
I highly, HIGHLY recommend you use modded textures however.
It brings the game more up to date, and really polishes the visuals.

As for the expansion packs, it is pretty commonly known that Tribunal just adds a little extra main quest, that, by many opinions, is pretty straightforward and boring.
Bloodmoon, however, is exactly what an expansion pack should be.
It adds an extra island to travel to, (About 1/4th the size of Vvardenfell, I'd say.) with a whole new design scheme. This island is technically part of Skyrim. (If you've played Skyrim with Dragonborn DLC, yes, it's that EXACT island.)
It gives you TONS of all new quests, and the biggest thing? You can now become a Werewolf.

All in all, Morrowind, despite it's god-awful engine, has remained an excellent game for now over a decade. It's not the graphics, it's not even the gameplay, it's the theme. It's the quests. It's because it's Morrowind. It's a whole new world, and I would like to thank the developers of this game for using their creative talent to build a world that is unlike any other I have seen. Too many games these days focus on 'teh grafiks" and constant, unrelenting action. If you have a good amount of spare time, and some patience, buy this game. You won't regret it.
This game is SO much fun. The multiplayer is fun, but the campaign is even more fun, recommended for everyone!

review_headline: Everything Assassin's Creed III Should Have Been
review_body:
This review can be most helpful to those who are familiar with the rest of the Assassin's Creed series.

I've played all of the main titles in the Assassin's Creed series and found all of them enjoyable, and I think Black Flag might just be one of my favorites (along with ACII). I'm going to list out some notable elements about the game that make it stand out from the others.

EDWARD KENWAY: New Assassin, new direction. While I will not go into the story for the sake of spoilers, Edward is very likable yet also different. Unlike previous Assassins, he does not initially have a strong moral code or sense of justice. But those values are hidden, yet to be discovered and realized. The game's story develops his character to make him more sympathetic. The story highlights his growth as he adjusts to his surroundings and relationships with others. I finished ACIV feeling that Edward had grown throughout the entire story and became a strong, responsible Assassin by the time the credits rolled. I think I speak for quite a few AC fans when I say that ACIII was missing a strong character. Connor was a rehash of Ezio, except his story that brought him into the Assassin's was not as tragic as Ezio's. He was also less tough and more angry. Edward is a strong Assassin who shows a fresh, new kind of growth instead of a recycled revenge-driven development.

MORE TO DO: Every time I finish the story of an Assassin' Creed game, I feel like there is nothing else to do around the maps other than kill/loot guards and take Assassin contracts. But, with this huge map of the Caribbean, containing about 3-5 cities and dozens of islands, you can finish the story and do MUCH more afterwards. You can use your ship to take over naval forts and complete naval contracts, travel between cities to complete new Assassin's Bureau missions, hunt all sorts of animals (land and sea) to easily craft materials, pillage and plunder rival ships to upgrade your ship, take on legendary ships to gain money, use the various treasure maps you have found to find plans and treasure, anything. In fact, few story-based missions occur in Havana, giving you a city left to explore after the story is finished.

MODERN STORYLINE: We don't follow a single, modern-day Assassin in this game. We play in the first-person perspective of a speechless and nameless test subject for Abstergo (aka the modern Templars) who is testing their new products of virtual-reality gaming (powered by the Animus). Desmond Miles' memories and lineage (the subject of the previous games) have been uploaded into a cloud for all of Abstergo to access and market in several Animus machines. Occasionally, breaks in the historic game occur in the modern day, where you are secretly led by the Assassins to hack into Abstergo's computer network and bring that information to them. I am giving no spoilers, but the modern day story ties very well with the historical story of Edward Kenway. Many references to the supernatural beings of Assassin's Creed are implied. The story itself is quite questionable and ambiguous at the end, like most Assassin's Creed stories. Each game plays as a snippet of the story of the ongoing, modern war of the Assassins and the Templars. The end of each game's modern story is left to ambiguity with no definite conclusion.

IMPROVED GAMEPLAY: I will elaborate some new elements of the game in bullets:

- "Whistle" feature: When hiding in areas to use stealth tactics, you can now whistle to attract the attention of a guard. This is very helpful in speeding up the game; instead of waiting for someone to walk in his cycle that the game programs
him to do, you can lure him right to you if you're close enough. If not, then hide in a closer spot!

-Faster reload: The reload took forever in ACIII. I was lucky to shoot a gun twice in a fight. The reload is faster and gives guns and weaponrymore use against enemies. Four single-shot guns can now be carried once you have finished crafting all of the holsters (see below), allowing for quick succession of shots.

-NEW EAGLE VISION: The new Eagle Vision in the game allows you to see enemies and targets through walls. You must activate Eagle Vision when you can see your enemy in sight. Eagle Vision will "tag" that enemy in sight so you can see him through all solid objects if you or the enemy moves. 10 targets/enemies can be tagged at a time. This is especially helpful when you are tailing someone in a mission or when you need to know where your enemies are looking. The only drawback is that you cannot use Eagle Vision when running anymore.

-NO MORE LOCK-ON: The lock-on feature that was in all of the previous Assassin's Creed games has been removed. I found this to be an improvement, because this allowed combat to flow easily, instead of having to stay on lock-on. It also avoids confusion when trying to target a Templar. I revisited ACII to play with the lock-on feature once more, and found myself running into confusing camera angles. The removal of lock-on helps avoid confusing camera angles, improves awareness of the surroundings, and makes fighting easier to control. The lock-on has been replaced by an aim feature (like FPS games) for your pistols and your blowpipe.

-Crafting accessibility: Crafting can now be accessed in the start menu. You can craft objects from the various hides you have hunted to produce useful objects, such as armor and ammo pouches. I found this to be easier and more convenient, since you can essentially craft whenever you want, instead of having to run to a specific store.

-Plundering ships and warehouses: What else does a pirate do besides plundering? On sea, you can use your armed ship to provoke attack on any ships of your choice. You can destroy the ships defenses and steal all of its goods, or sink it andsteal half of its goods. Each ship has its own materials that you can use to improve your own with a cost. (Metals can be used to add more cannons, wood can be used to improve hull armor, etc.)
On land, you can infiltrate restricted, well guarded areas. Find the key master, loot the key from him, and reach the warehouse to steal its goods. But don't get caught, or else the guards will move its goods away for a certain amount of time.

-Improved weapon select: Instead of having to hold a button and scroll through your weapons to choose one, you only have to tape the D-pad (for PS3) to access weapons. If you press the left D-Pad once, you get a gun. Press it twice, you get smoke bombs. A cross is displayed on the side of your screen to remind you what to tap with to get a specific weapon. This feature increases the pace of the game and allows you to choose your weapons quickly. The combat weapons (swords, bare hands, hidden blades) are still separate from projectiles. Up and down arrows switch between combat, left and right arrows switch between projectiles.

-Deep-sea Diving: New to Assassin's Creed, you can dive deep in the ocean to collect treasure hidden in the ocean floor. You are unarmed while scavenging through the ocean, leaving you vulnerable. Some deep-sea missions lead to hidden caverns with camps set up by other pirates. Other enemies include vicious eels and sharks that can lash out at you in the ocean.

Overall, Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag is an improved version of Assassin's Creed III. Ubisoft has mastered the elements it created in ACIII and made them easier and more fun for the user. I didn't particularly enjoy the new naval contract missions in ACIII; in ACIV, Ubisoft added the new option of ship-sinking and plundering (which I found more engaging and fun) in this game to add to the experience and make it more enjoyable. Ubisoft also added more to AC to make ACIV a stand-alone game that is significantly different compared to its previous titles. Assassin's Creed IV: Black Flag features new gameplay and more elements for a better game experience.

product_title: Super Mario 3D World - Nintendo Wii U
review_headline: The Perfect Mix of Mario Greatness New and Old
review_body:
When this game was first revealed many were unimpressed as it seemed like a rehash of the 3DS game super Mario 3D Land. Then we saw more and saw how wrong we were. This game is amazing. It is the culmination of all Mario games and a mix of old and new. Before even going into the multiplayer aspects I have to say that this game has so much to offer.
There are many secrets to unlock (including a 5th character), so many modes of gameplay and so much innovation. Whether it's the double cherry that creates copies of your character or the powerups that let you fight ghosts or the throwbacks to old powerups like the Kuribo's shoe, this game has it all. There are levels with Music reminiscent of Super Mario 64, Boss battles that are incredibly fun and amazing visuals throughout. This game must be seen to be believed. Running at 720p (upscaled to 1080p) at 60 fps, the game is gorgeous! At times you will simply stop and look and admire the visuals.
Speaking of the levels there is so much variety putting this on the same playing field as the Galaxy games (made by the same team) and other 3D Mario games. There is a level with silhouettes, a level that plays like an overhead shooter (with the double cherry as special powerup) and a Mario kart themed level and that's just some of it. The levels start out somewhat easy but this is to ease you into the game. It gets harder as you progress and it makes you want to play until you beat it.

The music is amazing and varies between big band music and orchestral remixes of older Mario music. It really fits the game well and you will want to listen for hours.
Now about the multiplayer, it's fun but be warned, the more players, the more chaotic it becomes. This isn't a bad thing though. Playing in single player and then in multiplayer will give you very different experiences. Playing with four players locks the camera up while playing in single player or with less than 4 characters allows freer roaming camera angles. As for controls, there are so many options, ranging from the gamepad, to the pro ctontroller, thewiimote to the nunchuck and the classic controller and they are all awesome!

While there isn't online co-op, the truth is that online co-op isn't needed and the game is fun without it, however there is an option to go online and submit your playthroughs of level and access other peoples' playthroughs and race against other peoples' ghost data. There are also stamps that can be obtained in the game and shared on miiverse and take part in the online community.

The different modes in this game are amazing, whether its speed running with the clock starting at 100 seconds, or the bonus levels, there is so much variety offered (including a hidden bonus game) and the game never stays constant and is always changing things up. There is no way to get bored and so much to unlock. This is the reason to buy a Wii U right now if you haven't yet!

This game marks the beginning of a new era of awesomeness for Nintendo and the Wii U. Its time to get hyped!

For years it was seen as a pretender to the throne. While different enough to be its own game, it wasn't until the third entry in the series that it came into its own, and the fourth installment of Saints Row made it very clear it was no pretender. In his PC Gamer review of Saints Row IV, Rich McCormick notes,\\" Saints Row was born of Grand Theft Auto, but although both feature open cities and freeform violence, they've diverged.\\" Saints Row IV proves it leads the pack with a ridiculous, yet hilarious plot, absurdly fun game play, and an amazing soundtrack.

This game is absolute madness! Having left off as the head of a global media empire, the player once again reprises the role of the nameless \\"Boss\\" of the Third Street Saints. Opening with an internationally coordinated assassination, the Boss winds up saving the White House from nuclear destruction and is sworn in as President of the United States. As the Commander-in-chief, the Boss must become humanity's savior when the Earth comes under attack by alien forces. To overcome the mighty Zin Empire's grasp on mankind, the Boss enters a virtual simulation akin to the The Matrix. What follows is several hours of action, seemingly nonstop laughs, numerous pop-culture parodies, throwbacks to previous entries, and ribs at the competition. Saints Row IV revels in the madness and makes it clear this was meant to be a game, not a film meant to move hearts.

The ride from start to finish is incredibly fun and wild. Featuring a fully customizable array of advanced weaponry, access to several super powers, and an open world to abuse them in, the game is truly a blast. Jim Sterling from Destructoid has even gone as far as declaring \\"Saints Row IV perhaps one of the best open world sandbox games you could ever hope to play, and practically a culmination of everything the genre's worked toward this generation.\\" He may just have a point. Nothing beats super speeding into a group of enemies, unleashing a burstof ice to freeze every foe in sight, super jumping high into the air, and finally crashing back down to the earth with the force of a small nuclear bomb (that's not even an exaggeration, it's a literal power upgrade).

Despite providing a high level of entertainment however, the powers may have been granted too early in the game since they tend to overshadow the other well-done mechanics. Weapons such as the alien abduction gun, which does exactly what it sounds like, are rarely used in favor of throwing cars with the power of your mind. Even so, whether the player decides to wield artillery or become the artillery, the mayhem is made all the more fun thanks to the character creator. Allowing for a character that is male, female, or anything in between (such as a floating toilet), the options are near limitless. For instance, the chosen avatar of destruction may be an oiled up, masked wrestler that suplexes aliens into oblivion, or a straight-cut office woman leveling the battlefield with a Dubstep Gun.

Given the description, one may wonder what the walking apocalypse sounds like. Well, that too is up to the player. Among others, famous voice actors such as Troy Baker and Nolan North offer their talent as options for the character's voice. Their superb acting, combined with the rest of the cast and a magnificent soundtrack leads to an amazing audio experience. The opening mission sets the bar high with the touching inclusion of Aerosmith's smash hit, \\"I Don't Wanna Miss a Thing\\". Another brilliant, yet ludicrous example includes using Haddaway's \\"What Is Love\\" as the backdrop for a high speed space chase. Not all music is tied to the story though; there are several radio stations in game that feature a number of popular songs across multiple genres. This way the player is free to choose the musical accompaniment for their rampage.

Saint's Row IV may just be the most awesome game ever made. Given its roots as a \\"clone\\", the series hastruly come a long way. Based on a story so absurd it has no peer, game play that is far too addictive, and a soundtrack that perfectly accompanies the madness, it is hard to deny the Saints a place among the kings of video game entertainment.

review_headline: Happy Anniversary Madden!  This Game Delivers!
review_body:
The longtime football series celebrates the same silver anniversary as my spouse and I this year and like a marriage it’s seen its good years and bad ones. I’ve probably owned a good 15 versions of this game yet I would still label myself a casual football gamer. Knowing ahead that the next gen systems would be delivering Madden 25 I decided to hold off so I can’t really compare how this version stacks up against the 360 or PS3 versions.

What I can say is that my fears of getting a stripped down version have been put to rest as this game has all I want in a football title…in fact, it delivers quite a bit more than I would expect. This game has it all for any football fan – dynasties (both single player or with friends), fantasy teams via Ultimate Team, co-op seasons, and challenges that mirror recent events you see on Sunday. This game could easily provide hundreds of hours of entertainment and you still will find more new things to do.
After playing a few games to see how the next gen graphics look (answer – fantastic), I realized I needed to brush up a little on the controls and see what was new. It was a real treat to come across in-depth training full of mini-games that really show you how properly use the skills at your disposal. The games are not only helpful along with clear videos showing exactly what to do, they are fun to try and better your scores.

I am equally impressed by the in game menus – very little slowdown going between them and they are laid out in a way that makes them easy to navigate and understand. This game has a TON of options but everything is put together such that it’s never an issue to find what you want.

This year’s dynasty mode is a definite improvement from last year giving you more options to control things to your liking. I was especially excited to see a wide variety of NFL Legends unlocked from the start allowing you to recreate their careers as part of today’s NFL.

As far as the gameplay itself, I not really much of an X’s and O’s guy that will take apart a game for it’s faults, I just want the games to feel believable in action (not too many fumbles, INT’s, or too many $$$ plays) as well as offering some exciting variety and rewarding challenges. While I haven’t played enough yet to reach a definitive conclusion, everything I’ve seen thus far looks and plays fantastic.

One surprise I wasn’t ready for was how well Kinect voice commands worked within the gameplay. All those days of pre-snap menu navigation have been dealt with making you really feel like a field general while playing.

So after reading all this you may wonder if there is anything I don’t like about the game. Besides needing more cheerleader action, I did find the commentary and crowd noise a bit lacking for my taste. I managed to pull off an amazing 60 yard run just short of a TD all the while the commentators were driveling on about some story – in real life they would have broke short and started counting down the yards to the endzone. I’d also love to hear more crowd chants, better half-time shows, and maybe some type of plays of the week show as you progress.

All in all, with this being a celebratory year for EA SPORTS and Madden Football, I must say I am going to enjoy the party with them. Happy Anniversary Madden, thanks for the memories, and great year for NFL football!

***** Update ******
After a solid 10 hours of play here is what I have.

This is definitely not like any other COD so far. Nothing like MW2/3 or Bops 1/2.

---Pro's---

* The new Perk System allows for a lot of customization. Having that many choices allows for many different combinations to see what is right for you. The 8 point cap keeps things from getting too OP.

* The maps are much bigger. Not quite battlefield sized but, noticeably larger than any other COD game and so far I like the Maps, particularly Stonehedge.

* This is no longer a run and gun game. If you do that here you will be killed over and over. It creates for more strategy and more thought rather than just run, drop shot, rinse and repeat. There are problems with this though that I have listed in the Cons.

* Character customization. It took them way to long to finally implement this (although some of the upgrades are too expensive in my opinion considering you also have to save the tokens for gun/perk/kill streak unlocks.

* They brought back support and specialist.

---Con's---

* This game feels a lot like battlefield 3 which isn't bad considering Battlefield 3 was a good game. The only problem is, BF4 just came out. From the physics, to the maps, to the colors used in things like TDM (orange and blue), it reeks of battlefield. It still feels enough like COD to keep me playing but, most of us purchase this game to play COD, not a battlefield hybrid. If we wanted that, we would have purchased Battlefield.

* No S&D? Really? That is a huge knock. Whether it was in random games or in MLG, Search was my favorite mode. The new modes are tacky at best. 30 seconds to live once you get a kill? Stupid.

* The other game modes are lacking. For example, they brought back infected and even though the maps are larger the max is 12 people. How does that make sense?

* This is not a run and gun game which is what COD has always been (Ill explain why this is a PRO and CON). This is a sit and wait for the stupid soul to run in the middle of the map and hope you are the first one to get him. This is where the game loses me. I liked Battlefield 3. I own it and am planning on getting Battlefield 4. This is what Battlefield is, a strategy shooter. When I play COD, I want to run and gun. I want to rain down with kill streaks like a reaper or a predator or a chopper gunner. Which brings me to my next point...

* Kill streaks. They suck. Hard. A armor suit and a knife where you can run and light speed? Great. That would be an awesome kill streak in ANY other COD game... except when you have maps half the size of Russia it is useless.

The main characters, the special weapons/abilities each main character possesses, and having the option to play the game in side-by-side co-op make the game Fuse standout from your average third person shooter. The main characters in Fuse are Dalton Brooks, Naya Deveraux, Jacob Kimble, and Isabella \\"Izzy\\" Sinclair. Dalton is a former mercenary and the team leader. His special weapon is the Magshield. It can be used as moveable cover, it can also be used a stationary cover by Dalton or any of the other main characters. The magshield can also fire devastating blasts to enemies at close range. Naya Deveraux is a British with daddy issues. Her special weapon is the Warp rifle. Her special ability is to cloak herself which basically means she can go in invisible mode and not be detected by the enemy. This is great for taking out unsuspecting enemy and healing downed team members without drawing attention to yourself. Jacob is a former cop. His special weapon is the Arch shot which is a long range cross-bow that shoots bolts of Fuse-augmented Mercury that ''melts enemies alive.'' He can also use his cross-bow to nail enemies to the walls. Izzy is a rebellious young scientist. Her special weapon is the Shattergun which is an assault rifle that encases enemies in crystal for a short time. This gun is highly effective against enemies who use magshields. Her special ability is that she can deploy a Med Beacon that can revive and heal teammates. Together these four outcasts form a team called Overstrike9.

Game play wise Fuse can be played in Campaign mode or Echelon mode. Campaign mode is the story mode. Echelon mode is where players will combat wave after wave of enemies. Playing in this mode allows players more opportunities to earn money and fuse credits. All of which you will want to do to enhance your game playing experience. Echelon is incredibly fun, addictive, and rewarding.

Also Fuse can be played in single player mode, two player side-by-side co-op, or 4 person co-op on-line. The best way to get the most out of this game is to play it in side-by-side co-op or multiplayer online. Fuse feels like it was designed for human controlled squad mates to work together against a smart A.I. controlled enemy.

Players have the ability to switch between characters at any point in the game just as long as the character they're switching too isn't being controlled by another player. This makes it easier for players to execute various strategies and to overcome difficult locations/enemies.

Story wise Fuse won't be winning any awards, but the story is serviceable enough to keep the player engaged from the beginning to the end. Basically, while on a routine mission Overstrike 9 encounters a notorious mercenary group known as Raven that steals an alien substance known as Fuse. Their job is to retrieve this alien weaponry which leads to a lot of globetrotting and amazingly fun battles and shoot-outs.

The replay value for this game is high since each of the main characters has different personalities, melee skills, special weapons/abilities. Based on who you choose to play as can drastically change how you play the game which helps to keep things fresh.

When I was growing up I was introduced to the genre known as first person shooter. From fighting demons in the depths of space to liberating france from the germans there are tons of shooters to choose from. Now EA is coming out with the next installment simply called Battlefield 4 but should you be running towards or away from this engagement?

In single player you will step into the shoes of Sgt Daniel Recker part of an elite group called \\"Tombstone\\". The game takes place in 2020 six years after the events of Battlefield 3. Your team is searching for a rogue Chinese general and missions will be taking place all over the world. product_title: Rune Factory: Tides of Destiny - Playstation 3
review_headline: A step in the right direction...
review_body:
I have been in love with the Rune Factory series since the first one was released on the DS. Having been a longtime fan of Harvest Moon, the fantasy take on the farming simulation game was a great breath of fresh air for me.

However, Tides of Destiny was finally given the scale Rune Factory deserves. A staggering amount of content, excellent artistic direction, voice acting that excels far beyond what the previous entries offered, and - more importantly - a dizzying combat system that the series has been waiting for. Those are the highlights.

As with most games though, Tides of Destiny is not without faults. One of the very first issues I had was that - due to it being a Wii port - the PS3 controller is not fully utilized as it should be; my best example would be lack of camera control which could have easily been given to the right analog stick. Next up would be something very familiar to pretty much every other entry - that being the underwhelming story. What is even more saddening there is the fact that the game doesn't truly open up until the "story" is completed, as if to say, "Hurry up and finish the fantastically underwhelming and vague story to get into the good stuff!" My last complaint would be in regards to it being a Wii port - and an obvious one at that. Though the visuals go far beyond the other titles, they aren't far beyond what the PS2 was capable of pushing. Basically, if it were up to me, a little more time could have been allotted to the PS3 version to make it truly worth the price tag.

All in all, it is a great game and has a massive amount of replay value. If you like simulators and action RPGs this is definitely a quality title for the PS3.

product_title: Saints Row the Third - The Full Package
review_body:
Saints Row: The Third is great. The full package brings all the DLC together (except for the Unlockable Pack, and the Bloodsucker pack.) These DLC were not included of course because not everyone wants instant cheats that cannot be deactivated like the cellphone cheats. There is a licensing issue with Xbox that causes some of the DLC not to register because if you install the Online Pass, the Bloodsucker Pack, or Unlockable Pack they will overwrite the full DLC \\"Saints Row: The Third- Pack: The First\\" file from the installation disc. In order to fix this delete the \\"Saints Row: The Third- Pack: The First\\" file from your hard drive. Next, plug in your Xbox formatted flash drive, install the online pass, or the bloodsucker pack and the unlockable pack (if you have purchased either) to your main hard drive. Then go over to your hard drive panel in the options menu and move the \\"Saints Row: The Third- Pack: The First\\" file to your flash drive. After this is done put in your installation disc for The Full Package to reinstall all of your disc DLC to your hard drive. This should fix your problem 100% and Saints Row: The Third should read your DLC files from both your hard drive and flash drive. Definitely DO NOT let this issue hold you back on getting this game if you plan to use the Online Pass or other DLC. It is a great game, and it's definitely worth it.

Notes:
*How to format a Flash Drive: http://support.xbox.com/en-US/xbox-360/accessories/usb-flash-drive
*Buy an official SanDisk Xbox 360 Flash Drive (Most other Flash Drives work as well, but this is recommended by Xbox) [[ASIN:B003EV7ED8 Xbox 360 Flash SanDisk SDCZGXB 016G A11]]
*If you have another Hard Drive plugged in to your Xbox that may work in replacement to a flash drive, but I am not completely sure on that.

review_headline: Sub-Standard Graphics, Unsatisfying Gameplay, Lack of Personality
review_body:
I am a big fan of the Lego games, and especially enjoy them on the go, via my 3DS XL. Like other reviewers, I understand and have come to expect that the portable version of these games is not always as "complete" as their console cousins. Regardless, I must agree that this latest installment in the Lego franchise suffers a great deal.

The first thing I noticed when beginning Lego Marvel was the markedly bad graphics. Admittedly, this is my first outing on a made-for-3DS Lego game. (My other games were Lego Star Wars and Lego Pirates for DS and Lego Batman and Lego Indiana Jones for PSP.) Even so, the graphics for this game seemed like a DS port rather than taking full advantage of the 3DS's great graphic capability. To make the problem even worse, the game looks stretched out on my XL screen. Being a brand new release, I expected a lot more out of this game visually, and was really excited to see crisp, 3D capable cinematics. There's another dud. Not a single 3D scene to be found.

Next--and even worse than the poor graphics--is the gameplay. You feel constricted to do what Lego games have always been about--exploring and scratching that completionist itch. With the inability to even jump, I feel pushed along and really unable to enjoy myself. Each mission feels more like a chore than a joy, which is a shame.

The nail in the coffin for me is the lack of what I call the Command Center. In Lego Star Wars, you had the Cantina. In Pirates, you had the Port. In Marvel, you just get menus. This really kills the personality of the game and makes it seem even more like a checklist than a solid, enjoyable Lego game. Quite a break from tradition.

In closing, sub-standard graphics, unsatisfying gameplay, and lack of personality really kill this game for me. Regardless, I will probably try to beat it and unlock all the characters and powerups before trading it in for my next--hopefully much more enjoyable--3DS game.

So I’ve had the Rocksmith 2014 guitar bundle edition for about 2 weeks now. I've always wanted to learn how to play but never had the time and didn’t want to spend money on lessons (heard they can get real expensive).
My first impressions were...let’s just say I couldn't put the guitar down. I played for about 3-4 hours the day I got it. The guitar was nice, better than expected. I was worried it wasn't going to be full size due to it saying "junior", but was pleasantly surprised that it seemed like a normal guitar (at least to me). It came with a strap, and 2 picks. The game does a great job at following your progress and helps you with the problems you’re having. At first you only play a handful of notes per song, but they gradually add notes depending on your progress. I noticed a few times where they added a note or group of notes that I just could not get down yet and they adjusted accordingly to my play style. After 2 weeks I look back and laugh that I was having trouble with that part of the song. Let’s hope 2 months from now I’ll look back and laugh at all the parts I’m messing up on now.
Despite my absolute love for this "game", it does have its problems. It likes to randomly freeze up on me every once in a while. It hasn't become a major consistent problem yet, more like a minor annoyance. Happens probably once a day. A few times I noticed I hit the wrong note and it registered that it was the correct one. And the tuner can be a bit finicky at times. That’s really it, nothing major.
This is a great way to learn how to play guitar, it has video lessens you can watch, a session mode that I’m sure by now you have heard all about. It has a riff repeater so if you’re having a problem with a certain part of a song you can practice it slower or on an easier difficulty until you have it down. The guitarcade is a blast, it has around 10 mini games you can play to hone certain skills like chords or fret position. Ilike to use them to warm up. I can’t yet say that it replaces an actual teacher, but it comes very close, and it’s cheaper.

product_title: Call of Duty: Black Ops II
review_headline: Fun, but not as much as it should have been
review_body:
It took me a while to understand why this game wasn't nearly as much fun as it should have been.

The multiplayer looks great and has solid mechanics as expected. The maps are pretty well designed, although a little too favoring of long rage. The big failure is that all the need for skill has been replaced by a rock, paper, scissors sort of system where this perk beats that weapon type, which beats an attachment, which beats a certain play style. It's stupid. The shotguns and light machine guns were overpowered, further encouraging camping. So were the snipers, encouraging half the team in any game sprinting around quick scoping.

The zombie mode is the best part of the game. The epic sized maps provide endless hours of cooperatively slaying zombies in the name of solving ridiculous puzzles.

The campaign has a great story line with some really intense characters. There's some choices to make about the path of the game, which kept me thinking about the consequences of my decisions.

review_headline: I'm Having Fun! from a Non-Elite Lifetime COD and BF Veteran player
review_body:
I was worried that I had made a mistake in pre-ordering this game as there were over 40 comments posted before I had even received it and those comments were mostly negative. I am 40+ gamer who has played all of the CODs and BFs. While I play every night I am not an elite player and typically get killed more than I kill. I am used to horrible spawn points, camping, quick-knife kills etc. as I am usually on the receiving end of those.

So, with low (and almost nervous) expectations, I throw in the disc and install the game to the hard-drive. The installation process was fine and the game loads and plays with no lag at all for me. Once that was done installing, I immediately jumped into multi-player (skipping the squad stuff-- more on that later in this review).

The maps are larger than COD BOII but I like that. The combat and gun feel felt the same to me as BOII as did the leveling up and weapon attachments. Honestly I think they could have just sold us more maps for BOII and we wouldn't have really been able to tell the difference (and I wish they would just keep doing that-- every season issue a new set of map packs but keep the core game alone).

Despite the fact that the game-play appears to be the same, I am enjoying myself with Ghosts and am getting roughly the same stats for a match that I would get on BOII (I usually get around 10 kills and am killed between 10-20 times--- like I said, I'm not an elite player) so for me I don't feel that game play is all that different from BOII.

Finding and joining a match is fast (much faster than BF4).

Graphics are fine...I'm not hung up on graphics but I think the maps look great. The maps seem to have more paths and doors, which provides for fewer bottle necks and lots of ways to approach enemies-- I like that. Again, with larger maps, players like me that are not great actually can survive longer because the enemies are more spread-out... to me this is a plus.From time to time there are blue briefcases hovering about the ground over a dead body. At first, when I picked these up I thought it was like capturing your dog-tags back (like in kill confirmed) but last night I discovered those are mini-quests that earn kill streak rewards. So one might be \\"get a kill with your secondary weapon to earn 1 kill streak\\". I didn't attempt to meet the conditions but tonight I will.

I don't have real complaints, but there a couple of things (one minor and one major) I don't like about this game (which keep it from getting 5 stars from me):

--menus (I like the BOII menu skins more-- I wish they were here) (MINOR)
--knife attacks-- too deadly--- I wish there was a better way to do melee. It seems that you are always killed with one knife strike regardless of how far or near the person is. I think there should be a mini-game of some kind (pound X and B faster or in some rythmic pattern --like the pinning mechanics in the WWE2k14 game) to simulate the struggle with the knife. I am fine with instant kills from behind, but not when you are facing the person. (MAJOR)
--Leveling is too fast. I think BF4 does a better job of slowing down the leveling and having levels for kits, weapons and vehicles. I wish COD were slower paced XP so not everyone would be level 60 within a week (minor).

WISH LIST:
I always wished that skill-streak rewards were attainable by the average player (I never can get above 5 kills before I die and have to start over). I would like to see some \\"banking\\" or something that would allow me to have kills accumulate during a match regardless of whether you die for the non-support load outs (play with \\"support\\" killstreak package does allow banking but the rewards are less exotic and fun, in my opinion).

UPDATE: November 7, 2013

SQUAD REVIEW: So last night I tried \\"squad\\" mode for the first time and I really like it. Basically, from the matches thatI played you (plus 5 of your computer controlled squad members) square off against another player and his squad. So while it \\"looks\\" like a multi-player match it really is more like one on one with some BOTS (like Red Faction PVP, if you remember that game). I had a blast playing this mode -- its hard to put my finger on it but perhaps its because I am better than the AI controlled players so it gives me (a very average player at best) the feeling of being a more elite trooper (aka, a UBER ELITE MULTI-PLAYER, hehehe) who rang up about double the number of kills that I typically get in a regular multi-player game (e.g., I was getting about 20 kills in squad mode when I normally get between 10-13 kills in a multi-player game). To my relief, the computer AI squad members do not hop around like rabbits (which is common in multi-player games) so to me it seems, I don't know, more \\"real\\". You gain XP and coins from this mode that allow you to upgrade your squad. I can see the deeper RPG element of this and the long-replay value of trying to level up each squad member-- which is a big PLUS in my book. All in all, I like this mode.

BUG REPORT: November 20, 2013

I have leveled up 5 squad members to between level 5 and 10, rotating between to try to keep them all the same level. Well last night, when I was leveling up one of my level 6 squad members, a level 60 joins the match. Suddenly on the screen in GREEN text is the following message \\"LEVEL 60 PLAYER LEAVE IMMEDIATELY OR YOU WILL LOSE RANK.\\" I ignore the message as I am only level 6. Once the match was over, I was shocked to see that my level 6 squad member was now level 60! Even more interesting and puzzling is the fact that prior to that I might earn a squad point or two per match but now I am earning 10-25 squad points per match regardless of which character I am using. I have a feeling that there was a major bug that infect my profile following that match with the warning.
