review_headline: Great graphics engine, weak story, rinse and repeat gameplay of the 2nd game
review_body:
Having played all 3 games, I have to say that the first game is what really set the benchmark. There were many elements in the 3rd one that left me feeling disappointed.

**SPOILER ALERTS!**

First off, had I have known that the co-op option was only available for users with a paid Live! membership, I would've purchased the PS3 version instead. I think it would have been fun to try the co-op mode.

The graphic engine is unreal like no other; the environments, the character modeling, the breaths of air, everything is superb. The audio for it was well done too, and it was totally rocking with a 5.1 soundbar system.

The new weapon upgrade system that was implemented had potential, but I found it to be rather clunky for the original purpose. Instead of designing multiple weapons, I stuck with 2 frames that were able to essentially allow me to carry 4 weapons simultaneously. Once you acquire 2 heavy elite frames, you can do just the same. You can swap out the weapons in the frame without having to lose the parts - they're salvageable continuously. The tips for each weapon contained within the frame are what change its behavior, and the upgrade chips help a lot.

The salvage bots that you can use in conjunction with the workbench were a hit and miss. You slowly will acquire up to 3 bots in the gameplay, and obtaining materials is very scarce, causing you to use your ammo wisely. There were times where I had to run around with the electric hammer because I ran out of ammo, or even just flat out ran past mobs.

When mobs were triggered by events in the game, it became very frustrating rather quickly. Instead of being attacked by 1-3 necromorphs, I'd get attacked by 6-10 simultaneously. This became rather tedious considering that my weapons were not up to par at various points, and I had to set the difficulty to easy just to make it past them. I detested the fights with necromorphs that were indestructible - it reminded me of the undead elites that were in various Resident Evil games. It was hard to enjoy the horror element of the game because it felt overly emphasized by the amount of necromorphs that spawned each time. There were certain chapters that really portrayed the horror part of the game rather well, by they were few and far in between. It didn't feel like a horror game overall, but more of a shooter frenzy game like Resident Evil became.

The love story between Isaac and Ellie was dreadful. After 2, they dated, and then broke up. Ellie moves on and starts dating this other guy, and Isaac just seems like a soulless corpse chasing after this woman that has fallen in love with another man. Isaac acts like a puppet, and follows the commands of whoever is over the commlink. It was disappointing to not see any traces of Isaac's memory of Nicole, especially since the marker taunted him with her memories in 1 & 2. I wish Ellie would have died early in the game, at least it would've given Isaac motivation for doing what he was enduring. I mean, if my girlfriend broke up with me, and moved on with another man, why would I go out of my way to save her? It felt overly forced and cliche.

The story involving the marker, the aliens, and the brother moon was ok. The ending leads me to believe that there will be a 4th one, if not 5 and 6 to follow as well. I'm afraid that EA will take it to the next step and repeat Capcom's mistake with Resident Evil by making countless sequels when it should have ended with the 3rd. If a 4th release of Dead Space is released, I'll highly consider borrowing it from a friend rather than purchasing it. I'm the kind of gamer that plays a game because I enjoy feeling a connection with the main character and his influence within the game, and this one missed the mark for the me.

Pokemon black is the first game in the 5th generation of pokemon games. It aas revamped certain aspects of the gameplay to make it a better experience overall. There also many newer functions that make trading simpler and faster than ever. The game feels new and fresh while still keeping true to the classic pokemon formula. Here are the main things that make this game great:
- reusable TMs, now TMs can be reused so you can experiment with different movesets. They are a bit more challenging to find, but the rewards are great.
- C Gear. This takes up your touchscreen and includes infrared functions for trading/battling and NFC functions much like the union room. Also some wifi capabilities for your pokemon.
- GTS negotiations(wifi), this is like an edited version of the GTS that allows you to engage in live trading with another trainer from anywhere in the world. You can't directly communicate, but you can sort of indicate what pokemon you want and it is a lot more useful and faster than the original GTS.
- Random matchups(wifi), you can now battle anyone instantly over wifi, very cool feature.
- No old pokemon until after you pass the game. This forces you to really explore the new generation and is great for getting the hang of things.
- Revamped exp. system. It is now MUCH easier to level up weaker pokemon. Basically the game gives out exp based on the difference in levels of you and your opponent now.

Overall a great game and I highly recommend it.
*NOTE* In this game the exclusive legendaries are Reshiram and Tornadus. You can get Zekrom and Thundurus in pokemon white only.

Yes. BEST GAME EVER. Few single player games give you reason to want to play them after finishing the story mode but Arkham City isn't one of those games. Finishing the main story leaves you with tons and tons to do. From side story to riddles to interesting side characters, there's just so much to do. Where I find heavy replayablity though is the Riddler challenge maps. This is the sole reason I still haven't sold this game. I've completed the game 100%. Done all the riddles and everything but every few days, I'll put in the disc just to play the challenge maps. You get to intimidate thugs and just mess with them. I can sit there for hours messing with them just to see their reaction which is usually funny.

In terms of story, I really enjoyed. Some people will nitpick and talk about this and that but overall I really enjoyed it. I like that they didn't try to tie this in to any comic or movie because some major events occur in it that would and did upset some Batman fans.

Voice acting is top notch. They used a lot of the voice actors from the Animated Series (which in my opinion is one of the BEST CARTOONS EVER, you can probably tell I'm a Batman fanatic. Lol). Anyway, Mark Hamil, Kevin Conroy etc all reprise their roles and they do an excellent job as always.

The music. Oh, my. Let me just say, I went out and bought the soundtrack to this game. It's that good. The dark overtones, the chorus vocalizing all make for really good music that ties into the themes in the game. The music is dynamic so certain music play at certain times like grabbing a thug from under a gargoyle or activating a certain side mission etc.

As for graphics, it is really good for what the Xbox 360 hardware is capable of pushing. The snow falling on his cape. Cuts in his cape and bruises as he gets battered up in fights. The cinematic cutscenes are really amazing as well. My favorite is when he puts on the Batman costume for the first time in the game.

If you're a Batman fan, do yourself and get this game. Even if you don't play videogames. Just get it.

review_headline: Improves From the First Game but Weakest of the Four Games
review_body:
As the last one in the series to get and finish, I have a lot of things to say about it.

First off, this game improves on everything the first game failed to do in terms of gameplay. The monster race has improved considerably from being useless canon fodder to monsters that can still be canon fodder but have abilities that can actually support their allies. I think this game introduces the two weapon types for monsters that is attack and special attack oriented but it helps differentiate the two monster types. The weapon mastery is the same from the first game. Each character now has their own ability that can support them in battle (Adell gets stronger when he fights enemies stronger than him, Rozalin powers up male units adjacent to her etc.) Other than that, the gameplay is overall an improvement.

Can't say the same for the story. This is generally why I consider Disgaea 2 the weakest of the 4 games that are out so far. Because the game revolves more on the power of love instead of the power of friendship of this and later games, it comes off as a bad attempt at trying to be a dark romantic comedy given how Disgaea is known for its dark humor. That's another thing addition to the romance plot, the fact the game is the most serious of the 4 makes it hard to think it's Disgaea without characters from the previous game. Adell is the only protagonist that lacks any funny quirks that the other three protagonist have (Laharl is a spoiled brat but still manages to be adorable and appealing. Mao is the mad scientist and his voice actor Vic Mignogna makes Mao funnier than his Japanese counter part because of hearing Edward Elric flipping out. Valvatorez is all around a wonderful protagonist that makes Adell look like nothing taking his traits of honor and still managing to be funny because he's a noble demon.) and therefore loses a lot of the appeal the main characters have. To be fair, Adell is supposed to be the most serious of the 4 protagonist (Disgaea 4 would love to disapprove that though) so he can get away with it. Adell's goal is to save his family and his village from a curse and he's stuck with the female protagonist Rozalin (who I don't mind at all).

But I'll say this right now and it's totally not because I'm an Axel fangirl. -suspiciously specific denial- Axel saved Disgaea 2 for me in terms of the comedy and story. Not only do I have him funny and a powerful ally in battle (I constantly call him on the cell phone) but I found his character endearing and more memorable than the majority of the cast (Dark Hero Days and later games seem to agree given that Axel is always unlockable post game while Adell and Rozalin are demoted to DLC). I found myself more interested in Axel's side of the story instead of the main problem that Adell and Rozalin had to face and the idea of hearing Axel's theme song and seeing him again made me continue playing.

I still give the game a high rating because it's a very good game but I found the story weak...and I hate that stupid frog Tink character wise and he should have died in that one scene. review_headline: A meh story and meh multiplayer
review_body: The only reason to buy this game is to continue the story of Master Chief.  Otherwise, 343 studios phoned it in.  The graphics are the only upgrade from Halo 3 to 4.  I miss Bungie studios.  The guns never carry enough ammo.  The amount of ammo the old guns could hold has been reduced in an attempt to make the game tougher, it doesn't work.  The new weapons are pointless and redundant. The only fun I had playing this was on easy or normal mode, as the Master Chief is a super soldier and only those modes compliment who and what he actually is. Spartan ops is a poor replacement for the infinite Firefight mode which is sadly gone.  They just use the same levels over and over and offer a very poor story suitable only for children who won't notice they keep renaming the same level. I love Halo, but this just feels like a poor attempt to continue the saga. And what is the point of introducing a new bad guy if you never get to fight him?  Also, the new enemies are extremely bland and lack any sort of personality.  Even the old grunts and Elites seem to not care about why they are in the story.  The Co-op in this game is very lacking and some stages require the second player to simply watch and die over and over in order to progress. 343 studios needs to stick to making add-on maps, not full games.  Let's hope Bungie's next story "Destiny", can fill the void.

If you are a fan of the Monster Jam series of games, then you should really enjoy this one too. Even tho this game does have rights to Monster Jam, what I am talking about is the series of games called Monster Jam. This one here is different to that of the other series, but none-the-less, still very enjoyable in different ways. The graphics seem to be nicer, the environments are much bigger, however there is not as much to destroy laying around the tracks.

4x4 puts you in the drivers seat as a goofy looking rookie whom as you complete your first circuit race, a pimp shows up and says he can help you out with money by racing private races for him. quite frankly, the plot is ridicules and pointless. You pretty much race across America in a series of 3 events; Circuit (drag race), Exhibition (stunts) and these races across parks/fields/beaches/woods/snow fields/counties etc for this pimp dude who wants to see some private races for some unknown reason. You can skip the private and exhibition races and just play the circuits, however you need money to enter those events, so playing the other two will give you the cash you need to enter.

Some other stupid things are your mechanic is a polygon woman in a bikini that is supposed to be sexy? However, her cleavage looks so horrendous that it's almost funny every-time she shows up. Buying upgrades of shocks, wheels, and other parts is just about useless, so save your money and just buy nitros, they are all you will need to win races.

The controls are decent, not quite as good as Monter Jam titles, but it's close enough to be ok. The music is ok, the commentary is repetitive, and can get pretty annoying, but it's worse from the pimp guy during his races, as he tends to be even more repetitive and has an annoying voice. The voice acting in this game is 1 of 5 stars, they sound cheap, and almost laughable.

Overall, turn the commentary off, and enjoy a decent ride. Not quite as good asthe Monster Jam titles after Maximum Destruction, but none-the-less a refreshing game to play if you are a fan of the other series, just to see how another company would have done it!

Cons
- Gravedigger is not unlocked at first. Not sure how to unlock it? Possibly from gathering stars on certain races.
- Annoying Commentary.
- Ugly breasticles.

Would those cons be enough to keep you away from monster mayhem and madness?

review_headline: One of the best WWII RTS games available
review_body:
This is a really good RTS game and pretty engaging. Of the WWII RTS games that are out there I've tried most of them, CoH is still probably the best but Axies and Allies lets you play against all factions and is more along the lines of Command and Conquer than CoH. Overall the game has a bit more base building and supply line concerns than those in favor or rapid attack RTS games may like. But I prefer building up base locations and putting down artillery and machine gun nests. There are quite a few additions/subtractions that could make this game more interesting, but overall it's a fun game to play. And worth the time. The individual campaigns are fun, or you can move into world map mode which I think they intended to be like the board game. Either are fun.

The best part is that you play all sides (American, British, German, Russian, Japanese)...I don't know of any other RTS that as a stand alone game offers that.

There are some parts of the game which can be unnerving. You can't build ships, so you work with what they give you. DDay can be excruciating to figure out as the German lines are so long their armor just keeps rolling around messing up any foothold you try to gain (sort of unrealistic given how they held their panzers back on DDay). You can build nukes in the Japanese campaign, but they don't do as much damage as you'd suppose an actual nuke would. Airplanes are kind of limited in their actual use in this game, more control over airfield building would have been better and infantry units at times can be garbage compared to the mechanized units.

Overall the game is fun though, certainly one I keep in my library to play when I'm bored. I don't know of an RTS that has attempted to take on so many theaters with so much actual RTS development. I wish they'd release a second edition of this game, as I don't know of any games that successfully have allowed you to play the Japanese in RTS (aside from boring Pacific Fleet games) or the Russians, though I suppose CoH2 comes out this month. This game has a combination of all. The game is fairly polished as well. I will say that the complaints about how this isn't like the board game are just dumb, it's an actual RTS game with the board game's name. Read what a game is before you buy it thinking it's going to be a board game for your computer, RTS is way different.

...it was a better investment than Diablo III.

Diablo III is an mess, it will never be fixed no matter how many patches and \\"improvements\\" Blizzard rolls out, because the game was fundamentally created wrong and Blizzard would have to go back to the drawing board to correct the design flaws that make this \\"game\\" a craven cash grab with little redeeming value. Blizzard is not going to do this, but we can likely expect some half-hearted \\"expansions\\" that add in content we were already promised for the original release.

The nicest thing I can say about Diablo III is that, if it worked as a stand alone experience, the game would be just about average. The cinematics are nice to look at but the story is pretty bad, there is almost no characterization for the protagonist and if you've played previous Blizzard games you know it's all about an important character becoming corrupted by evil forces, teach your pony a new trick, Blizzard.

The graphics are pretty good for the low system requirements, the sound effects are satisfying (I even read a glowing review from a well respected gaming site that cited the sounds as the best part of the game, newsflash; if the best part of a game are the sound effects, you're doing it wrong).

Digging deeper, though, what's important is the gameplay, and that's where this game falls down and starts tunneling its way to the center of the Earth.

What we have is a mildly amusing (for a few hours at least) action RPG with absolutely no meaningful character customization/development, no choices that can alter the state of anything within the game world, loot that isn't inherently interesting apart from the stat increases, being the unquestioning errand-person of other characters who order you to do their bidding to progress the pathetic excuse for a story, a mini-map that needs constant re-exploration, because it, apparently, only exists in your current session, weak equipment upgrades with socketable gems, and, to progress very far beyond your initial play-through; your choice of grind, grind, grind or pay-for loot (either with almost worthless in-game gold or REAL, ACTUAL $$$MONEY$$$).

But not much of that matters because you will be struggling with latency issues, service drops, and, if you're unfortunate enough to want to play this online-only game with other people, the very real possibility of your account being stolen and all your stuff and gold taken. God forbid if someone in your household wants to watch Netflix or download something while you're playing, because you will watch with confusion, annoyance and horror as your character swings his or her weapon at nothing for several seconds and then dies in a hurry. These issues pretty much destroy any hope of the actual challenge of the game; permadeath-only Hardcore mode.

Basically what I want to say is this; Blizzard made a couple of great action RPG's and garnered a massive following of fans who, to this day (myself included), play those games rabidly. There was massive potential and a frenzy of hype for a sequel. Some pinhead saw the trend of people trading in-game items for cash in various games such as World of Warcraft and decided that the future of the market was not in a quality product but the ability to capitalize on this market and a half-baked system of trading between characters for real money became the true driving factor for every decision that followed in the making of this game. There was also the decision of the developers to take away the aspects of thinking and planning in character building in order to appeal to a broader audience. The end result is a game with an unfortunate core of profits first, entertainment second.

Oh, and if you want to mess with the content of your copy of the game you're SOL, modding is not only not-supported but actively punished.

I may have mentioned Blizzards tired storyline of corruption; I hope that the irony isn't lost on you, reader.

Play Torchlight II ($20) or Path of Exile (free, Currently in open beta) instead and save yourself the heartache, headache and wallet-ache.

review_body: Exactly 28 days after ordering, we got the blinking red light of death.  From what we've read online, we can kiss goodbye both the console and the $60 game that is trapped inside.

It's rather poignant - well as poignant as wrestling (excuse me... \\"Sports Entertainment\\") gets - in the regard that this is THQ's last wrestling game and it brings the connection to their earlier Nintendo 64 titles full circle with the WWE Attitude gameplay.  I haven't really even played any other aspects of the game yet as I'm thoroughly enjoying reliving the heyday of the late 90s wrestling era.  Being that WWE Wrestlemania 2000 and No Mercy are considered two of the top wrestling titles of all-time (I might even consider them the best from a gameplay standpoint), it makes this year's retread of last year's game (and last year's retread of the previous game and so on, so forth) SO much more enjoyable by bringing in those classic moments and personalities.  It's sad to see THQ dissolve - on the other hand, it could revitalize and refresh the WWE video game series to have a new developer take over as THQ stopped innovating some time ago.  Then again, WWE stopped innovating a LONG time ago, so this isn't surprising.  I've heard that EA or Take Two has picked up the rights - EA doesn't thrill me on the basis of the Madden series (which is BEYOND redundant at this juncture) and Take Two could be excellent based on the NBA 2K series.  Anyhow, and moving away from all this pontificating, if you are a fan of the Attitude Era, then this game is a must.  If you have last year's game and don't really care about the new superstars/add-ons, then you don't need to run out and get it.

product_title: Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Future Soldier
review_body:
I purchased Ghost Recon: Future Soldier from a buddy last week for $20 after he was finished with it. My review is based on single player campaign mode only, I don't have the option of playing online because I'm overseas.

I have been a big fan of the Tom Clancy games, especially the Splinter Cells, which is my all time favorite game franchise. I have to say I was disappointed with this game. First off the graphics were good, but compared with even Splinter Cell Conviction, which is over 3 years old, there were pretty poor and unimpressive on many missions. They certainly are not even close to any of the latest Call of Duty's, especially BO II or any of the Gears of War games. I realize they weren't aiming for a Call of Duty clone, but for instance in the cut scenes, most of the characters looked like they came off of a game released a decade ago(non blinking eyes, mouth barely moving when speaking, etc). The actual gameplay wasn't close to being as bad as most of the cut scenes, the actual Spec Ops characters looked great, but the enemies were pretty lame looking. On some of the missions, the terrain looked beautiful, on some it was very cheap looking. I read on another review that it looks like they put all their time into the main characters and forgot about everybody else; I couldn't say it any better.

Aside from most missions being very linear, the actual gameplay, graphics aside, was pretty well done. The movements are fluid, comparable to Gears of War more than any of the other military type shooters out now. But there were some things in the gameplay that were very annoying. Multiple times, I threw a grenade or the enemy threw one at me, where the grenade would land and be a dud, wouldn't explode. Also, when you're in cover behind a wall, etc and are in a firefight, if the rounds land close to you, they made it so the camera starts wobbling around in a circular and up/down motion and it's hard to reorient to the targets you were lookingat and cannot see anything above your head. Basically, it just wasn't realistic. Everything from the mounted machine guns to the C-4 to the mortars were not even close to producing the effect that they would in real life. You barely could even hear the rounds coming out of the SAW equivalent in this game. Mortars were landing and had the effect of a bullet taking one guy out, but the 3 people right beside him were still alive. You were able to completely destroy a Styker type vehicle with a mounted 240b type weapon, etc. Lastly, I started out playing in \\"Elite\\" difficulty. Apparently elite means only that that every one of the enemies aim at you. Even at a hundred yard, the enemies, all of them, have pin point accuracy and can spot only you even while in cover, but paid little attention to your teammates.

The actual conversations and speaking by the characters certainly showed that the script did not come from somebody that's ever been in the military or even familiar with the military beyond movies, very generic. For instance, the characters spotting somebody and saying something like \\"1 rifleman with an assault rifle\\" or in the middle of a firefight yelling \\"assault rifle, assault rifle!\\" or \\"light machine gun!\\", was just stupid. Maybe it's because I've been in the military and deployed, but nobody talks talks like that, it was really cheesy and generic.

This game was good and has a pretty fun campaign, but wouldn't say great. It looked like they rushed to put something out. This is a game that would be good if you are in the mood for a military shooter game, but bored with the Call of Duties or Battlefields. If they would have put more time and effort into this, it really could have been excellent. Good story, fluid movement, decent weapons, etc, but too many annoying things and cheap graphics makes this a game one that I wouldn't pay more than $20 for.

THEN I got this, which for the money blows the other 2 away that were in the 10-20$ price range.

Pros:

Crisp, clear audio that can be amplified far beyond a volume i'd ever need at my hearing level.

You can remove the feedback that most headsets suffer from by lowering your mic's output volume, and my friend was able to hear me perfectly clear even at that low. Though this is plausible as i'm not sure what sound system HE's working with, but I had no feedback and he had no troubles hearing, so it eliminated that fairly common issue.

Mic's flexibility is very smooth. It doesn't feel like a twist-tie coated with plastic as do the basic headsets when adjusting their angle.

Amazing audio for stereo output, I can hear footsteps in-game from across the level if I raise the volume high enough and i'm almost deafened by sounds i'm not prepared for, which is arguably a bad thing, but you can always lower the game's audio to a relaxing level if you don't want immersion that loud.

Cons: None, to be perfectly honest. Does what it's supposed to do. Loud game audio through the headphones and clear, loud audio from the mic.

Conclusion: Definitely worth the money, I was excited the entire time I waited for shipping and it didn't disappoint. It seems a little tedious during the initial plug in because unlike what i'm familiar with (simply plugging the jack into the controller's port) you actually have to plug in all provided cables into the Xbox, which is: A USB plug, that I have connected into the front slot. 2 standard stereo audio cables that are fitted into either the Xbox's A/V cable or the one provided in the package, and then you have to plug it into the controller. All of which leaves wires dangling across my floor towards the Xbox, but in my opinion it's all the more satisfying letting this headset take over my Xbox like that, lol. On a semi-negative note, it's going to take some breaking in for the headphones to feel comfortable on me. They're cushioned and look AND feel nice, but even on the loosest adjustments to the headset I felt a bit constricted by the headset being wrapped around my head. This may just be my own personal issue as I've never owned headphones that were pressed against my ears before, but it was the only noticeable thing about the headset I didn't like, but if I remember correctly the others took awhile to get used to as well, so i'll just have to wait for it to become mundane. 5/5 for the headset.

Wow, normally when a different developer takes over a AAA Franchise (or any franchise) you could end up with a disaster. This is not the case with Halo 4.

Concept: 10/10
Create another Halo game with more focus on the Master Chief and Cortana and add a new Alien Race complete with an arsenal of new weapon types. They pulled this off beautifully. Add a ton of Multiplayer Modes, too.

Story: 9/10
For the first time we get a real look at the background of the Master Chief. If you're a die hard Halo fan, you already know that the government kidnapped children and raised / engineered them as supersoldiers. These people have no conscience and are sociopaths. If you think about it, the Master Chief has killed thousands of enemies and he doesn't lose any sleep over it. These Spartans are paired up with an AI. The Master Chief has always had Cortana. She's guides him through the missions and acts as a link to his humanity. The story focuses on their relationship as they encounter a new alien threat to the human race. This is the most \\"human story\\" the Halo series has ever had.

Graphics: 10/10
Halo has never looked better! The characters are more detailed, there are more FX, and the environments are HUGE, which usually translates to EPIC!

Gameplay: 9/10
The gameplay is very well paced where you trade off from infantry battles, vehicle battles, air battles, etc. Many of the encounters give you great weapons AND vehicles and it's up to you to complete it any way you want. This works exceptionally well with their Co-Op system. Halo 4 also includes 4 difficulty levels and their Skulls System, which allows you to Turn On specific difficulty features. For example: Enemies have more Health, Enemies drop less Ammo, Enemies are more resistant to some damage, and less resistant to others... There are so many options to play through the campaign.

Multiplayer: 10/10
It's Halo Multiplayerwith everything that you'd expect from the franchise. You have the campaign options, Spartan Ops, which are missions designed for Co-op Play, and a ton of Competitive Modes. It's just about everything that you'd want.

Replay Value: 10/10
With so many ways to play through the Campaign and a variety of Multiplayer Modes, you could play Halo 4 for months. Play with your friends, play against your enemies, play on different difficulties with skulls turned on to test your skills...

Maturity: Teens
The Halo Franchise is always rated M because when Halo 1 came out, congress was freaking out about sniping in games and head shots. This is just a sci-fi adventure where you kill aliens with laser guns. There's no sex or swearing... There are a few cinematic deaths, but it's no more violent than the stuff on TV. If this was a movie, it would be PG-13.

Overall: 10/10
This may be my favorite Halo game. With a human story, beautiful graphics, smooth gameplay, and epic missions, it's definitely a GREAT addition to the franchise. This is a must buy for fans of the series or fans of the FPS genre. If you shop around, you can get it for $39.99, too.

Buy it if you love Halo.
Buy it if you love FPS games.
Buy it if you love Epic Sci-Fi.
Buy it if you will play the Multiplayer Modes.
Rent it if you just want to blow through the 8 hour campaign and play through the story.
Avoid this game if... umm... I can't think of a reason other than not liking the genre.

review_headline: Game crash is due to IP problem but it can be fixed
review_body:
We love this game and have it already on the Playstation, but really wanted it for Wii U to be able to play it on the pad. We bought the Wii U version of the game and returned it 3 times. The game kept crashing and locking up the system so bad that the system had to be unplugged to unlock it.

We tried several suggestions... standing it on it's side, setting the language to english, deleting saves amd restarting, and plugging into different USB ports to no avail. We thought maybe it was the machine (although we have never had any problems with any other games).

FINALLY, we found a post by googling the problem. Turns out the Wii U likes to have a dedicated IP address. Otherwise it will \\"piggyback\\" on other devices and crash. We have several internet devices in the same area, so it made sense. We looked up how to set a specific IP address and VIOLA... No more crashes!!!

This was the first Rayman game I played, so the characters and the story are all new to me, and it didn't matter much. The game play is fantastic. It's challenging, but doable, and so much fun to play together. My husband and I played this nightly this winter when it was too cold go go out, and we are sad that it's over now that we've beaten it. The difficulty ramps up at a nice pace, so you are comfortable with the controls and the new tricks you learn before the challenges get much bigger. The art work is beautiful! Sometimes, when one of us would die, instead of floating in our bubble over to the other person to be brought back, we'd just stay in the bubble and check out the background and take the time to appreciate the graphics, the detail and the colors.
The soundtrack is amazing. The lyrics are gibberish as far as we could tell, but we memorized the sounds anyway and sang along. The music is so much fun.
We beat the game and got to the credits before we had collected all 10 stone teeth, which confused us, so we went back and collected all the teeth and found that grants access to a bonus 11th level called land of the livid dead, which is SO HARD. I think the game creators made two levels of endings, the first at the end of the tenth level for kids or adults who don't want THAT much of a challenge, and then the 11th bonus world and boss for people who are serious platform gamers, or just tenacious as hell like us. We did a lot of cursing and screaming at the game to get through that 11th world. Most of requires perfect technique, perfect timing, and no stopping to regroup or to think for a second. The bonus boss is not easy either, and when we finally beat her we were glad to go to bed.
I would recommend this game to anyone who likes beautiful games, with a lighthearted theme, great music, and especially those who plan to play with friends, or people in their family. It was the most fun I've had since playing Super Mario 3, which waswhat, 15-20 years ago?!?
Get it, have fun, and get ready for that bonus world. It's BANANAS.

product_title: E-3lue Cobra EMS109BK High Precision Gaming Mouse with Side Control 1600dpi
review_headline: WARNING: NOT FOR GAMERS. YOU GET WHAT YOU PAY FOR.
review_body: The annoying thing about this mouse isn't even the mouse itself. It's how all these inexperienced so-called \\"gamers\\" (probably web browser gamers?) are saying that this mouse is fast and precise and is the best mouse. For the price? Maybe. But from day 1 of using this mouse I have already become quite disappointed with how the performance is turning out. Instead of wasting valuable investments on the fancy blue LED lighting, I just don't understand why 3lue or whoever the maker of this mouse is didn't invest in a better tracking system.    Basically, what I mean is, if you move the mouse fast enough (left right up or down), the mouse will not track your movement. The cursor stays exactly where it is and barely budges at all. It actually feels like it has NEGATIVE acceleration. This means I cannot do a fast 180 if I am playing an FPS game and I'm being shot from behind. That basically spells death for the player. Not to mention the lift off distance is horridly high (probably around 5~mm or more) which means my wrist is having a harder time doing more circles. Confused? Go here for more details:   [...]    You really can't go wrong for $17? Oh ho ho yes you most certainly can. Save up and buy something in the $30-$50 range. I promise you won't regret it. Once you start using a $50 mouse you can never go back.    Is it comfortable? Yes, definitely. Is it fancy? Yes, I like the blue LED lights. Is it flexible? I'd say the DPI settings say so. Is it cheap? Yep. Definitely.    But can it perform?    In the hands of an experienced gamer who's played competitively before, the answer is short and simple: No. Don't be fooled by the cheap price or the fancy LED lights or the fact that it's made in Japan and therefore must be of some \\"better quality\\" than a mouse made in China.    You get what you pay for; that's the only thing you gotta remember when it comes to the world of gaming.

review_headline: will the real Devil May Cry please stand up
review_body: To start, I'm forty two years old and don't play with my cell phone all day so that being said I'm sure my opinion wont connect with some but for those out there with a half a brain, (and I know our numbers are dwindling) I know you can relate. The joy I once had and still have in the Devil May Cry series simply does not exist in DMC 5 (notice the(DMC), what? is it cool to say DMC instead of saying Devil May Cry, will saying DMC relate to a younger audience? Were the earlier Devil May Cry's so good that Ninja Theory/Capcom thought they should distance themselves from the actual Devil May Cry title and replace it with DMC. It never fails to surprise me that when a game or a movie develops a winning formula someone feels the need to change it for something completely new. And it is so profound that so many reviews say something to the effect of \\"those of you who don't like Dante's new look need to get over yourselves. Whenever there's a game or movie coming out and it's a sequel or prequel to something previously successful and they have reportedly done something drastically different to the formula that made the film or game successful in the first place and you constantly hear the chorus of \\"come on people give it a chance, get over yourselves, the new look is going to be great. Two things immediately come to mind when I hear the \\"give it a chance\\" chorus, Final Fantasy x-2 and Star Trek with that jerk Chris Pine. I don't know about you but nothing they have done since can even hold a candle to Star Trek the original series. All we have with J.J. Abrams is Spielberg reincarnate. But back to Devil May Cry, I played it for about an hour than turned it off, knowing that I was going to trade it back in at Gamestop. The beginning scenes are trashy, not that I'm some sort of prude, but the scenes do not fit the spirit of Devil May Cry even given that Dante, as is well known, has the persona of a bad-ass and likes fast women. The people at Ninja Theory apparently are lazywhen it comes to creating lush environments. The environments are no where near as interesting and inspiring as previous Devil May Cry's, and this includes all of them with the exception of part 2. Well, even the environments in part 2 are better than 5. I think the particular individuals that made DMC 5 got together with the individuals that made part 2 and said to each other lets do everything wrong again, you know like the way you guys did in part 2. I cannot help but think that adolescents made DMC 5. The game reeks of immaturity and lacks the spirit of fascination that the earlier games had. Also what is going on with these large phrases that keep popping up on the walls, the floors, etc...And Dante to me looks like a tall skinny Justin Bieber. Anyway I am so disappointed in this travesty DMC 5. Us adults are getting old a suppose and I guess I'm suggesting that in this case talent has faded with the earlier Devil May Cry games and those who made them and it appears that children are now at the helm of a what was once a very, very exciting series, and one of the best franchises of all time. And it's a shame that less talent has to be synonymous with youth. And if it's not children that made DMC 5 than those responsible acted like them. Now I know you can probably site many good games that were made by young people and my only argument to that would be \\"yeah but they were mature young people\\"

review_headline: Good game, odd and long setup.
review_body:
I played this game on the XBox, and I figured I would get this for PC so I could play it with some mods.
With that, it's great. It's almost like playing a brand new game!
It still takes time to play through everything, so the game itself is great, if it wasn't for the long install and pointless extra security on the game I would have given 5 stars.

However, the install was a bit odd and lengthy. When you install the game, it's the original version of the game. They did not include the patch with it, so you need to download it.
The second disk with the additional content takes a good couple minutes to load up. I'm guessing it's because of vile validation as the drive I put the disk was constantly reading it. After a couple minutes, the auto-start kicked in and it installed just fine.
Oddly enough, you need to enable the content through the games launcher.
Thinking it might be a bad disk, I copied the install to my hard drive and tried to re-install. It took a couple minutes off it as well, though slightly less time. I just deleted the files off my hard drive and will keep the disk as obviously it's fine.

The game by default loads up the launcher that allows you to configure the video, audio, and add-on settings for the game. However, that launcher requires the install disk to be present. You also need to register the game in Games For Windows LIVE, so why the crazy checks?
There are ways around it, but I won't be discussing them.

review_headline: It's too bad I need to buy it
review_body:
I am a young father without much time for gaming. I am very reluctant to pay to use my gaming console which I own for simple "media center" things. HuluPLUS and Netflix are individually subscription based already, why should I pay to have the ability to pay for a subscription?
That said, I am currently paying $4/mo for the luxury of less clutter by the TV and using a single interface. I could buy a $50 Roku, but that cramps my minimalist style ;)

Pros:
-Unlock usage of separate subscription based apps (Netflix, HuluPLUS, etc.)
-Play Xbox online with friends (I do have friends on XBL)
-Skype-like Video chat online via MS messenger

Cons:
-Why should I pay for things that I pay for additionally? (Netflix, HuluPLUS, etc)

Final:
I get that the "Xbox network" needs maintained, but why not let Hulu and Netflix maintain that themselves? Wii has allowed them to do that effectively, as has [mostly] Sony. Roku and all of the other smartTV oems make it free... Why should I pay extra for a paid subscription?
Some things would be better with free access(READ: Playstation, Wii, Roku, etc.)

product_title: GAEMS Halo UNSC Vanguard Personal Gaming Environment (Xbox NOT Included)
review_body:
As the title suggests, this product is without a doubt the best mobile solution for any traveling gamer. I am a college student who doesn't live too far from home so I go home quite often to visit. Got my first real test run of it over the weekend and, I have to say, the Vanguard definitely exceeded my expectations.

Whats awesome:

- The display is absolutely gorgeous. 19\\" is an excellent screen size for on-the-go gaming and this one really shines. Luckily, I did not encounter any dead pixels on my screen (yet) as this seems to be one of the biggest problems most users have. Other than that, I really can't elaborate enough how awesome the display looks. Very crisp, no detectable latency, and the matte coating is a must have. I love the blue accent lighting around the display too, as it just adds a really cool touch to the unit.

- Sound quality is crystal clear. I was pleasantly surprised at the volume these little drivers are able to deliver and, as such, had to actually turn it down when I first used the Vanguard. But for those of you out there that like to game loudly, fear not as these drivers deliver powerful and crisp sound without distortion. The included remote is a convenient bonus to throw in as well.

- The overall build of the unit is also top-notch. Very durable plastic molding and ample rubber feet all around to make sure this thing isn't going anywhere. Secure latches are a definite plus to make sure it stays closed wherever you're going and the handle is very solid and easy to grip. The straps inside of the case that hold the console are also extremely well designed with perfectly placed rubber pads on them that hold the console in place while ensuring no scratches. I'm not much of a carrying strap person so I didn't really try it out but it is pretty solid material and the cool UNSC branding on it is neat and pretty soft for comfort. It gets a little heavy with everything in it, but hey, theres a ton of stuffthis box holds inside it. All in all, I am confident in the Vanguard's ability to easily and safely transport my console.

- The little mesh bags included for accessory storage are pretty nice too. They're made of soft, spongy material that doesn't feel like it's going to rip or fray over time. I suppose they hold as much as possible given there really isn't a lot of room in the case to hold a bunch of stuff but, like other users, I too was a little disappointed there wasn't room for a second controller. But it's definitely not a game changer. Either way, when you get it all packed up it's a nice and snug fit and I'm pretty amazed all that stuff fit in there.

What could be improved:

- Theres no dedicated place for game discs. While this isn't the worst problem to have, it is a little bit of a bummer to have this amazing case that elegantly stores all the cables, adapters, and a controller but had zero space for a few discs. I feel like the foam base included could have had some pockets/sleeves stitched on the back of it to hold the discs. I'm not asking to make room for the actual cases for the games, but basically forcing you to take an additional bag/case for games along with the Vanguard seems like a step backwards. Again, not a game changing problem, but I feel that a solution would not have been hard to implement.

- As said above, if there was anyway for GAEMS to squeeze in a little extra room for another controller it would be pretty awesome as gaming is always more fun with others, but frankly I am not sure if that's even possible given the tight confines inside the Vanguard.

- Having an integrated power supply for the console and display would have been really, really cool and could have made room for other accessories (like that controller!) but I know this is probably not GAEMS' fault. Microsoft would clearly have to be involved in the development of this as to ensure the product would not damage the console and comply with the warranty. But I believe I saw a post somewhere that this is a work and progress and GAEMS is collaborating with Microsoft on a solution.

- I really like the idea of the kickstand for the display to give multiple viewing angles. However, it'd be nice if the kickstand were designed in such a way to work better on soft surfaces such as a bed. If it were a bit wider I feel like it could have propped up the display a bit better but its essentially useless on a bed, couch, etc. Also if the kickstand supported a couple more angles, maybe if some sort of locking mechanism were incorporated into it, I'd be even more pleased with it. But if you're on a hard surface like a table, the kickstand works perfectly.

- I also hope GAEMS rolls out a line of the Vanguards that don't feature any Halo branding on it. While it wasn't a terrible nuisance to me, I would have preferred to have a solid black or navy colored case with no graphics on it. But it's not a huge deal as I am indeed a Halo fan, but I'd hate for this to be a turnoff to any potential customers out there as the Vanguard is pretty sweet.

Personally I feel this is a top quality product that obviously had very meticulous engineering work put into it and the negative aspects outlined above are honestly not even close to outweighing the positives. The price is steep, but for what it is, I seriously challenge anyone out there to show me a quality product that does everything the Vanguard does in such a sleek, compact, and downright cool package at a cheaper price. I am also blown away that one of the top dogs at GAEMS goes out of his way to give feedback to customer's feedback on Amazon. It is rare to find this level of appreciation for the customer and I must give the highest of praise to GAEMS for doing so.

So far the Vanguard has proved to be an amazing solution to transporting my Xbox around. I have a PS3 as well but have not yet stowed it in the Vanguard, however I am confident I would have the exact same experience. The Vanguard is a solid piece of work that does exactly what it advertises very well and I am sure any hardcore gamer out there will appreciate this fine piece of gaming hardware.

review_headline: Fun at first, but gets old quickly
review_body: When I got first got this game, I was extremely excited to play it, and had a great time for two hours or so, then I started to get frustrated. VERY frustrated. There's a feature where you reset if you go too far off the track, and although it seems good on paper, it's very annoying. I feel like whenever I'm winning, I'll drive ten feet off the road, have to wait 60 seconds to reset, and then find myself a mile back and in last place. Another aspect that makes it frustrating is what parts of scenery are immovable, and what parts aren't. It's very counterintuitive. There are things that, in other racing games, you could drive right through without affecting your speed, but in this, you'll total your car and have to restart. The first day I got it, after being incredibly determined to beat it, I later found myself sitting alone with my Xbox sobbing and screaming at the TV at 3:00 am. Even a year after getting it, whenever I play it, I'll have fun for 20-30 minutes... and then end up throwing things around the room in anger. This is easily the most frustrating game I have ever played. Overall, decent game to rent for a day, terrible to buy. Just don't buy it. Please.

Forget what you know about MMORPGs. The Secret World takes the mold and breaks it, then hides the pieces and leaves you clues to find them. Unlike anything you have ever played before, TSW has a riveting story line, fascinating interactions with mythical creatures, and a culture based around superstition and conspiracy. Once you get into it, it will be very hard to leave.

The only downside is that this is NOT your typical, brain-on-autopilot online game. You have to think, use strategy, and rely on your wits as much as your guns or super powers. product_title: NCIS: Based on the TV Series - Nintendo 3DS
review_headline: Not bad, but a little short
review_body:
I watch NCIS occasionally - pretty much weekly considering my Dad watches the marathons every weekend. I enjoy the show well enough, particularly the characters. I was unsure whether or not this game would be able to accurately portray what happens in the show.

As for the length of the game, it didn't last too long; it only had 4 cases that were linked together. I don't know if it was necessarily worth $40, maybe $25 or so based on the length. It might just be me, considering I usually pay $30-$40 for RPGs that last me a good 50 hours plus.

As for gameplay, I thought that was okay. I did not enjoy the puzzles very much, especially decrypting things - the first few decryption puzzles were okay, but the last one or two were hard to figure out to get a perfect score, so I had to reset many times and I still didn't get a perfect score. The crime scene investigations were pretty straight-forward; all you had to do was make sure that you found all of the clues, and there were extra things you had to click on to get all points for the crime scene; basically you need to click on everything and you'll be fine. The interrogations could be a little annoying, because sometimes you didn't necessarily know what you need to say or what evidence to present. Save often, especially right before interrogations. I do wish you didn't have to use the stylus for everything.

With the graphics, the character portraits were good, but the other parts reminded me a little bit of PS1 graphics in general. This is a 3DS game, but I never play with 3D on, so I can't say how well the 3D worked with this game.

I feel like the story was actually decent, although I felt it was slightly predictable in the end - I won't say anything else so that I don't spoil it, but I really did think it was pretty easy to guess the ending. I did love the character interaction; I feel like Tony, Ziva, Abby, and Ducky were especially well done. Tony frequently referenced recent movies, which I liked, Ziva constantly mixed up phrases, Abby's obsession with Caf-Pow was quite evident, and Ducky constantly interjected with random facts. I feel like Gibbs and McGee were just okay.

In the end, NCIS 3D was a cute, amusing game, if not a little too short. I enjoyed the character interaction, and I quite enjoyed being promoted as cases went by - only in a video game can you be promoted to \\"Very Special Agent\\" within 4 cases. :)

The Silpheed series is known for adding a bit of cinematic flair to the shmup genre. I won't blame anyone for not knowing this is a sequel, as the first Silpheed game was released on PC-88 and Sega CD. That cinematic flair continues here, with briefings between levels, and lots of interactive backgrounds and story elements happening mid-game.

The most interesting part about the gameplay is the weapon system. You can equip different weapons to the left and right side of the ship. Ship positioning can be important if you equip them differently.

Scoring is based on enemy proximity. The closer you are, the more points you get. So basically, optimal scoring is like a kitten: Act nice and snuggle up close, then unleash your claws.

Level and weapon design is unfortunately where the game becomes less interesting. Pacing needs work, as there are several long boring stretches that just aren't exciting enough. Weapons, while varied in execution, are weak and limited in usefulness. This could have been a fun game with a bit of extra firepower and more enemies. I find it difficult to play all the way to the final level, not because it's too hard, but because there game just isn't all that fun. Speaking of the final level, that's the best part by far though, and offers good amount of challenge. So the question is, is the journey worth it?

The PS2 has a lot of really good shmups. Silpheed: The Lost Planet is decent, however I'd only suggest it to someone who already has the better ones and is looking for more.

review_headline: Harder difficulties make this one fun.
review_body:
Demon Attack is a shooter where you fight waves of flying demons.

Yea, there's a level in Phoenix that plays sort of like this. However this is a really good version of that stage! Large demons shoot a huge swarm of bullets at you; while I'm sure this is just a large sprite with a bunch of dots, when this game first came out it really looked like they were shooting massive amounts of bullets.

Depending on the difficulty and how far you've progressed, shooting demons will either destroy them outright or split them into smaller demons. Demons will also sometimes try to suicide into you, with a screaming sound effect.

The background sound effect is handled well, and it increases in intensity as you defeat the demons on each stage.

I suggest playing on the harder game modes (I like 7 best), which lets you see all of the game features quickly. On the lower difficulties the game is less fun.

review_headline: Will not run on many desktop computers
review_body:
Even though your processor and operating system my meet the specifications, very few video cards, do. You have to be running a video game type high-powered graphics card. Most power supplies won't support the extra wattages pulled by these gaming cards and computer mfg. only build dedicated gaming systems that can handle this type of card. We are talking about $1500-3000 desktops. You could buy a brand new XBox or PS3, and new 46-inch flat screen and a new Gibson Les Paul Studio for what you'd spend on the computer that will run this game properly. Huge disappointment Christmas Morning. To top it off, it took 6 1/2 hours for the program to download from Steam. Even though it comes with a CD, the software has to be downloaded, Its a 13GB file that my ISP throttled to 400ks/s max download speed after the first 5GB. That's with ATT U-verse at the highest plan.

Update: I've researched all day. Went to Best Buy, took the game and asked them to recommend a system that will run it, without breaking the bank. The tech recommended the HP Envy which was on sale for $649 or the HP Pavilion which is $749. Keep in mind, this was after a techno-geek deciphered the vague system requirements listed on the box. So, $1500 to $3000 may be a little extreme. Still doesn't make sense to me to buy a new computer for a video game. My eMachine EL1352 does every thing I need, up until I crossed paths with Rocksmith. UPS is stopping by tomorrow to pick it up and take it back This is the reason I buy on Amazon. It's scheduled for pick up, free to return and easy.

Hunting can be annoying; I've found that sticking to the trees with the hidden blade equipped provides the best result, that or stay in tall grass so you're hidden and throw bait, this is how the game teaches you to hunt in the introduction to the feature. The only hunting method I'm not sure how to do properly yet is the snare.

I do agree that full sync is hard if not impossible (for me yet) to achieve and that you have more fun going for just a few of them if any at all, sometimes it is fun to do but after a few failed missions because of trying to complete the optional objectives it's funner to just give up on them and play the story. As to the varying damage/controls being rigged to make you fail missions I've never encountered this, I didn't have any issues saving Terry or any other mission where I felt like I'm taking more damage or not acting like I should be.

I do however slightly dislike that one click of the mouse will do a massive combo attack to show off the fancy animations, while the game doesn't seriously suffer from the \\"one button does everything\\" syndrome some others do, I don't like it as much and still find myself clicking the attack button plenty while attacking because of the sheer number of animations going on.

review_headline: A good replica of the original
review_body:
The new Neo-Geo X joystick is a faithful reproduction of the original AES joystick. The stick itself has the great \\"clicky\\" tactile feedback and the buttons are just like you're back at the arcade.

The cable on the joystick is relatively short at just five and a half feet long, but you can extend the length by using a standard USB extension cable since the joystick now uses USB connections. It's worth noting that because of this the original AES joysticks and the new Neo-Geo X joysticks are NOT interchangeable.

The joystick also has Select and Start buttons. The Start button functions the same as it does on the Neo-Geo X handheld, while the Select button is used to pause the gameplay (the same as the R1/R2 buttons do on the handheld unit).

Since there is no Menu button on the joystick you are not able to exit your game and return to the main Neo-Geo X menu from the joystick. If you want to change games you have to get up and push the Reset button on the Neo-Geo X docking station.

All in all this is a great joystick. Anybody who picks up a Neo-Geo X should also add an extra joystick to the cart so you can play the many two-player games that come preloaded on the Neo-Geo X!

review_headline: This is a MUST Play for any Shooter game Enthusiats.
review_body:
To give one word describing Spec Ops the Line's release into an over saturated military shooter game market, is none other than \\"wonderful.\\" Now, I know you are thinking \\"wait, why wonderful? Wouldn't that word be pertaining to something positive or gleeful nature? Not some 3rd person shooter that shows the horrors of Post Traumatic Stress Disorder and war in general?\\" It would yes, but the developers Yager and publisher's 2K games unleashed a single player experience that needs to be played at some point for the violent military shooter game enthusiast.

The main thrill of Spec Ops The Line's firefights are pretty much hit or miss. Where it misses, the game immediately makes it up in the dark, gritty narrative presentation. At first you think this trio of Delta squad operatives are going to hint at the typical cockiness we've seen in games like Gears of War or other first person shooters. But as the story progresses into it's Heart of Darkness theme, the main characters start to show very realistic emotional and physical responses to what they do to enemies and civilians in Dubai. The dialogue is once again top notch with Nolan North in probably one of his best motion captures and voice overs. Please note that this game's content is very Mature rated. Profanity is abundant and the violent imagery is tremendous. The scenery of post sandstorm Dubai is beautiful. Lots of debris \\"invisible walls\\" persist, but the amount of detail to various locations are displayed dramatically and strangely beautiful. When playing on PC, the in game character models are very well done. Most notably is the transition the main characters endure and how their models change as the story goes on. Sand plays as the new destructive barrel gimmick and I welcomed the idea of shooting glass to have sand crashing down burying enemy soldiers. The music soundtrack helps the atmosphere while in game with very familiar tracks by well known artists. The original score created by the development team adds the perfect desperate and \\"time is running out\\" mood. Players who watched Apocalypse, Now! will notice these music elements fit perfectly. Spec Ops the Line is officially the \\"Silent Hill\\" of military shooter games.

The most discussed subject of criticism this game received was it's very lackluster multiplayer. I did not touch one bit of it because my intent was to play the campaign. In honesty, they should have taken it completely out. Not every game that involves shooting has to have the element of multiplayer. Most cases, it can't help a game's longevity, especially if you direct your marketing to the single player portion. Yager could have focused more on the single player to polish up loose ends and add more play time. The biggest issue I had was with the control. It handled okay on PC. My hiccups were sometimes trying to aim right while messing with cover and sprinting. It felt weird, but it is was a small issue. The AI for this game will not be like Call of Duty or Battlefield variety. Sometimes it will be easy to dominate, other times you will be aggravated at the random difficulty increase of trying to flank while being barraged by bullets. It did get old watching the screen change color with the sound muffling mechanic when close to death. I've never been a fan of these, but 3rd person shooter developers (Naughty Dog or Sucker Punch for example) love to include these annoying effects. The strangest moment I had was after reading a loading screen tip about a certain sniper rifle able \\"to kill any enemy no matter what location,\\" and a direct chest and head shot on an heavy soldier didn't allow that. The final gripe I had was the quick slow down in time after getting a random head shot that the developers thought would add to the grittiness in game. The over the top gimmick of a headshot resulting the head completely blown off from a single bullet be if from a M1A4 assault rifle or M-9 pistol was not needed. This mechanic fails when you look at a body model's lack of design effort. It's just weird.

The story gets dark and morbid fast, and it's nice to see how your squad mates react to the destruction you wrought upon enemies and Dubai itself. This is a rare gem in these days of shooter video games. I loved how Yager wasn't afraid to show how screwed up a militaristic action could go then take the action seriously. Killing is never easy and the justifications of what is murder and righteous start to blur each other out. If you thought the airport level/scene in Call of Duty Modern Warfare 2 was shocking, just wait till you experience certain parts in Spec Ops The Line. The game version I played had Steamworks support, which is an immediate plus in my book. I personally would not have paid full price for this game. If on a Steam or Amazon sale, I would consider purchasing it for a weekend play.ou look at a body model's lack of design effort. It's just weird.

This review is for the 60 day Rift Time Card. What I was looking for, was game time I could buy online and recieve a time code via e-mail or electronically. That is not the case with Amazon's Time Card. You have to wait for it to arrive in the mail before you can get the code off the back. If you're looking for a way to buy game time and get an instant code to put in your game I have 2 suggestions.

1.) Gamestop.com
Their prices are the same and they have the 30 day option as well. If you buy from them, you'll get your time code pretty quickly. They have an application, like Steam that shows all the games you've bought from them. If you buy a game time card from Gamestop.com, you'll see your game on their app, you just hover over it and there's your product code.

2.) I didn't realize it at the time I bought this time card but you can actually purchase 30 or 60 days worth of game time straight from within the game. They had a free weekend this weekend, which is what I was playing, and after purchasing this card, I realized in game there was a store icon. I clicked it just to see what they had to offer and sure enough there was 30 and 60 days worth of time right there staring at me for the same price. I could have just bought it from within the game and it be automatically applied. This is also good if you're getting ready to run out of your current time, you can just keep buying from within the game if you don't feel comfortable putting your credit card in for a montly fee.

So if you want the physical card, this is the way to go if you don't feel like leaving the house to get one. However, if you're wanting an instant code to apply to your game don't get this and read 1 & 2 above.

review_body:
So I'm sitting here watching the ending credits after a play through, being that this particularly game was given to me by a lovely woman of gracious kindness, I can now describe whether or not you the interested player/buyer would like to purchase this title.

I will give this an overall 3 stars but I would concede that as far as pushing the envelope and trying to turn a new spin on an over done game type ( First Person) --- Bethesda took a dice roll on this one and managed to crank out an imaginative world that held your interest, long enough to conclude the tale... with issues along the way. I didn't care for the very monotonic script the characters you come across, particularly the main NPC's whom have the most influence on your quest. It comes off as a robotic world with particularly attention to details in some ways, while others, are very repetitive and attempting to fuse the Gothic with the steam punk, giving it a sort of a Jules Vern/Sherlock Holmes/Howels Moving Castle (for you Anime Fans) approach, set in what could be in late Victorian England where your expected to accept that the machinery and tools you find is supposedly powered by something as simple as Whale Oil. I find remnants of particular past games in Dishonored --- Fable III, Bio Shock, elements of Thief, I was even looking for Ebeneezer Scrooge to come out one of the Victorian stores to tell me the Plague has reached poor Cratchet and if I could finish the job because he was too cowardly to do it himself. There are cliche bad guys, some with bald heads and sporting monocles, pigeon chested bobby type guards whom at times resemble Austrian soldiers in the early centuries to even WW1 vintage German Officer uniforms. The people are also generic, you can't have Steam Punk without usual characters wearing over the top gloves and factory overalls! The Rich resemble French Revolutionary era clothing, long leather boots with huge bustles or the dudes with those sharp coat tails and Redbaron like mustaches. They really insured you pretty much knew where they wanted to come from, Plague ridden Dunwall is a nasty place, with nasty characters that are either consumed in sometimes harrowing acts of the occult, authoritarian government with its tall and menacing guard towers,complete with propaganda posters attempting to sell approved statements of public behavior and morals. Loud speakers blare warning about contamination, wanted posters littering alleyways and light posts, looming last ditch attempts from draconian enforcement tactics to even walling off entire city blocks to their doom. In this environment, you are thrust into a world of desperation, blurred good vs evil, conspiracy, corruption, greed, death, sex ( implied, written --- but tasteful and nothing over the top nor gratuitous, something painfully missing in other games but done nicely in this title), blind ambition, and abuse of power. Your getting what you got from Les Miserables, Uptown Sinclare's \\" The Jungle\\" --- Soooo your ready get on down and get you a copy right? STOP.

Although the mood and environment is set correctly... once again, you can tell an artist and graphic design master put a lot of effort after all, this is a Video Game...but the story does fizzle out after your 5th helping of steam-pipe/boiler room/sewer system crawling. The plot is predictable and the characters make it even worse with laughable speech that doesn't fit the events taking place. The various points of the plot are dimmed to simple mission giving by this square jawed, big framed military type, you almost want to see him jump on his desk and claim \\" I AM MIGHTY!\\" --- you have an assortment of weapons but if you use them too much, you are indeed penalized. No. Its not a sudden change but you get a slightly different ending if you play the Assassin that never Assassinated anyone and forgive just about everybody who tries to poison, stab, beat you to death in a torture chair, or kills your precived love interest --- although its never really truly discussed as to whether Corbo was or wasn't the main squeeze of the Empress before her said event. All of these nifty gadgets and quasi Full Metal Alchemist type powers that lead you into this netherworld where a floating deity talks about the various things you'll choose to do and the characters in the story --- and yet... your reduced to two options of non-lethality which are sleep darts, sleeper grips, and certain passive powers that are made to aid you in covert tactics rather than brute strength.

I highly disagreed in how the moral mechanics worked in this game, it defeats not only the main purpose for the game \\" Guy wants revenge for the death of his Ladyship and those who wanted to hang him for a crime he didn't commit\\" but also... the whole get up of the Metal Destro mask for intimidation purposes to countless charms that are basically made to either take pain or keep you fighting better. Why anyone would spare someone in the situations that are presented and the background of how the more shady characters are treating the world around them....and forcing that as a path to good is just plain stupid. I know if you give me a poison glass of brandy then shove me in a rickety John boat in an plague infested river of waste with zombie victims and acid spitting plants.... you bet when I come back it isn't to preach the bible to you.

Game play is not smooth. Its not broken... but its not smooth. Sneaking and being unseen is at times hit-or-miss. Your projectile weapons are garbage until later upgrades. Melee combat is also hit or miss in many occasions ( a frequent problem that has been mentioned already)and at times, when you think you can reach a ledge or get to a point you need to be --- it isn't so, and you wind up head first into a swarm of eating rats or those peg-leg guys. There are a few shining examples of greatness --- such as the infamous costume ball you need to infiltrate (beautiful colors and reflective patterns, really treasure for the eye), and the dark and foreboding office of the Regent --- the great background of a dark and stormy night with imposing pictures of statesman long dead, nepolianic figures with military metals and sharp eppeletes, with complaining female maids scowling that they have to endure gross perversions by the evil hierarchy to keep their jobs. Great scene development there.

The efficiency of menus is awkward and not as fluid as one would like compared to other games. The prices of goods and weapons are expensive comparative to the availability to gather wealth. Some powers are somewhat a waste of time if not for simply to mess around when you're r bored. ( My Opinion).

Graphics --- 3. Its not the staple of this game but its good enough to look over these minor flaws.

Over all fun --- 3. As many reviewers report --- its a blast at first but quickly gets hampered down by repetitive looking levels and events.

Replay value ---- 2. I did not think it warranted another go for what you get.

Creativity --- 4. There are some points and creativity in the story that deserves its perfect rating. The books you get to read. The scenes. The environments. The designs of the contraptions. The Sci-Fi, fantasy, Horror and mysticism. It acts and feels like a Tim Burton movie with Johnny Depp as the pale and weird guy in a Victorian suit, flying and appearing on high steeples doing mischief and uncovering deadly conspiracies.

Story --- 2. Wasted in its execution, they started something great but couldn't keep the vibe. There was tremendous opportunity and fleshing out but its a case of way too much attempting to be packaged in a short experience. However there is enough to make up your own story using the imagination and implications found throughout Dunwall.

Dishonored is good at $30.00. I would not have bought this retail though as stated before,it was a gift for me. The current used price is well enough but otherwise, its a one hit show that is most likely better off rented. It doesn't have replay value in my opinion, I do not know if there is a DLC for this game as of yet but even so --- it would be way low on someone's To-Play list.

3 Stars.

I've played the core of Spider-Man games - since the first two on PSOne, to Spiderman 2, and even the mediocre Spiderman 3. I skipped over all the filler games in between, because they just didn't seem like they had much effort put into them. I was in the mood for another go-round with ol' Spidey, so I finally decided to pick this up from RedBox to try out for a day. The rest is history - beat the whole thing in the past 24 hours (probably spent around 12 hours with everything)...and I'm amazed. This game is incredible fun. If you've played other Spiderman games, then I must warn you - it's different. The feel is just much different than the previous games, but once you play it for awhile you realize that it all works very well and is finely tuned (e.g. Spiderman swinging/playing very differently indoors and outdoors, and perfectly suited for both). Swinging around New York is amazing...you go much further, higher, and faster in this game than any other iteration, but it's welcome. It brings an entirely fresh, new, and exhilerating experience to the table. The story is good, fighting gets fun after awhile after you earn some upgrades, and somehow it managed to not get too terribly repetitive. Then again, I love 'busy work' in games - rescuing people and taking them to hospitals, stopping car chases...it's all part of Spiderman, and they're all very fun. Concerning the featured low review of this game, why would you want likenesses?? This game benefited MUCH more by being separate from the movie characters than it would have by incorporating them. I probably wouldn't have played the game if I would've known emo, prissy, and miserable Andrew Garfield was under the mask. To end this, if you're a Spiderman fan, then get this game. It's DEFINITELY worth the play, and DEFINITELY worth the buy. Deserves at least 4.5 stars on here!
