review_headline: Whether Your 1st JRPG or 100th, This is Amazing!
review_body:
I played the PS2 version of Persona 4 last year and still I eagerly found myself downloading this title on launch day. Why? Because it's that good. So good I couldn't wait to jump back in and solve a mystery with my friends in Inaba.

And here it is. It's back, and better than ever. We all know the graphics are much more crisp, but what actually took me by surprise is how much additional polish they put into the game. Menus are rife with color and I love watching the opening cinematic everytime I turn on the game. It's like a bag of Skittles exploded, yet somehow all of the colors blend well together. And the soundtrack is spectacular, and yes, there are some new tunes in this updated version.

One of my favorite new features of the game is the updated Shuffle Time post-battle. Instead of randomly choosing cards, you're given chances to score multiple prizes and go for a Sweep which will give you further bonuses on your next Shuffle Time. It's ridiculously addicting.

The skill cards are also a great addition that make it much easier to customize your favorite Persona to your liking. Want a Jack Frost with Bufu, Garu, Zio, and Agi? Farm the cards and knock yourself out! I recommend giving them to the all new NPC, Marie, however. That way you can get the skills whenever you want for a monetary fee.

My only knock on the game is Chie's new voice actress. I understand they couldn't get the original back, and while the new VA does a great job, it's hard for me to shake the feeling that something is off. This is probably because her old voice is still fresh in my memory from recently playing the PS2 copy. Teddie's VA is also new, but I think he comes really close to the voice of the original, and it was much easier to adjust to him. Of course, if this is your first time playing, you don't have to worry about this paragraph at all. They do a great job, it's just different from the original!

Overall, I think everyone with an interest in JRPGs and turn-based combat should play this game. It's a unique adventure with amazing personalities, and you'll have an unforgettable good time!

product_title: Call of Duty: Black Ops II
review_body:
Dont let all these biased 1 star reviews dragging the overall rating down influence your decision whether or not to try this game. Most of the angry so called gamers come on here and trash the game because whatever play style or tactic they relied so heavily on doesnt work the same way in this game. Most play it for a day or 2, and when they arent doing well doing whatever they did in the previous game they blame bad game design, lag or whatever as the reason.

This is another fine entry in the COD franchise by Treyarch who has clearly taken the lead in the COD franchise after 2 Infinity Ward disasters. Common complaints I hear are campers, bad spawns, lag, etc. Problems that people claim exist in every FPS since the invention of the genre, no worse no better than any other FPS game, at this point its just a scapegoat for kids to blame when they lose or are outplayed.

I've spent hours playing every COD to date. This one is fantastic and refreshing. The pick 10 system is great and long overdue. It allows thousands of possible custom class options, dont use your secondary, take a second tier 1 perk. Dont use tactical grenades, take a 3rd attachement for your primary weapon.

The killstreaks are also nice and balanced, they are back to being what they are supposed to be, just an assistance, not the main focus of the game like the Infinity ward games with 30 vehicles in the sky at all times. They have adapted the scorestreak system from MW3, where capturing objectives, calling in UAVS, pretty much everything adds to you scorestreak. Objectives count considerably more towards the streak than just kills. This has considerably elimnated the objective game killstreak campers created by the Modern Warfare games.

People are complaining about the spawns but what do you expect them to do, each map has a finite area and if the enemy team is spread throughout the map, at some
point someone is going to be within a few seconds of you. Dont blame the spawns, there is nothing that can be done to make every spawn perfect 100% of the time.

If you are running around with a sniper or an assault rifle an you run into an smg user at close range you probably should lose the battle. If you use the weapon wrong, which most people do in these games, they lose the battle and cry lag or spawns.

review_headline: My favorite monkey, hampered by lackluster controls
review_body:
DK Country was my favorite game from the 16 bit era. I was really looking forward to playing this modernized edition, but it has unfortunately fallen well short of my hopes. This is a game that requires VERY precise platforming skills. Normally, I would embrace this challenge, but Nintendo decided they wanted to implement some goofy motion controls into the schematics, thereby ruining the experience. Even while playing with classic controller setup, a brief movement of the wiimote will accidentally send DK into a roll... right off the edge of that platform. Even in the 90s, I never experienced such poor platforming controls.

Please note that this an Amazon Verified Purchase... I tried my best to enjoy this game, but I just can't do it. Playing it only makes me want to return to the super tight controls of Rayman Origins, which has this game whipped in every conceivable category. You can't expect every game to be as good as Rayman Origins (especially since it came out one year later), but the difference in quality is downright staggering.

On the plus side, this game has very good art design. I enjoyed the weird enemies, and DK and Diddy are just as lovable as ever. But... as a platformer, this game is not in the same league as Rayman Origins.

product_title: G155-Gaming and Entertainment Mobile System (Xbox 360/ PS3 Not included)
review_body:
Overall, this is a wonderfully made product!

1) Size, weight and transport:

About the size of two briefcases stacked together. It is easy to carry considering its bulk and what it houses (we have PS3 as well as all the accoutrement).

Weighs a little over 10lbs by itself and with the game console and accessories, easily another 5lbs. While it is not heavy for me to carry. It is NOT designed for laps.

I find it easier to use the handle than the strap (It does NOT come with straps, but I had plenty of straps laying around. So I hooked up two key-hooks to the latches' baggage/luggage lock-loops and then hooked up a strap over it).The strap option was not that comfortable and it makes the case swing when I walk. It also makes me feel like I have to clutch it tight; otherwise, it would fall off my shoulder. Looping it over my neck gives me strap burn and is extremely uncomfortable.

2) Protection and Security:

Its hard plastic is durable. But it does scratch easy. However, it does a good job protecting what's important: Your game console. Its built in screen seems well housed in also.

I have only dropped this twice from about 3 feet. And was glad nothing cracked or broke inside, including the screen itself.

The two lockable latches are fast to attach and detach with an option to place baggage/luggage locks on it.

3) capacity:

For its dimensions, it did a great job utilizing all the spaces. The two storage bags on the sides hold one controller each and the USB cable as well as power/HDMI cable along some other minor cables that you need. If you are thinking about a noise reducing headphone or more controllers, you are looking at cramming them in that might damage your cords. You can place them on top of the gaming unit itself, but that will be very tight plus you run into scratching your monitor.(you can cram two controllers in one bag, but I would NOT recommend it)

I'd say comfortably: holds TWO controllers and their USB cords, two plugs (one for the case for its monitor, and the other for the gaming console). A couple of HDMI cords(one for backup). You definitely want to consider buying a multiple outlet for the plugs as sometimes it is hard to find a place that would have two open outlets for the console and the case.

4) A/V:

Video quality is pretty good if you don't compare it to a 120hz 1080 HD TV. At very very high speed, there could be a slight line or lag. But barely noticeable unless you are absolutely anal about perfection. But for on the road, this is wonderful. You can adjust the settings on the monitor. Which is a nice plus. I do worry about scratching the screen. But have been extremely careful.

Audio quality is decent. When you are close to the console, the sound is rich enough that you aren't missing out. I prefer to use the headphones when I use this console anyways. But for those times that you don't want to use a headphone, the sound is decent.

5) Console placement:

The PS3(it has to be SLIM)fits snuggly in the unit and there is a strap to secure it. Perhaps a little bit too snug. As I find the heating issue does happen. Highly recommend buying a tiny fan to direct the heat. The front where you have to plug in the USB can be a bit of a nuisance to maneuver especially if you are getting into the multi-player/dongles.

6) Not just for gaming consoles:

We have tablets/smart phones that use mini/micro HDMI. They all work with this case. (you have to buy the cables). Our Panasonic Blu-Ray(not 3D) DVD player works with the case (for the times when our kids are using the PS3 on the big TV and we take out the old Blu-Ray and use this case for it).

One of the best things that I use it for is for when I am on the road, my kids, of course, have the PS3 at home. But I bring this case and I plug in my smart phone. I now havea 15\\" screen to watch my netflix that I can stream in a 4G network. Sometimes, when I am taking a break, I stay in my van, plug this case into my 120 vote outlet and plug my smart phone in it to catch a show on netflix or use any of my apps for games or to read the news or surf the net or Facebook.

product_title: Activision Skylanders Giants Single Character Pack Core Series 2
review_body:
Inititally I wasn't going to get Pop Fizz, but when I went on release day there was a very limited amount of Skylanders, and the only way to get series two Whirlwind and Trigger Happy was to get the triple pack with Pop Fizz. I'm actually glad that I gave him a shot. Not totally elated, however.

Speed: Fast
The way he runs is a little awkward, but he does get along pretty quickly.

Primary Attack:
Pop Fizz's primary attack is tossing his currently equipped potion. This attack, even when upgraded, is kind of clumsy and not very effective. You start out with an exploding orange potion, then a purple potion that creates little beakers that attack your enemies, then a green one that creates a puddle of acid that damages enemies that step into it. I will admit, the green potion is good for Wandering Trogs, as they take damage very slowly. If you chose the Mad Scientist upgrade path, your potions have increased damage and improved effects, you can release up to three potions at once, and the potions may be mixed when thrown (ex: if you throw an orange potion onto a green potion, a flame will spring up.)

Secondary Attack:
Far better than the primary attack, the secondary attack allows you to go into berserker mode. Pop Fizz is an alchemist, which explains why he uses potions, but he also has the Jekyl and Hyde ability to drink his potions (sometimes called \\"soda\\", probably to deter children from mixing dangerous things together and drinking them) and turn into a big, powerful beast. I like melee attacks, and the beast uses his big clawed hands to swipe crazily at enemies. It starts off not lasting very long, but gets better when upgraded. If you choose the Best of the Beast upgrade path, the beast meter drains slower, attacking enemies increases the meter, and he can preform attacks depending on whatever potion you currently have equipped.

Tertiary Attack:
Unlike a lot of the new Skylanders, Pop Fizz does not have a third main attack.

Soul Gem:
This redeems the potion abilities. You can shake the potion bottle rapidly, and it will cause an explosion that deals a serious blow. The only downside to this is that Pop Fizz becomes momentarily stunned from the explosion, and is therefore vulnerable to enemies.

Overall:
If you really want a new magic Skylander, hold out for Ninjini. She seems like her attacks are going to be much more effective, and she's a Giant on top of that. I'm not saying Pop Fizz is a bad Skylander, he's just not very powerful unless in beast mode.ave a third main attack.

review_headline: EASILY the Weakest of the Trilogy
review_body:
With the benefit of having played all three games in the series now (and yes, I played Mass Effect well before its sequels were released), Mass Effect is the most skippable, superfluous entry in the series. BioWare simply over-promised and under-delivered, as many game developers are apt to do to generate hype and sales. BioWare's biggest deception was the promise that player choice would impact the plot.

Now that we've seen Mass Effects 2 and 3, we know that the claim was a bald-faced lie. Initial interviews with BioWare developers suggested that there would be literally \\"hundreds of permutations\\" of branching plotlines that would have had a significant impact on the main storyline. Simply put, the idea was that by playing a different Renegade or Paragon Shepard, or some flip-flopping permutation thereof, you could affect the fate of the universe. Skeptics, myself included, knew that this couldn't possibly be true, especially with BioWare's promise of full voice acting and cinematic presentation. The research, development, technical and writing challenges alone would be unimaginable.

So we were left with the illusion of choice: \\"choices\\" that feel emotionally powerful for a moment, but have zero effect on the outcome of the game. I won't bother giving major plot spoilers on a game this old, but suffice it to say, it really doesn't matter whether you like Kaidan or Ashley better. It also doesn't matter if you think Anderson or Udina would be a better leader. None of the choices you make will have a lasting effect on the universe of Mass Effect or its sequels. So what does that leave you?

All of these broken promises would have been acceptable if the gameplay were up to snuff. Instead, Mass Effect is an awkward third-person shooter with ham-handed \\"RPG style\\" character development shoehorned in. The cover system is terribly inconsistent and easily eclipsed by Gears of War, a game that predated Mass Effect by nearly a year. (This is fixed in Mass Effects 2 and 3). Weapons are shackled to a poorly conceived \\"heat-buildup\\" system that was mercifully scrapped in the sequels. The inventory management of your completely frangible items is infamously god-awful, especially on the PC version, which requires multiple clicks to delete each and every useless item (which you will have to do frequently, sometimes multiple times per mission).

The best thing about Mass Effect is that it gives background to the excellent Mass Effect 2. With MUCH improved gameplay, more interesting characters/hireable teammates, and a refreshingly dark plot, Mass Effect 2 dispatches with much of BioWare's false RPG pretense and delivers a satisfying third-person shooter. Mass Effect 3, for all of its infamous plot \\"twists,\\" manages to refine Mass Effect 2's gameplay further for another great gameplay experience. The multiplayer is an addictive and polished spin on Gears of War 2's \\"Horde Mode\\" and is a nice touch overall.

Let's face it: BioWare hasn't crafted a good roleplaying game since Baldur's Gate 2. Even then, I suspect much of its quality was the result of executive oversight from the legendary team at Black Isle. Mass Effect is a poor compromise between the cinematic aspirations of the Xbox 360 generation and true CRPG elements defined back in the 1990's. The purpose of this review isn't to make you hate the Mass Effect series: it's to save you time and money by pushing you straight to Mass Effect 2 and 3. And if you must torment yourself through 20+ hours of awkward gameplay, go with the Xbox 360 version. You'll avoid a few bugs and feel less frustrated compared to the PC version's terrible control scheme.

I don't nearly get excited about video games like I used to. Call it aging or just time, but I've been a gamer (not hardcore) since the days of Atari. I must admit, I was drawn to Sleeping Dogs by the all star cast of actors and George St. Pierre's involvement in the development of this game. There have been very few Asian themed shooter games that have had so much invested into a production like this one. So why not give it a shot I told myself? Sleeping Dogs is the culmination of amazing games and movies from the past decade!! It's rather cynical to label Sleeping Dogs as just another GTA write-off. GTA laid down the foundation for a genre that offers a unique role playing experience. The developers of Sleeping Dogs used a GTA inspired engine with Batman Arkhm Asylum fight engine, a Max Payne inspired slow mo shooting experience, an inspired Karaoke mode a la Rock Band/Guitar Hero (only in presentation not actual gameplay), and a little blast from the past- Need For Speed racing experience. The fluidity of movement within the game is quite impressive as well. I'm a fan of Mafia II and while it was a decent game- I felt like they didn't do enough to push the boundaries with the current technology. Sleeping Dogs in my opinion has. The dialogue while quite vulgar (to be expected), mixes English with Cantonese for a very unique experience that engulfs you into the action like no other game has.

If you are a fan of Hong Kong cinema than Sleeping Dogs is worth a look. We can dismiss the collection of actors as voice actors as just hype, but I find the experience of playing a game with actors who have been in major blockbusters to be a surreal experience in the same way movie studios have built their success on utilizing big name actors as voice talent for modern day animated movies.

I hope the success of this game generates into the continuation of this series.

Now for my criticism of the game. Please note that the following is a SPOILER ALERT:

While I have praised the game for using inspirations from past video games and movies alike; I was actually disappointed more in the overall story. Don't get me wrong, the story line was great and I thoroughly enjoyed the twists and turns. I'm a huge fan of Tom Wilkinson, but if you are old enough to enjoy the likes of Rush Hour, than it was a big gimme from the start he was one of the main antagonists. Yes, take inspiration from an older movie, but make it less predictable next time. If you are looking forward to Emma Stone's character in the game, be prepared to be disappointed. I was hoping her involvement in the story would be more profound, if not profound, at least give her character a little more than just Will Yun Lee's character romantic fling of all a total of 5 minutes. I was hoping to see her return at the end of the game to sail off into the sunset with Lee's character but it just didn't happen. Obviously she was part of the equation to attract non-traditional gamers with her star power, but I felt they could've added more without having to add substantial amounts to production costs. Finally, the game is laced with tons of graphic sexual dialogue. Let's be frank, this game has a M rating for a reason and so it is expected to have elements of sexual entertainment. I for one am not going to lie, sex is just a part of entertainment that excites the senses as much as the gore and violence. While there was plenty of references to prostitution and seedy sexual situations, there were absolutely no scenes with nudity involved. Only suggestive scenes that panned away with suggestive language in a PG manner. In terms of decency, this game gets an A for pouring more efforts into the gameplay, but if you are going to have tons of allusions to sex why not show the full monty. AKA Heavy Rain.

Aside from the few nuances that makes this game a 4 and not a 5 star title; it is still worth picking up. Play the game for the enjoyment of pure action, storyline, and the beauty of how far video gaming has come. Hope this little review helps.

Considering the success of the Paper Mario franchise, from Nitendo 64 to GameCube, much was expected from Paper Mario Sticker Star. Unlike the Wii's Super Paper Mario, which was more platformer-based than role-playing, Sticker Star reverts back to the classic formula the series is known for. However, with the introduction of stickers, the idea of having role-playing elements becomes completely shatteted. Stickers are the basis of all attacks in Sticker Star; jumping on Goombad, shooting fire at Koopas, and hammering away at other enemies. There are weak stickers, and there are powerful stickers, but when it all boils down a a 300-hp boss fight in the desert, which stickers are you more likely to collect? Because of this simple sticker system, the game felt like it required little to no strategy while I was playing through, which is completely opposite of PM64 & PMTYD. Remember Huff n' Puff? You had to be careful when making him multiply and causing more trouble, but you also want to deal the most damage whilst taking the least damage. In PMSS, the sticker system feels constricting and ruins the strategy you might desire. The game is also fairly easy until the final boss, and the in-game hint system will become very useless at times. For instance, when I was in a jungle section, I had no idea I had to hit an invisible block to proceed without taking damage; it be and a bunch of guess and check. Although all Paper Mario games are linear in a way, this game felt too linear, and I felt like I was playing New Super Mario Bros, but this was far less of a problem than the aforementioned. The bosses aren't very inspiring because we've seen them before, Goombas, Bloopers, Pookies, Kamek, Bowser...speaking of Bowser, the same generic Mario story is used; Princess gets captured, Mario saves the day. What's new? It was okay for PM64 because the formula was still evolving, but there should have been more in PMSS. The story - if any - was boring and dull, and I didn't feel sad (if I was supposed to) during certain parts of the game (no spoilers!).
Despite the myriad of shortcomings in this game, PMSS should be given credit to its beautiful music, design, art, and sense of humor. I liked playing in 3D throughout the entire game with my volume turned up all the way because it was beautiful . The game also controls very easy, and for those who don't like 3D, \\"gimmicks\\" aren't forced in this game. The puzzles that you have to use for \\"things\\" (yes, things) are clever, such as using a bowling ball to knock down pins and reveal a secret exit.
All in all, Paper Mario Sticker Star was a disappointment. I regret preordering this game, but I shouldn't have expected a full console experience on a handheld.

review_headline: doesn't work - no tech support - "bent" copy?
review_body: I recently purchased the Sold-out Software version of the game \\"Undying,\\" which claims to be upgraded for Windows XP, and although I was able to install it, it didn't work.  The game crashed to the desktop when started.  The game's installation window includes a link to a troubleshooting web site maintained by Mastertronics, the parent company of Sold-out Software, and the web page offers several suggestions for correcting this problem, but none of them worked.  So I contacted tech support and explained that I bought the game on Amazon.com from a vendor called Harley's International in England, and I can't get it to work.  I was told that Mastertronics will only provide tech support for games purchased directly from them, and they don't sell any games in America.  The person I communicated with, a man named George Bland, said the game I purchased was a \\"bent\\" copy, whatever that means, and that was probably the reason it didn't work.  What the manufacturer seems to be saying is that the product being sold on Amazon.com (US) is an illegal, nonfunctional copy of their product, so it probably won't work, and they won't provide tech support if it doesn't.  I reported this to Amazon, and they are apparently conducting an investigation.  Until this matter is clarified somehow, I would not recommend purchasing this product from this dealer.  I ended up throwing my game away in frustration.

Thinking about how to rate this game is like trying to combine a personality summary of Dr. Jekyl and Mr. Hyde.

Let's start with the good. The cell shaded graphics and how they animate in this game make this an unbelievably faithful homage to the Naruto series and just the anime genre in general. The graphics are so good, they look even better than the anime itself (if you compare with the very first episodes of this series). And the animation is ridiculously fluid while retaining that hand-drawn look, I don't know how they managed to pull it off so well. This game was made years ago and just seeing this game run now is a testament to how amazing it was made when it first came out.

That being said, there's about an equal amount of utter B.$. I had to put up with to get through the Ultimate Storyline Mode in this game. It was a design choice by the developers, maybe to give us players the illusion that this fighting game has some depth to it. And that game element that I am going to be talking/griping about in this next section is the open world. Oh..my..god.. why do I have to play side quests (e.g. finding and delivering flowers from point A to B in this town) in order to gain enough XP to play the main missions?! I'd rather just have a quality cutscene that included all the back story leading up to the battle rather than having to perform some random mission before I can fight my arch nemesis.

So those two aspects of this game basically canceled each other out in my book, leaving it up to the final aspect that could tip the scales into the \\"like\\" column or the \\"dislike\\" side...and that would be the gameplay. And to say the least, the gameplay is pretty decent. It's not super deep like a Tekken or Virtual Fighter, but deeper than maybe a Street Fighter 2: Championship Edition. I wouldn't say all of the characters are really balanced, they are more akin to the skill level how they stack up in the anime. I really noticed the difference towards the end of the storyline mode when you they make you fight these boss characters with some of these scrub side characters (which are the equivalent of 'Dan' in the Street Fighter series).

So in the end, you have amazing cell shaded graphics coupled with a ridiculously pointless side questing system in the storymode, the saving grace that makes this game worth playing through a couple of times is the decent gameplay. It's not going to change your mind about fighting games, but it may get you either more interested in the Naruto Universe, or give you that satisfying feeling of fulfillment that your favorite anime has been faithfully recreated into a video game. In either case, I enjoyed it to some degree.

I give it a 3.5/5 stars.

Nope, I actually had this for months before breaking it out finally since I have been pretty busy. This week however I was sick and playing Xbox was about the only thing I felt like doing, so out it came. And man, what a great time I had with it.

A little background hopefully without spoiling the story: Reach takes place before the original Halo games. Most probably know what the deal is but I won't address that, I'll just say you're not going to play Master Chief here. Nope, you get to choose a mysterious new Spartan addition to Noble Team. I chose the female because I thought it was neat to have that as a choice for once. 'Noble Six' is similar to the Master Chief in that he or she lacks a name or much in the way of background other than hints in the dialogue. I however am drawn to the opportunity to fill in the blanks in my mind, though I suppose not everyone feels that way.

When the original Halo was released, I worked at a certain national video game retail chain, and one of the freebies we got was the first Halo-branded novel by Eric Nylund - again don't want to spoil things, so you can look it up if you're interested. Normally I hate serialized fiction, but I honestly loved that book, and knowing the basic back story made me anticipate this game more. When well executed, as I feel Reach and the novel were, I really enjoy finding out other details of a given 'universe' in fiction.

One thing I read in other reviews was that players didn't feel any emotional connection to the other Noble Team members, but I certainly did for most of them.

Another complaint was that the game got rid of some fancy toys from Halo 2 & 3 - my response to that is again, this game takes place FIRST. Yes it would have been 'cool', but honestly playing this game felt incredibly similar to my first time playing through the original Halo on the original Xbox. It was a little simpler in terms of controls/weapons/vehicles than 2 & 3, and I enjoyed the return to the 'roots' of the gameplay. The same person also complained it was too linear - while I haven't played those in several years, again Reach feels like the original Halo and I found that other than the Noble members telling you to hurry up with the objective, you could easily run around the edges of the environments and explore for a while.

My first time through was on 'easy' because I wasn't sure how hard it would be and I just wanted to get through it. That took me about 9 hours or so, not super long but IIRC, about the same length as Halo 2 was. I've started a 'normal' game now that I feel like my skills are a little more honed, and it's nice knowing where some of the more powerful weapons are hiding. No idea how long that will take since I am in school, but I will probably finish it at least once more.

Overall I really enjoyed this; I love the series and while online matches are awesome, my time is more limited now so it was nice having a solid campaign to fall back on. review_headline: Will the Real Batman and Joker Please Stand-Up!
review_body:
This review is for the Batman Arhkam Asylum: Game of the Year Edition for the PS3.

When this game originally came out in 2009 (Being a Big Fan of The Comic Book since the 1980's) I had originally planned to get this game on the PC Platform but waited for the price to come down. Then about 7 months ago my son acquired a launch 60GB PS3 from his friends for Christmas (which I quickly upgraded the drive to a 500GB hard drive) and I got hooked on that gaming system. So after purchasing my own PS3 (The 320GB Slim, inferior to the PS3 Launch Model but still does the job) a month later I purchased this game from a competitor for the PS3 instead. However, I did not actually play it until just over a week ago (Got stuck on Playing the Uncharted Franchise, COD: Modern Warfare Franchise, RAGE, and so forth) which in hindsight I regret not playing sooner. All I can say is that this game is the closet you will experience in actually getting to the \\"Real Dark Knight\\" Experience originally written by Bob Kane & Bill Finger and later more closely emphasized by Frank Miller's version of the Dark Knight.

Plot: The Game's Cut scene starts off with Batman (Voiced by Veteran Batman Voice Actor Kevin Conroy from the 1990 Batman Animated TV Series Circa to Present) transporting a recently recaptured Joker (Voiced by Veteran Joker Voice Actor Mark Hamil AKA Luke Skywalker from Star Wars fame, also from the 1990 Batman Animated TV Series Circa to Present) back to Arhkam Asylum in the Batmobile (The Batmobile from the \\"Tim Burton\\" Batman Movie Franchise) after once again escaping Arhkam and trying to take the Mayor Hostage. As Batman turns over the Joker to the Arhkam staff, Batman feels skeptical about the \\"Ease\\" of the Jokers capture and accompanies the Arhkam staff (who agrees somewhat reluctantly) into the Asylum's \\"Intensive\\" Treatment Ward as the Arhkam staff \\"re-process\\" Joker back into the Asylum. Near the end of the \\"re-processing\\" the Arhkam Security start to escort the Joker back to a cell (Batman tried to follow him but the guard stopped him so he would not \\"agitate\\" the other inmates), As the Guard and the Arhkam Orderly pass the first security checkpoint Joker trips and falls then subdues the guard and orderly after faking his \\"injury\\" while being assisted by his twisted Assistant and Psychotic Girlfriend Harley Quinn (Voiced by Arleen Sorkin also from the 1990 Batman Animated TV Series Circa to just recently) who has taken control of Arhkam's main security center and allows Joker to escape using alternate Security Doors. At this point Batman reaches the area of Jokers escape to late and must find a way of re-capturing Joker and anybody else that has been set loose by Harley Quinn before it is too late.

Gameplay: The Majority of this game is in the 3rd person aspect with only in the First Person Aspect when Batman is crawling through Arhkam's Air Ventilator shafts (There is one small part where Batman is in the Full First Person Aspect but this is near the end of the Campaign and is only for about 15 seconds). For the Most part Batman will Fight, Problem Solve, and be challenged throughout the Island of Arhkam Asylum. You will be able to upgrade not only your own abilities (Fight Combo, Armor, Weapons) but also get additional items throughout the game (Multiple Batarangs, explosive gel, Zip Line Gun and more). In line with the \\"Infamous\\" Franchise Arhkam Ayslum is pretty much a Open Ended Sandbox game (At least as far as being \\"confined\\" to explore the Arhkam Estate) that allows you to continue to complete the \\"Side Missions\\" after the end of the Main Campaign, you can also do this during the actual Campaign as well while in between \\"objectives\\".

Plus Side of the Game:

- I love the \\"Free-Flow\\" combat system of the game to where you can earn extra point by consecutively keep knocking out henchman.
- The graphics are just astonishing, makes you feel like you're actually in a BatmanComic.
- Superb Job on the Voice Acting, Mark Hamil is definitely the Heath Ledger Voice Actor version of the Joker and Arleen Sorkin's Brooklyn accent is just hilarious as Harley Quinn.
- The problem solving is not hard and not to easy which makes it fun to do (You also need to do it to completely finish the game at 100%)
- Great Story by Veteran writer Paul Dini who did a good job about getting a good handful of Batman's Classic Rogue Gallery other than Joker like Killer Croc, Poison Ivy, The Riddler (In Voice Only), Scarecrow, and of course Bane.

Negative Side of the Game:

- While the game itself did not have any real \\"negative\\" aspects in it does have one annoyance and that the controls do not always perform like they should, but nothing I would deduct a star from.

DLC (Downloadable Content): The game of the year edition features exclusive DLC from the PS3 PSN Store (There not included on the Disc like the GOTY Edition of Arkham City) like the Joker Challenge where you actually play as the Joker in both the Fighting and Predator Challenges (Available only on the PS3), Batman and Joker themed Wallpaper, along with additional challenges and Maps that are completely free (Again they are available for free via the PSN Store). There are 2 Predator Maps however that are unfortunately $3.49 a piece at this time, which is not bad but would also like to see dropped as well in the near future.

3D: As far as the 3D goes I am unable to comment on this since I prefer to play the game only in 2D, Just call me old fashioned but I feel the 3D would \\"ruin\\" the experience for me. Also FYI, The 3D Glasses DOES NOT COME WITH THIS EDITION OF THE GAME (The Red Box of GOTY). You will have to go to the Trioviz web site at www(dot)Trioviz(dot)com to order the 3D glasses (Or just do a google search for the Trioviz website).

Overall: This is by far the best comic book themed Video Game I have played to date (This includes The X-Men Origins: Wolverine Uncaged Edition and the Infamous Franchise). review_headline: A fun game, but lacking in quality
review_body:
First of all, I bought this game about 6 months after it released, and with the patches have noticed barely any lag at all. Sure it freezes every once in a while, and there are definitely bugs, but the game is totally playable on the PS3. I do have complaints about this game, but not so much about the bugs.

I will say that the first 30 or so hours you spend playing this game are going to be extremely fun. The game begins with a very well done introduction- probably the best part of the game story-wise. You start off as a prisoner who manages to escape his execution due to an unexpected interruption. After your escape you begin to explore the beautiful world of Skyrim. Skyrim contains some incredible visuals backed up with an equally wonderful soundtrack. Simply running through the wilderness and striking down deer and wolves with a hunting bow was relaxing and fun. The world of Skyrim is more realistic than it is fantastical- which I kind of liked. It made it seem more authentic. The gameplay is alright, although it's not the game's strongest point. This game really shines due to its RPG elements. You have tons of freedom in regards to which parts of Skyrim you want to explore first, which quests you want to complete or ignore, what type of skills you want your character to specialize in, and what type of combat you want to engage in.

The game, however, isn't perfect. Like I said, the first 30 hours of this game are amazing. After all, there's so much to explore and so much to do and so many ways to play, right? Well, not quite. After a while, you begin to see patterns in the game. For instance, in the first dungeon you walk into, you'll probably find yourself wandering through burial crypts fighting draugrs- a nasty looking zombie-skeleton creature. At first, this is really cool. However, this type of dungeon is repeated in nearly the exact same fashion roughly 70 times throughout the game. I'm not exaggerating. There are two other dungeons repeated endlessly throughout the game- 1. a fort manned by bandits (or occasionally mages) and 2. technological ruins guarded by ancient spider robots (srsly). All of these dungeons are set up the same: progress through small rooms and hallways killing enemies in groups of 1-3 until you reach the end where a boss waits- one that has more HP and stronger attacks than his cronies but often times uses the same mode of combat. Every now and then in these dungeons you would see Bethesda's attempt at a puzzle. One often repeated joke of a puzzle consisted of turning a pillar around so the imprint on it matched the imprint on the wall behind, which is neither challenging nor interesting.

Apart from the repetitive dungeons were the repetitive quests, which consisted of three different objectives: 1. go talk to this person and see what they want, 2. kill this enemy, or 3. progress through this dungeon and obtain an item. I suppose I wouldn't mind doing quests like these if the dungeons and enemies themselves actually varied. But they don't. It's always the same. Even the world itself is very repetitive- all the towns look fairly similar save for maybe Markarth. The wild also consists only of forest-based wilderness or snowy forest-based wilderness. No desert level; no lava level; no tropic level; no jungle level. Nothing but forests and mountains. I mean, it was beautiful, but repetitive.

Another big problem with this game regards to combat. The combat is decent- but there are some serious problems when it comes to interface. Only two buttons are assigned for combat-based moves, with a third button assigned for rarely used powers and \\"dragon shouts\\". Every time you want to use a different weapon or spell, you have to pause combat in order to scroll through the menu and select the item or spell you want to use. Constant interruptions during battle became irritating fast, and eventually I ended up using nothing but my bow to avoid them. I rarely switched weapons and never used magic. I can only imagine how annoying it must be to play as a mage and have to pause combat every time you want to use a different spell.

I also have issues with the whole character creation and skill system of this game. When it comes to skills, the game revolves around a \\"perk\\" system. Every time you level up you pick a perk that enhances one of your skills (for example, making two-handed attacks 20% stronger). Once you get into higher levels, you are simply useless in any skill that you have not unlocked perks in. These perks cannot be changed ever. As such, the only way to try out a different form of combat is to totally start over with a different character. Even a little change, such as going from dual-wielding swords to using a sword and shield simply won't work unless you have the perks for both. Unfortunately, if you're playing expert or master difficulty, you probably won't have a lot of perks to spare since you'll most likely be maxing out smithing and enchanting (and possibly alchemy)- the most over-powered skills in the game. With these skills maxed (after hours of tedious grinding) you'll be able to create more powerful weapons and armor than anything you can obtain from anywhere in the game- I suppose that makes completing any quests or obtaining gold meaningless. Meanwhile, skills such as lockpicking and pickpocketing are breathtakingly useless. Also, it should be noted that warrior type builds are very overpowered while mage builds are quite underpowered.

Despite all this, it is still a very fun game, and I'm definitely going to buy the sixth elder scrolls game when it comes out to see where they go from here. I want to see more of what I like- the freedom of gameplay, the visuals, and especially the sound track, and I want to see improvements on the gameplay, button-customization, balancing the skills, and quests. If they tried less to overwhelm players with hundreds of mediocre quests and copy-pasted locations, and spent more time actually trying to improve the quality of each quest and location, they could create a very good game.

review_headline: Absolutely disappointed with this new game from the creator of Final Fantasy
review_body:
As a fan of the original Final Fantasy games (4, 6 and 7 in particular) and Chrono Trigger, I had high expectations for The Last Story which was being touted as Hironobu Sakaguchi's return to JRPG splendor. After playing, I was utterly disappointed and wanted to throw the game away after 4-5 hours.

The characters are unlikeable stereotypes who have personalities as interesting and deep as cardboard. The main character is the most wishy washy nothing character I've seen in forever who has to keep spouting out what all his desires and dreams are because otherwise you wouldn't know you're supposed to care. His partners are unremarkable except with how they're dubbed with really bad European accents. One main character in particular does nothing but talk about drinking any opportunity she has. She literally cannot go 2 lines without mention something about drinking, alcohol, or missing being able to drink alcohol in the first 4 hours of the game. This is the depth of her personality.

The character designs look like they were trying to be modern, edgy and hip like Tetsuya Nomura's style from Kingdom Hearts/later Final Fantasy games but it just doesn't work with the heavy European fantasy world the game presents. You live in a fantasy castle town and you can run around and see townspeople in traditional European clothing, meanwhile you and your friends have immaculately styled hair and are in short shorts and chaps with belt buckles covering everything. Also your sibling wears an eyepatch because it's cool or something. (In the game's defense, you can change your equipment and it'll change how your character looks, but half of the stuff still looks incredibly tacky. I just dressed all my characters in full Winter outfits so they could look like something that resembled respectable people.)

This game doesn't learn anything from the past and instead uses boring new stereotypes to tell an awful story about awful characters. Everything is exposition, characters talk all the time about nothing, and none of it is interesting. In Chrono Trigger and old Square SNES JRPGs, characters were introduced with impact and you liked them immediately upon their first 3 lines of dialogue. In this game people won't shut up about how boring they are. It's baffling how the creator of FF could've come to this point after making so many great games.

To be fair, the gameplay seems like it could be alright. The battle engine integrates elements of popular FPSes by putting in a cover system with team mechanics making for what could be interesting combat. If you're willing to skip all the cutscenes and ignore the stupid plot, then the core game might be somewhat enjoyable. But then why even play a JRPG at all?

Coming from an avid Super Smash Brothers fan, I have to admit that this game gives me SSB nostalgia to a certain degree. Despite what I've seen a lot of people say, the game really does remind me of the Nintendo equivalent in the respect that, artistically and stylishly, there is a vast amount of similarities. This does NOT mean, however, that the games are identical or that All Stars is a \\"rip off\\" or an example of Sony's lack of creativity.

For the fans of classic Playstation games- like Spyro or Banjo Kazooie- I'm afraid you'll only find disappointment in AS's character roster. Granted the game does feature such favorites as Jak and Daxter, Sly Cooper, Dante and Kratos I find myself looking for that 'classic gamer' aesthetic that SSB was actually able to bring to the table. (Yes, I know, comparisons are bad, but bare with me here.) I've not done my research- so I couldn't say for certain why Sony chose to leave out select favorites from their character list- but I do suspect it has something to do with money and character ownership. With any luck we'll be able to see some beloved favorites landing themselves on some DLCs in the future!

The game itself plays like your typical free-form 2-dimensional fighter, with each character bringing something unique to the table as far as maneuvers, techniques and 'super' moves go. I consider myself impressed by the amount of effort that went into the design of each character in regards to their fighting moves, and I do imagine that anyone who's had the time to 'test the waters' with their character assortment in-game could vouch for that. Don't let negative comments about there \\"only being three buttons\\" you use when fighting. Granted the fighting revolves around your square, circle and triangle controls there's a LOT more involved than simply clicking three buttons. Like in SSB (sorry, more comparing) you utilize your analog sticks to trigger attack move variation. This makes for a more dynamic fighting experience as a whole, at last in my opinion.

Ya' know the thing I love the most about it? The fact that it's multi-player. I cannot express how long I've been waiting for a Playstation-based multiplayer that wasn't racing or a shooter. This is certainly more of 'my thing' when it comes to multi-players!

Complaints?
I have a couple, though they are relatively gnit-picky and perhaps even a bit childish.
The biggest thing that irks me is that Sly Cooper feels like he's a bit overpowered. From his super moves to his normal controls (one which enables him to turn invisible for what feels like the entirety of the game depending on the user) he's a nuisance to deal with when playing online- simply because, as I've found, those who use Sly normally have a tendency to run around as a 'shadow' the entire time. His recovery time for the maneuver is practically nothing, which is what creates the irritant in the first place.
My second complaint would have to be that there seems to be no way to fight using a health bar. Yeah, that right- for those reading this who've yet to invest in the game, say bye-bye to that HP counter you surely know and love (Or hate. Whatever floats your boat). It's all \\"kill\\"-based, and you can only obtain 'kills' by using your character's respective super maneuvers. To be honest I've taken to this style more than I thought I would- it's an interesting twist on the normal hit-point based fighting- but I still wish there were an option available that you could actually turn on hit-point counters.

But, as you can tell my the amount of stars I gave, the pros far out-weight the cons as far as I'm concerned.

product_title: Nyko Charge Base 360 S for Xbox 360
review_headline: Great Option For Those Who Hate Play and Charge Kit
review_body:
I have been trying to find an easy way to charge my controllers for quite some time and believe I finally found the perfect solution.

I hate using the play and charge kit because I feel the charging cable just gets in the way and I have found the longevity of the Microsoft batteries to be quite poor. On batteries I only had for about 2 years with moderate use, I found I could not even play for an hour without needing to plug the cable in to charge the battery.

I also tried using just regular rechargeable AA batteries and that worked okay but I found it annoying to change batteries every couple of weeks.

Then I found the Nyko Charge Base and figured for $25 it was worth and try, and I am glad I did!
It comes with two proprietary batteries that you snap into your xbox controllers the same as you would with the Microsoft batteries but is had metal contacts on the outside that fit into the cradle dock to charge. The charging is automatic and resumes as soon as you put the controllers back after using them. So far I have not had any issues with the batteries dying in between charges but think that Nyko estimates of \\"25 hours\\" on a full charge are somewhat exaggerated since I did notice a \\"one bar (25%)\\" drop in power level after 3 hours of continuous play.

I really like the LED screen on the front that tells you that the controllers are correctly placed on the cradle and charging, it is a nice touch and more aesthetically pleasing than a glowing light like other battery charging solutions. It also has a USB port hidden on the front under a little hatch that you can use to charge something else like a phone, iPod, etc. I haven't used it but again another nice touch.

Overall, I'd definitely recommend this considering it comes with two batteries and a complete charging solution for $25, if you already own a play and charge kit and aren't bothered by connecting the charge cord during play sessions than I'd say saveyour money.
You definitely need a rechargeable battery option for xbox controllers and if you are in the market for a new system this is by far the best solution I've seen, you will not be disappointed!

review_headline: Was a skeptic but now I understand.
review_body:
Bought a new Scuf Controller and didn't quite like the domed sticks I got on it so I decided to try some CQCS since I've heard the buzz and I have smaller hands. The concept of kontrol freeks makes sense but I just couldn't see it improving my skill THAT much they are only molded plastic and rubber right? Install is non-existent; simply snap on the freeks and you are good to go. (Note: I have removed and places my CQCs multiple times and have yet to see any wear on my controllers or sticks) I instantly felt more 'at home' with my CQCs since they are a concave surface similar to Xbox controllers. After a couple of games of CoD I was worried, my aiming was AWFUL. So I dialed down my sensitivity from 7 all the way down to 4 and the rest is history. Believe it or not, I find myself turning on people fast and with more accuracy, I can easily pinpoint \\"head glitchers\\" and get headshots, and overall my accuracy is steadily climbing from 22% to close to 24%. Which may not seem like a lot but I have well over 100,000+ kills. The only downside to the CQCs is they are small and I feel like off my controller they could be easily broken. Also even with the grip 'dots' I find them to a be a bit slippery during long gaming sessions.

PROS

+Great for Xbox users on a PS3 controller (or people who prefer concave vs. convex aka domed sticks)
+Easy setup
+Minimal adjustment period (could vary per person)
+Requires less thumb movement for fast movement/response

CONS

- Plastic feels cheap
- Not enough grip

product_title: Call of Duty: Black Ops II
review_body:
Super big fan and avid player of previous Call of Duty games (since COD4). I liked every single installment since, but Black Ops 2 does not feel like a COD game at all!

This is the worst COD to date.
Black Ops 2 is HORRIBLE! I was so excited for it, such a big fan of COD, and even got it at midnight. Let me tell you, it is the WORST Call of Duty to date. I was so disappointed in it, especially because it seemed good on the YouTube videos. Please buy my copy if you're not convinced, it sucks! I actually went back to MW3 because I thought it was THAT bad.

Reasons it is bad:

The graphics are a step down, it starting to look very cartoonish and is resembling Medal of Honor (in a very bad way). The graphics just look clunky and lack the \\"crisp\\" look of previous games. Its hard to explain but if you get a chance to play it you will definitely see what I mean. (Compared this and MW2 side by side and everyone I asked who wasn't familiar with COD said that MW2 looked like the new game... which I found to be quite sad that a 2009 game looks better graphically than a 2012 game).

The guns look and (worst of all) sound like plastic toys! Seriously so disappointed. Footsteps sound like someone popping bubble wrap, you have to hear it, its terrible! I just do not feel immersed in the game at all.

Zombies is ruined, they claim to have added new ways to play but Black Ops 1 zombies are tenfold better than what they did here. There's way too much fog that its impossible to see and gets annoying to look at. You cant even seen 10 feet in-front of you most of the time. Also they decided to add lava cracks in the ground, which might seem like a cool new idea, but it was an epic fail! The lava hurts your character and makes your screen red (its everywhere you go!), and when coupled with the constant fogginess only makes the game feel even more annoying.

Although I have super fast internet, the game is buggy and laggy at times. Games don't finish 40% of the time --- the whole lobby loses connection to host in multilayer and zombies just because one person decides to rage quit. This is the best selling franchise in the world and they cannot even give us dedicated servers in the year of 2012...REALLY?!

Please stay away from this game, it will save you $60 hard earned dollars. I really hope the developers see this and actually give us a game that's worth the money.
In short I have to laugh about the whole thing, if I don't laugh....I'll cry I'm out of 60 bones.

I have to admit that this may be a \\"good\\" game for some but I was looking for a strategy game where I could play admiral and direct fleet movements, etc. In this game you have to drive boats, shoot at airplanes, fly airplanes and shoot at airplanes, and that is as far as I got before deleting it from my computer. Total waste of money for me.
If you like being in the center of the action and do all the flying, driving, shooting, etc. you might enjoy it if the price is cheap enough but be aware that the graphics are VERY dated.

I have not played any games in the Metroid series, so I didn't know what to expect. But I found the game to be very good. The dual action required of the remote controller (nunchuck not needed) was a little awkward at first, but soon it felt normal enough. The graphics were really cool and the sound was great. It is just the kind of game for me. I give it a 9 out of ten.

review_headline: I Am Not Disappointed with My Pre-Order
review_body:
Fresh out of the case, Assassin's Creed III admittedly feels a little cumbersome and glitchy. I assumed this was due to the revised controls and game engine, which is probably correct, but it is something that must be addressed if this is to be an honest review. Nevertheless, I am still left extremely satisfied with having pre-ordered this gaming epic months ago.

The storyline is certainly of AC caliber with the usual plot twists and well thought out narrative, despite taking way too long to get to the juicy part(s) gamers care about most. As another reviewer said, the 5-6ish hour tutorial levels/missions are highly unnecessary and hinder the overall flow of what is an otherwise great story.

Graphically, I think this is a spectacular homage to the wild frontier of young America. The wildlife, cities, wilderness, and people are all rendered much more aesthetically pleasing and \\"alive\\" than in previous iteration in this series. That said, I still doubt that I will ever feel the same adoration or sense of breathtaking awe for Boston, New York, or the Frontier that I felt when I first looked around Florence as Ezio in AC:II.

Overall, the gameplay aspect is still as fun as ever. Not much has changed in this regard from previous AC games. Overlooking the graphic glitches and other minor detractors, I have already poured quite a few hours into running around the treetops of the Frontier and hunting wildlife. By creating an entire wilderness to explore without the hindrances of rooftop chases, haystacks, etc. Ubisoft has definitely upped the quality of this game's \\"extracurricular\\" activities, not to mention the trade-based economic system.

Like I said, I am extremely pleased that I pre-ordered this game and anxiously awaited its release. Sure, there are some relatively important issues that could have been polished (and I apologize if those are what stand out in this review), but in the grand scheme of things, this is yet another successful Assassin's Creed release that I am sure my wife and I will spend hours playing through completing every side objective. Nobody will regret buying this, even if it's for one play through.er successful Assassin's Creed release that I am sure my wife and I will spend hours playing through completing every side objective. Nobody will regret buying this, even if it's for one play through.

Borderlands 2 is just around the corner and Borderlands re-invented the FPSRPG (First Person Shooter Role Playing Game). While many have tried to combine these two very popular genres into one title (anyone remember Hellgate: London?) Gearbox and 2K have done a great job mashing up the two styles into a game that can be enjoyed by fans of either genre.

The graphics deserve special mention as they are quite unique. The stylized realism in this game uses cel-shading technology. The result is an odd mix of very realistic looking comic book style 'flat art'. It's very surreal to see how something can look so real and so very not at the same time. It may put some players off, but I think it works well.

Players will notice early on the loot-fest this game is. Enemies drop tons of guns and ammo when killed, and there are a rediculous amount of containers to open for loot as well. Occasionally you'll find a very small amount of cash, but most often you'll find lots of ammo and plenty of guns of different styles. Shotguns, sniper rifles, semi-automatics and more litter the landscape in a matter of minutes. The fact is, like many similar loot-fests, a large percentage of these guns are soon discarded as junk, but the chance for a rare weapon dropping keeps the players eagerly playing and killing, in a diablo-style quest for better gear. The sheer number of possible weapons, grenade mods, class mods, and shields is overwhelming, which is a good thing. You're constantly bettering your character, even outside of gaining levels.

The storyline is excellent and contains many hours of content. The GOTY edition includes all the DLC content and probably has over 100 hours of play time easily (haven't completed the game yet). Many people find this a fun game to play alone but say it shines multiplayer. I disagree here, and strongly prefer playing alone.

When playing with others, the enemies scale pretty harshly and the game can get frustrating easily. There's no way to communicate what quest the host wishes to work on, and people tend to scatter and each go their own way. People will initiate travel before you completed your task on the current map, and most people seem to only want to 'duel' or be disruptive. There's also a number of cheaters running around with hacked items that grant invincibility and other game-breaking gear. So personally, I enjoy the game more as a solo experience, but there it shines.

Parents should be aware of the persistently crude humor in this game. For example, the first real boss is a guy named \\"9-toes\\". When you first see him, you'll see a cut scene ending with a freeze on a full-body shot and the caption \\"9-toes (also he has three balls)\\".
Very good game.  My kids love it.  Can be a bit gorey, but not too bad.  Very good graphics.  Excellent user experience. Definitely worth a shot.

review_headline: A modern handheld gaming comparative analysis featuring the 3DS XL
review_body:
I recently got a 3DS XL and after I got a chance to use it for a while I am impressed with how it compares to the Vita, as well as how it stands out over the original 3DS.

Basically the 3DS XL feels like it is a 3DS that can finally compete with the Vitas screen.

The vita still has an obviously superior screen when you get down to the detail, but the 3D effect is good enough to make up for it. The larger screen really makes the games feel more alive, it is definitely what I was looking for when it comes to using a 3DS at home. The 3DS stands out for it's unique library of first party titles which are not only what clearly stands out on the system but is what makes the 3DS desirable over the Vita.

I still think the Vita is a better system for what it is, but to be honest I think this just shows off how these consoles have truly found their own identity. The Vita stands out as a home console on the go, it took the idea the PSP started with and transformed it into a well refined handheld in a league of it's own. If I want to play a console port on a handheld the Vita is without a doubt the handheld to get it on, as Vita console ports are as close to the console version as you are going to get, many look virtually identical. With it's sexy, highly detailed screen and true dual analog sticks it is hard to feel like you are missing out.

In comparison the 3DS simply stands out for unique offerings. The 3D is as well executed as ever, and first party games such as Mario Kart 7, Mario Tennis Open, and New Super Mario Bros 2 are what sell it. The reason is obvious, the online multiplier well executed, addictive and the single player doesn't disappoint. So the games are good and so are the handhelds, to be honest it is hard to complain about the quality when it comes to any of these handhelds, and they all stand out for their own reasons.

For example I still think the original 3DS stands out in it's own way as a better system to travel with if you want to keep it on you. It is smaller and easier to put in your pocket, easier to use while you are outside, and surprisingly enough it generally feels like it was slightly better made. My original 3DS simply has this rock solid feel to it, like it is a seriously well built piece of high-end gaming hardware. While the 3DS XL is undoubtedly well made and also feels well built handheld, for some reason is just feels a little more delicate, you know, as if it is made out of cheaper materials. Not that it feels cheap, I honestly think this just goes to show well Nintendo built the original $250 handheld. If you have ever used a DSi XL the 3DS XL feels quite similar, and it is basically the same size as well.

Robotron X was originally designed for the Ninetendo64, and this is a terrific port of the game. The problem is this game came out before the dualshock 2 did, so this game does not have dual stick support, which is a real drag, because Robotron was the game that popularized twin stick control. Playing RobotronX without twin sticks is like playing Silent Scope with a game pad.

I'm not saying you can't play with the d-pad for movement and the 4 buttons for firing, but it's clunky. It's easy to overshoot where you're trying to move to, and hence, easy to run into the enemies, or walls, etc.

Not a bad game, just released at a bad time.

Back in 2005, LEGO Star Wars came out and became a surprising success by adding it's brand of innocent humor along with letting players play through the prequel trilogy in LEGO form. It was an enticing idea. One that worked splendidly. Since then the LEGO games have taken a hold of gaming, allowing us to experience some of our favorite films in LEGO form. The original Star Wars trilogy, Indiana Jones and Harry Potter are but a few film sagas to be turned into LEGO form. LEGO Lord of the Rings was to be expected. It's finally here and it's pretty enjoyable stuff. The LEGO formula is starting to wear off a bit and overstay its welcome, but the game is still fun.

Like the other LEGO games before it, LEGO Lord of the Rings will have you playing through the whole saga as the fellowship. It follows the trilogy quite well, recreating some of the most memorable moments of the film in LEGO form. In the past the LEGO games haven't been known to do a lot of voice acting, but here you'll find moments in which certain lines are ripped directly from the film and spoken by the characters as opposed to the gibberish they talk in in the other games. That being said, it's really nice to hear some of the more iconic lines. There are some liberties taken with some of the moments, of course. Like the previous LEGO games there's a good sense of humor here and so some scenes are changed for the sake of comedy. It's all in good fun and is sure to remind you of some of the best moments of the trilogy, while giving you something to laugh about from time to time.

There are a grand total of eighteen levels in LEGO Lord of the Rings. You'll begin in The Fellowship of the Ring and keep proceeding until you eventually play through The Two Towers and The Return of the King. Along your journey you'll play through set piece moments and be able to switch between whatever characters are there on the fly. When first playing through the game it's all story based and thus you'll only be able to play as any character that's actually staged to be there. Each character has their own abilities that make them handy in situations. Legolas can jump really high or use arrows as platforms. Gandalf can use his wizardry. You can throw Gimli at certain stones to break them. But perhaps the most amusing is Frodo who's only ability is to scream and that (somehow) makes enemies simply stop attacking him. It's a good setup and the game will constantly make you switch between characters to solve puzzles or to make use of them. Simply put, you'll never be playing as the same character throughout.

The first time through each level, however, you'll always come across puzzles and items off the beaten path that you simply can't get to at the moment because you may not have the character for it. Luckily you can play through levels again with other characters who will have the ability to get you to these secrets off the beaten path. As you complete the levels you'll unlock other characters who have abilities you can use when you choose to go back in Free Play mode.

There is a lot familiar about the LEGO series by now and if you've played any of the previous entries you won't really be surprised by much of this. As you go through levels you're encouraged to get studs which can eventually be used to buy more characters and the like. There are a lot of characters that are fun to play as, but of course, some are just clones of another (as in, same abilities). Nevertheless, getting them all and seeing your favorite characters in LEGO form is still a treat. And because of goingback for all those goodies and more studs there's a lot of replay value for what amounts to a relatively short campaign.

A buddy can always jump into the fray and drop out any time they wish to do so. Much like how it's been done before, co-op isn't much of a problem. If someone wanders off too far the screen will automatically split until you're both reunited in the same vicinity again. It's not likely to happen too often, however. LEGO Lord of the Rings is a pretty linear affair. You won't find yourself getting lost along the way very much and most times when you can go off the beaten path, you'll only have to return onto the right path.

As you might also imagine, LEGO Lord of the Rings has a non-existent challenge. For the most part, you'll have your rough spots but the only penalty for death is really just the loss of studs. You'll always continue right where you died and you have an infinite number of lives. There has never been such a thing as a game over in the LEGO series and it's not going to start now. The games are a lot of wholesome fun. They've never embraced challenging the player.

Production wise most times the LEGO games usually look good. The same is true here. The animations of the LEGOs are great, but what really bears mentioning is the attention to detail. All the LEGO games tend to do really well here. From seeing your characters as LEGOs to the expression on their faces during cutscenes and the like. The environments are also really good looking. The game runs at a consistent frame rate, though I have noticed a glitch or two from time to time. The games usually look nice, but it's not uncommon to see the games suffer from strange glitches. In particular, my copy seems to randomly freeze after I've been playing for a couple of hours and I have to reset it.

The voice acting is great because it's all ripped from the movies. Sometimes it doesn't overlap perfectly with the movements but that's fine by me. The score for the game is also ripped directly from the movies themselves and plays rather nicely. the sound effects (particularly of LEGO pieces breaking) is also a nice touch. It's a great blend of LEGOs and Lord of the Rings.

The LEGO games have always been fun ways to enjoy some of our favorite movies in LEGO form. Despite how the formula is starting to wear thin it's still a lot of fun to play these games. LEGO Lord of the Rings is definitely among the better outings. product_title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 - Playstation 3
review_headline: Fasten your seat belts for an adrenaline rush like none other (campaign review)
review_body:
PREFACE: I'm an \\"old school\\" gamer in my 30s, who plays games only for their campaigns. Multiplayer looks like fun, but I simply don't have the time to get into it, given my job, obligations, and other interests. All of my reviews are based SOLEY on campaigns, and they are simply my own opinions. I typically enjoy games that can be completed in an afternoon or evening, due to my schedule, and the fact that I grew up with games like \\"Bonk's Adventure\\" and \\"Contra\\". Nowadays, I like shorties like \\"Journey\\" and \\"Limbo\\". If you can live with this, please read on!

Wow... just wow. Activision did what seemed like it may very well be impossible, and delivered their most exciting campaign yet, besting even MW2 and Black Ops. The intensity of this game, and its breakneck pacing, simply cannot be adequately described in words. By the time the final credits rolled, I was actually sweating and shaking a little bit- I felt like I had been in the heat of the battle! Time to debrief with a couple of cold beers!

Unlike most of the COD games, they don't ease you into this one with a nice, slow tutorial. In a stroke of genius, you hit the ground running in this game, and experience an intelligent \\"on the run\\" tutorial that works much better than the previous installments (while NYC is blown to pieces all around you, by the way). From that moment on, it's one mind-blowing level after another (submarine takes the cake), offering variety, visual splendor, and the most excitement I've ever experienced in a game.

The campaign is nice and short- about five hours, which is more than enough for me, particularly considering that it's five hours of straight action, as opposed to any backtracking or filler. There is not one wasted moment in this campaign, and I liked it so much, I played through it a second time within days. I know a lot of people complain about the linearity and the \\"roller coaster\\" effect, but like a lot of other gamers, I love that! I like roller coasters, and to me, games are like interactive books or movies. I want to enjoy a ride that has been lovingly crafted, from start to finish. For those of us who grew up playing the original \\"Doom\\", MW3 is a remarkable testament to how far the FPS genre has come in immersing the player.

If you're looking for a game that puts you into that \\"action movie experience\\", it would be hard to do better than MW3, in my humble opinion. \\"We're Oscar Mike!\\"ller coasters, and to me, games are like interactive books or movies. 1 Rosters aren't updated, at least not correctly. Arizona's roster is missing the Sr QB who will be starting this year. I can see them giving us the LB who left the team a few weeks ago because timing wise that's though to keep up with. But the QB is a redshirt SR who has been on the roster going on his 5th year (and was previously a starter).

2 Stadiums aren't updated. Arizona stadium doesn't have the large 'jumbotron' in the South end zone that was installed and in use last season (in real life). It's the 3rd largest screen in college football so it's kinda hard to miss. Last years game didn't have it but I gave them a pass because it was new.

This is just 1 team, but it's in a major conference and it's very easy to get the info (any sports site will have rosters and if that's too much effort then just request the media guide from all the Big 6 schools which they'll readily provide). Did they update your team? You may have to take that chance.

I am a Dynasty player and they have made a few changes, most notably recruiting. When you set up your preseason recruiting board you will notice 20:00 SCOUT time. Be sure to use this before you start your season because once the season begins you only get 3:00 hours per week. Scouting is used to identify \\"gems\\" and \\"busts\\".

Gameplay is similar with only slight tweaks. The graphics are ever so slightly better. Some controls have changed (option pitch is now L1 rather than L2). Broadcast team has the same commentary you're already familiar with from '12.

To 'save the earth' the game doesn't come with a manual, it's loaded onto the game disc. A noble effort for sure, but the brochure included is printed in black and white rather than color, leading me to believe they were driven by printing costs rather than more noble concerns. Not that you need the printed manual but it's something I had become accustomed to.

I will still be playing this game a lot (especially between now and late August), but thought for the $ they could have worked a little harder on updates.

review_headline: EA dropped the ball. Not worth buying.
review_body:
So after putting out arguably the best Madden ever with Madden 12 last year, EA puts out the worst Madden in the history of the franchise.

Here's what you get with Madden 13:

-Biggest and most glaring problem - Franchise mode is a horrible mess - its called Connected Career Mode, and unless you want to play with the outdated rosters from around April, you have to play it online, and even then you can't update your own rosters, so you're at the mercy of the latest roster update which is always a couple weeks behind. Franchise mode in 12 was PERFECT. This is crap. And forget playing it with friends at your house. Thats done away with. Don;t have a good internet connection? Just throw this game away, because its pretty much useless.

- The menu system is crap. The first hour I got this game was spent confused as hell trying to figure out where the hell franchise mode was, and even then, the rest of the menus are confusing.

- The music is awful. Every year Madden was great with updating the soundtrack with new music. Now its like a loop of the Jurrasic Park theme over and over again.

-The intro and layout is awful. It looks like Calvin Johnson got stuck in Tron. I feel ike I'm back in 1992.

-Your in game subs don't stay so you have to re-sub EVERY FRIGGIN GAME. Thats fun.

-The \\"infinity engine\\" is garbage. Tackles now look like two sock monkeys falling over on each other. Gee, I didn't know John Kuhn was double jointed enough to whip both legs over his head when he got tackled. You made the game LESS realistic with this crap, everybody just looks like drunks when they get tackled now.

If you haven't bought this already - don't. I'm going to spend the next two weeks updating my Madden 2012 rosters with this years rookies and Free agents and just play the franchise mode in that. Unless you SOLELY play 1V1 exhibition games online - Madden 13 isn't worth playing. Ever.

Alright, as a kid I grew up fascinated with the Resident Evil series. I have beaten 4 and 5 and have played Code Veronica, 0, 1, 2, and 3 as well.
