review_headline: Mediocre and boring collection of rip-offs
review_body: Well, I totally agree with GameSpot review (75/100), and only because the game is big. Unfortunately I belong to a a group of RPG gamers who value a good story, great characters, and a living world, and not just good combat.  First of all, the huge net of narrow corridors and wider openings with a gratuitous amount of invisible walls do not make an open world. But it would be not a big deal if a story were good. Well, it is not. It is not too bad either, just very generic and uninspiring.  Second, after playing for 10 hours I still do not give a damn about any event in the game. Probably it is because NPCs are nothing more but answering machines, with zero personalities and any lack of emotions, with dialogues being wooden and boring beyond belief. As if this game has been made by robots, or a kind of computer-generated product, with no humans involved.  Third, man, it is such a rip-off!!! Practically everything was in other games, but made way better. It makes me wonder why, for example, Divinity 2 DKS, which is a similar game in many respects, but with a real personality, really good characters, humor and charm, was not very successful financially, and in the reviews, but KOA is praised left and right.  Combat is good, but without a good story for me it does not matter. May be I am too old already to be happy just with a mindless hack and slash.  Alchemy, crafting, and such are OK, but without a good story is is kinda pointless. Overall KOA is a huge disappointment for me.

review_headline: Not horrible for $10, but not very good either.
review_body:
Kinect games are very hit or miss. And Hulk Hogan's Main Event is no different. There are some things to like, but there are more to hate.

The graphics are atrocious.

The sound is inconsistent.

But I actually think the Kinect sensor registers pretty well.

Some moves are ridiculously difficult to pull off, but many Kinect games are.

Overall, it's probably worth the $10 I paid for it, but I would probably rate it lower if I paid $20, $30, $40 for it. If you can get it cheap, try it out.

I was looking forward to this release for the last year. This was supposed to be the release that \\"brought back\\" the armored core series from the AC4/FA titles which not of the same caliber as AC2 and AC3. So, I bought it the day it came out... and had the following experience:

Single Player Missions: Worse and orders of magnitude more limited than previous AC titles. There are a total of about 10 maps in this game, and they get continually recycled for different missions, so you are essentially playing the same 10 maps with different enemies and objectives. Also, the maps themselves are small and boring, and don't compare favorably well even to AC2. Also, the same awkwardly-written dialogue that has been plaguing us since AC1 is still here.

The single player story line is basically a mashup of cliche japanese anime plots: \\"Oh, there is an evil emperor!\\"... \\"Oh, there is a brave resistance!\\"... \\"Oh, there is a skilled AC pilot with vastly superior abilities who will save us all!\\". This is not what I was hoping for when I watched the gritty and dark WWII-esque trailer for the game.

There is also no single player parts progression like there was in previous AC titles. Normally, you would start with the terrible default AC, and then have just enough cash to scrape together to buy a new part that might help you in the next mission. No so in this game. The single player missions reward you with ridiculous amounts of money for trivial kill-the-ac scenarios, which can be played over and over until you are a millionaire in an hour.

Multi Player: Overall, it seems like the developers really focused on the online play, which shows promise, but feels half-complete.

Horribly unbalanced weapons... absolutely horrible. Parts balance in previous AC games was always somewhat bad, but not THIS bad. I've literally been killed in one burst by a charged laser cannon that everyone uses. Of course, I don't have access tothis part, because I'm not in the right clan and I don't have enough team points. Victory has more to do with the parts you install than your skill, unlike in previous AC games where I could fly circles around my opponents and beat technically better ACs. Nope, you will only win if you have the Chosen Parts, and these are only granted to the Chosen Few clans.

Player battles are separated into ranked vs unranked battles. If you fight an unranked battle, congratulations, there is no benefit whatsoever. No money, no team points, obviously no rank points... nothing. If you fight a ranked battle, prepare to be torn apart in 3 seconds by player after player who use the same three builds using weapons you don't have access to yet. If by some miracle you do manage to win, the other player will just disconnect out of the battle and it ends immediately... no points for you.

Griefers are also a big problem in this game. A lot of the mercs will sign up for missions with you, and then one-shot you in the back with a laser cannon, just for the lols. The game gives you no history to show who you've played with (if you don't happen to remember their name) and no way to report them for griefing, and basically no consequences for them whatsoever. This is especially problematic when you are on missions where you lose ALL of your team points if you lose. Griefing is very easy (and an effective tactic for opposing clans) because the online features are not fully developed and thought-through.

The online play system is set up architecturally wrong in a couple different areas. If you lose a ranked player match, you also lose rank points. This means that we will always have rage quitters and plug-pullers in this game until this gets changed... which is probably never. Also, on certain online battles one of the players has to be stuck being the \\"operator\\" which means you spend the match looking at a poorly-drawn mini-map to mark targets for your team... it gets boring very quickly, and nobody wants to get stuck doing this. There are no CPU opponents to speak of, which means sometimes I'll wait 30min in a room trying to get a battle royale started, just trying to get people to join. Then it takes so long to start, some people leave the room, and everybody is like \\"NOOOOOO!\\" because now we have to wait even longer. Somehow this is not how I would imagine online battle would be in 2012; this is reminiscent of how the first online FPS games operated in the 1990's.

The territory battle system is really bizarre. Basically, you click on a territory to begin a mission, and then you dash around destroying stationary helicopters or going from X point to Y point. I think other ACs from the other team are supposed to show up, but they never do, so you're left to do the entire mission with the only resistance being a few default turrets that the enemy placed there beforehand. I always do these missions alone, because I can take out all of the forces by myself, since they are so predictable, and mysteriously empty. I doubt this is the way these missions were meant to be played. Also, if you want to defend your territory, you have to sit around for hours waiting for another team to attack, which may or may not happen. The territory battle system is basically completely unplayable as intended.

Communication between teammates depends on a headset, which can be weird if you're online playing with strangers. There should a way to call targets and communicate basic things like we see in MMOs. I don't like having to turn on my headset and make everyone listen to my girlfriend yelling at the cats just to say \\"Hey, I'm going to target the helicopter in the back\\". In a truly team-based game there should have been a team-oriented HUD addition to Scan Mode to take care of this.

Controls: Astonishingly bad. Gone are the days of lightning-quick combat, mid-air dogfights, and complete freedom of movement. We had complete freedom of movement in the PS1-era AC games, but apparently it's too much to ask of our great next-generation games on our great next-generation system. One time I was hopping up the side of a building, and I got the leaving area message, because apparently the building was too high? Seems kind of odd for a building that the developers placed in the map... if it was indeed too tall for their desired level of gameplay, why didn't they just make the building less tall??

Some new boost maneuvers off the sides of buildings have been added, but the controls are so slow that they don't make much of a difference. With prior AC games, you could dart around enemy fire and weave in and out of missle volleys, but in this game you basically just sit there and take it because the controls are so slow. Using the overboost is a chore, and it can't be activated in mid-air which kind of defeats the purpose of it. If an enemy is firing at me, I have to land, turn off my boosters, and then overboost away. There is no longer that big of a difference between tank legs and reverse-joint legs, for example, because the maneuverability sucks with either. Boosting is a chore. Jumping is a chore. Overboost is a chore. Simply turning your ac is a chore.

Scan mode is how you replenish your energy and get targeting information, but it disables your weapons. I'm using it more often now, but it seems like a pointless addition. The only time I run low on energy is when I'm in short range in the heat of battle, and the only way to get my energy back is to retreat and then turn on scan mode. It's a really cool concept, but again it's killed by the slow, unresponsive control over your AC, lack of good overboost, lack of free flight capability... so your retreat doesn't do any good because the enemy can easily keep you in his sights. So this good gameplay mechanism is completely ruined and poorly executed.

Also, when I'min the heat of battle, I end up cranking the left analog stick to move out of the way, trying to get my slow hulk to move, and then accidentally press the stick down... causing scan mode to activate and disables all of my weapons. Not a fun experience.

Graphics: maybe comparable to AC2 but with a worse framerate. Washed out, bland colors. It's very difficult to see what I'm even shooting at on most of the missions, even on my big screen HDTV. Not only are the graphics not pretty, but they significantly impact gameplay in a negative way. There is just no excuse for this in 2012.

I've been a fan of AC since AC1 and I've tried on several different occasions to enjoy this game. I wanted to believe that this game was good. I lied to myself and said \\"Hey, this game is good\\". But no, it's not good... it's crap. It seems only about 80% finished and they just rushed it out to make a quick buck.

Between the disappointment of this game and Silent Hill:Downpour I really think about giving up videogames for good. It's sad when the latest games don't even match up to their predecessors released almost 15 years ago. I had such high hopes when I was a child, looking forward to all the great games I'd play as an adult. Now, I'm left with this... pure crap, everywhere I look.

product_title: The Legend of Zelda: Skyward Sword with Music CD
review_body: Skyward Sword is definately the best Zelda yet.  As a 25th Anniversary celebration game, it did a great job of paying homage to previous Zelda titles and tying some of the story lines together.  The graphics aren't as good as Twilight princess, but they are even more charming, which makes up for it.  The motion controls were unbelievable.  I never want to go back to Zelda without motion controls.  The characters were great. review_headline: Some good things going for this game, but technical issues get in the way
review_body:
Since I always find the Pro/Con bulleted points in reviews the most insightful parts, I'll list mine first. If you'd like the expanded version you can read on after.

Game: Venetica
Genre: Action-RPG
Platform reviewed: PS3

Pros:
- Stunning and breathtaking environments. Absolutely beautiful - brimming with expansive, colorful and well-lit vistas. Visually these environments are more impressive than some recent Bethesda games (*cough Kingdoms of Amular, *cough *cough)
- Good gameplay, lots of fun hack n' slash action
- Well implemented RPG leveling, magic, and item systems and variety
- Great music and surprisingly way above-average voice acting.

Cons:
- Technical problems abound and can be very frustrating;
a)The camera system is one of the worser ones I've seen in the past few years and can impact gameplay and even cause you to lose a battle when it goes awry.
b)collisions are badly implemented. Count on getting stuck on corners and small objects often.
c)texture-ripping and lighting bugs are a common occurrence
- Character artwork is poor and models are low-res. Compared with the environments, characters feel totally out of place.
- Character animation is very, VERY poor. They remind me of PS1 games - remembers how characters in Final Fantasy VII moved? Yeah, like that...repetitive movement loops and all.
- Dialogue/Script could be better
- too many \\"fetch quests\\"

There is so much good going for this game - the audio and voice acting in particular are excellent. The gameplay is entertaining - very similar to 60% of current-gen (people are still using \\"next gen\\" but that word no longer applies to PS3 and Xbox360 after 6 and 8 years since launch, respectively) but that doesn't bother me much - I enjoy hack n' slash RPG games in general, and loot gathering and leveling is always a satisfying and vital ingredient. So from a gameplay standpoint I do enjoy it. It does have some antiquated or inefficient things going on in places - for instance:

Early in the game (first 6 hours of play?) you reach a tavern on a cliff, and way below at the bottom of the cliff is the a beach you'll need to go to and back a few times for a quest. The only way down is a long winding wooden staircase built onto the spire-like cliff column...and you have to walk down and up the entire thing, taking nearly two full minutes just to traverse the stairs.

This adds nothing to the game, there's no reason for it and no battles occur on said stairs - its an empty and long climb/descent. So in some places the designers show questionable judgement, but overall it doesn't seem to happen too often. The upside is that the environmental visual presentation is stunning. Beautiful hi-res environments and large, sweeping detailed vistas fill this game to the brim. Honestly its worth trying this game just to see the world itself. In fact the environments are SO good that the character artwork - which is substandard even for a massive RPG - looks downright trashy in comparison. There's a noticable divide in quality for sure - like the developers blew their whole Tris budget on the environments and had to keep the characters very low Tri (Tri = triangles, used to describe how smooth or blocky a 3D model will look. 3D models are comprised of hundreds to thousands and sometimes millions of little triangles). However, character animations are crappy...really crappy...like Playstation One crappy. I think they just didn't put much priority in the Character art department.

That leads me into my diatribe to other developers (I am a game developer) that internal, dev team game testing/QA DOESN'T PRODUCE GOOD RESULTS. These are engineers, artists, designers and producers - use their time and energy to create the game. Use a fifth of the budget you paid them to test in off-hours and contract a dedicated QA House. I don't know if that's what really happened here, but technical polish is kinda non-existent. The technical problems in this game - most notably the camera and collision detection - are horrid. Its a frequent situation where Ill be playing along and I'm really getting into the game and then the camera starts spinning or gets stuck inside a solid model leaving me to play blind(thick bushes most often) or Ill get stuck on a small rock's collision box issues and have to button-mash for 30 seconds to get out of it. I've died a few times already and fallen \\"through the world\\" once because of technical bugs that have no place in a AAA budget game. ESPECIALLY the camera flaws.

Overall its a decently fun game with some truly breathtaking environments and music, and excellent voice acting. Its also very unpolished in terms of some basic technical structure in the game - camera, collisions, animations - and the character artwork is completely 1999-2003 era-looking in contrast to the amazing, colorful, high-res current-gen environments.

I want this game not to have these issues. I WANT to play this game through, but it gets so frustrating because of the technical shortcomings and some bad design decisions...I think my playing time would be better spent on other games. Off to the \\"gamestop trade-in bag\\" you go, Venetica. A game cant rely on just being pretty, though you were REALLY pretty in spots. Oh well.

By nearly every account, the Nintendo Gamecube was a commercial failure following its 2002 system launch. It was beaten to the punch by Microsoft's new X-Box, as well as falling behind the DVD-playing PS2 & that system's online capabilities. When the final tally was made, the Gamecube ultimately precipitated Nintendo to create the ground-breaking Wii to once again compete in the video game market.

That being said, the Gamecube was home to some of the most enjoyable video games ever created. It didn't fare too well in the always-popular first-person shooter & \\"epic games\\" categories, but its own licensed stable of games/characters was still as strong as ever. Games like \\"Mario Power Tennis\\", \\"Luigi's Mansion\\", \\"Super Smash Bros. Melee\\", & \\"Mario Kart: Double Dash\\" provide hours upon hours of entertainment, while installments of the Madden football series and the MVP Baseball series were some of the best ever created on this system.

Simply put, the Gamecube was never meant to be anything more than a console for brand loyalists who wanted their Mario, Zelda, DK, & Pokemon (among others, of course) games. While Microsoft went for the \\"online gaming\\" crowd and found a winning market (although it actually took the 360 to accomplish that goal), and Sony was the first to grasp the concept of an \\"all-in-one\\" entertainment console, the Gamecube was perhaps the last bastion of gaming console meant for the sole purposes of video games.

In terms of \\"specs\\", the graphics in this system were excellent for their time, and the controller was easily the most ergonomic I have ever played (with the 360 a close second). Here we are in 2012, and Nintendo has yet to even match, much less surpass, some of the graphics of, say, Super Smash Bros. Melee or Zelda: Twilight Princess.

Overall, the Gamecube was a fun system that played very well to its niche: Nintendo brand loyalists. Though other systems reshaped the public perception of video gaming, the Gamecube provided one last throwback to the traditional console market. In the process, the Gamecube turned out to be perhaps the best overall Nintendo gaming unit ever in terms of fun, functionality, & quality game titles.

One final thought: While the N64 now looks and seems quaint by today's standards, with only nostalgic games like Goldeneye or Mario '64 to keep it relevant whatsoever, the Gamecube still touches a core market even today: those who want a traditional gaming experience with the \\"old gang\\" of Nintendo characters. I want to comment on one thing first. This game is brutal. Casual gamers should not buy this game. This game is directly catered to people who like challenges or who have been playing games for a long time.

Every fight lasts a very long time. Typical fights last 1:30-3:00 minutes. You often fight bosses that take 6 minutes+. These are not just mindless attacking but constantly paying attention to what is happening and shifting your tactics mid-fight to account for what is happening in the fight. Combine with the fact that there is no rest in this game. This game is relentless. You are ALWAYS fighting or experiencing a really dramatic moment. This game really gives you no opportunity to catch a breathe. I often play for a couple of hours and end my sessions really exhausted.

Dying is also inevitable. You WILL die when you play this game. Many fights require some prior knowledge or experience about the opponents in order to win. Many fights which require some planning to win often come out of the blue(which leaves you with no opportunity to plan for the fight). You will die A LOT playing this game if you aren't reading a guide or being told how to play. And even then you will die. If you are the kind of person that can not understand dying as a learning experience and sees it mainly as a source of frustration, avoid this game. The penalty for dying in this game is very negligible if not non-existent so there should be no reason to be angry about dying.

I want to address the lack of towns in this game. Towns provide an opportunity to take a break. Side quests that are less serious provide this opportunity. But I believe that they may not be necessary if other there were other ways to compensate.

You do not buy or find \\"better\\" weapons. All weapons serve their own purposes depending on what role you assigned to your characters. Need for Speed has taken many different directions, but the mid to late 2000's were the worst for the series. ProStreet is probably the worst NFS I have played, and I can't really recommend this to even hardcore fans. The game has good customization options, and varied event types, but after a couple dozen races you will be bored.

Races consist of earning a certain amount of points to \\"Dominate the Day\\". These events range from Drifts, Drags, Grip, Time Attack, and Sector Shootout. Sector Shootout is where you have a track divided into sections and you must get the fastest times in those to win. Grip races are straight up races, and the rest is history. Out of these events the Drags are the best because you need to heat up your tires before racing. You can only win by getting perfect shifts, but after you get NOS upgrades the drags become really easy. There are 1/4 mile and 1/2 mile drags, but I would have liked to see 3/4 and 1 mile drags as well. All the other races are pretty boring, and drifting in the game feels like dragging an 18 wheeler through dirt. No matter what car you use drifting never feels right, and is a huge pain to pull off.

The game was one of the first NFS games that used real-time damage which is supposed to affect the way the car drives but really doesn't. You can get light and heavy damage, but I never really noticed much of a hit in performance. If you damage your car you have to repair before the next race, but you can use cash or repair markers that you earn. My biggest issue with these \\"Race Days\\" is that if you quit in the middle you have to restart the whole thing. This drove me nuts because I couldn't go upgrade my car and come back.

Upgrading your cars is pretty fun because there are a lot of options for both performance and cosmetic. You can fine tune your car as well, but there is a quick upgrade option for impatient people. You can only have certain cars for certain event types, but you can only save customizations as blueprints. This allows you to have multiple looks and loadouts for your cars. I found that cash is given very slowly and parts are very expensive so you won't be upgrading very often which is a huge bummer.

Lastly, the game is just monotonous. After about a couple dozen races you will feel fed up with the same tired races over and over again. The physics feel too weighty, and most cars feel the same no matter how you upgrade them. The whole game is really unbalanced and poorly designed. The game doesn't even officially support the Game for Windows controller, and just show keyboard buttons instead. I just gave up about half way through because some races were always easy no matter who you did, and some extremely difficult no matter how good you were. The visuals are decent, but not anything to write home about. The announcer is just extremely annoying to listen to with his stoner one-liners and he just blabbers on about nonsense.

Sony's longest running title is back a pounding with metal & rock to fit the tone. This Semi-black Sequel/Semi-Reboot adds new interesting modes such as race, cage match & Nuke, very interesting modes to the game play but don't come without major flaws.

THE CONTROLS:
there your standard car combat controls only being that L2 for primary is swapped in favor for the more modern feel of R2.
the games responsive enough on commands, however aiming up and shooting down air vehicles can be a pain especially at times instead of locking on to the vehicle that is closest and straight forward of your vehicle, you may be blasting him with your machine guns but your missles will be set on a further distant car that isn't your priority. controlling talon feels his missles flat out refuse to lock on anyone and sometimes has trouble with his mega gun lock on, adding to talons poor aiming is his special, the tri-gun which can't make up its mind what vehicle it wants to lock-on, I'll keep the reticle steady on an enemy only for it to bounce randomly to 4 other vehicles wasting all of the special, vehicles which were not even near my target. The vehicles don't drive, act or feel like other car games, which twisted metal never did but turning can feel awfully jerking.

THE SINGLE PLAYER:
The single player is a blast with some difficulty spikes,things get big in the story's levels but the whole campaign ends on a short notice hinting at upcoming DLC. with 3 characters 1 played after the other, it clearly shows that the single player was rushed and slapped on for the full $60 retail price and is the weakest and most disappointing feature in this twisted metal installment
the race events which, as fun as they are the gates seem to have trouble registering you going through them.
The AI at times can range from fair to downright you VS everyone as they seem to fire 70% of what they got at just you and regenerate specials 3x faster, adding to that is the freeze missle, yes the AI's best buddy which they will not let up on this 1, they can also snipe you 5x faster and half the time you don't know your being aimed at because the laser forgets to show up. TWISTED DIFFICULTY is by far crushing with 2 prizes at the end to \\"prolong\\" the single player and is downright unfair, If something is not a legitimate test of skill (meaning it's actually balanced enough to be doable with every car in the game), then it cannot rightfully be called \\"hard.\\" The odds of anyone ever being able to fire up Twisted Metal on this difficulty and beat it with a random non-Juggernaut vehicle are absurdly slim. Even with Juggernaut and Talon this comes down to more luck than skill, which is profound evidence of it being broken, not \\"hard.\\"
Trial-and-error gameplay like what the Battletoads and (old-school) Ninja Gaiden games were built off of back in their day has gone out of style for very good reason. It's needlessly irritating, and it artificially lengthens a game by forcing numerous restarts instead of offering ample content. This game is a marvelous throw back to that era, but for all the wrong reasons. Virtually every event on Twisted difficulty is like suffering the hell of memorizing Battletoads' speeder bike level from start to finish, all over again. It's just not fun. I've beaten it on twisted difficult and it is by far the dumbest choice I've seen put in a game this year.nobody here can legitimately claim to be good at it. Not a single one of you, especially those of you calling the rest of us \\"wussys\\" and \\"losers\\" or whatever for not enjoying this sadistic trash difficulty. You didn't unlock Warthog by way of skill; you did it the same way the rest of us are doing it: by spamming two vehicles over and over until something goes right, maybe the AI glitches out, rams a wall, and never recovers. That helps too, and some of you know very well you owe at least one victory to that.

THE MULTIPLAYER:
When it works, its good, there has been patches that have finally fixed the majority of the issues with connection and drop-outs, though its still broken due to some vehicles needing rebalancing (talon being a near game breaker). but here is where twisted metal shines as it was suppose to be an online only game and it shows, ranging from the tried and true Deathmatch/TDM are hunted & nuke. Nuke being your ATTack & DEFend mode, with a slight change, by far my favorite mode. hunted, pretty much 1 vs everyone so, might as well play twisted difficulty and actually unlock things. there isn't much in modes but it'll last. I would love for them to create a ROGUE TRIP Mode based off dev teams other game rogue trip, which there is a lot of to in this game (the unofficial twisted metal 3)

CO-OP: it's all local couch co-op like the old school TM games. I love it when this feature is in a game and it should be how this is played. with this you can Split screen and take on the entire campaign with a friend (recommended for twisted difficulty) up to 4 players & split-screen Online play! (great feature)

THE MAPS: The maps are good ranging from there own large scale medium & small. but some of the race courses drag way to long to the point I'm getting pod-racing flashbacks, some range from previous titles like TM: Black. TM: Head-oN & TM1 (sadly none from 2) but altered differently.

PAINT FEATURE: Its good though limited, all the customizing you want to do is on the website and... that site hasnt worked in a long time, still doesn't, cant log in, cant sign up, cant use the custom paintings or save to your garage, can't redeem NOS dlc skins, just another incomplete feature...

All in all I'd say it is not worth the full $60 retail price especially since the game plays so brokenly in the multiplayer and everything in the single player feels unfinished. this adds a problem since its a PS3 exclusive that means it also requires an ONLINE PASS CODE, but David Jaffe added 2 codes for TM Black ps2 digital copy(SD non HD remaster) and a sweet tooth starhawk skin code to make up for sony's new rule, which is real cool to do that. This games hard to rate since it is a mixed bag, since when did sweet tooth get a masters degree in engineering and literally turn his ice cream truck into a jet packing autobot... just no... the game knows its origin and doesn't stray away that much from its formula, over the amount of fun i did have with this game, mainly the whole time I felt a bit let down.

review_headline: This game will suck you in
review_body:
Dark Souls is an amazing game that goes beyond its predecessor in every way. Stunning visuals, seamless combat, and lurking danger are the cornerstones of this game. You will spend countless hours exploring the diverse environments, ranging from haunted ruins, to an undead castle, to a forest where even the trees want to kill you. The new covenant system allows you to join a guild, each with unique perks. The customization and weapon crafting have also been improved upon.

The fighting is more or less identical to the fighting in Demon's Souls. If you have not played either game yet, it will take a bit of getting used to. This is not the kind of game where you can win by constantly mashing the X button; you will need to fight strategically, whether it be by using your shield or dodging your enemy's swing and kill it from behind. The boss battles require extra precision. Most bosses can kill you in few hits, yet can take many hits themselves. You will need to study the boss's movements to figure out when it is most vulnerable. This requires trial and error, and yes, you will die. A lot. Dying is part of the game, and anyone who complains about it should have known what they were getting into. Fortunately, you have the ability to summon help in the form of other players or computer NPCs. This summoning ability is the backbone of the game, as it also means that your player can be invaded. If the conditions are right, another player can come into your game and kill you for various reasons. Sometimes it is just for fun, other times it is because you wronged their covenant. Regardless, this is the most fun, and most frustrating part of the game.

There are times that the combat lags while engaged in multiplayer--I have been in the middle of a fight where I am hitting the other character but nothing is happening. Then lo and behold the character teleports behind me and kills me with a swift backstab. The multiplayer combat is rarely an even match; I either destroy the other character or am destroyed myself. Rarely is there a good fight that feels like a true victory. However, your pulse will raise and you will start to sweat any time you see the \\"You have been invaded\\" text.

Overall, great game full of excellent combat, beautiful graphics, and plenty of mystery. You will think about this game even when you are not playing it, wondering what is down a certain path, or how to get around a certain obstacle. Stop reading, and start playing.

review_headline: Amazing World -- Repetitious Dungeons and boring fetch-Quests
review_body:
Open world is beautiful, and fun to explore. Dragons and Giants add a great deal of added fun to open-world explorations. Leveling system is fun and very customizable.

Fun Game for about 40 Hours of Gameplay. After that it is more an exercise in tedium.

Basically the exact game-play as all Elder Scrolls. Very rough 1st person melee. For this reason -- I am always heavy on Mage and Archery builds -- since I find ranged combat so much more suited for the controls in this game. This is not a game to be bought for the combat mechanics --- they are clunky.

Very few Mission lines of any interest. Hundreds of hours of play -- if you want to repeat doing the same thing over and over. Talk to person -- get mission to retrieve object or person at cave/Dwarf Ruin/fort -- fast travel or horseback to destination -- Go through series of tunnels that are one of pretty much 3 types (cave/Dwarf Ruin/fort) --- fight some easy bad guys...and then a tougher bad guy at the end -- collect treasure chest..return.

No exploration in the Dungeons -- just linear, and all caves look pretty much the same, with the same few enemy types -- so once you've done one cave mission -- you've done them all. Do one fort, you've done them all, do one dwarf ruin, you've done them all (other than 1 major Ruin - \\"Blackreach\\" which actually requires exploration) -- you get the point.

Do this bewteen 50 and 5000 times...whichever you prefer -- and why some say they played 400 hours (doing the same thing over and over) -- and when you get tired of it, go fight a dragon and/or advance the main story quests.

Story improved from prior Elder Scrolls. However -- people still do not in any way react to the story Advancing. Other than the stupid Guards saying random things (you know, the guards with the stupid \\"took an arrow to the knee...\\" quote) -- no one acts any different, even after you have defeated the Final Boss Dragon. This, to me, really detracts from RPG world immersion -- which is essential for any RPG to get 5 stars IMO.

Also the main side-quest lines, like the Guilds, were way easier, and more repetitive than their counterparts in Oblivion. The Dark Brotherhood is probably the best of 'em; and the side quests related to the Daedra tend to be the most interesting/varied. Becoming \\"Arch-Mage\\" or \\"Harbringer\\" (head of the fighter's guild) was too easy and not at all rewarding...

Always a classic, the graphics might not be considered 'top notch' by some, but the gameplay overall is excellent. Only concern is that I seem to be having trouble applying the BGtutu mod (allows playing Baldur's Gate 1 on the Baldur's Gate 2 engine). My guess would be that this is not the North American release of the game. It is otherwise playable, however, and every bit the game I remember growing up with.

product_title: Super Mario RPG: Legend of the Seven Stars
review_headline: Super Mario RPG: The Grandpa of Every Mario Role Playing Game
review_body:
Super Mario RPG is one interesting classic. As the title of this review suggests, it is the first Mario RPG ever made. It is considered by many fans to be the best of all the Mario role playing games (I could'nt tell you as I'm only halfway done with Paper Mario and I have not played any of the others). This game also has a few other points of interest. It was the last Mario game ever made for the SNES and the (Shock) first time Mario, Bowser, and Peach have ever worked toghether. But anyway, I'm just going to stop writing this boring intro which you probably did not read and actually write about the game.

Story: 10 out of 10

If you're a person who has not played this game before (and quite possibly if you are a person who has played this game before) you're probably thinking right now ''What is wrong with this guy. A 10 out of 10 for the storyline in a Mario game. Ha Ha Ha Ha Ha.'' Well I'm giving the story a 10 out of 10 because by Mario standards, it's actually very good. The reason why? Well, basically this is story.

So this game starts off with a storyline that any gamer, casual or hardcore, should be familliar with. Bowser kidnapping Princess Peach and Mario rushing as fast as he can to her aid. Like you have never seen that before. Mario arrives at Bowser's castle and beats up all of his incredibly weak minions before meeting up with the big turtle himself. Bowser is than defeated in an easy battle and Mario reclaims Princess Peach! Wait a second... What? We are only five minutes into this game. Why have we already saved the princess? Suddenly a big rumble is heard and Mario, Bowser, and Peach are all flung far away from the castle. We than see a big sword crash into the castle and see seven stars fall out of a cloud. Mario travels back to the castle and the giant sword says to Mario that he is part of a group called the Smithy Gang and that nosey people like Mario are only halting them from taking over the world. So, Mario isleft in a really bad situation. Now he has to save the world from the Smithy Gang...

As you can see this game's plot is very none Mario-like. Along the way, Peach and Bowser become Mario's allies throughout his quest which makes it even more unique. It is satisfying that there is more to it than Bowser kidnapping Peach which makes it awesome! This is why I love this game's plot as it manages to be unlike any other Mario storyline.

Gameplay Mechanics: 9.5 out of 10

Here's something that from my experience (No pun intended) that not that many people seem to realize. Except for one feature, I'd say this game's battle system is a total clone of Chrono Trigger's battle system. That's not a bad thing given that Super Mario RPG and Chrono Trigger were both developed by the same company. But still, it's amazing how simmilar the two are. Like in Chrono Trigger, the battles are fought from a top-down view. There are no random encounters and you can only have three characters in a battle at once. The game features cool animations for attacks and if your character dies or gets a status ailment, they will automatically recover after the end of any battle. Everything I just mentioned is in Chrono Trigger as well... however the one aspect that seperates this game's battle system from Chrono Trigger's battle system is a feature called timing.
In this game, timing is when by pressing a button at the right time, you can double the damage you recieve. For instance, let's say Mario punches an enemy. If I were to press the A button right before the punching animation begins, Mario would actually punch an enemy twice instead of just once. This is something that is essential to the game and this is what makes this RPG unique. There is also defensive timing where if an enemy tries to attack you, if you press the B button right before the enemy's attack animation, the damage you recieve will decrease.

So anyhow, I love the whole timed hitsthing this game has going on here. It really is cool and unique. It's what makes this game's battle system not a complete rip-off of Chrono Trigger's battle system.

Anyhow, when you're not in a battle, you're entire party is represented by just the main character (Mario) which is simmilar to Final Fantasy. When you are in the overworld, Mario's famous jumps are key to progressing. By pressing the B button, Mario jumps over ledges or whatever is blocking his merry way. The issue with overworld jumps though is that because of the game's top-down view, some of them can be difficult to pull off. For instance, there is an area in the game which features a bunch of large cliffs that are all right next to each other. You have to jump across each one in order to cross. I think I fell numerous times while doing that because of this game's top-down view. So yeah, occasionally the jumpng system of this game is a little akward and clunky but other then that I see don't see any other issues with this game's mechanics.

Graphics: 10 out of 10

This game's graphics are one of it's strongest points. Okay, we are living in 2011 and this game's graphics are not as amazing as they were fifteen years ago. But for me, when I look at aN old game's graphics, I usually don't try to compare them to the graphics of today. Instead, I think of how well they looked by the standards of the system it was on. And by SNES standards, these are graphics that pushed the system to it's very limit. They highly resemble the graphics used in the Donkey Kong Country SNES trilogy and that's because I think they used the same technology. They really are superb and in my opinion, I'd go as far as saying that these are the most advanced graphics that ever appeared on the SNES. It's just too bad that this game came out only four months before the Nintendo 64, which drew away alot of attention from the graphics (and this whole game in general). It's a shame...

Longevity:7 out of 10

This is one of the two main cons this game has. It really is not that long of an adventure. As a normal game, yeah sure, it's very long. But by RPG standards, it's very short. It is by far the shortest RPG I've ever played for the SNES. It only clocks in to about 10 - 15 hours of gameplay. That makes me mad because when I get an RPG I expect a long thirty to forty hour adventure that will keep me occupied for months. This... will not. It will keep you occupied for 2-3 weeks. I wish it was longer...

Challenge: 5 out of 10

This is even worse. The challange of this game is hardly exsistent. I mean, most of the bosses will go down easily, the enemies are not really threatining... It's just too easy. As said in the Gameplay Mechanics section, any status ailment or death is cured at the end of every battle. I really wish it was harder. There is actually an optional boss that is very challenging but I'll talk about that later.

Music: 8.5 out of 10

I like this game's soundtrack. I'm not going to say I totally love it but I do like it. I don't know why, I'm just not particulary fond of this game's music. That does not mean that I don't love some songs in it. Obviously, I can't say too much about because this is a review but if you want to hear it yourself, type in ''super mario rpg soundtrack'' on Youtube. I'm sure that should take you to some pretty awesome songs.

Sidequests: 9.5 out of 10

While this game does not have as many sidequests as let's say, Chrono Trigger, it still has some pretty cool ones along the way. Some of them include making music for a frog, fighting a Final Fantasy boss who is more difficult then the final boss, and competing in a casino found under a pipe. The sidequests can be a little boring from time to time but they can also be awesome (mainly the sidequest where you fight the Final Fantasy boss). I do wish there were a little more but I like the ones this game has to offer.

Closing Comments

Super Mario RPG is a good game that any RPG fan should check out. If you can look past the easy difficulty level and the relativley short length, than you're definitley going to have fun with the red plumber's first dive into the RPG genre.

review_headline: Not what I was expecting, disappointed.
review_body:
DISCLAIMER: I've owned this game for about 2 weeks and have played it once, but I was so frustrated with it I doubt I will play it again...My review explains why:

I recently got an Xbox simply for the kinect. I prefer my PS3, but I really wanted to play Dance Central. The kinect offers the capability to make these dance/fitness games much better than their counterparts on the wii and ps3. Unfortunately \\"Your Shape\\" doesn't benefit from the kinect at all.

While playing I found that I'd be doing the exercises but the game wouldn't count me as completing them. It's possible that I need to play with the configurations (I was playing straight out of the box) but I've never had any trouble with my other kinect games (Dance Central, Dance Central 2, and Kinect Adventures). As I was doing the exercises I didn't feel like I was receiving any added benefits by playing this game on the xbox. I was doing some of the same things I would be doing on the wii, and the wii games made it way more fun.

I became very frustrated with how the game is set up. I set my weight and fitness ability thinking that it would set up a work out for me, but instead I was brought back to the main menu and had flags next to various work-outs...What does that mean?? I was completely annoyed with the lack of guidance. I decided to go through and do these workouts with flags. Maybe, I thought, it would alert me of my progress after I complete them. Nope. Nothing. I decided to continue working out. When I filled out the fitness survey, it made it sound like I should be doing about 30 minutes three times a week. So I continued, hoping it would alert me when I had exercised for that amount of time. I did between 35-45 minutes of exercise and never got alerted. I checked out my profile, it only said I worked out for 17 minutes!! One of the dance routines was 13 minutes by itself and I had done jogging, and various strength training beyond that. I have NO IDEA what it was calculating for time, but I definitely had done more than 17 minutes. Keep in mind that I was doing the \\"flagged\\" workouts too, so you'd think that these would definitely count (as opposed to non-flagged exercises.) No where in the menus did it explain what I was suppose to do. Normally in other games they'll have you start with a nice warm-up and help you select exercises for your work-out. This left you high and dry. Where was my virtual trainer? Or my work-out plan for the day? If I wanted to feel clueless, I'd go to the gym and monkey around.

I was also very disappointed with the lack of exercises too. This reminded me of high school gym class. Everyone is made to do crunches but no one tells you that you don't have to kill your neck and back by doing them lying down. There were no alternative positions for working out in this game, nor are there many strength training exercises to begin with. Instead of providing variety, you just get to do MORE sit-up reps!(yay...) I have bad knees and I'm only beginning my training, therefore I have no strength anywhere. Where are my standing crunches? Alternative push-ups? etc? I need ways to work up to some of these, not just jump in and get discouraged when I can't do them.

And last, aesthetically, this game is hideous. As a graphic designer I enjoy things that are designed well, and thought out. This looks like they had no creativity and/or budget. One of the segments I was looking forward to was the \\"run around the world\\" exercise, and come to find out, that is simply a colored dot moving along a colored path through wire-framed buildings. There goes my enjoyable jog around London.

Summary:
-Horrible \\"personalized\\" exercise feature. (They guide you through entering your weight and exercise level, that's it. Maybe guessing what to do next is part of exercising my thinking skills?)
-No variety in workout moves (you push up, you sit up, you dumb bell up. Then you unlock level 2 which means more of each of those! Nothing interesting. Gets boring quick, and terrible for anyone just starting and wants to ease into exercise.)
-Ugly user interface. (While not really a deal-breaker...why suffer through it when you have EA Sports Active? or Dance Central? SOOO much nicer to look at.)
-Seriously lacking positive reinforcement. (You don't realize you like the corny reinforcement in other games, until you don't have it at all)
-Want to get exercises beyond the game? Fork over the money. (Have to buy with Microsoft points)

I own these two games on the wii and would recommend them over \\"Your Shape Fitness Evolved 2012\\"

The game designers of Dark Souls have made this game a horribly boring experience for the typical gamer, and fans of RPGs. They failed to created a 'Reward' system and a sense of accomplishment in trying to progress through this game. There is no fun in playing Dark Souls. It's simply designed in such a woefully dismal manner in that you the player, are constantly killed coming against Mini-Boss after Mini-Boss and Bosses, and losing everything. Leaving you to farm the same souls in hopes of eventually getting back to the Boss and collecting what you dropped before the Boss kills you again. And then you've lost it all for good.  Dark Souls fails to reward the player with adequate pick ups of anything but souls. The few weapons or armor the enemies drop are usually weaker than your beginning items or too heavy to bear until you level up several times. And you're stuck running through the same small areas of game play over and over again simply killing the same easier enemies  which give minor amounts of souls ), until you are bored to death. And to upgrade your lesser weapons you again need to farm and farm and farm and farm souls.  Get the point? )  And any sense of progression is only met far too soon upon defeating a Mini-Boss, with another difficult enemy or enemies, and your health is dangerously inadequate for another round of difficulty so soon.  Another sadly lacking element to the weak effort put forth in delivering this game to market is the absence of any sort of guide to explaining the various symbols and such. The meager 5 page booklet does nothing to offer insight to playing the game. Dark Souls designers have failed to deliver any help at all. It's as if they are saying, any player wanting to experience their game will have spend the additional $$ for the 3rd party Guide to understand how to play the game.  I've reached Level 30 in 40 hours and I've gotten nowhere that hasn't left me frustrated and bored to tears in having to revisit the same areas numerous times farming again and again, hoping to stumble upon humanity to proceed out of this hellish bore.

I found this game to be pretty reasonable overall. The battle system was enjoyable if not noteworthy, and I had a lot of fun playing around with materia and getting all my characters set up exactly how I wanted them. I only enjoyed one of the multitude of mandatory minigames, making them a significant downer. I left with the impression that Square wanted to make the game longer without necessarily forcing the player to grind in dungeons, so instead they forced the player to complete minigames to mix things up a bit. I think it was a decent idea, but the implementation was off a bit. No, Squaresoft, I do not want to practice marching in step and doing parade drills in sync with other soldiers. Fortunately, only a small amount of the game is devoted to these, leaving the majority of the game enjoyable, if not particularly outstanding.   I'm not concerned with the graphics, given that the game had already entered development before the Playstation was even on the market. I think the underlying story is one of the better ones among the games I've played. The story itself is probably 4 to 4.5 stars - but again, the implementation is sloppy. Key plot points that should leave the player breathless are muddled and instead leave them confused. That said, the game does follow up nicely on some of its most powerful moments. After a catastrophic, very emotional moment for the player, the game developers send you into an exploration of unusual, largely unexplored territories. This tactic worked nicely to re-engage me in the game world and get me down to business again, without making me feel like the scene had no meaning. A moment that powerful is a VERY hard act to follow, but Square pulled it off brilliantly.  The characters are all very by-the-book. Granted, some of them wrote a good portion of that book (Cloud, for instance). Square was careful to include a certain amount of backstory and a decent motivation for most characters. I got the impression that developers had actually paid attention to all the party members, and yet - they still entirely failed to capture me. I was fond of Red XIII and actively disliked Cloud and Yuffie, but I was apathetic towards most of the rest of the cast. I found most of the antagonists shallow, which is unfortunate because they were otherwise diverse. Square could have done fantastic things if they had given individual goals and motivations (of any consequence) to, say, the Turks. If they tried releasing this game today, I would give the characters one star. Still, the cast is reasonable for the time period.   It goes without saying that FF7 has legions of fans who will defend it to the death and question the intelligence of anyone who thinks otherwise. They are, of course, fully entitled to their opinions. I still think that public opinion of the game has been inflated by factors other than gameplay, such as its convenient release time and superb marketing. I also think that since its release, its reputation has led other gamers to think of it as \\"the best game\\", rather than developing their own internal standards and then comparing the game to those. That said, I'm sure that there are many people who would love the game regardless of its environmental factors, and my thoughts on this matter in no way lower the validity of their preferences.  TL;DR: A solid game, just don't expect miracles. Would make for a decent addition to your game collection - but not at $200.

review_headline: King Of Fighters XIII... K.O.'s its' predecessor!
review_body:
I picked up my pre-order at GameStop this morning alongside my four disk soundtrack. I can't review this game without mentioning kof xii, I did not hate the twelfth installment in the franchise but if you played it, then you'll know what I mean when I say it felt like an expensive demo. King of Fighters XIII knocks out its' predecessor in everyway!

Content (5/5)
This game has so much more content than the previous one. Several game modes to choose from: Tutorial, arcade, story, versus, practice, network, replay, gallery, mission, and customize. Most of these features were missing from the previous installment, including arcade mode which is a strange exclusion from a fighting game. This also has more than fifteen stages, which was a much needed improvement. The four disk soundtrack with music from kof 94'- kof xiii was just the cherry on top.

Story (4/5)
In my opinion this is the least important part of a fighting game. From what I gather this takes place after kof xi.

Graphics (5/5)
Starting with the epic opening scene and displayed in up to 1080p it looks simply beautiful! Over 30 hand drawn characters, all of them look very unique and are very detailed, with only slight pixilation in some of the sprites motions. I'm not sure if the backgrounds are hand drawn but they look amazing, off the top of my head... I couldn't stop staring at the stage with all the elephants in the background must see to appreciate.

Sound Effects and BGM (5/5)
High quality original music, can't say much here kof has never disappointed in this department. You can choose from two setting in the music section, from what I gather one is kof xiii music and the other is randomized music from various kof games.

Game play (5/5)
The game play is solid as always, this is the strength of the kof series. I'm going to focus on \\"Arcade mode\\" which is the one I spent most my time on so far. My opponents never felt overly cheap, the A.I. was challenging but satisfying to compete against. Difficulty is well balanced on all five settings.

Controls (5/5)
I had no problem pulling off some special moves and short combos without looking at a move list. Overall most of the moves are instantly familiar if you played kof in the past or even fighting games in general. If you have a choice I do recommend the use of a decent arcade stick for extended play sessions.

Replay value (5/5)
The extensive game modes will keep you busy for a while. I can't stop customizing characters; it's a fun little feature. You can customize every character up to five separate times, not to mention the custom colors that are already pre-made. The online experience will ultimately extend the life of the game. I spent about 2 hours getting by behind handed to me over the network, the connection with other players was a lot better than I expected, I only had two or three sluggish connections in a 2 hour period. The improvements of this feature are like night and day over kof xii.

Minor Imperfections:
Three small things I do want to mention: Vibration on the duel shock 3 is poorly utilized so far, it would have been nice if this feature was better supported during game play. Also there is beautiful animation and cut scenes during the arcade mode which lack voice acting. The other small complaint I have is the omission of \\"Dynamic\\" zoom in and out of camera perspective, its still there but not during actual game play. This makes some of the sprites seem thin. All of these are just small things I noticed, not a big deal.

General View (5/5)
I know I'm going to spend endless hours playing online and trying to achieve gold and platinum trophies. I'm glad SNK did proper justice to this installment, the arcade port out does the previous one in every way. My pre-order choice was very wise and I encourage others to pick up this game, it is worth every penny to own even without the soundtrack, it's a great alternative to Ultimate Marvel vs. Capcom 3, and it's an awesome game for your library. King of Fighters is back baby!!!King of Fighters is back baby!!!

product_title: Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty
review_body: It is now very hip to bash Metal Gear Solid 2, a fearless synthesis of multi-layered film and stealth video game.  Why all the hate and why now?  You see, back when MGS2 came out, it was a technical showcase for the PS2; nobody had ever seen anything quite like it, and those who would later revile it submerged their hatred for certain elements in deference to the incredible graphics.  Later, when other games began to surpass it visually, these hatreds bobbed to the surface, with the end result that it has become the unclothed emperor du jour in many circles.  Broadly speaking, people who hate it think it pulls together way too many disparate elements.  For one, though the gameplay appears to aim at simulating a drawn-out, nerve-wracking struggle where moving cautiously is paramount, silence is golden and death is a misstep away, the field of play is overflowing with the lighthearted symbology of an '80s arcade:  spinning power-ups chirrup happily when you grab them, corpses flicker and vanish (in more action-packed scenes) like something out of Double Dragon, question marks and exclamation points leap out of the heads of enemy soldiers when they suspect or confirm your presence.  In the minds of some players, this all seems patently absurd; why should a foe issue a heart-rending scream as his mortal wound gushes blood and he takes one last, stumbling and genuinely pitiful step -- only to have his corpse emit a huge floating can of life elixir?  The game's most synergetic and thus most despised aspect, however, is its most prevalent: its story.  It is inextricably linked with the gameplay; try as you might, mash A as quick as can, you can't avoid it.  Lengthy radio messages from supporting characters interrupt play, long, over-the-top cinematics bookend the various gameplay scenarios.  In the end, one spends as much time sitting back and watching the game as playing it.  So naturally, if MGS2's narrative rubs a player the wrong way, then nothing else the game has tooffer will salvage it for him.  This contentious (and assertive) story is a heady potpourri of comic book derring-do, speculative psychoanalysis, science fiction, government subterfuge, theatrical monologues, sobering tragedy and humor that borders on the Tim and Eric-esque.  To further complicate matters, it twists and turns, turns and twists, folds back on itself, laughs at the player's predictions and then blithely does the obvious when it's got him trained to expect the off-kilter.  This story, according to its detractors, is not only a discordant welter of themes and genres; it is so hopelessly tangled as to be INCOMPREHENSIBLE.  Oh, and it's somehow cliched, to boot.  Obviously, I disagree with MGS2's detractors; my feelings are on the opposite end of the spectrum.  I am gleefully disturbed by the crazy combination of arcade silliness and well-animated mortality.  I find the narrative style to be incredibly pleasing, having long been fond of storytellers who include discursive sections full of color -- and having long been fond of storytellers who, like Kojima, are unafraid of doing the BEAUTIFULLY ABNORMAL.  To my perception, the plot is not only comprehensible, but *perfectly logical* within the bounds set by its author; but then, I've always enjoyed the writings of A.E. van Vogt and Philip K. Dick, both known for their twisting, borderline schizoid tales.  And cliches?  I'm a little confused on that point.  What familiar patterns are used, are used only to create a sub-structure for all the weird little details to build upon, not as a crutch for lack of writing ability.  In the end, after all my piles of words, I must say that MGS2 is hard to defend.  It's just such a matter of individual likes and dislikes.  It's not just some homogenous thing that most people automatically get . . . or automatically fail to get.  It's got so many different elements that one is statistically likely to clash with a player's sensibilities . . . unless, of course, you're oneof those odd people that MGS2 was made specifically for.  With this in mind, it's truly a miracle not only that the game was such a high-budget production, but that it was made, period.  I suppose I can step outside myself a little and begin to understand why so many dislike the game . . . but since I personally love it, and all the elements that compose it, all that hate just seems wrong in the end.  To me, Metal Gear Solid 2 (and the series of which it is part) is a mosaic of the strange and wonderful -- a beautiful, abnormal synthesis.

review_headline: Dragons, Gems, Gnorcs, and my generations classic game
review_body: Spyro The Dragon was my first ever videogame and is still one of my favorites today.  It holds a special place in my heart and I have played a lot of videogames including almost the entire Final Fantasy frachise,both of American Mcgee's Alices, Trapt(Kagero 2:dark illusions in Japan), Primal, Dragon Age Origins, all 3 Jak and Daxters,Okami,both Valkyrie Profiles and many many more and while Spyro may not be my favorite and it doesn't hold a candle to them in violence or depth it is still revered by me as a FANTASTIC game.  It is artistically done in music and graphic design the game is simple without being to simple there are still a few challenges a young child probably couldn't figure out on their own so in other words the game isn't so challenging you get infuriated at it but it also isn't so easy that you get bored with it.  You basically collect Gems (the dragon's treasure), free your dragon friends who have been turned into crystaline statues by Gnasty Gnorc, chase down dragon egg thieves,and eventually have the final showdown with Gnasty Gnorc and you do it all in the form of an adorably spunky little purple dragon: Spyro.  This game is practically devoid of violence (although the entire Dream Weavers worlds weird me out even to this day) and is perfect for children 3 and up (although as I said they may collect enough items to advance to the next homeworld and even enough to defeat Gnasty Gnorc they still probably won't find everything 100%) it is a game that I think like Pacman will withstand the test of time and will still be played 20 years from now-at least by me!

Who created this game and why? I get the concept and it's a really good one. Then why did I give it one star? This game is created for people who find Call of Duty and Halo so easy they get bored and refuse to play them. The mini-games must be beaten absolutely flawlessly or you don't get any points whatsoever. Sometimes you even lose points for not absolutely mastering the mini-game. If you're 99% perfect, sorry no points. The biggest flaw in this game is that it has to be four players. If you don't have four players then the computer will take over the rest. Be warned, the computer always wins every single mini game. There's a choice for computer skill...easy, normal, or hard...huh? What is hard skill? Does that mean the game is hard for the computer player or the computer player is hard for you to beat? No explanation whatsoever. But, it does not matter, Ive tried all three settings multiple times and it makes no difference in the computer's amazing flawless skill at mastering the game. The point of the game is to get 20 coins, by absolutely mastering the mini-games as flawlessly as inhumanly possible, then randomly landing on the space where Toad is selling stars for 20 coins. Watch out, there's also a space where, if they have 50 coins, other players can steal your star. They should call this game Star Stealers. The only real trick to the game is to be the one who lands on the star stealing spot the most times...and thus steal everyone else's stars. There's no friendly competition here...it's all about bing underhanded. If you don't have 50 coins to steal a star you can, for zero coins, steal coins from other players. this game always leads to everyone ganging up on the player who is doing the best. There's no skill involved to winning the game over all because it's all about who's lucky enough to land on the star stealing spot the most times. One turn your in first place and the next your in fourth, but when you're in fourth you're stuck. Whoever happens to have the most stars when the game ends wins the game no matter how poorly you played the game. Oh, and don't forget they the shortest version of the game takes 45 minutes minimum. The longest version takes 3+ hours. Ridiculous and frustrating to no end. Its a game that takes a minimal of an hour to lose. No thank you! You should try Chef's Luv Shack, it's based on the same concept but you can actually win the mini-games once in a while.

review_headline: Learn, work up your callouses, and have some fun.
review_body: I am not a complete beginner, but I am just getting back into guitar with having taken a decade or two off.  LOL.  I play acoustic guitar, and at first the game had a hard time hearing it.  I think the game works a lot better for electric guitar, but it did work with my acoustic which is pretty impressive.  On to the pros...  1.  Really great for learning how to hold and pick a guitar for the easy lessons.  2.  Really great for creating the callouses needed for nice metal strings.  Plastic do NOT hurt as much.  Buy plastic, if you don't like pain.  You will still grow callouses, but it will take longer and be less painful.  For me I just can't stand the sound of plastics.  3.  There is a lot of fret work, which is great.  I have never done a lot of fret sliding or moving around, so this opened up a whole new aspect to playing.  4.  It allows you to play and practice until you are satisfied with how well you did on a song.  And you can even go and practice them again after you have moved past them.  5.  There are a lot of songs from a lot of different genres.  Something for everyone.  6.  It is encouraging to play something that sounds like a song the very first song.  7.  If you don't like the game option, you can just practice songs in different ways in the song section.  The combos (of single chord and chords is great, if you suck at switching from picking to strumming like I do.)  8.  Teaches a variety of techniques and structure which is great.  9.  I actually like that there is almost no game play involved.  It is fun and encouraging, but I would NOT call this a game.  10.  I think this is great for beginners and even intermediates or getting reaquainted with the guitar.    Now the cons:  1.  I have yet to experience the lags that some are talking about, but I think it gets worse as the songs progress.  2.  They do not teach chords at all.  I know them pretty well, so this is less of an issue to me, but for beginners learning the chords is VITAL!  3.  They could at least throw some tabs in there.  That would increase people's knowledge and at least open up tabs to players.  4.  In the early songs I wish they would have you switch up the fingers you were using to hold the strings with, so you would get finger work lessons, and for metal string players like myself, you could play for longer than an hour at a time.  5.  They also don't penalize for not placing your finger close to the fret.  You can play horrible notes and still get credit for them.  I know this is picky, but I think finger work should be meticulous.  Perhaps as the 'game' progresses there will a higher standard, but I doubt it.  6.  They are pretty lenient with timing, as long as you pick or strum ahead, and it is still reverberating.  7.  Part of me wishes they wouldn't allow you to move onto the next song until you reach a certain percentage.  I am pretty meticulous, but it would let me move on when I was at 54% which is ridiculous in my opinion.  8.  I wish they wouldn't make me re-tune for each song.  9.  A game improvement would be to make someone at first tune to a tone and not just to a gauge.  You wouldn't be able to move on until you were in tune.  10.  Another game feature would be to allow you to slow down the song for the first and second run through, so you would get to know the notes and changes ahead of time.  Some of the shifts happen pretty fast for the first time through and since they change it up from time to time it would be nice to know ahead of time.  Overall i would say this is fantastic and encouraging, but as everyone else has said guitar lessons are a must and this is not a game so much as a learning tool.

product_title: SteelSeries Spectrum 4xB Gaming Headset for Xbox 360 (White)
review_body:
I already own an [[ASIN:B004EDSBYQ Xbox 360 Sharkoon X-Tatic SX Stereo Gaming Headset]], so when I got the opportunity to review the 4xB I couldn't pass it up, as it would allow my girlfriend and I to have our late-night gaming sessions without disturbing anyone else.

I thought the Sharkoon had a lot of cables, but this one is even worse. The Sharkoon can be used without the mic cable being plugged in to save some cord, but that's not the case here. The 4xB headset has a mic cable and a headphone cable coming out of it. These plug into a piece that doesn't *quite* fit into the controller. Then, a thick cable runs out of this piece, one end of which runs into a USB port for power and another end into a jack, which then plugs into an adaptor, whose other end is the white and red audio plugs that go between your 360's jacks and the inputs on your television. The headphone cable coming out of the headset itself technically could work on its own, but the cord length is designed to go from your head to the controller and is just too short to go to the TV on its own without an extension. So, resign yourself to a lot of cable.

Now, that in and of itself would not be so bad, but the bad connection I had with the controller got me lots of crackling. Other users have said that trying to force the piece in has broken their controller's port, so I'm not willing to risk that. I did get it to fit so that it wouldn't crackle after a few tries. Once I solved that, though, I noticed the low hum that budget-level headsets like this often have - it's low enough that you don't hear it if any sound is going, but it's noticable when you're on the dashboard or in a quiet space in your game.

The retractable mic is a nice feature, though I had some issues getting it in and out easily. The headset isn't uncomfortable, but I like the feel of the Sharkoon better.

All in all, it's a decent set of headphones, but it's not the best, and not the easiest to use. They'll work, but there are better options out there.r options out there.

I would like to begin my review by stating that I'm a gamer. I play PC games, console exclusive games, and portable games. I treat all platforms equally and only judge the content. In addition, I'm fortunate enough to have been alive and well pre, during, and post the golden age of gaming.

Visuals:

review_headline: Orcs and Trolls and Uruk-hai.....Oh My!!
review_body:
I just finished my first play-through last night and I have to say that LOTR - War in the North delivered a very exciting and satisfying gaming experience (although I do wish it could have been longer).

There have been some negative comments regarding the linear game progression as well as not having a deep RPG experience. While true, I actually found this to be a refreshing departure from the RPG's that I usually play. War in the North is focused heavily on action, with less attention paid to side quests, party management, and character interaction (there are some of these elements, but not nearly as prominent as classic RPG's). The story develops at a fast pace and to accomplish your goal you have to hit often and hit hard.

The graphics and visuals are excellent. The developers did a fantastic job with the environment, it really has a Lord of the Rings feel to it (visiting Rivendell was awesome...the same overall look as the movie). The character graphics are top notch as well. Trolls abound in this game, and they look just as they should....I swear, I could almost smell their hot, fetid breath as they tried to pulverize me into the dirt!

In addition, this game delivers a fun and exciting combat system. As a Ranger (my first play-through), you have the ability to use a bow as well as a two handed weapon or dual wield. Switching between ranged and melee weapons is very easy. Fighting in melee is visceral and fast-paced. The combat is very fluid, with the ability to dive and roll, relentlessly attacking from all sides, from one enemy to the next. As you chain together attacks and perform critical hits, you enter hero mode which deals more damage and gains more experience the longer you can keep attacking (this leads to some very exciting fight sequences).

The fighting is graphic and intense, with the ability to sever your opponent's limbs or head with a final blow that is very realistic and satisfying. Believe me, diving from one enemy to the next, raining down blow after blow, and severing limbs left and right is not something I will soon tire of (hey, what can I say...it's me or them, and this is war after all). The graphics hold up throughout combat...for example, after severing an orc's leg, he falls lopsidedly to the ground clutching his stump in agony. I never found the fighting to be repetitive or boring. With weapon skills, standard attacks and heavy blows, you can become a powerful force of destruction.

The inventory and leveling system is well balanced and fit in with the scope of the rest of the game. Set items were implemented particularly well. Bonuses are gained based on how many pieces you are wearing, so you don't need to find the whole set to see a boost in stats. I was able to attain 5 items of a six item set and it substantially boosted my dexterity, damage, and armor.

All in all, I had a lot of fun playing this game. I do wish it was longer, but I will enjoy continuing with the Ranger on the Heroic difficulty, and look forward to checking out the other characters as well as co-op. The game cetainly has some age on it but it's still a great game.

It's no run and gun shooter to be certain and is quite challenging. The graphics are acceptable to good depending on your anality about the issue. These days they're pretty dated but the quality is there which is what matters and the gameplay is so good that the graphics definitely take a back seat. The game can be run on very high settings with even the most mediocre of systems. That in itself is a big plus.

It has a simplified mission editor as well that allows you to not create maps but to choose existing maps and put in as many baddies as you want, adjust their skill levels, weapons, etc... You can add in numbers of civilians and adjust their demeanor as well... You can determine primary and secondary objectives... All this gives the game substantially high replayability.

About the only problem I have with this game is with the AI pathfinding and your squadmates occasional absolute refusal to get the hell out of your way. This wouldn't be so bad if they didn't insist that you get out of there's even when you aren't blocking them. The pathfinding is rarely an issue but when you're dealing with unknown doors and hallways you want your squadmates to take the most obviously safe route to their destination. This isn't always what they do and sometimes going the stupid route gets them dead.

At any rate, Amazon has already laid out a fair description of the details of the game so there's really no point in going into much of that. Suffice it to say that even in 2012 this game is very definitely worth having. There's not another one like it and nothing similar appears to be on the horizon. I recommend you snatch it up while you still can.
