I'm writing this review for the gamers that are still trying to decide whether or not to buy this game.  Here's the short answer; Rent it or wait until it hits $30 NEW.    Mini Review (Short and Fun Just like the Game-lol):    The Story (wait Bulletstorm has a story?)  The story is set in the future and the character you play is a guy named Grayson Hunt.  He's a mixture of Marcus from Gears, Russell Crowe in Gladiator, and a drunken' swearing Uncle.  If you so much as tripped over a FPS (First Person Shooter) you'll know the story cuz there all the same: You're a badass, who's got a chip on his shoulder, and someone backstabbed you so now you have to go get some revenge.  You go from point A to point B like any other FPS, but in this game you're doing it in style. I did laugh occasionally thru ought the story mode but I basically skipped most of the cut scenes toward the end (which is cool that Epic allowed the player to do that).  Oh yeah and there's a lot of swearing ....a lot.    Graphics/Sound  If you have surround sound this game kicks.  I also can't say enough about the graphics. They're no Crysis 2, but they sure look good.  Nuff said.    Gameplay  Let me start out by saying just get thru the first Two Chapters.  The rest of the game (7 Chapters overall) is a blast.  By Chapter 4 you're able to start really leveling up (more guns and add ons) and experiencing what the game really has to offer.     This game was made buy Epic (Unreal and Gears of Wars games) so they know what there doing.  The controls are tight and fluid. Like I said before if you've played a FPS before you'll feel right at home.  Bulletstorm's gimmick is something called the \\"Leash\\".  You hit one of the thumper buttons and it brings your enemies to you.  Which from there you can kick that enemy back into walls, kick'em and shoot'em, or just blast'em right there.  This gives you kill points or kill/style points. The crazier your moves the more points you get.  This overall is fun and cool butit does get stale only because of the game's limit of understanding of skill points.  What I mean is I \\"Leashed\\" an enemy, kicked him up in the air, shot him in the head and a guy right behind him all at the same time and got 250 pts.  It's hard to explain but if you saw it you'd be like wait he did that, and he got the minimum? What gives?    Replay Value  Online play has horde mode (fight swarms of enemies with friends/online players), and Echo's mode (Revisit any chapter and try to get a higher score).      Bottom Line (3 our of 5)  It was a simple, fun, funny experience, just short on replay value.  Even though this game isn't selling that well I hope Epic decides to make another one.    No Online Multiplayer ( Team Deathmatch) kills buying this game for $60 for me.  If you feel the same rent the game (to just play the story mode) or like I said buy it for $30 NEW.  If you rent the game or buy it used ...you have to spend $10 online to unlock Echos Mode or the online horde mode (which isn't worth it).

Portal 2 plays very much like the original Portal with a few exceptions. I won't go too much into gameplay because the game really does feel very, very similar to the original, so I'll just lay down some of the differences I've perceived.    *) Graphics and art. Portal 2's art style is different. Aperture Laboratories is in ruins, and Portal 2 puts you right into the heart of it. As a consequence, Portal 2 takes you all over the Aperture facility. You are not confined to specific test chambers like you were in Portal. The art style in Portal 2 seems, on account, more realistic than Portal. Lots of improvements in the small details. And, with respect to graphics, Portal 2 looks much smoother than Portal. Graphics improvements all around, from quality to performance.    *) Humor. In my opinion, Portal 2 falls short of its predecessor in this department. This was expected. The running joke in Portal meshed well with the surprise in the ending credits to produce one of the most memorable experiences I've ever seen in a game. GLaDOS has not lost her wit in Portal 2, but, if you've played Portal, all the cards are on the table from the start of the game.    *) Mystery. Portal was a curious beast. You woke up in a clearly dysfunctional laboratory, having no idea who you are or where you are, what you're supposed to do, or who that odd woman on the radio is. Portal 2 does not feature this intrigue. It's a puzzle game, first to last, and though some of the environments in Portal 2 do seem spooky, the feel is more reminiscent of a first-person zombie shooter, only without the zombies. Urrrrghhhh.    *) Puzzles! Portal 2 has some far more involved puzzles over Portal, mostly on account of added toys for you to play with. Since the Portal series is, from A to Z, a set of puzzle games, this aspect is immensely important. Portal 2 does not disappoint with the ingenuity of its puzzles. I will say that, for me, the puzzles in Portal 2, though more numerous and interesting than thepuzzles from Portal, are easier to figure out than they were in Portal. I'm not sure, though, if they're actually easier or if I just know what to look for from playing the original. Regardless, the puzzles are just more fun to play, what with the super speed slime and jump launchers.    *) Content. This game has more puzzles than Portal, but I'm not convinced it has more content. Some of the puzzles in Portal took me hours to figure out, and I died many times. In Portal 2, I died once, and that was because I jumped in water just to see if I could swim. (I was convinced at that point it was impossible to die in the game unless you were playing with a blindfold.) The game took me about six hours, start to finish. Don't get me wrong, those six hours were full of fun and butterflies and rainbows, but retail price for the game is $50. There is not $50 worth of content here. Period. After having experienced it, I would not buy the game again for more than $20. Your mileage may vary.    Overall, Portal 2 is a solid sequel to the original game. It's got it where it counts (the puzzles) and is certainly a good game, but it's burdened by a high price point and by the expectations raised by its predecessor. Multiplayer capability is the only aspect of this game that comes anywhere close to justifying the $50 price point, but I haven't tried it yet as I don't expect it to be challenging. (How hard can a puzzle be, where two average gamers who aren't communicating with voice chat should be able to solve it?) I give the game four stars in spite of its high price because the price will go down with time and because, ignoring the price, the game is a good game. While it has no laugh-out-loud end-game like Portal had, the voiceovers and puzzle elements will keep you chuckling and guessing every step of the way through Aperture Labs. Definitely a game worth playing.

review_headline: Red Faction Returns to its Roots...
review_body:
Red Faction Guerrilla was a big step in the evolution of the franchise... going from FPS to a more Sandbox style game. Despite its success at drawing in a new crowd of fans for the franchise, Red Faction Armageddon takes a step backwards to return to its roots. In doing so this may alienate new fans of the franchise and Sandbox style, but may appeal more to the traditional FPS gamer.

GAMEPLAY
Armageddon changes it up from Guerrilla by going with a over the shoulder Shooter style vs the Sandbox element the previous title had. Instead of running missions and driving around to pick up objectives you are given a clear cut path to travel. Armed with a variety of weapons you find and can upgrade along the way, you will shoot, destroy and rebuild (only to blow it up again!) your way through the campaign. Armageddon has a linear feel tot he game and does little to change that feeling up. While there are sometimes two paths you can take, it always leads you to the same place and puts you through similar trials(or just leads to a secret). Despite being linear with little in the ways of exploration, the devastation this game brings is very enjoyable. On top of your regular arsenal of weapons you have perhaps my second favorite weapon in the game.. the magnet gun (as seen in the demo). This gun is just pro at causing mass devastation and squishing enemies between scrap. Acquisition of your weapons like most shooters occurs linearly through gameplay. Upgrades are tied to completion percentage to prevent you from becoming to overpowered.

Overall the gameplay is a lot of fun.. Linear yes.. but very entertaining as the game almost taunts you to kill as stylishly and destructive as you can. There is plenty to destroy, tons of enemies to have your way with so in the end you will be left satisfied.

GRAPHICS
The graphics here are not anything mind blowing.. but they are very nice. The real meat and potatoes here is the physics. While not perfect the destructive and rebuilding elements of the game is what really sells the effects. There are some cases where objects are rigid and do not bend nor break but for the most part, once you see your first large building almost implode on itself you'll be in awe.

SOUND/STORY
Sound effects are fairly solid. Weapons have a fair feel and sound to them but the voice acting is a bit weak in my book. Not bad just could of been better I think. Perhaps a lot of that has to do with the storyline. It is very generic almost existing to take you from A to B, but I don't think people tune into Red Faction to get drama so as long as there is reason behind your actions I am fine with it. Besides, a reason to go from A to B means more stuff to blow up!

REPLAY/LENGTH
Replay value I think is decent. There are some online modes included with the game the main one being infestation mode. Basically survival mode as you try to survive waves of mobs while using the environment to your advantage and mix in some objectives. There also is a mode where you try to rack up as much damage as possible within a set time(Ruin Mode), but I have not checked it out yet honestly. The campaign itself is short.. You can probably breeze through it in 5-7 hours if you just Rambo through BUT there is a plus here.. Game plus mode that is! Once the game is completed you can re-start the campaign with all your existing stuff to further upgrade gear or just see how much more chaos you can cause.

OVERALL 81% ... B-
Red Faction Armageddon is not a bad game by any means. It took a few steps back from the previous title, but returned to its roots with gameplay in doing so. Storyline and Sandbox took a back seat to Linear progression and in your face action. This might work for some and not for others. With that said RF: Armageddon is a game one really needs to play to see if they enjoy it. If you are a fan of the originals you will feel athome with this title. If you are more into sandbox style this game might upset you with its linear, closed-in feel. With that said I give the game an 81%.. a solid game but not for everyone.

**NOTE: If you are on the boarder about the game, check out the demo to see if you like the feel of the game. It does a fair job giving you a taste of the arsenal you will have and destructive capabilities.

**NOTE: This game has perhaps the best weapon to date... Mr. Toots. Once you unlock Mr. Toots you won't stop laughing.me might upset you with its linear, closed-in feel. With that said I give the game an 81%.. a solid game but not for everyone. **NOTE: If you are on the boarder about the game, check out the demo to see if you like the feel of the game. It does a fair job giving you a taste of the arsenal you will have and destructive capabilities. **NOTE: This game has perhaps the best weapon to date... Mr. Toots. review_headline: That Nintendo Magic, and how I lost 10lbs in 1 month
review_body: I'm sure the other 260 reviewers talked about the 3d effects to death already. I'll just add i like the 3d and prefer it on than off.  But I am still waiting for a future game to really take advantage of it. I know it can be done because the menu screens really pop crisply and sometimes in the launch games it really is cool.  But the extras on the system really add value and that is what my review will be about.    I bought my system on release day and actually went to the midnight pick up line. (I've never done that before... neat)   I got Pilot Wings and Ghost Recon 3ds with my system.  Both are excellent games and tons of fun.    One of my favorite features is the built in step counter. I didn't even realize i would enjoy this feature and didn't bother looking at it until I went on a 4 day trip to New York City a week after i got the 3ds.  I realized I was walking a lot in that humongous city and had my 3ds with me so I took a peek.  I was walking 16,000 steps a day!! I looked online and saw that average Adult male should be walking 10,000 steps a day.  Then I looked back at the previous week in which I only did normal daily routine activities.  I barely got over 1500 steps a day.  And on 2 days < 1000 steps.  (i am a master at planning my bus route so i can jump on transfers to avoid walking). Now my interest was peaked, this step counter adds a gaming element to my daily life. Suddenly I wasn't so eager to hop on the transfer, and would rather walk the extra distance.  Or if the bus wasn't arriving for another 10 minutes, I would walk to the next stop or 2. Just by changing little things, I now do a minimum 5000 - 8000 steps a day.  But that is not the only change, now I also watch my portions on my free lunches at work, and cut down on free snacks at work.  Plus all this health slant has also made me stick to my daily exercise.  Net result I have lost 10lbs and feel much better now than I have in 2 years.     To take the idea of adding game elements into dailylife further, there is the street pass feature which is delightful.  You start off with an empty plaza with just you in it.  Then at the end of the day, you open up your Mii Plaza and see who you might have passed.  If you pass someone regularly, you can set up a special greeting they will get next time.  Its totally non intrusive, and its just neat to collect all these different Miis'.  I didn't even discover this feature until a few days ago.  But now I eagerly open up the app at the end of every day and see who I've collected.    There also is some decent stats recorded for your game playing in the activity log. So far I have played Pilot Wings 35 times (15 min avg session) , and Ghost recon 22 times (41 min avg session), and have taken 190,000 steps (86 miles) since I got my 3ds exactly 1 month ago! (yes i am obsessive enough to measure how many steps in a mile, i measured multiple routes and compared to google maps and just took the average about 2200 steps per mile)    In short, Nintendo has done it again. They just know how to make seemingly silly/boring features ridiculously fun.  I love Nintendo (the company, the bastard stock is another story grrrr).    Now I know that theres thousands of games cheaper and free on the iPhone.  I know there are step counter apps.  And location aware apps.  And now I carry 3 (I just got a kindle ...love) devices around instead of just one.  You smart asses.  I have an iPhone 4 and download a ton of games and apps I never play or play once never to look at them again. I used to think like that, why would i need a ds or kindle when my super magic infinity device is so sleek and cool?      I dunno why but playing games on a handheld Nintendo system is just more inherently fun.  Maybe cause i grew up in the 80s and have been deeply imprinted. I had the original gameboy and played that to death.  And kindle, i can't describe what a difference it is to read off a kindle vs the iphone or that stupid iPad (had one for 3 weeks thensold it).  Its smooth like butter for your eyes.

review_headline: Good game overall, but it needs some work (focus on campaign)
review_body: First of all, I purchased the PS3 version from walmart.com in order to get the spec-ops dlc (which I can't use until May 31 [maybe...]).      Story:  Overall decent, but there are some plot holes.   The island is supposed to be self-sustaining, but the chief complaint from the story is lack of water (after 20 years of \\"isolation\\") so that it is rationed.  You can take either sides of the story with the rebels or the security forces.  Characters have little depth and I don't have any connection with any of them (I tried figuring out the names for my teammates besides \\"you\\").  It seems that they are there as fillers between battles.      Gameplay:  I found it to be challenging and fun, but there are a few points that the game needs to address.  First, having a buff ability to your character is fine but when you add it to the same button as 'reload' it screws up the gameplay (and there is no way to separate reload from the interact/buff button).  I find myself ducking behind a crate to reload, and I suddenly run out in the crossfire in order to buff a teammate and die.  I find it hilarious that my character runs faster to buff a teammate rather doing a regular sprint across the battlefield.  The SMART system only works for a few points in the battle field.    Graphics:  Graphics are really good, but it tends to slow down in particular parts of the game (mainly story).  Otherwise, the 8 levels (6 main levels and 2 'what-if' levels for each side, so 16 total) are well thought out but I have yet to see the multiplayer as of yet.    Music:  Music is good and it fits with game, but it is not remarkable (ie same style of music for both sides).    Weapons:  You can get all of the guns in campaign mode.  In order to unlock the guns and attachments, you have to complete the \\"challenge\\" portion of the game.  It is a separate portion that is more of a training arena so that you can get some familiarity of the gameplay.  There are four key challenges that include:  follow the objective (go through a list of objectives successfully), parkour course (SMART system basics), escort (getting a robot from point A to B), and tower security (control a tower and handle enemies from multiple angles).     ---The 14 primary weapons (for medium build) have a range of attachments from 2-4 attachments (front, top[sights], bottom [grip], and magazine.  The two-three attachment weapons are mainly 2 rifles (Everett rifle and the Dragonov rifle) and one shotgun (Messington shotgun).  The most you can attach is four are sub-machine guns and assault rifles.  There are 19 primary guns (including chain and light machine guns) for heavy builds, while there is only 7 primary guns (mainly assault rifles or SMG) for light builds.    ---The 9 secondary weapons (for medium builds) also range from 2-4 attachments.  You can find the rifles with sniper scope attachments (only 2 scopes).  The rest are pistols or SMG's.  The heavy builds have an additional 19 guns (assault rifles, grenade launchers, etc.) while the light builds have 5 guns (all pistols).    ---Factors in gun choice:  damage, range, rate of fire, accuracy, stability (kick), reload speed, equip speed (transition speed between two weapons), and ammo clip.    Creating your character:  I liked the idea that range of ethnicity that you can choose in the game.  You choose a specific face, voice, and skin tone first then you work with build, tattoos, etc.  You keep this keystone figure, but you can create more characters.  You are only allowed to adjust the face, skin tone, tattoos, etc. at the beginning of the game or creating a new character.  The only way to get more options and choices (clothes, hairstyles, gear, etc.) is to gain a higher experience by either playing the campaign or multiplayer mode.  Build can be changed before each mission with advantages/disadvantages for each.  Medium is the standard you start out with and eventually you will unlock heavy and light builds.  The heavy builds have higher health, but are slow and are limited in parkour movements.  The light builds have extended parkour movements and are faster, but have smaller health.  The guns choices are also determined by the build you choose.  I still think that people will never notice any gun skins in the game (the main reason why I didn't choose Gamestop or Best-Buy pre-orders).     The four jobs:  ---Soldier:  Any explosives are this jobs primary responsibility.  Key buff is to resupply your teammates with bullets (yes, he technically has unlimited ammunition for a little while).  Other attributes include enhancing explosives or increasing his defense or health, and stealing supplies from opponents.    ---Medic:  The healer of the group.   Once you are shot down, you have a chance to be brought back into play by the medic.  You only \\"die\\" when the opponent actually finishes you off when you are on the ground.  Key abilities mainly improve health, adding adrenaline/metabolism buffs (increased stamina/regeneration), auto-regeneration, and having the \\"Lazarus bomb\\" (all teammates are healed within blast radius).    ---Engineer:  Mainly fixes, repairs, or creates multiple tools and weapons for the team to use.  I used this character the most since he can build shortcuts/blockades, plant invisible mines, build gun turrets (there are 3 types), destroy hacking attempts or explosives, giving teammates kevlar vests, and can enhance the weaponry of his team.    ---Operative (aka Hacker):  Mainly the scout/spy of the team.  He can infiltrate the enemy (actually puts on a dead enemy's clothes to look like them), can also hack into a downed enemy's equipment to find the opponent's locations for your teammates, locates explosives (including mines), hack into systems, make it harder for the enemy to get into particular systems, can hack into enemy turrets, and can control turrets from a distance.    Main complaints:    -The front attachments (silencer/brake muzzles) do little to enhance your gun.  The enemies isstill able to hunt you down with the silencer (firing gives away your location if enemies are nearby), and the brake muzzles do little to enhance accuracy unless your strafe firing.  Even the game states that the multiple brake muzzles have little difference to the others and are \\"mainly cosmetic\\" or how you look when firing.    -They should have added women as particular members of your team or as character options.    -There is minimal room for sniping opponents since you can only go as far as kneeling (rather than prone).     -The melee button is mainly to stun rather than kill opponents, but they recover immediately when I knock them down (they can still shoot at you when they are down).    -I created additional characters and choosing different voices for each, but I found out that the first voice I chose ended being the voice for all the additional characters.    -The computer bots on your team cannot follow objectives that will result you doing ALL the objectives yourself to accomplish each mission.    Overall:  The game has definite replay potential, but the story could have been enhanced even further.  The story cut scenes are your team complaining about the opponents before EACH battle.  The SMART system also has potential, but it doesn't really enhance the battle in the game that much (it is faster to go around a crate rather than jump/slide on top of it). In 2007 a small Eastern European game developer (CD PROJEKT)...teaches BIOWARE how to use their own Aurora engine. The original [[ASIN:B003KTMW9K Witcher]] was the game that [[ASIN:B003P9WNBM Neverwinter Nights]] had promised to be. Two years later BIOWARE picks up the glove and comes back with a strong response, the masterpiece [[ASIN:B0042RUDNG Dragon Age: Origins]]. Unfortunately, its 2011 sequel does not live up to expectations. And this is all the opening the perfect sequel needed to come in and, once more, steal the show.

THIS IS HOW TO MAKE A cRPG SEQUEL!
Although there may be Xbox and PS3 versions of this game later on, this is a game designed from start to finish for the PC. In an age when 5-6 years old consoles set the standard this is very important. From the brand new engine to the very last script line, everything that could be worked on was and everything that could be improved shows improvement. The story is now even deeper; the graphics are several notches higher; character development has been both streamlined and more balanced; equipping Geralt is now more detailed whereas loot is abundant.
It is possible (although not necessary) to import your character from the first WITCHER. If, like me, you liked the original game, you will simply love the sequel.

LOOK AT THE SKY: IT IS THE WITCHING HOUR - EVERY HOUR!
The graphics are simply A-MA-ZING! I like the way the rock formations catch the moving shadows and how the wind stirs up dust. I like the subtle movement of the grass and the exploding colors of the wild flowers. I like the textures of the clothes, the shine of the armor and the glint of the swords. I like the way the sun gets in your eyes and the way rays of light play with the tree foliage.
What is also important, these graphics and dynamic lighting are achieved even on medium-built systems (Minimum specs: Intel Core 2 Duo 2.2GHz/AMD 2.5GHz, nVidia 8800/ATI 3850, 1GB of RAM for WinXP/ 2GB for WinVISTA&7).
Even more impressively, the game is set in a day/night cycle, and this is reflected not only on the levels of ambient light but also on the activities of the surrounding world.

THE WORLD AROUND YOU COMES TRULY ALIVE
Remember how in most RolePlaying games approaching a Non-Playing Character (NPC) usually means he or she would utter any one of a small number of preset phrases? After a while, you have heard them all and it got very predictable. Well, prepare to be surprised. Again and again.
This is a world you will truly be immersed into. A world that wakes up, goes to work, gossips, bickers and barters, and unwinds in the tavern. Walk the same streets at night and they are eerily empty. And that is without taking into account the ever changing weather!
The immersion is so total for yet two other reasons: not only is the world fully open from the very beginning (no blocked areas or closed bridges!) but there are no loading delays between areas (only between chapters).

THE LIFE OF A WITCHER IS NEVER BORING
Geralt is a real warlock, combining a mix of sword fighting with potions and spells. These are the three main character developing trees, Swordmaster, Alchemist or Mage. Sword moves, potion ingredients and spells can be combined - and all choices are meticulously balanced.
With the original WITCHER it took me a while to master the timed sword-strokes - but it was really satisfying after that. In the sequel, sword-fighting has been simplified to the classic mod - and that is one of the gripes I have with this game. The other is the short dialogue options. I like my cRPGs wordy.
Now, the story is far from being linear. Choices matter and choosing a path will bifurcate the story, most of the times irrevocably. And the story in WITCHER 2 is as important as the fighting.
What I also appreciated was the return of consequences. Those of you who have played BALDUR's GATE Saga know that bashing or picking the lock of a chest was a punishable offense if anyone saw you. In contrast, in DA-O you could rob the town blind and (quite unrealistically) the NPCs could not care less. Well, in this game, your character better behave or face the ever vigilant guards.

ADJUST TO YOUR ACCEPTABLE LEVEL OF BINDING
Most retail versions of the game come with a simple disc-check, implemented by SecuROM. If you own FALLOUT 3, for example, you have experienced the same thing. Compared to the customer-abusing schemes out there (UBISOFT's and 2K GAMES' ears should be burning at this point) I find this solution not ideal but palatable. And yet it gets better: if you are objecting even to this mild version of SecuROM, the developers made sure to also release the (digital) GOG version of the game which is DRM-free. Just for giving us this option, THE WITCHER 2 gets full marks in my books!

A FINAL SPELL
I have only praises for this magnificent sequel to a great game. It was one of the rare cases when I pre-ordered a game before I knew anything about it and was rewarded with a game that exceeded my highest expectations. I do have some advice for the game developers though.
First, keep showing the same respect to your customers and you will see that gamers know how to repay this with equal respect and loyalty. And finally, when the mega-publishers show up at your door with their mesmerizing bags of money, try to remember what happened to so many great game developing groups in the past that did not resist to temptation.

product_title: Snakebyte Final Fantasy XIV PC Controller (SB 000009)
review_headline: Good controller for a good price.
review_body:
As an avid gamer, two qualities are most important to me in a controller: Comfort and compatibility.

I already own a Logitech Dual Action USB controller. It served its purpose, and was also roughly the same shape as the Sony PlayStation controller. However, I felt that the Logitech was a bit bulky and uncomfortable when used for long periods of time. Additionally, the control sticks were in a somewhat bizarre square base (instead of the circular one used by Sony), and this led to problems getting it to respond properly in certain diagonal directions. At any rate, I chose to shop around for a new controller.

I stumbled upon this one and was drawn to it because of the Final Fantasy connection. While I have steadfastly ignored the series' online forays, the fact that this controller was licensed by Square Enix caught my eye and I took a chance and ordered it to use with my other games.

This controller is much thinner and more angular than the original Sony controller, but its slim design fits in the hand very well. After hours of continuous play it felt just as comfortable as when I began. While people in other reviews have mentioned the light weight of the controller as a negative, I find that it's one of my favourite attributes. Despite its weight, it still feels well put together. The buttons, joypad, and control sticks are all responsive and comfortable to use. I would say it actually feels nicer than most of the other PC controllers I've tried. I wouldn't recommend hurling it against a wall or tossing it out a window, but it's not nearly as fragile-feeling as some people are suggesting. I've accidentally dropped it a few times while packing to move and it still works perfectly.

The vibration is a little weak, if that's something that's a concern for you. I would say it's something like a console controller set on the lighter vibration setting. It's not going to shake you to the bone, but you can definitelyfeel it. If heavy vibrations aren't important to you, this controller might be a good choice (I actually didn't realize it supported vibration until I received it - it was a pleasant surprise for the price).

The compatibility with this controller is great. It worked plug-and-play with both my Linux and Windows machines. Individual games or emulators might require a moment or two of configuration to meet your individual preferences, but in my case it worked perfectly right out of the box.

To summarize, if you want a heavy controller with strong vibration, get a USB adapter for a console controller and find out how to get it to work on your system. If you want a lightweight, comfortable controller that works without a hassle, pick this one up. It's well worth the low price.

review_headline: Easily one of the best games ever!
review_body: Obviously this game has plenty of reviews, but I felt like throwing my opinion in. I honestly did not find the first Uncharted all that fun. I have always loved any game naughty dog had ever made and once I finally got around to owning the original Uncharted on the PS3 I was super excited. Unfortunately, I don't know if it was the point in time I was playing the game or what but I found it to be a little frustrating. I have no issues with difficult games and quite like a challenge, but with the original Uncharted it felt like they intentionally forced you to die sometimes as there was really no way to not die in certain sequences and I found that annoying. I also found the gun fights to be pretty repetitive overall. With that said, I finally went back and finished the original Uncharted (I left off at like 75% completion 8 months ago). I still found it just as annoying in certain ways, but once i beat it I decided I wanted to give the second game a chance. Just to be clear, I loved the characters, graphics, audio, voice acting, cut scenes, etc of the first one, just found the fighting a little annoying.     I was reluctant to buy the second game as I had read not much changed in those regards...honestly the sequel is AMAZING. This game simply takes every single thing that was great about the first game and builds upon it so much it's absolutely ridiculous. I have had NO frustrations with the sequel at all. I've found the fighting to be much more varied which is great. You have a lot more options as to how to approach enemies this time around. Also, I don't know what it is about this game but it just gets everything right. I simply find myself happy while playing this game. There are so many little details and obviously major ones that just make this game a masterpeice. Anyway this might not be the most coherent review at the moment (quite tired from work) I just wanted to let anyone know...even if you had some problems with the first game PLEASE buy this game. review_headline: Hey look, it's the DS version with Yoshi and some new costumes.
review_body:
I didn't think very highly of New Super Mario Bros for DS. It wasn't a bad game, but after years and years of waiting for a new classic platformer with the plumber that started it all, it sure as heck wasn't memorable. Levels weren't challenging, 'hidden' coins were always easily obtainable with platforms or ledges that looked like they didn't belong where they were, and the game just felt rushed. But many people didn't mind- they were too distracted with 'omg old skool mario!!!11' syndrome to notice that it had nothing on the NES classics, even the Doki Doki Panic sprite swap Super Mario Bros 2. What got me the most was that the power up items in New Super Mario Bros weren't very creative. You had a mini mushroom that made Mario tiny, and a rarely useful giant mushroom that'd let him smash his way through the level for a few seconds. 'hate to say it, but this Wii version isn't any better than the DS one.

Once again, Princess Peach is kidnapped by Bowser and his kids, the Koopalings, during a birthday party. As they take her, some of the presents open up, revealing new power ups that Mario can use. As usual, it's up to Mario to rescue her. You'll run, jump, shoot fireballs and...oh heck, you should all know the drill by now. Even younger gamers who didn't get to grow up with the old Mario games get the gist. New Super Mario Bros Wii keeps the tradition going with similar level design to the stages in Mario 3 and even Super Mario World. Yoshi returns as well, and up to 4 people can play at the same time, though you're better off not doing that unless you're just up for mindless fun. While there are a few new items, enemies and obstacles, there isn't a whole lot that feels new in this game, and that's my first big problem. The transition from each big Mario game was huge. The first game introduced us to the world of Mario, the second game was a rip-off of a lesser known Japanese game but still vastly different, Mario 3 started the world map trend and even let you store power ups for later use, and Super Mario World just plain made everything bigger and better. Here, everything's very basic and feels like a step down from the sequels. The new level obstacles weren't challenging at all, time was plentiful in every single level, 1 ups were given out they're going out of style, and it feels like this was made for someone who never played a game before.

Next, the new items. You have an ice flower, penguin suit and flying hat. The ice flower and penguin suit essentially have the same use- freezing enemies, who you can jump on for an extra boost, use as platforms when they float in water, or just pick up and throw at other enemies. But the penguin suit lets Mario slide super fast and swim better, similar to the frog suit from Mario 3. However, there aren't many times when the penguin suit is useful apart from freezing enemies. There aren't many water levels in the game and the slide attack isn't practical except in a select few stages where you have long platforms that make up most of the level. The flying hat is an ok idea, but pales in comparison to the raccoon leaf and super cape. To make Mario fly, you have to shake the Wii controller. Nope, you can't simply press a button- you have to shake. While Mario isn't restricted to flying just after running a short distance, you have to land before being able to fly again with the hat. Odd huh? What bothered me about flying in New Super Mario Bros is that where there were tons of bonus goodies in the sky in Mario 3 and Super Mario World, there's not much to explore in the skies here. Like I said, Yoshi's back, and I don't know why. He's only in a few stages, and doesn't bring anything to the game this time around. What's worse is that you can't keep him after beating a level- once you clear the stage with Yoshi, he's gone. Why???? My last main problem is the lack of challenge from the bosses. It's the same as it was in the old games: you jump on them 3 times, or shoot'em with enough fireballs, and they're out. Only Baby Bowser and the last boss have a slight twist, but even then, I got them both on the first try since their attack patterns were so slow. How is it that Baby Bowser in Yoshi's Island still gives me a little trouble now and then?

Multiplayer...ugh, the less said, the better. Many people abandon this after a few levels, and it's easy to see why. Players will constantly bump into eachother, knocking one another off ledges, into enemies or just to mess with them. It's fun to play this just to give your friends a hard time, but if you want to seriously beat levels with one or more people, that's probably where the only challenge in this game lies.

The game's graphics are good for what they are- an upgrade from the DS version. Some of the character models like Bowser look really good, and I wish we'd get this quality (or better) more often on the Wii. I never experienced any slowdown either, even when a lot of things were going on on-screen. Unfortunately, the music isn't memorable, and they stuck with the DS tunes from what I could tell. Aside from the bland track that plays in the first stage, I can't remember any other tracks, not even the ghost house or castle stages, which you'd think would have some effort put into. It really bugged me that they didn't give the characters any real lines either, instead sticking with Mario's now standard grunts ('ha-hah!' and 'oomph!'). Come on Nintendo, step it up for god's sake! Either put in some real dialogue or don't have any.

While all I do here is go off about how much I don't like the game, that's just coming from someone who grew up with the old Mario games as they came out over the years. For a younger gamer who hasn't gotten to play any of them, this will probably be a good, fun title, but I highly recommend the Mario All-Stars collection over this. review_headline: Great game, but a couple points of caution
review_body: TL;DR: play this game, don't get it from Amazon, EA's DRM alienates consumers    I need to start by saying that this is a great game. 99% of the people I know who have played it agree. Sure there are a few things that could have been tweaked, but I can't honestly tell anyone who loved KOTOR that they shouldn't pick this one up as well. That being said, I would NOT recommend buying Mass Effect from Amazon, as I've had a number of problems that I don't want others to have to go through. Mass Effect is NOT SOLD BY AMAZON, and while the seller has chosen a picture of the US edition of the game, THEY ARE SHIPPING THE UK EDITION, which doesn't work in the US. On top of that, there's no way to contact the seller, so all you can do is ship it back to Amazon and get a refund. On the plus side, I've met some really nice people with Amazon Customer Service, but I still don't have a working copy of Mass Effect. Great game, but I wish I could play it. If you want to know more about the game and why it's good, as well as why others disagree, the rest of this review focuses on EA and their DRM rather than the game itself.  I have beef with EA's SecuROM nonsense. I understand that they want to make sure that only people who have paid for the game are playing the game, but when you alienate your customers by only letting them install the game they paid for a certain number of times, that tends to degrade the overall experience of the game, and not because of content or plot. A lot of my friends, and myself as well, are very hands-on when it comes to our computers, and we like to modify them on a fairly regular basis. If each time we modify our computers counts as a de facto change in our system configuration which requires us to use another install of the 3 allotted, then we quickly end up with some rather expensive coasters for Mt. Dew, Dr Pepper, and Bawls. Not so much a critique of the game itself, but EA has really made some bad moves when it comes to endearing its PC gamer base. A more recent example would be how they are removing access to their games from anyone who bought them on Steam, which is why I'm trying to buy the disc in the first place. EA apparently has a way for more installs of the game to be permitted, which is nice but it's still a hassle that they are creating for their customers. I don't pirate games because 1) IT'S ILLEGAL and 2) I like supporting developers who make good products, but shenanigans like this have resulted in more than one thread on places like Reddit where I'm not sure that everyone shares my stance on not pirating things. DRM should protect your product and not infringe on the consumer's ability to enjoy it, thus helping to ensure that they would like to purchase your products in the future. SecuROM seems to fail on both ends by frustrating users and encouraging people to figure out ways around it, even if it's just so that they can play the game they paid for while not connected to the internet, which SecuROM does not allow.

Being a 26 year old man child, I can honestly say that I grew up playing Need For Speed.  I bought the game looking forward to the series return to their roots and I was completely and utterly disappointed.  This game had one huge flaw that I could not get past despite my best efforts.  That flaw, ladies and gentlemen, is the lack of a manual transmission option.  Honestly, the game is filled with all these awesome fast super cars and they are all AUTOMATICS!!!  Soooo, realistically the only buttons you push for the whole game is the \\"right trigger\\" to accelerate, the \\"left trigger\\" to brake and the \\"left joystick\\" to turn left and right (XBOX 360)?  You mean to tell me that with all the buttons available on the controller two more can't be mapped for up and down shifting?  I thought this was racing game!!!  I have never returned a game before finishing it until now.  I do not recommend this game to anyone.  Even if you an \\"automatic transmission\\" type of player I would not recommend this game based on the catch-up/yo-yo racing game play.  I have never seen a worse example of catch-up since Mario Kart 64.  I hate the fact that after driving flawlessly throughout the whole race you pass the guy in first and no matter how flawless/fast you drive that guy you passed is on your six like Oprah chasing baked ham.

product_title: Ear Force DSS 7.1 Channel Dolby Surround Sound Processor
review_body: I bought this a while back because I heard that it could be used with any stereo headset and provide a good 7.1 virtual surround sound which is something that my Razer Orca's were lacking. Once I plugged them into my PC I did notice a difference however, it was definitely not worth the $80 price tag that I paid. On top of that, hese do not include a Digital Audio cable and I was forced to pay an additional $25 to buy theirs from Amazon (only PC/PS3 users). I was able to hear sounds a lot better however, it is still very difficult to distinguish the direction of the sound in Call of Duty: Black Ops. In addition, there is also a very noticeable hissing/buzzing noise when it is quiet or I have no sound playing. You would be much better off in my opinion just to invest a little bit more and purchase a surround sound headset because this processor is overpriced for the slight difference it makes.

The PlayStation Move is amazing tech, especially at this price, but if you are running in expecting to be racing through the Apocalypse or shooting blue and orange coloured portals, then think again. product_title: Divinity II: The Dragon Knight Saga
review_headline: Remastered version turns mediocre into sleeper hit!
review_body: In january 2010, a game called Divinity 2: Ego Draconis was released. This game was met with very mixed reviews, partially because it was a buggy mess. The game was just completely unpolished, and obviously felt very rushed. Most serious reviewers who had given the game a chance said that the game had massive potential to be great. The core gameplay mechanics and exploration / story driven elements were perfectly integrated in this RPG, and if it had not been for failed execution, it would have been a hit of massive proportions.     The good people at larian / atlus realized that they had an amazing game in their hands, and that their initial rendition simple did not do it justice. And so came Divinity II, the dragon knight saga. This fully remastered version of Ego Draconis brings the polish that the initial release had lacked. In addition, they add an expansion to the game called \\"Flames of Vengeance\\", which expands on the initial game by a good 20-30 hours. The result is an adventure of epic proportions, and buyers should know this: you will not be able to put this game down. This is one of those games that simply engrosses you.

product_title: El Shaddai: Ascension of the Metatron
review_headline: A beauty that runs only skin deep.
review_body:
I was hyped when I saw the initial trailer for this game and was blown away by the crisp looking frame rate, art style and music. I'm a fan of games like okami, odinsphere and others that have their own unique flair and dare to stand out from the crowd with something new. El Shaddai, while beautiful, failed horribly to deliver on every other aspect. The story is there but not as fleshed out as it should have been and is non-sensical at times. Gameplay consists of one attack button, one jump button and block. At first I thought there were two jump/block buttons but they both essentially do the same thing with the one exception of the jump+guard/jump+attack button presses which still do little to add to the shallow and repetitive combat.

If you hated running through a corridor in Final fantasy 13 repeatedly and killing a small variation of enemies then you will HATE this game. I pushed myself onward until I beat the game telling myself maybe it will be different but it doesnt get any better. Each level consists of running through a linear pathway whether its 2D or 3D... killing enemies in an enclosed area...rinse/repeat until you encounter boss.

The music was my other gripe. I loved the music i saw in the trailer which is a single track on the game and then the rest seems pretty much like forgettable elevator music. I will say I've been spoiled by games like demon's souls that have musical scores that are equally as characteristic and layered as the game is... El Shadai's is ...just bland most the time.

I would like to end with the fact that this is just my opinion, some people I have seen on various message boards thoroughly enjoyed it, I didn't.
My advice to anyone even considering plunking down 60$ of their hard earned cash on this short and half baked game would be to download the demo first from PSN, Rent it or wait until the price drops.

I'm a big fan of detective games, but for some reason I was disappointed with my purchase. It's just dull; the cases become dull; the ending is dull. I only paid thirty bucks for this and I feel ripped off; if you have money to burn I would suggest 'Deadly Promonition', which is 10 bucks cheaper and a lot more fun.

I've been considering getting this game for some time, but I was unsure.  I bought it on sale recently, and it turned out to be one of the best games I have ever played.  It is definitely worth it even at full price, and you will be hard pressed to find a game that will give you more play time and enjoyment for your money.  Without completing anywhere near all of the side quests available, Origins and Origins: Awakening gave me a solid 72 hours of game play.  And that is just one character!  This game has great replay value, and you can easily milk hundreds of hours from it.    The game play is fantastic, and the world is huge and diverse, with very good voice acting and character writing, amazing stories, and satisfying reactions based on your choices.  If you love traditional RPGs, this game is for you.  But for a few bugs that are few and far between (and mostly inconsequential), this game is nearly perfect, and even though a couple of years old, it feels fresh and engaging.  The graphics are nothing overly special, but the game is relatively bugless, and feels great.  You won't find yourself lamenting your purchase.  The game also has a huge amount of mods available online to customize the game play.    Overall, this is a great game, and in my top ten games of all time.  If you are considering buying this, do it!  I don't regret it, and neither will you.

Great game.  Lots of fun.  Challenging puzzles, but not too challenging where you could get frustrated.  The co-op is really well made, and a lot of fun to play online with a friend, it's really cool.  Can't really say enough good things about this game, definitely worth picking up at this point.    Oh yeah, and you get a free copy on Steam too, just in case you wanted to play it on computer also.

It's early in my ownership of the game, but this is what I have so far. The dialogue in the standalone game has fallen greatly. They went from having pretty good voice acting to some rather uninspired interchange.

The graphics have a good deal of improvement, however, the game doesn't feel as smooth as the original.

Multi-player is really changed up with how stages and rules are set. You can choose from a free-for-all (no radar or lock-on) to a pair of team setups. The goals have expanded as well. The arenas are pretty good, some old, some new. And hopefully with the updates, the cheating will be minimal, ie no rapid fire rocket launchers. Speaking of which, in multiplayer, you need to earn a certain number of experience points in order to upgrade to better weapons (the rocket launcher is really up there), and now there is an option for improved body armor. Based on my experience last night, some people have already picked up some serious armor.

The play is very fun, the visuals are improved, but perhaps not as smooth, the music is good, the voice overs in the standalone game are dreadfully terrible and I don't particularly care for the calling cries of downed players either. Don't let the negativity of that make it sound like the game isn't great because overall, I really like this game so far.

review_headline: Probably as good as the Jasper model
review_body: This 4gb slim model of the xbox 360 does not have an HDD. I bought this model because I had an older HDD already and I just stick that HDD into the slim and it works well.     This 360 model is probably as good as the Jasper motherboard model. I had the very first 360 motherboard and that was really crapy. With every new 360 motherboard that came out, the 360 has less risks of overheating and/or red ringing (RROD). The slim is the newest and in theory is the best for NOT RROD. But, I would say the Jasper model has a fighting chance of beating it. It just depends on the user's own usage and maintenance.    Long and gone are the days of just using a system anywhere, anyhow, and anyway. Back then, I had systems that I can abuse and use like crap and they still work today. Now Microsoft and Sony both have made systems that are made for very light touch, light abuse, and light everything.     The first thing I like to say about this slim is the the placement or the set up of the console really matters. You can't just place this thing on the carpet. You can't place this thing in an entertainment center. You can't place it in a high cabinet. Honestly, the best place you want to put this thing is next to a window. How high up or low it is matter too. 3 or 4 inches away from the window is a good idea. Same for the high. You can put something underneath the system for this high.    These things are NOT durable. You want a light touch on these things.  During game play, you don't want to knock or tip this thing at all! Also, moving the console while it is off could be bad if there's a game inside the machine. Tapping, pounding, or smashing the machine would cause it to go bad quick! One fall from 1 or 2 feet would probably K.O. the thing! lol Older systems would probably take the hit and survive, but this thing; nope. If it does, it probably wouldn't last long without you seeing some problems with it.     Cleaning the machine is a good idea. Computer experts know that dust kills electronics and the 360 is known for overheating and dust would do that. I recommend getting a dust buster and blowing out the dust inside from time to time. With older system, you would never had to do this, but with these new babies, you will learn to do it. Some people like to vacuum it out and you can if you want too.      The overheating can still happen with a slim model. If you don't ever want to see that happen, you will to do some things. One thing you can do is to place your console horizontally. Heat can get out easier if you let it be in this position and the fan will blow it up. If you play the system vertically, you will see that a main air vent is now blocked. You really want air to get in the system so that it can cool it down. If you block a main vent it will tend to overheat easier. I will agree that it looks cool vertically. But, I would rather have a working system then a cool dead system.      If you really want to get something for your system to protect itself from overheating, then get something that blows in air from the side. When you do that you create a better airflow circulation. Cool air goes in from the side and warm air comes out from it vent. This is great for the system.    Since, we are talking about overheating, I would say this once and only once. I do not recommend you getting the Nyko intercooler STS. That product does nothing for the slim and may actually hurt the system. What you doing is putting an exhaust fan, on top of another exhaust fan. The airflow isn't really increase, but actually stays the same or decrease. Since, the 360 is blowing out air and the STS is collecting it and blowing out air, what did that do? If the 360 fans are blowing out more air that the STS can take in the extra air is still in the system. Heat kills and you want to get rid as much air as you can.     Some minor things I don't like about the slim model is the touch sensitive buttons. They will detect anything that come close to it and will start or open up the disc tray. I like the idea of having it, but it just a pain to see it do that when you didn't want to do it. Also, I would had like the slim to have more air holes. The older 360 design had air holes on the bottom of the system and on the top.     The power brick is better with this model. It has air holes that let out heat. Also, there is a fan in there and it helps with the heat too.     The new 360 slim controller feels a little better. It has a better look to it and has a better d-pad. The older 360 d-pad felt very hard and make it hard to press it. The new d-pad feels smooth and softer.      If you know how to take care of your toys, then I say this is a good system.

I bought this for the $35 deal which is the Tekken 6 game with the wireless joystick.  I don't really play fighting games much so I'm not going to judge the merits of the Tekken 6 game.  I do play the old school Super Street Fighter II, but that's about it.  The game has received good reviews from gaming sites so I'll bow to them on the game itself.    I bought the bundle to get the joystick.  I love old arcade games like Pac-Man as well as shmups like Raiden IV.  Many XBLA games like Castle Crashers also are meant for an arcade joystick.  And this joystick delivers.  It's a light controller that sits quite comfortably on your lap or desktop.  The base is of a good size.  Not too big or too small.  It has the throw distance of an arcade stick so it's a longer throw than the joysticks you may have grown up with on your Atari or Commodore.    It is a wireless stick so you won't be tethered to the 360.  There is no force feedback or rumble so you'll miss out on that.  It is an 8-way joystick with a square gate.  It has 8 buttons.    \\"2-way gates\\": these only allow movement in the up/down or left/right directions. Galaga is common game that uses it.    \\"4-way gates\\": these only allow movement in the up, down, left, right directions. Pac-Man is the most well known game that uses it.    \\"8-way circular gates\\": These detect movement in the up, down, left, right, and diagonal directions and you won't feel \\"corners\\" when you spin the stick around. These are commonly found on 90's American arcade machines like Street Fighter 2 and have a \\"bat-shaped\\" top handle. HAPP manufactures these joystick parts.    \\"8-way square gates\\": These detect movement in the up, down, left, right, and diagonal directions and you will feel a \\"corner\\" in the diagonal directions (or coordinal depending on orientation). These are commonly found on general Japanese arcade machines and usually have a \\"ball-shaped\\" top handle. Sanwa and Seimitsu are the popular manufactures of these parts.    \\"8-way octagonal gates\\": These detect movement in the up, down, left, right, and diagonal directions and you will feel \\"corners\\" in each direction. These are commonly found on later Tekken machines. Sanwa and Seimitsu sells replaceable gate parts for their main joystick lines.    If you think your D-pad on your game controller is fine, you really should try out a joystick.  It makes a world of difference.  I was playing Pac-Man Championship Edition and my scores instantly went up and Pac-Man went exactly where I wanted him to.  I was no longer frustrated that Ryu was jumping across the screen when I meant to walk across the screen.  Combos in Street Fighter instantly became easier to pull off.    This is my first experience with a joystick on the Xbox 360 and I've been extremely happy with it.  People complain that it doesn't have \\"Sanwa guts\\".  Well, if you must own Sanwa guts, there are Youtube tutorials on how to replace the guts of the joystick.  Me personally, I don't see a need.  If the joystick parts wear out for whatever reason, I'll replace parts as needed.    There are some nitpicky things that I don't know if they only apply to this stick or all sticks.    1) I'll use Castle Crashers as an example.  If I play a game with a regular 360 game controller, that 360 controller becomes controller 1.  If I turn on the joystick, that becomes controller 2.  Perfectly reasonable.  When I then launch Castle Crashers, and I am starting a game, it won't let me play with the joystick as controller 2 unless someone is playing with the 360 controller at controller 1.  This is a problem with the Castle Crashers programming.  So I go to turn off the 360 controller and then turn off the joystick and turn it back on, hoping the joystick is now controller 1.  However, the controller stays controller 2.  I believe this is a 360 issue rather than the joystick issue but without a different branded joystick to try out, I can't verify.  2) It is an 8-button joystick with the LT, RT, RB, andLB buttons mapped to 4 of those buttons.  However, when it comes time for cycling through menu options, I can't use those buttons.  So it's frustrating because I have to go back to turning on a regular 360 controller so that I can cycle through menus and options.  If it's simply LT, RT, RB, and LB mapped to those buttons, those buttons should behave like LT/RT/RB/LB on a 360 controller.  Frustrating.  3) this is more a problem with many 360 games than with the joystick itself.  Many games don't allow you to remap the buttons.  They only have certain templates to choose from and invariably, all these templates are meant for a regular 360 controller so they aren't ideal for the button layout of a joystick.  So for a game like Castle Crashers, it took an adjustment to learn the buttons because I had played it so much for a regular 360 controller.    Reason #2 is the reason why I didn't give 5 stars (especially since reason 2 links into reason 1).  But as an actual gaming experience, I can't effuse enough about how much I love this joystick.  If you play games that don't need dual analog sticks, you must own a joystick like this one.  If you play any game that is arcade-like, you owe it to yourself to get a stick like this.  I even use the joystick for simple stuff like Uno (if I happen to have the joystick out, it doesn't improve the experience enough to actually go digging the stick out of a drawer).

I've always liked Mario and figured I'd enjoy the game, but I kept asking myself, \\"Is this game really worth what Nintendo wants for it?\\" So, I waited a year or two before picking it up used for what seemed like a less wasteful thirty bucks. Friends, let me be clear: This game is well worth the fifty dollars you'd pay for it new. This game is the best Mario game yet. Here's why:

Difficulty: This game could have been titled, \\"Super Mario Bros.: The Lost Levels 2\\" if Nintendo had been so inclined. As most Mario players know, The Lost Levels is the most difficult game in the Mario canon. If New Super Mario Bros. Wii wasn't so forgiving in terms of the amount of readily available lives, it would be harder than The Lost Levels. I beat the game in two days without a single game over, but I what must have been at least one hundred times. You will be challenged, and you will be insulted when Nintendo's \\"Super Guide\\" feature offers to play the level for you! (although, this is a nice option since the game is really hard and probably even harder for someone who hasn't played that much Mario).

Graphics: I like the style they employed here. It didn't try too hard. You don't want your Mario to look too realistic. Although, I think that HD capabilities might have made a few spots look a little better.

Overall Gameplay: It's Mario my friends. It most closely resembles the style of gameplay presented in Mario 3, but some elements of Super Mario World and other titles come to mind at points.

Controls: For the most part, it's NES-style gameplay with the Wii Remote held sideways. You can basically play the entire game just running with B and jumping with A, but you have a spin jump that can be employed by shaking the Remote. There are also some platforms that are moved by tilting the Remote. The only time I was really annoyed by the motion controls was on 7-4 where I kept spin jumping when I wanted to move the platforms. It actually made rather mad that the controls got me killed so many times, but it's just one level and not a big deal.

Music: Most of your favorite themes from Mario games long past make a return here with new versions. I was particularly happy to see the Hammer Brothers battle theme return from Mario 3. The Castle levels seem to have a more \\"epicy\\" soundtrack that makes you think, \\"Hmm, I didn't realize Mario's quest was so important!\\" It's kind of weird, but also kind of awesome. If I have one complaint, it's that the main level theme is a little overused. It would have been better if they'd used different melodies on the different worlds.

Multiplayer: I've only played it for an eve with a single friend, but I wasn't too too impressed by it. You and your friends always seem to want to jump to the same places, and the camera zooms out to cover everything when you're spread out. Also, I'm lamenting the lack of a traditional alternating Mario multiplayer.

review_headline: Welcome Back PS3 Program Ends Early
review_body: It had been reported everywhere, including Sony's site, that the \\"Welcome Back\\" program for loyal customers who put up with their network debacle was set to end on July 3.  Just got off the phone with Playstation Customer Service at 10am PST on July 3.  They have indeed shut down the \\"Welcome Back\\" program.  The customer service rep's explanation was that action had to be taken \\"by\\" July 3, and hence the last day to redeem anothing for the \\"Welcome Back\\" program was July 2.  I explained how misleading that is.  If you say \\"by\\" or \\"through\\" or \\"ends\\" or \\"expires\\", customers are going to expect that they have until the end of that specified date to redeem.  This has lawsuit written all over it.    If Sony was smart, they'd reinstate the program for the day. And if they actually cared about customers, they'd extend the program.    Based on the way Sony handles security issues and treats their customers, those of you in the market for a console would best look elsewhere.    UPDATE: Yes, indeed, the program was extended until the morning of July 5th, but not until those of us complained about how misleading their original communication was. Hence, I'm bumping my review to three stars. One star off for the security situation in the first place, and another star off as I've already had to replace two PS3s that have died.

review_headline: The best racing and F1 game ever!
review_body:
If you love cars then F1 is the best thing you can imagine. It's top-notch technologies, brilliant drivers and glamourous places from around the globe. If you pack it into this awesome Codemasters game, then you get what's best out there for racing. If you want to drift, take corner at 240 mph or jump bridges this game is not for you. If you are looking for something fun but sim-oriented, then F1 2011 is the game you should get. DRS (drag reduction system), KERS (Kinectic energy recovery system) and short life Pirelli tires! Everything is there.
There another little goody you want to get; a wireless force feedback racing wheel. Otherwise you won't be able to get anything out of this game. F1 is about precision and finesse not power and brutality. Therefore, a standard controller or pad is definitely not appropriate or recommended.
Good job Cody. Now I hope you guys will come out with DLC to maintain the fun and excitement.

On second thought (second review):
This game is still awesome and especially in comparison with the 2010 edition. Everything is much better but I have to downgrade it a bit after few hours spent lapping around the world. There are some unfortunate flaws that none of the reviews (Gamespot, IGN,...) have mentioned :

1- while driving at slower pace during a race week-end you can get penalized because the AI is not smart enough to drive by your car. He got stuck behind you. You need to drive off track to avoid any penalties (5 grid spot at least)

2- There is nothing happening in between two races or qualification session. Your racing engineer is silent, no interview, no news and not even weather report giving you forecast on when the rain will come. You can get out on track and it starts raining. No warning from your team nor from your engineer.

3- difficult to track gaps between two cars unless you go into the a mode called \\"Director mode\\". Basically it captures all the event that are happening on the track.

4- Even on the 4 out of 5 level of difficulty the AI still brake too early and allow easy passing

5- During qualification the AI stays on the race line even if they just got out of the pit. They'll jeopardize your lap easily if you catch them at the wrong place (like on a slow corner).

6- I did one full race (awesome) WE but after qualifying 2nd after Q3, my car had an engine failure. The HUD or UI did not show it, nor did my engineer tell me that I had an major technical issue.

Bottom line is, I had to find out by myself after losing 0.5s per sector and looking back to see a huge smoke coming out of my car. How can the AI or a game miss that!!! Major malfunctionnnnnnnn!

So in summary AI is not as smart as one would have expected and very few things help you figuring out what is happening around you (crucial info not communicated by your team or on screen display). Good news is a patch can easily fix that.

review_headline: Resistance is Back and Better than Ever
review_body:
I'm the author of the featured critical review of Resistance 2 here on Amazon and after finishing Resistance 3 I can gratefully say that Insomniac has restored my faith in the Resistance series with their latest offering!

Resistance 3 lands almost three full years after Resistance 2. The extra year in development, according to press reporting, was to be used to polish and refine Resistance 3 to levels unseen before in the series. I'm happy to say that Insomniac's extra efforts mark a dramatic increase in just about every facet of the game.

The story of Resistance 3 picks up where R2 left off. Nathan Hale is dead at the hands of Joe Capelli one of his squad-mates once the Chimera virus began overtaking and changing Hale. Capelli finds himself making a meager living in Oklahoma with wife, child a few fellow survivors. The Chimera at this point has completely overrun the United States and most major cities have fallen. New York seems to be the epicenter of the Chimera's terraforming activity though no human survivors of New York are known. Humanity is on the brink of extinction as Earth's weather continues to cool to fit the Chimeran plan for settlement.

The graphics in R3 have taken a dramatic turn for the better. In my review of Resistance 2 I was critical of the frequent graphic flaws and poor attention to detail. In R3 it's clear that Insomniac took more time and care in crafting the game world. The initial scenes in R3 start with a gritty grain reminiscent of films like The Road. The intent is to portray humanities desperation as the Chimera continue to erase the remaining pockets of humans from the map. As you progress through the game you'll be treated to several different areas of the United States from the humble towns and villages of the Midwest to the Industrial wastes of St. Louis and then to the frozen remains of New York. Each area has its own distinct feeling and style to separate it from the rest. In New York for example you'll find yourself running from ruined building to building advancing against a horde of Chimeran snipers and assortment of enemies.

My complaints about Resistance 2 included a lack of many of the gameplay features that made the original Resistance: Fall of Mankind so endearing too many of us. Insomniac has gone back and tweaked R3 to more closely resemble the original title. Vehicle segments are back in limited scope; this time you won't get to pilot any human or Chimeran craft but you'll at least get to ride shotgun and engage enemies as the gunner. There are various vehicle segments including a dramatic train sequence that will have you running from car to car and desperately fighting off a series of enemies. Another change comes to the health system. R2 incorporated a Call of Duty-esque regenerating health system. You could get shot up to pieces then hide and your health would regenerate. In R3 the health bar is back and there is no regenerating health system. This adds a sense of urgency and suspense when you're barely hanging on to life in an intense firefight sprinting for the green canister that is a health pack. Also back in R3 is the weapon wheel. Just like in the original Resistance, you'll be allowed to carry all your weapons concurrently and select them via the weapon wheel!

Speaking of weapons many of our old favorites from previous Resistance games are back including the Bullseye, Auger, Deadeye, Rossmore, Hedgehog grenade and more. New additions include the Cryogun, Mutator, and Atomizer. Each weapon is unique and useful in situations you'll be faced with throughout your play through R3. Each weapon in R3 also features a 3-tier leveling system; you gain levels by killing enemies. These levels serve to strengthen your weapons and unlock upgrades such as incendiary shotgun rounds for the Rossmore or an upgrade to the Deadeye that marks the enemy's heads for easier headshots. It's a fantastic addition to the series that adds much to the gameplay. Each weapon also features awesome alt-fires that are alternative uses that you'll find very helpful. The Auger for example has an alt-fire that creates a shield in front of you. The Atomizer generates a mini black hole that sucks enemies into groups that can be easily dispatched and so on.

At this point I have not yet tackled much of the online gameplay. My understanding is that the online multiplayer in R2 is a bit more contained and smaller than the massive, chaotic battles of R2. R3 also features an online cooperative feature. More on this in a future update to my review.

Much has been made of the online pass that Sony implemented with R3 and it's worth mentioning here. The online pass is a code that comes with new copies of R3 that have to be redeemed via the Account Management section of the XMB in order to access the online portion of R3. If you purchase R3 brand-new you have nothing to worry about, it's business as usual. However, folks who purchase R3 used will need to purchase a new code via the PSN Store for $9.99. There can be many accounts that can be used on one PS3 console. Two players (or more) with different accounts can play using the same online games on the PS3 system. Further you can activate the code on up to 5 different PS3 systems.

Lastly, though my review has been overwhelmingly positive thus far there are some minor stutters in R3 that should be mentioned. First, there are some technical issues; one for example in New York pitted me against a boss creature that unbeknownst to me couldn't be killed. This of course was a glitch but I still spent 45 frustrating minutes fighting the creature over and over again. A restart of the game fixed the problem. Second, the story is generally very good and does a great job conveying humanities last throes but there are moments that can only be described as \\"cheesy\\". Whenever Capelli is interacting with his wife and child it's almost painful to watch and worse on the ears. review_body: I really like this game, but I would not recommend buying this product as the game is now DOWNLOAD ONLY. That's right, after changing hands several times in the last 7 1/2 years, the current developers (Virtrium LLC) have made this game download only via istaria [dot] com so the disks no longer have the proper files. There are also three types of subscriptions: Free Access (free for life), Basic Access ($9.95/month), and Property Holder Access ($14.95/month, $77.70/6 months, $155.40/12 months). The Free Access subscription allows you one character (who must be human) and no plots of land, Basic Access grants you 5 character slots of any race but no plots of land, and Property Holder Access grants you 7 character slots 1 plot of land and the ability to buy account upgrades. There is also a 14-day trail available that gives you 3 character slots of any race, but no land. All non-plot in game content is available to all account types.    The graphics are almost 10 years out-dated, but the game still looks better than most other F2P games out there. If you do decide to try this game, do not fret if it seems like no one plays it, the in game world is HUGE so sometimes the relatively small community is hard to find. Just join some of the global chat channels if you need help. If you are unsure about how something works or where something is, other players in the global chat channels can help, or you can visit the wiki (istaria [dot] wikia [dot] com) or crimson-dawn [dot] org for help. In all it's pretty fun game, and I would recommend signing up for a 14-day trial or Free Access subscription.

Anyone who grew up during the '80s arcade scene will remember playing this game. Bad Dudes VS. Dragon Ninja is a action beat 'em up where you and another player take on all sorts of ninjas through 5 stages. The fun comes in picking up weapons, drinking cans of soda for energy, using clock icons to extend the timer and defeating bosses who were parodies/cliches of the ninja world. It was eventually ported over to the NES with a shorter name: Bad Dudes. It was a decent arcade port but because of the cartridge limitations, it wasn't a perfect port by no means.

The PROS: Essentially, Data East managed to capture the core design of the game: the one and two player co op modes, same enemies and bosses from the arcade version are here, same weapons and items are here and the stages are nearly identical to what you saw in the arcade. The sound effects are decent as well as the memorable music. Plus, this is one of the better arcade ports attempted for the NES.

The CONS: In order to fit this onto the cartridge, Data East had to cut corners. Frames of animation were cut and it made the game run slower than the arcade version. The graphics aren't as detailed and the controls are very rigid which made jumping a real chore. Finally, the game is a lot tougher so that can be good or bad depending on the player.

Despite the fact that it is not a perfect port, Bad Dudes still succeeds as far as bringing the arcade experience to a console. It was one of the better ports ever attempted and sold well for Data East. But I didn't buy it because I played the arcade game a lot and still prefer it to the NES version. And I suggest you check out YouTube video clips to see the game in motion and decide if you want to attempt to find a copy.
