review_headline: This is not just about a sexy witch
review_body: This review is for PS3 version of Bayonetta. Myself have the PS3 version and I played my friend's XBox version too. Yes the PS3 loading time is driving me nuts but you can install game data now to PS3, so it isn't that bad anymore.     I read many reviews saying \\"this game's purpose is only to show a sexy woman beating bad guys,\\" or \\"this game is way too easy,\\" blah blah blah. Honestly, I bought this game when it first came out in US and I am still playing it!     First of all, if you like Devil May Cry, get this game! It's produced by the same director and everything you see in DMC pretty much appears in Bayonetta.  Second, this is a fast-pace game. Yes you basically have almost all the moves at the beginning, but look at the move lists - do your worst to memorize them! Not to mention that each weapons combination can create new moves that are not on the list at all. You have to really spend time to explore the game. In Very Easy/Easy levels, you get through the game pretty quickly and easily; but if you start the Normal difficulty and you will see why we need Easy level to learn the moves. Dodging is very crucial in this game; you must master dodging in the early difficulty 'cause once you get to Hard or Climax you don't have Witch Time anymore! And that will make this game very difficult! If you get hit in anytime, you might get kill in seconds and don't even have time to re-attack.     Story plot wise, it's not really an amazing story. But it doesn't really matter to me (lol) All the fun I have playing it make up the lack of storyline. But the plot is like a comedy movie, very cute and funny!    Character design: oh yeah Bayonetta...*heart* I am in love with her even I am a woman...I mean I am straight too but whatever~(LOL) Everyone else blends in just fine to light up the whole game.    Overall it's definitely a game to own.

Taken in small portions, this is an absolutely amazing game experience - it really is as fast as advertised, runs as smooth as butter, and feels absolutely great to play from the off. The sound is excellent, the gunplay is BAD ASS, and the whole thing seems like an instant classic. It is hardcore. It is a tough game and not for casual gamers, and I fell very quickly in love with it!     I think the early levels in the game were best -- there's lots of close-quarters combat, and this somehow suits the game's mechanics. Gradually though it opens out into an 'epic' and the battlefields become huge expanses with either giant bosses or little enemies who can be swatted like flies. Same problem as in Gear of War 2 -- the scale reduced the feeling of actually being in the middle of a fight. I never had less than fun, but it did start to feel like a chore at times - and the run of boss battles at the end? Surely all game designers by now know that this is just stale.     I was hoping that it would be in the same mould as Bayonetta - a game that demanded and rewarded mastery, where the first playthrough is really a warm up for the main course - but although Vanquish has some challenge rooms, it doesn't really have incentives for sinking a lot of time into it. You don't unlock anything, and there's a slightly annoying punitive weapons upgrade system, whereby upgrades are deducted when you die. Also, upgrades don't seem to carry over when you replay missions and you start with your default set. Huh?    Despite these minor disappointments, I thought the game was brilliant and I absolutely had a blast for the most of it. And I didn't find it too short as some are saying - I actually thought it was too long. Either that or not quite varied enough. Anyway, if you like to shoot stuff, this is one of the best out there!

review_headline: I'm a kid again!  Autobots! Roll out!
review_body: I waited for this game with such anticipation for months, yet was etremely skeptical  about what we were going to get upon release.  Transformers games, and  games based on mega popular IP's, always seem to be underwhelming, or, downright  aweful.  I think there were 1000's of fans like me anxious in that regard! =)    In fact I rented it, before I decided to buy it.    Well, I am happy to say any fans of the first Generation of Transformers from the 80's  and even new fans of Transformers are going to fall in love with this game.    Peter Cullen voicing Prime is just aces, and the other voice actors do a terrific  job.  The graphics, while yes, might be a bit repetitive due to being on a metal  planet.  But how can you incorporate the traditional, colorful, sand zone, water zone,   forest zone, etc on Cybertron?  You can't, and I think the developers nailed it  with what they had to work with.  I don't think the Decepticons planted flower gardens. =)    While I am loving the campaighn, I have to say the PVP is the most fun I've  possibly had in a PS3 game..to Transform into a Cybertronian Truck and ram  an opposing player or unleash a missile barrage, then transform seemlessly,  into a Robot and unleash your cannons is just  amazing.  The controls are tight, and aiming is just right.    With four classes to choose from, and nice customizing options, you will surely find  a class that will work best for you.  Even when getting blasted to dust by an   opposing player, I can't help but have a smile on my face...well... sometimes :)    There are some minor negatives. For me, running out of ammo in the campaighn  has been a little frustrating as times.  There are a few other small things..but the good so outperforms the bad, I just can't   bother to be so picky.    This is the game Transformers fans have been waiting for, for wayyy too long.  Another nice part is that Hasbro has allowed this game to be cannon, so you  are playing an actual history of the Transformers.Thank you High Noon, and here's hoping the game is successful enough to have a part two  in the works, and we have a new series here for years to come!

The controls are as tight as ever, and this game is still entertaining, but beware if you are looking for more of the high-pressure surgeries and challenging gameplay as you may be disappointed. To make the game more accessible (and also to keep it from becoming stale) this installment adds the possibility of working as six different doctors, not just the lead surgeon.  There is a \\"doctor dash\\" which makes you treat 5 different injured patients at the same time, adding a very unique tension, although at times it can feel like half-baked minigames.  The new Orthopedics and Endoscopy are more similar to the traditional \\"Trauma\\" series, but each adds new unique twists.      The two other new modes are a \\"diagnosis\\" and a \\"forensics.\\" You have to analyze patient statements and survey a crime scene. They are very intriguing and some scenarios are quite engaging, though it feels fairly removed from the more traditional \\"Trauma\\" gameplay.  These two modes also slow-down gameplay considerably.    It also has a coop mode, but if you decide to skip it you're not really missing a whole lot.    In short, the game offers more gameplay options, the overall difficulty is lower, the game feels shorter than previous installments (owing to the adventure-style diagnosis and forensics modes). Overall still entertaining.

Of course, I'm also playing it on the new DSi XL, so I don't have to worry about the small-screen complaints either.    If you liked the PC game, this is the exact same game, but for the DS, and for me, that was just fine, seeing as I'm a fan of the whole series, and can now take it on the go.

Single Player is OK, not brilliant, but nothing special either, everything in the game has been done before, and better.  The multiplayer component of this game must rank as one of the most frustrating I`ve ever played, definitely feels rushed, and in my opinion DICE's poorest and laziest offering to date.  If you're the kind of gamer who loves to camp hours on end (personally I don't have the inclination, and anyway...life's too short) then you will love this game; if, on the other hand, you're a casual gamer (like me) who likes the occasional `run & gun' foray, then be prepared to get your head blown off...A LOT!!.  It did not take me a very long time to realise that for me, this game is missing something very important....the FUN factor.  I've never had such a miserable time playing a video game before.

product_title: Ear Force X41 Digital RF Wireless Game Audio+ Chat with Dolby 7.1 Surround Sound -Xbox 360
review_headline: The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly
review_body: The Good    **Every thing you need to get started is included in the package. A USB power cable, optical audio cable, and 2 AAA batteries are included in the package. It seems that almost every electronic device you buy needs a special cable or attachment that has to be purchased separately, so it's always nice when a device has everything you need included.    The 5.1 surround sound works pretty well. Though obviously not as good as physical surround sound set up, you will be able to tell what direction different audio cues are coming from (footsteps, gun fire, voices, etc.) The real standout feature here is the dynamic chat volume. The X41s allow you to adjust the volume of game audio and voice chat independently, but will also automatically increase or decrease the voice chat volume so that it is always slightly louder than the game audio. A nice touch for fans of online shooters.    The Bad   The X41s look and feel cheap. From the very first time you pick them up, you will feel that you need to handle them with care. The ear cups jiggle and rattle every time you pick the headset up and the white molded plastic makes them look and feel like a toy. People with small children beware.     The Ugly    Audio quality is suspect. Some mid-range sounds on the X41s can sound as if you were listening to them through a tin can on a string. It's not very noticeable, and most enclosed speaker headsets have this problem, but when combined with the audio pops, you can't ignore the quality issue here.    All in all, They aren't bad headsets. They work well with xbox live voice chat and they're pretty comfortable. The x41s could be the perfect gaming solution if they were $100 or less, but they're not. So, I can only recommend them if you want a gaming headset specifically designed for use with xbox live. However, if your primary concern is getting the full enjoyment out of your games without disturbing your spouse or roommates, you might want to pass. There are better less expensive options.    **If you use an HDMI cable to connect your 360 to your television, then you will need to plug the optical cable into your televisions optical out port or an optical out on your stereo receiver.

review_headline: Great Kinect game for DDR fans.
review_body:
Kinect had two Dance games at launch. Dance Central, and Dance Masters. You can't help buy compare the two. I happen to like both. They are different though.

Dance Central is more follow the moves the dancer is doing, and Dance Masters is a lot more like Dane Dance Revolution. Where you hit the marks at certain times.

Dance Masters has better multiplayer, with 2-player co-op on a single console and versus over Xbox live. But Dance Central has a better Single Player and a more mainstream music selection. While Dance Masters is more DDR (J-pop) type songs.

There are a few different types of \\"arrows\\" you have to hit at the certain times. (Note I only call them arrows to compare them to Dance Dance Revolution).

-There is a basic hit the mark type of circle, where there is a circle with a larger circle around it that shrinks. You have to move your hand in that space at the time both circles match up (usually goes with the beat).

-There is a hold circle (similar to the hold arrows), where you hold your hand in the circle for a set number of beats.

-There is a multi-beat circle (indicated by a number of dots in the smaller circle) which you have to hit the circle multiple times in a row to the beat.

-There is a foot marking that you hit with either left or right foot on the ground, also usually to the beat.

-There are silhouettes that you have to match the pose of. Which usually aren't too hard, but there is quite a variety in these. Usually if you are following the on screen dancer you can get these pretty easy.

-There is a steam line type of wave, that can vary in speed and location. You hit these by waving your hand across the line, at the same speed as the on screen dancer.

All of these are pretty well varied, and on the harder difficulties can be mixed together or doubled.

The songs consist of the typical DDR songs, with more unlocking as you progress though the game (or by meeting certain criteria).

Overall if you liked DDR, this game is a must buy if you own Kinect.

review_headline: The Outer Rings of Locked-Level HELL
review_body: NOTE : This review will ignore SFX, Music and Graphics to focus on the gameplay.    By far THE BIGGEST DISAPPOINTMENT about this whole disaster has been our misinterpretation of what 'World Party Games' means : we had hoped to play games with some cultural relevance - such as Sumo Wrestling (remarkably, this IS one of the games safely locked out of reach) and other activities people from other cultures enjoy.  Heck, the box says ''play exciting games from around the globe'' -- SERIOUSLY ?!?  do Italians play 'Toss-a Da Pizz-a at-a the Italian a-Guy-a' ???  i seriously doubt it.  (ATTENTION Dreamcatcher employees : maybe the Italian Mafia should pay you idiots a visit, and ''teach you'se guys some manners, ya know what ahm talkin' 'bout ?'')    ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** *****    There is a SERIOUS CANCER of '[WHATEVER] GAMES' packages spreading on the Wii platform, but these can be SAFELY AVOIDED if you watch for the EARLY WARNING SIGNS : neither a comprehensive list of the games is included, nor details of gameplay.  There is a reason that information is not included, and that reason is called marketing : few people would buy if they had a clear idea of what they were actually paying for.    ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** ***** *****    The first insurmountable hurdle : the only games available initially are 'Spinning Camel', 'Running up the Eiffel Tower' and a 'Pizza Toss' fiasco.  For the 'Spinning Camel' game you tilt the remote (or shift your weight on a balance board) to counteract the current tilt and roll of the camel . . . think 'virtual mechanical bull ride', but without any of the fun.  The 'Pizza Toss' game will build endurance as fast as any repetitive-stress inducing factory job, simply shake the remote up and down (theoretically this simulates cutting a pizza) to 'reload' after tossing slices (which is accomplished by swinging the nunchuck Frisbee-style) to the various Italian cooks (?) popping out of the doors and windows that line the street, as well as the occasional passerby on foot or scooter.  THIS is fun ?  Maybe you will think so ; different strokes, right ?  'Running up the Eiffel Tower' was every bit as exhausting as was the pizza toss, and just as repetitive. And just as repetitive. And just as repetitive. If you enjoyed reading that three times in a row, this game might be for you !  (For the record, let me say that repetitive can be fine, but none of these mini-games is engaging in the least - not even top-notch music from Nintendo could save this one.)    So how long until you unlock something that might be interesting ?  Beats me ... not soon enough - that much i can say for sure.  it will be an unpleasant period of time spent (if i can manage), with only a hope of getting to something interesting.    The frantic waving and seemingly endless remote-pumping activity was not what we got the Wii for (i have all the other game consoles for that sort of thing).  Most nights my wife and i enjoy bowling a few games, a round or two of Mini Putt-Putt, or some other fun activity not requiring an excruciating setup (such as unlocking levels in the hope of finding something entertaining), endurance-based button mashing activity, or extensive training (she refuses to make the commitment required by a Zleda game, for example, but i'm working on her).    What did i expect ? Maybe instead of a spinning camel i expected to play 'Arabian Polo' with a sheep's head (i'm neither judging nor kidding - i wanted to experience what other cultures consider 'fun').  But tossing pizzas at Italian stereotypes was a mite insulting, and i say that as someone who grew up laughing at cultural stereotypes on Saturday morning cartoons. What 'World Games' did they miss ? How about Ball-in-a-Cup (played against a cadre of barefoot Mexican children, most likely) - that is about all this company might have achieved, in my opinion : utter crap.    World Party Games was a failure of the first order.  ** because i do not want to ''poison the well'' should others think it worthwhile.

Definitely get this game for the unlimited multiplayer experience you will get from it... or at least for the solo skirmish modes it offers. The AI is quite good on hardest level. I enjoy playing because it is smart like Chess and fun like a video game should be. One clarification is the campaign, well, consider it one long and fancy tutorial that is a must in order to appreciate the depth of the game. The game is called RUSE because ruses are essential element of the gameplay. They are the novelty and innovation of the game. RUSE is a unique game in that sense. So plan on using them all the time and you are guaranteed to hold an edge over your opponent. In fact, ruses are quite realistic as the campaign will teach you that.    Do not be fooled by any bad reviews. They were harsh because the developpers messed up the campaign story and acting. Well, sincerely the story is not boring or stupid nor is the acting mediocre. I would say they are Ok! But this is not why you will be playing it. The true value is the playability and the fun factor you get from its depth, sort of like Chess. RUSE is quite different from say Company of Heores, C&C etc... in many ways. One difference is the units (far more numerous and varied and historic than CoH or any other) move over a huge landscape (think strategy and ambushes in cities and forests...) a bit slowly so that gives you time to SRATEGIZE, BREATH and THINK more. No need to multi task as much. You still need to coordinate and organise your defenses and attacks so you will definitely be busy all the time. Occasionally I take a break to zoom in and marvel at the 3D world unraveling... the bombers, the hills, sea...quite nice with the fast zooming and fluid technology.    So finally, make sure you play the campaign to learn all the properties of the units and how to deploy ruses. I recommend the hardest level if you like some challenge. It will make you tough in the multiplayer arena. This is where the game RUSE really begins.

product_title: Star Wars: The Force Unleashed II Platinum Edition
review_body:
There are a lot of bad reviews for this game so I felt that I needed to write a review of my own. I actually quite enjoy the game. I will state first off that I don't feel the game is too short. Many other reviewers have said that the game was too short but I don't agree, if you play the game on easy mode and just run straight through it then maybe that would be true.

Difficulty:
There are four different levels of difficulty: Easy, Medium, Hard, Unleashed. I would recommended playing either Hard or medium on the fist time through, depending on how hard you want it to be. If you choose the right difficulty level for you then you will be much more satisfied with this game.

Gameplay:
There are loads of techniques and light-saber combinations, force powers, etc. The game engine runs smooth and controls are excellent. This game is well polished anyone can enjoy chopping down a couple of storm-troopers. The force powers are upgradeable which makes you want to kill more enimies so that you can purchase them. You will also find crystals that have different light-sabers that have various effects.

Graphics:
The graphics are every bit comparable to any other game. The movie graphics are amazing, some I think may look as good as the movies. You won't be disapointed with the graphics. The programmers definitely spent their time making things look nice.

Overall Value:
This is not the greatest game ever made, but it is a freaking tight game. So if you are looking for the best game ever made you may want to turn away now, those of you looking to play a game that rocks then this is the game.

Replay Value:
It's pretty cool to replay a couple of times maybe. There are some challenge modes that you can spend some time diddling with.

Overall:
My overall review is that this is a good game. I personally like it.

The story line is continued from the Path of Radiance Game Cube version (which is also a fantastic game that I highly recommend playing before this one because you may be completely lost otherwise). The graphics are far superior to the game cube Path of Radiance. There are many MANY ways to customize the game ending (most changes are only available on the second play through and up) so it is never boring. My basic gripe about the game is that you have limited play time with the Greil Mercenaries because you are constantly switching off between The Dawn Brigade, The Crimean Knights, and (of course) the Greil Mercenaries. However, this issue is somewhat necessary for the (amazingly grand) plot so whatever! Also, the cut scenes are superbly done and well voice-casted (except for Mist and Zelgius). I HIGHLY recommend this to anyone who enjoys a good game and for anyone who likes to watch their characters grow.

review_headline: A great approach to the Star Trek Universe in MMO form
review_body:
I've been a Star Trek fan for most of my life, and a gamer for a good chunk, as well. I've played numerous MMOs, but most of the ones coming out today just don't draw me in like some in the past have (Asheron's Call was one of the greats).

I beta tested STO, but found it's performance to be spotty. Once I built a new machine, however, I found that this game is a real gem (note: it doesn't require a super-hefty machine; a good budget gaming rig should be able to handle it). You can spend hours just creating your character, let alone customizing your ship and getting out there and actually DOING things. Of course, you don't have to; you can have as much or as little control over the character and ship design as you'd like, within reason (no heads sprouting out of your backside, people; we're all humanoid).

I will say this; the game isn't exactly well documented. You really need to be willing to research outside of the game before you get too invested in your character build, not to mention just learning the basic mechanics. Also, if you're looking to get creative in ship usage, you're probably going to need to know a little math in order to really get down and dirty with ship power management (it's all documented by fan sites, though, so don't worry).

PvP is a nice touch, but the game has been out for long enough that newbies will have a rough go of it, especially without the proper equipment. Also, balance is still a bit of an issue.

I do have some issues with the game. It seems everybody wants to fly the cruiser line of ships, presumably because they're exactly what you think about when you think of Star Trek (except in the case of the Defiant from Voyager, which is an escort class). Also, the crafting system seems just a little silly to me, but whatever. It's an added mechanic that's somewhat unique in it's approach, so I'm cool with it.

Ground combat is somewhat clunky compared to space combat, but you don't HAVE to engage in ground combat often, so it's forgivable.

I do enjoy the ability to get new missions and complete missions without having to go back and forth between the quest giver; utilizing the communicator makes that a LOT easier.

With this bundle of STO, you can get a reclaimed borg officer to act as a bridge officer on your ship... Very, very cool.often, so it's forgivable. review_headline: MAG: Not for the casual gamer
review_body: I recently acquired a PS3 in a trade, so I set out to get some of the top games, this being one of them. I used to be a hardcore gamer, but now I have so many other things taking up my time that I can barely claim to be a casual gamer. I've long been a fan of Counter Strike, and more recently, Call Of Duty. This game is absolutely nothing like those games. Maybe it's just that I haven't spent enough time to rank up, but as I played it seems like nobody is at all interested in teaming up or helping one another. I understand the concept behind this game is supposed to be a large scale strategy FPS, but it hasn't come close to that for me as a new player. I like the concepts of leveling up and having squads and leaders and all that, but I just don't think PS3 is a good platform for this kind of game. Lately when I play a console game it's just to pass some time, usually not more than about an hour. This is not the kind of game you can just pick up and play and have fun doing so. If you're just looking for another shooter to try out and spend a little time with, look elsewhere. If you've got the time to spend with this game I could see it turning into a pretty cool thing. I just don't have the time, and I don't feel this game is worth losing sleep over. As for the game play, it's extremely clunky and I feel like I'm playing a bad version of early Counter Strike. I'm pretty good at most FPS, but I can't seem to keep much of a positive ratio in this game. The weapon accuracy, or lack there of, is extremely annoying. The game completely lacks weapon selection of any kind, and with only three main classes to choose from, it gets old fast.

product_title: Harvest Moon: Sunshine Islands - Nintendo DS
review_body: I'm a 31-year-old woman who mostly plays casual games on PC, but I completely love Sunshine Islands on DS. There is so much to do in this game (fishing, mining, farming, dating, etc). The replay value is high, which is great considering how long the game is. There are a few small annoyances -- you have to \\"meet and greet\\" the game characters repeatedly in order to build up friendships and relationships, so expect some repetition -- but it's totally worth playing, and very addictive.

As a completionist, this game was both fun and hellish for me. The quest system, the upgradable weapons, there is a lot of things to do in the game, but perhaps too much, some of the quests require a bunch of drop items that you simply have to keep on grinding for. The story is not bad but the sidequests lack any real story, most of them are simply go grind for these items, go back, get reward, rinse and repeat.

Good game in the series, really good artwork.  Tends to 'freeze up' when running on Direct X 10 or 11 though. (I'm sure they will fix this soon)  Glad to have been able to download the world builder.  Does tend to want you to see the entire beginning credits.

review_headline: An Excellent Addition to the Rock Band Library
review_body:
I probably play Rock Band more than any other game in my library. That said, I put in countless hours on RB1, RB2, Beatles RB, RB Lego along with tons of DC and the AC/DC Pack.

I think a fair assessment of GD: RB would be to compare it to Beatles: Rock Band since it is similar in that its really a hybrid new game/expansion pack of sorts.

Here are the things you can expect from the game -

1. Similar to Beatles: RB, you get pretty comprehensive library of songs in Green Day's lineup. I would say it is more comprehensive than Beatles only because GD doesn't have a huge library of songs vs the Beatles. As a result, you'll find all the hit songs from the band, spanning from their early career to the most recent album. If you like GD, you will be happy with the songlist.

2. On the \\"Plus\\" version of GD: RB - you will also get 2 codes - one to download the recent song pack of 6 songs from their 21st century breakdown album and another to allow you to export your tracks to Rock Band 2 so that you can play their songs on RB2, similar to the AC/DC expansion pack released awhile back. If you play RB2 often, I would strongly urge you to consider purchasing this version of GD: RB since you can mix and match songs from your existing library (which, like mine, can expand to as much as songs from RB1, RB2, RB Lego, AD/DC and your existing DLC as well). This is also great since on Beatles: RB you can not export those songs over to RB2 so this alone is a great reason to consider buying the plus version of GD: RB

3. The interface of GD: RB is like a hybrid of RB2 and Beatles RB. It has the color scheme of the standard RB games (Green, Red, Yellow, Blue, Orange buttons - unlike the pastel colors featured in Beatles: RB) but it also incorporates the harmony system featured in Beatles RB which allows you to have up to 3 singers singing in 3 separate vocal tracks. Word is Rock Band 3 will also feature this system, so in many was GD: RB offers an early look at what you might expect in the future.

4. The graphics of GD: RB are decent. More often than not you'll probably be too busy to notice since you'll be glued to the instrument line that you're following at the moment. But I can safely say that the animations and characters are rendered nicely. Similar to Beatles: RB, GD: RB also features the band in different venues and styles depending on when each song was released during the band's career.

5. Like other RB games, GD: RB features a career mode, along with a quickplay mode that allows you to play solo or with other players locally or online on xbox live. After putting in 6 hours yesterday, I noticed no lag or issues with online gameplay. The calibration process is easy, and you can be ready to rock within minutes of loading up the game.

When Bionic Commando launched it was met with a lot of speculation and didn't receive many favorable reviews. Many criticized the game for being all of the map really and not doing any of those elements right. Having played through the game twice now people judged this game by the cover not by the overall contents, and having been gaming since back in ye olde days of the Atari 2600 this game brought the classic Bionic Commando into 3D without missing a beat.

Gameplay: Not your every day video game I will be honest. Like most games today there is a learning curve but they baby you into the game. Bionic Commando basically doesn't pull its punches. Right after the basic tutorial it is good luck, 'have fun storming the castle' pretty much. Practice a bit with your timing and next thing you know you will be Tarzan with a grenade launcher. Boss fights feel very epic and actually will make you think fast on your feet trying to find out the weakness of the boss. There also is no one way to actually fight enemies. You can do everything from stomping on enemies, swinging and shooting, grabbing and throwing them into the air, throw objects , or simply pull out a gun and pew pew them all. One gripe that anyone will notice is that until you get a hang of the game, your accuracy with firearms is pretty much terrible until you pull off some nice challenge stunts to unlock some bonuses

Sound/Story: The voice acting is actually some of the best I have heard in a long time and pretty much carried the weak storyline of the game. Sound effects were spot on also

Graphics/Presentation: The graphics were actually really good. The game runs at 720p unless you force 1080p. I was surprised at how detailed they went with the background of the game. The overall presentation of the game was smooth. The game itself can be a challenge even on normal, as you might end up doing 10-15mins on stuff only to die and have to redo it. Checkpoints are very fair though, and areas aren't super massive where 20+ mins of work magically vanishes because you missed that one grapple.

Length/Replay: The game could be considered short especially once you get really good at it. Master your swings and next thing you know in an hour you just plowed through 20% of the game. Though it may be short, the game doesn't pull punches and you will enjoy the little twists and turns the game throws at you. Replay factor is also a \\"plus\\" because there will be collectibles that just seem to taunt you. They look so easy yet 10 mins later you are still trying to line up that swing or release just right, and then there always is the phantom collectible that taunts you since you never found it but it has to be in the level somewhere! Plus once I got good at the game, it was just to much fun to swing and do a \\"death from above\\" onto a MECH since I got my timing down perfect.

Summary of \\"cons\\" I have for this game (with positive re-enforcement)
- Early on having to figure out shooting mechanics and grappling while avoiding bullets can be frustrating [But learning and mastering the system turns you into a complete unstoppable 'bionic commando']
- Short game (under 7 hrs) [good replay though with collectibles and voice acting. Plus some maps are just fun to figure out different ways around enemies or just replay it to try and best your challenge count]

Overall Score: 91%

review_headline: Bad online custom map system. Non user-friendly map editing.
review_body: Starcraft 2 is pretty fun online. I've now spent hours playing others 2v2 online.    -Gameplay  Basically, it's like starcraft 1 and Warcraft 3 mixed and ugraded. No heros in multiplayer or vs AI. It's better that way imo. It's tough to manage a hero amongst other things.  There are some things from SC1 and some new. Now, you need to pick what you build because everything has an appropriate counter. In SC1, you will see people mass out hydras and kill everything in sight.   The customs maps are addicting. They can do a lot with the map editor.    -Storymode  Storymode starts off with tutorial type missions introducing you to some game mechanics and the new units. They also have some practice usefulness that you can use against players. You can purchase upgrades, research and other stuff like that. For example, you can purchase mercenaries with your earned points to help you complete missions. Mercs are like the elite version of an original unit like a firebat or marine. The upgrades are usually things that you can research in multiplayer like the +10 life to marines. They have a lot of other stuff though. Medic and firebat are two that you don't find in multiplayer.    The voice acting starts off kind of corny. The voice actor for Jim Raynor sounds like he fell out of an old corny cowboy movie and landed on Starcraft 2. However, he starts to get comfortable with his role and his voice acting gets better. The support characters were pretty good. The big marine (Tygris or something) has an ok voice actor. The captain has good voice actor. You will mostly see lots of cowboy type references since the two main characters (Raynor and Tygris) styles are like that. Overall, decent story build up so far. Not in the \\"amazing, complex storyline\\" way but a \\"I have spare time\\" way.     -Multiplayer  League system allows you to play random or team vs others. 1v1 up to 4v4. There are 5 leagues and sometimes you'll be matched against a person 3 leagues up. If you win, you up your league or points quickly.   Custom games that people make using map editor is downloaded from battle.net. It shows the name of the game and when you join, you are put in the first available lobby of that game. They show 10 games at a time. You have to scroll a long way down to find a game you may want to play. You cannot download maps on the internet and play them online, they are all downloaded from B.net. I don't know what fail person thought of that one but he should be banned from anything related to games or any other thing I might come in contact with.     Again, the map editor is very open source. Blizzard doesn't even have a guide for it out right now because the guide would have to take the user through step by step programming lessons. That's why they said that they are bringing out articles instead of actual guides. These articles are mainly for people familiar with computer language. It's basically 80% of Starcraft 2's gaming mechanics you can play around with in Staredit.   They already have a final fantasy mod out that allows you to do turn-based combat like in final fantasy. Though, getting it installed is another story. There is no guide for how to do this.    -Other Stuff  You have to login for single player if you want to get achievements. Achievements are mainly for showing off. It does however, opens up locked portraits. I'm still stuck with that guy that wears the cap. I think it's an scv. The game has an offline mode for singleplayer and VS AI but you won't get achievements. Also, you have to log in every 30 days so Bliz knows you aren't a pirate.    - You chat by way of something called a Real I.D. You have to click on the persons name in your combat history and add them to friends list. Alternatively, you can find their name and number on the SC2 forum. It's not a chatroom but it's decent for setting up teams.     Pros  - Fast and easy match-making  - Puts you in matches with people around your skill level  - Graphics: Explosions, lighting, physx, effects, texture   (Some people don't like it because it is too close to warcraft 3. It is similar. Think about Warcraft 3 graphics but updated. I don't mind it though.)  - Fun custom maps  - Custom maps are easy to make and start. Just click on the name of the map and it puts you either as host or in a game.  - Lots of information available about your matches, rank and other stuff in your profile.    Cons  - LAN: I don't use that but who knows, I might one day. I understand why Bliz took it away though. Mostly as an anti-pirate tactic.   - No Chat-Channels: Perhaps they could add one but at the moment, not too much of a con.  - No cross-region play: You have to buy separate copies to play different regions across the world.   - Can't download your own maps and use them  - Map editor requires a degree to use. (It has lots of functions similar to Excel and a lot of it is mostly for programmers)  - Bliz is in league with Bobby Kotick: Not a real con for the game but I dislike that guy for the direction he's taking games.    Other Thoughts:  The storymode is mostly terran and 2 expansions coming out later for toss and zerg. They probably did that because of the amount of cutscenes.

review_headline: New and refreshing attempt at the game series
review_body:
With MGM fighting bankruptcy, the next Bond film will be a long wait ahead. Gladly, they pushed out Blood Stone to make some sort of revenue. I had low expectations for this game, honestly. But this game took some liberties, and without a movie to restrict the game's story, production designers had a lot of freedom.

The gameplay is 3rd person. I couldn't help thinking of the awful Tomorrow Never Dies gaming from the PSOne era when reading this on the game info. The contols are very solid for a shooter. Activision went with a shoot/cover scheme simular to Rainbox Six series. The firefights emphisise keeping cover and taking time for that critical shot, spray and pray gunstyle gets you killed terribly quick. There's also an added melee feature that has Bond perform CQC on enemies within an arms reach. I've found this feature to be the most entertaining. You're constantly pushing forward toward your objective, with an enemy attempting to block your path you can smoothly take him down and not miss a beat on your sprint. A very Bond move not really attempted in previous games. On a side note, the game is visually amazing. The ambiance in the background is polished off well.

And for the not so great. The game wants so hard to incorporate the Bond vehicle chase sequences, which could have been more refined before the game's release. Driving controls are very sluggish. I've attempted to get the driving physics down, but still can quite make the smooth drifting turns the game simply instructs. These driving controls are my only real complaint about the game. Thankfully, they took the time to really smooth out the rest of the gameplay. I also understand this is not a driving game and not the primary selling point, but if it's going to be put in the final product, it should be done well. Again, this wouldn't even be an issue if there was only a couple driving sequences throughout the whole game. I've only played the first few levels and half were a driving/vehicle chase. This seems to be the running trend for the game.

If you can manage with driving sequences that seem like a chore than gameplay, this game is an overall hit. Even with my minor complaint, I find the game addicting and entertaining. Highly recommended for any Bond fan, or anyone wanting to step away from first person shooters.g/vehicle chase. This seems to be the running trend for the game.

review_headline: Fantastic Game with One Giant Flaw
review_body:
Here's a great way to start a review: Folklore is one of the most disappointing games that I have ever played. Read on if you want to find out why.

Folklore's style is absolutely fantastic. This is the type of game that Neil Gaiman would envision on one of his really, really good days. The environments are colorful and dream-like, just filled to the absolute brim with wonder. I spent a good ten minutes early on wandering around an empty field just watching all sorts of sparkles and colors flow around the world.

This charming world frames a dark story about a girl named Ellen who lost her mother as a small child. As the game begins, she receives an obviously surprising letter from her long dead mother - asking her to come to a small village named Doolin. At the same time a dude named Keats, who works at a magazine that covers the paranormal, receives a phone call from a woman rambling on about magic and Doolin Village. Keats decides to go check things out, hoping to land a scoop.

The two characters above both arrive safely in Doolin and some serious stuff starts to go down. The story is told through a variety of techniques, from traditional RPG fare like cutscenes and character models trading text boxes back and forth to something a bit more progressive - a sort of animated comic book feel with frames and speech bubbles. This technique works very well and definitely keeps the storytelling feeling fresh.

The bulk of the gameplay revolves around battling weird monsters, the Folk. As you progress through the game Folk, you are able to rip out the Id (soul) of a wounded Folk in order to gain their powers. This is how you unlock abilities and become more powerful as the game moves along. Each Folk has a few different powers available, ranging from various attacks and shields to combo extensions and status bonuses.

Early on in the game you run into a Folk named Pouke, and absorbing his Id allows you to summon Pouke and perform a basic attack. Absorb five or ten more Pouke Ids and you'll increase the number of attacks in your basic combo. You'll also find a weird Folk named Henky, who flies around shooting bubbles. Absorb his Id and you'll be able to fire off bubbles to take down enemies up in the air. Give Henky five Pine Nuts, and you'll 'level up' your mastery of the Henky Folk and reduce the MP consumption. Some Folk abilities require you to provide items, some require you to defeat a specific Folk with another specific Folk, and so on down the line.

Once you gain a bunch of Folk abilities, you're able to mix and match as you see fit and assign each one to a button on the controller. This allows you to customize your Folk Id repertoire and design an arsenal that fits your style. It's a lot of fun to determine the weak points of new enemies and figure out the best way to defeat them. It's very satisfying to win a battle after busting out three or four completely different abilities. Visually the combat looks great and gives you plenty of sweet effects to keep your interest - the only bummer is that the framerate occasionally reaches the 'starting to get painful' level.

Based on everything I've said thus far, Folklore sounds totally badass doesn't it? Sure it does, and this is what makes it such a disappointing game. As I mentioned above, there are two main characters: Keats and Ellen. They aren't just main characters, they are both playable characters - which is the beginning of the problem.

The game is divided up into a number of different chapters. Let's say that you play and complete chapter one with Keats - you do not have the option of playing chapter two with Ellen. In order to play chapter two with Ellen, you need to go back and replay chapter one with her first. There are minor differences in the how the same chapters plays out with two different characters (different Folk abilities, some different items and abilities, different views of the storyline), but in practice things are very much the same.

After figuring out how things worked, I decided that playing every level through twice in a row is for suckers - I chose Ellen and decided to play through the entire game as her. it's been a long seven months since i pre-ordered this game and during those seven months my expectations grew higher and higher. usually that leads to the inevitable let down, but happily this was not the case with medal of honor. i'm glad to report that this is a great game and i recommend you buy it.

the single-player campaign started with a bang, but then tapered off a bit and i was concerned that pacing was going to be an issue. thankfully, it wasn't. once you get hooked up with dusty the tier 1 of all things bad-a$$, the game really takes off. the missions are nicely varied and very cleverly segue from one to the next. one particularly harrowing mission seems taken straight from marcus latrell's 'lone survivor.' if you've read that book, you'll instantly recognize it. the dialogue feels realistic [i've never been in combat, so i take their word for it], but some of the voice acting could have been better.

the only real disappointment for me were the graphics of the single-payer. i don't know if it's a limitation of the modiefied Unreal 3 engine Danger Close used or not, but they just aren't up to par for a game released in 2010. i also experienced a few glitches which forced me to reload a checkpoint, but that only happened twice; there were some minor frame rate issues, but the longer i played the less it happened.

the multiplayer is excellent. no, it's not COD. and that's a good thing. there's no teleporting across the map, no n00b tubes, no remote control cars, no nukes [and no nuke boosting] and all the other things that killed MW2. MOH actually requires you to be skilled with a gun. what a concept. if you do go online, be prepared to have you back side handed to you. repeatedly. it can be very unforgiving and more than a bit frustrating. when i first hopped on last night for my first match i died five times before i even saw an enemy. but by the end of the night i was more than holding my own. be patient. practice. plan. strategize. i think you'll find this a more rewarding experience than sitting under a stairway waiting for five guys to run by so you can call in your care package.

the multiplayer maps look amazing and the sound design, as we've come to expect from DICE, is off the charts. you really feel the heft of your M4a1 or ak-47. another nice touch is the scorechain, which is different from a killstreak. you get points for killing enemies, arming/disarming objectives, kill assists, etc. a certain number of points get an offensive or defensive reward [mortar strike, UAV, etc]. you can choose to reward yourself [mortar strike, missiles], or reward your team [match ammo, flak jackets, etc]. i saw a nice balance of both last night. it's a nice change that i hope to see other games incorporate. and we can only hope DICE releases NEW maps instead of new MODES of existing maps like they did on BFBC2.

if you're a parent and your kid wants this, be warned there are pleny of f-bombs. this is, after all, war. the gore is pretty realistic [a .50 cal gunshot will tear an enemy's head - or limb - clean off], but there's an option to turn the gore off in the menu.

i've not tried the Tier 1 mode yet [an arcady style single player campaign with an online leaderboard], but i imagine it's pretty fun and gives the game some replay value.

review_headline: I much preferred to be a princess... at least there was cake.
review_body:
The cake was and is, a lie.

Once again a tasty morsel was dangled before our eyes, loaded with promises and just short of sugary sweetness, it's been snatched away.

First off, I'd like to say that not even once did I encounter anything I would really call a \\"glitch\\". A few frame rate slowdowns and my dog's critical inability to play a simple game of fetch, not included. Okay, well, perhaps being pushed off-screen by a passing NPC during Pie Making counts, but it was amusing watching the pies make themselves.

Moving on to the good, I'd like to say that this game is a vast improvement over Fable II, especially in terms of story. As you play you honestly feel like the prince or princess you are in the midst of a revolution. However, there are times when I felt overwhelmed and more a figurehead, so to speak. Your opinion isn't asked for much and your dear tutor Walter holds your hand every step of the way. Also, you get no choice on with whom you'll ally. You either give into their demands or you sit there and stare at the screen, wishing a 'I decline' option into existence. That isn't to say it's BAD, it's just that there's a sort of disconnect. Aside from your brother being a jerk, it didn't seem as if my character had any real motivation to overthrow him. The graphics are much improved, the world is enormous and does a great job of creating the appropriate atmosphere in the right places, the music is pleasant, the voices are great and the Pythonian humor was... humorous.In terms of immersion, it did an okay job. I really grew to care for my little virtual family.

As for the bad, the game is short. Like, Emma Watson's pixie cut short. This in itself wouldn't be a bad thing if the pacing hadn't been shot to hell at the end. Once you become king or queen, the story completely undoes all of the good it's done by throwing you headfirst into a crisis giving you exactly one year to save your people. Again, this isn't bad until you realize that entire year is spent being bullied into a stream of choices (clearly marked good, bad and neutral for your convenience and once those are completed. Boom. That's it, you get tossed into the middle of the aforementioned crisis and spend a grand total of twenty minutes, at longest, fighting before the credits roll. Speaking of being thrown into battle, the revolution is much like this, not even letting you storm the palace. No, no, the tyrant just quietly hands himself over without a fight.

What? -insert shocked emote-

From what we were told, the revolution was only the beginning. Unfortunately, it was the best part and takes up most of the game. I breezed through being queen in the span of a few hours and felt horribly dissatisfied. Sure, the game is fun, but I feel there is very little replay value in light of the ending and it's color-coded for good/evil choices.

Bottom line? If I had to do it all over again, I would. I'd also hawk it as fast as possible for resale value as soon as I finished. Or rent it. product_title: Henry Hatsworth in the Puzzling Adventure - Nintendo DS
review_headline: What's puzzling is why more people haven't bought this yet
review_body: This game is amazing. If you're at all a fan of super polished, extremely charming sidescrollers (like Goemon or Strider or Kirby or Ristar or Rayman or Starfy or Mega Man) than stop reading and buy this game. I'm not even that big a fan of puzzle titles, and I gotta admit, the puzzle component to Henry Hatsworth had me hooked.     So the game is a sidescroller, but the bottom screen has a puzzle game constantly (slowly) going on. At any time, you can switch between which game/screen you're working on (while puzzling, the top screen is paused). As you do stuff in the platformer parts, you build up a bar that lets you stay in the puzzle game. And as you puzzle away, you earn powerups that take immediate effect in the platformer half. For example; clear a lightning block in puzzle mode, and when you return to the platformer part a lightning shock will paralyze all enemies on screen. There are tons of powerups, so you're encouraged to puzzle away, and since you only have to play it in short bursts, it gets quite addicting fast. It's frankly, brilliant. I can't believe no one has ever combined these two genres before! Let alone so well.    The game is gorgeous with personality to spare; this dude and his crazy, adventuresome, London-esque world (complete with his tea-time robot suit, and Union Jack anime-style swooshy background) is way too loveable. The art all around is great, with fantastic use of colors and loads of personalities for every character in the game. The gameplay is rock solid - this guy can platform with the best of them. The fighting is tight, responsive and rewarding, with nice amount of depth (juggles!). And the platforming is kept fresh with plenty of new moves. For example, once you find the Golden Gentleman's Trousers, you can do wall jumps - which comes in handy 'cuz you'll need 'em. The levels are really well designed. The game is fantastic!     It's original, it's charming, it's polished, it's unique - but most importantly it's fun as heck. I can't believe that Tiburon, the same EA studio responsible for Madden year in and year out, had the creativity and skill to put this together. If no one told me, I'd swear this was a long lost Konami or Capcom SNES game. It's fantastic.    Buy it!

review_headline: Challenging and fun but annoying too!
review_body: I had never played God of War on the PS2 before, and this disc sounded like a great deal (it is, by the way).  God of War is a good game, very challenging, but I had some complaints:    * The camera angle is fixed, so it's difficult to navigate some parts of the game.    * There are puzzles that require exact timing, with no margin for error.  I'm sure I died 50 times in some places before somehow getting it right, and don't know if I could do it again without dying another 50 times.   * Every third or fourth time you die, the game asks if you want to switch to \\"easy\\" mode.  No thank you.  Stop asking.   * You can only save the game at specific \\"save points\\".  * It is unnecessarily frustrating in parts.  Near the end, you have to balance across a very long maze of rotating beams with spikes.  Once you finally get past that (it took me a few days), you have to climb up a big rotating column covered in spikes.  And after that?  Another big rotating column covered in spikes.    Once I finished God of War, I was so annoyed that I don't really know why I started God of War II.  I had some of the same complaints with God of War II as I did with the first game, but perhaps I was used to it, since I enjoyed GOW II much more.  There are some insanely difficult sections here too, but it didn't seem as sadistic!    The only technical complaint I had with the game is that it's very hard to hear the spoken words during the cut scenes.  The sound is fine throughout most of the game, so I don't know why that would be.    Two good games for $30 is a great deal. I've had my fill of Kratos for now, but I'll play them again some day. I'm sure I'll play God of War III at some point.

product_title: XFPS 3.0 Sniper - Keyboard & Mouse Adapter for Xbox 360
review_body: Having spent years and years playing FPS's on my PC I found using the Xbox 360 controller was clunky and very inaccurate. I really wanted to be able to use a mouse and keyboard to give the Xbox 360 a PC feel. After reading the reviews on the XPFS 360 I was unsure about it, but I decided to take the risk. I am SO glad I did. The setup was easy and it works like a charm. I am using an Dell PS/2 keyboard, a Microsoft 5 button mouse and an off brand USB Xbox 360 controller all at the same time. I can switch between the mouse and the controller at anytime. This comes in handy for Halo where I do find the controller preferable to the mouse when in vehicles.     The setup is VERY easy. Just plug in the Xbox controller, let it identify the controller, remove the controller, plug in the XFPS and then plug in the Xbox controller to the XFPS and you are done. It is that easy. Worked like a champ on Halo 3. It is super easy to create your custom config. Hit the program button, hit the button or stick on the xbox controller and then hit the mouse or keyboard key. That's it, it is that simple. Instantly my game improved and it was like playing Halo CE on the PC. I was able to hit mid air sniper shots in multiplayer mode that would not have been possible with the xbox controller.     Now, it does take some getting used to and it is not exactly 100% like playing on a PC. However, it is pretty darn close and 100% better than using the controller (IMO). Plus compared to the PC there are no drivers to download, not patches to apply, no new video cards to buy, etc. I have read some reviews where people complain about the cost of this device. However, this device is 1/2 the price of a decent video card for a PC that will have inferior performance to the Xbox 360. All things considered I am EXTREEMLY pleased with this product and would recommend it to anyone who wants to use a mouse & keyboard on any FPS to improve their accuracy. Be sure to get the 3.0 version, it is a yellow color, notgreen like the picture.    Enjoy!

review_headline: Square is done. R.I.P Final Fantasy
review_body: Check out the reviews on AMAZON.JP if you don't believe it. It's not popular in Japan either.     SquareEnix should just start calling these games something other than Final Fantasy. I've been with this franchise since the original NES release and played and loved every installment through VII. This game XIII is really a departure from what made the series popular to begin with. Square is now catering to the Eye candy crowd who don't care about substance. Ultimately, this game can hardly be called an RPG at all. It's actually a beautifully crafted CG movie where between cutscenes you advance the story line by fighting a bit of monsters. If you're familiar with FF Advent Children movie, it's just like that but with a battle system.     Pros: Graphics are stunning, music is great, and story line is epic.     Cons: Limited character customization, no towns, no armor and limited equipment, EXTREME linearity meaning a map is actually a straight and narrow hallway which you just walk straight down until the next cut scene. Control only one character in battle. Cut scenes are long and numerous, giving me the feeling this is actually a CG movie with an integrated battle system.     Call me old school but IMO the best days of Final Fantasy are behind it. Final Fantasy III aka *VI* and VII were the pinnacle of the series. If you are a fan of the first seven installments I doubt you would like this game. And don't give me the *well this game is a JRPG and is too sophisticated for westerners*, the only reason there is a so called sophisticated FF XIII is because those original games were excellent and paved the way. Square needs to learn If it ain't broke don't fix it.     Also, it has come to my attention that many people believe that *FF HAS ALWAYS LED THE WAY IN GRAPHICS AND IT'S A SIGNATURE OF THE FRANCHISE*, please refer to FF III *VI*. It's probably the best FF title ever made and w/ simple 16-bit graphics. So no, they have not always led the way in graphics and that is not what makes a solid RPG.     Honestly I don't see how any true FF fan can accept this as part of the franchise. The good reviews are simply lies by fanboys, intended to defend the franchise they've gotten too close to. These blinded fanboys have lost sight of what an RPG is supposed to be. Don't reward mediocrity, not everything that comes out of Square or Japan is gold and XIII is a perfect example. Check out the review on AMAZON.JP if you don't believe it. It's not popular in Japan either.

product_title: Ear Force X41 Digital RF Wireless Game Audio+ Chat with Dolby 7.1 Surround Sound -Xbox 360
review_headline: The good, the bad, and the idiotic
review_body: Much of the good points of these headphones have been discussed already in other reviews, so I won't waste your time adding much more. Overall the headsets are a lot of fun for gaming, and I'm glad I have them, but there are some setbacks you should know about before purchasing them.    1 - comfort level leaves a lot to be desired. My ears aren't particularly large, and yet they barely fit in the headphones. The first half hour is fine, but after that the pressure of the headphones pressing my ear against my head becomes uncomfortable, and I have to readjust them every few minutes.  Not agonizing, but could be much better fit if only they were a little bit larger.    2 - there are some design choices that make you ask yourself -- how the heck did this make it through committee meetings, engineering reports, testing -- and make it into the final product. Like, I once drove a car where if you wanted to honk the horn, you had to press down a tiny button on the very tip of the turn signal. I mean, a truly moronic idea that was actually manufactured and sold into the car!    Well, these headphones have an idiotic idea built into them. Standard xbox 360 headphones (for voice chat) plug into your controller and have an easy to access mute switch right by your thumb. While you play the game, if you want to mute/unmute your mic, you just slide your thumb down and flip a switch. Never have to let go of the controller.     These headphones don't work like that. Nooooooo. There's a long, thin cable between the headphones and the controller -- that's fine. And 1/3 of the way up from the controller on this cable is a tiny rectangular box. The box has a tiny tiny slider on one side that controls your mic volume, and a tiny tiny switch on the other side that controls your mute settings.    So, say you want to mute your mic in the middle of a Modern Warfare 2 battle, and you're playing in a room with the lights off. Well, you've got to PUT THE CONTROLLER DOWN, feel your way up thiscable to find the plastic box that's just slightly larger than a quarter, and then, well, GUESS which side of the box controls your mic volume, and which side is the mute switch. They are so small there's no way to feel your way through this.    Wait, your lights are on? Better, but still plan on putting the controller down (this requires 2 hands, one to hold the idiot little box, the other to toggle the switch), but the text on the plastic cover is SOOO small, and the switches sooo similar, that it'll take you a second to figure out which switch does what.    Yo, Turtle Beach... find the designer who came up with this brilliant idea and give him a choice: he can be fired, or he can be flogged mercilessly and keep his job but be demoted to a human stepstool. Because this guy is a moron. Then, go get your execs that APPROVED Mr. Moron's work, and flog them all THEN fire them.     All they had to do was keep the mute switch right where Microsoft has theirs. But noooooo, they had to lose some IQ points and screw it all up by placing it in an inaccessible, difficult to find, constantly moving location (because, you know, thin cables move around a lot).    Oh by the way, the other controls? Headset volume, effects button, etc? Not easy to find without taking headsets off and looking at them, either. But not as bad as the above piece of idiot engineering.

review_headline: Much, much better than the previous version!
review_body:
having owned the 60GB version of this product (or was it 80), I was completely unimpressed. This is so much of a vast improvement over that, I'm surprised it's even related to the same product. This takes the 360 from behind the PS3 to the lead in the consoles, at least to me.

Benefits:
Kinnect ready - Nobody knows what games will be ready for this yet, but it's there
Wireless N networking - FINALLY they got this right in a console
250GB drive - It won't be easy to fill this one up ;)
Exclusive games - Both consoles have this on their side, but for me, the 360 wins this one. Halo, Too Human, Fable, these games make the console for me
LOW NOISE - If you had the 360 prior to this, I'm sorry. I KNOW how loud that thing was, and this seems to have gotten rid of that. There's still occasional noise on Hard Drive access, but that's to be expected, nothing is going to be 'whisper quiet'.

Thats the good part.

The DRM on this absolutely sucks. I will NEVER buy another game that runs on Steam. Its fine if you have a persistant internet connection or only want to play online, but if you want to continue to use the game you paid for, you MUST periodically get online and have it 'phone home' and check back in with Steam every couple days. They should mention that on the box with the game requirements, but they don't.

Even if you just want to play single player offline, you will soon get locked out of using the game until you can go back online and allow the game to re-connect with Steam. How about that? You can't use the product you paid for unless you let it check back in periodically.

I fully understand the need to protect the intellectual property of the game publishers, but this is far more onerous than that. A simple disc check would be sufficient, but when the game needs to check back in the Steam every couple days to keep running, thats simply unconscionable.

Never again. Don't buy into this kind of DRM.

I picked this game up in the store, thinking it would be fun. So far, not yet.

The main things that drag this game down from a 3 or 4-star game is the confusing interface, lack of tutorial, lack of instructions, and lack of tooltips. Absolutely nothing is explained to you, you have to guess at everything - which of course leads to repeated failures, game reloads, and hours of \\"not-fun.\\" A tutorial, or even a decent instruction manual (the one that comes with the game is worthless. It tells you what you can do, but doesn't explain how to) would save hours of frustration, and get the player into \\"enjoying\\" the game much faster (that's the point, right?).

The lack of tooltips is part of this. I'd really like to know what a button does before I click on it...not try to guess what it did after the fact. That, and there's no explanation as to why you can't do something. I'd also like to know how do do certain key things - like heal up my adventurer after battle, or how to split up a unit after combining it. I did eventually figure these things out, but those are just some examples of things that *should* be basic knowledge, and included in a tutorial or instruction booklet.

Overall, this game does not seem worth purchasing. I sincerely wish I could get my money back.

Edit: Due to the poor support of the game thus far (still no multiplayer, for example. That's a core advertised feature still missing, yet another indication we're only seeing a hastily put-together beta, rather than a finished retail product), I am adjusting my review downwards. I have been tracking progress on the game's forums, and the blind denial of the development team to massive issues within the game is disappointing and, quite frankly, astonishing.

I play a lot of casual games.  I particularly enjoy puzzle games.  I buy them and blow through them like popcorn.    Since I purchased Square Logic via Steam 45 days ago, my casual game budget has plummeted.  I'm too busy feeding all my spare time into this game to even be tempted by any other puzzle game.    I like Sudoku.  I like KenKen.  I like the pic cross games.  I love Square Logic.  Each of the modes is pleasurable, from the simplest, with a single board and every square in the board included in one of the clue sets, up to the hidden cage mode and the endless series of greater then & less then connectors between squares.  My favorite is the two board combos, where hints on one board inform the other.    I've probably played close to 500 puzzles, and there are thousands left to go.  Even after skipping all the 4x4 and 5x5 boards (too easy once you learn how to play), I anticipate playing this game for months to years.    If you are a puzzle person, enjoy entertaining yourself on the computer, and are comfortable with simple math, you owe it to yourself to buy this game.    I even shared it with my friend's 8 year old.  He didn't play it the way I play it (he guessed and used hints rather than trying to solve them w/o hints), but he enjoyed it as well.    Again, if you like puzzles and are comfortable with computers and simple math, you own it to yourself to try this game.  btw, you can get a downloadable free trial for an hour, so if you're not sure you'll enjoy it, give it a try.

review_headline: You can get more for less elsewhere
review_body:
This \\"[[ASIN:B001UL4JBY DSi Media Kit]]\\" contains a Kingston 2GB SD memory card, plus a generic USB card reader. But before you get this or any other similar kits, please consider the following facts:

1. You don't really need a SD card to play the Nintendo DSi or DSi XL. The DSi comes with 256MB internal memory, of which about 128MB can be used for photo files and downloaded DSiWare programs. The external memory card is only necessary when:
- You want to backup photos files from your DSi to your computer, or
- You want to play music files on you DSi, or
- You downloaded too many DSiWare programs, and need to off-load some to make room for system memory.

2. There are no special requirements for the external memory card. Any regular SD or SDHC card can be used, regardless of its capacity and speed rating. Note that the photo files of DSi are very tiny (typically under 100KB) so even a 2GB SD card can store something like 20,000 photos. Also you'll not see any speed difference whether you're using the slowest 'class-2' SD card, or the fastest 'class-10' card.

3. The USB card reader included here is of very poor quality (see my review on \\"[[ASIN:B0018L8V92 10-in-1 USB 2.0 High Speed Memory Card Reader]]\\" for details). Fortunately, most computers and laptops already come with integrated SD card reader. So you don't really need to buy a separate USB SD-card reader.

Knowing the above, you'll see that this so-called \\"DSi media kit\\" is really nothing special. For about half the price, you can buy a similar memory card (such as the [[ASIN:B000EOMXM0 Kingston 2 GB SD Card]] or [[ASIN:B003AM8A1G SanDisk 2 GB SD card]]). Or you can pay similar price and get a 4-8GB card instead. It will work equally well in your DSi.

review_body: We bought this game after not purchasing any olympic sports games since the n64 or super nintendo.  What a change!  The graphics of course are great but the real value is in the play and replay value of the game.  The variety of events and the ability to play all the way through the Olympics or just one event give this tremendous flexibility. review_headline: A lot of criticism is well founded
review_body: The issue with this game begins with the skirmish mode. First they took out base building which was a huge mistake. Took away from the defensive player and the rusher. The skirmish is all just rushing to capture different points while the other player captures separate ones. The whole thing is just a cat and mouse game capturing points. Furthermore they destroyed the greatness of the battle by allowing players to withdrawl and turn into speed demons that cower back at the base which is really weak. How does a unit getting shot up and scared allow him to run circles around healthy units. So they took away base building and allowed players to retreat back to a protected base with ease. So lets just say the battle is even and the neither player retreats (which is rare). The amount of troops you produce is cut by 60%. Every squad is smaller, more expensive so you can't amass this great army like you could in the first game. So if you enjoyed two great armies clashing with many men falling and you keep pushing ,and then run into a great defense that you have to sneak around or bust through that is in the past. Now what we are left with is one squad of 3 men go that way and two squads go up the middle and hope you win this funless chess match. No epic climax no great battle just constantly taking and retaking points.

review_body: I used to go to the arcades mainly to play video games but Pin*Bot was the 1st if not only pinball machine that caught my eye & \\"stole\\" my quarters before the original NES came out & pretty much made me a home gamer so when I saw Pin*Bot was one of the lower rated games on this collection, I had to check it out. Some were close calls but I made it so you don't have to be an expert at all. The Williams challenge only took me about 4 tries so it's highly doable though I had some close calls.  Jive Time is a bigdisappointment as a reward.
